# All4one ### 404 working tools. One portable binary. No plugins, no packs, no filler. Every tool gets its own page with its own options — search it, open it, set what you need, run it. ![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-4.1.0-6d8cff?style=flat-square) ![Tools](https://img.shields.io/badge/tools-404-3fb950?style=flat-square) ![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%2010%2F11-0078D4?style=flat-square) ![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-f7c948?style=flat-square) ![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial-blue?style=flat-square) **🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/All4ONE/)** · **🖼️ [Screenshots](#-what-it-looks-like)** · **📚 [All 404 tools](TOOL_CATALOG.md)** · **⬇️ [Download](https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE/releases)**
--- ## What this is A rebuilt utility suite for Windows: file and folder work, text and data, encoding and hashing, images, PDFs, media, documents, network diagnostics, system and disk maintenance, developer helpers, security checks, calculators and generators — in a single executable that needs no installer, writes nothing to the registry, and runs off a USB stick. It is a rewrite, not a reskin. The previous version registered 551 tools across 45 plugin packs behind one dense table; a large share of those were thin adapters with near-duplicate behaviour ("Image Cropper — Crop image.", "Sparse File Inspector — report internals"). That architecture is gone: | | Before (3.x) | Now (4.0) | |---|---|---| | Structure | 45 plugin packs, a Packs tab, enable/disable toggles | One flat catalogue — nothing to enable, nothing to install | | Tools | 551 registered, many trivial or duplicated | 404, each with a real implementation and its own options | | UI | Tkinter, one table + details pane for everything | Qt (PySide6), sidebar navigation, one page per tool | | Options | Free-text argument box | Typed controls generated from each tool's own schema | | Verification | Registry smoke test only | Every runnable tool executed against fixtures on every build | Nothing was kept just to keep the count up. Every tool listed in [TOOL_CATALOG.md](TOOL_CATALOG.md) runs, and the sweep that proves it ships with the repository. ## What it looks like | Home | A tool page | |---|---| | ![Home](docs/screenshots/home-dark.png) | ![Tool page](docs/screenshots/tool-page.png) | | Category listing | Light theme | |---|---| | ![Category](docs/screenshots/category.png) | ![Light](docs/screenshots/home-light.png) | ## How it works **Sidebar.** Home, Favourites, Recently used, then every category with a live count. Dependencies and Settings sit at the bottom; the sun/moon button switches theme. **Search.** `Ctrl+K` from anywhere. Results are ranked on name, category, summary and keywords — typing "split" finds PDF splitting, file splitting and text splitting. **A tool page.** The header carries the tool's name, category, readiness and a star for favourites. On the left, the options: text boxes, dropdowns, numbers, colour pickers, toggles, and file/folder pickers that accept drag-and-drop. On the right, the output console: streaming lines as the tool works, a progress bar when the tool reports progress, and buttons to copy, save or open whatever the tool produced. **Running.** `Ctrl+Enter` runs. Long jobs stream and can be stopped. Tools that change or delete data ask first, and show a red badge on their page. **Readiness, not gatekeeping.** A tool that needs FFmpeg, Tesseract or a Python package is still listed; it says what is missing and how to get it. Nothing is hidden and nothing silently fails. ## Quick start ### The portable build Download `All4one-4.1.0-windows.zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE/releases), unzip, run `All4one.exe`. That is the whole installation. ### From source ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/All4ONE.git cd All4ONE pip install PySide6 # only needed for the desktop UI python main.py # desktop app python main.py list # every tool, by category ``` The engine and every standard-library tool run on bare Python — PySide6 is only for the window. ## Command line The same binary is a proper CLI, and every GUI option has an identical flag: ```powershell all4one list # all 404 tools, grouped all4one list --category PDF # one category all4one search hash # ranked search all4one show pdf-merge # options, defaults, readiness all4one run hash-file --file report.pdf --algorithm sha256 all4one run gst-calc --amount 10000 --rate 18 all4one run pdf-extract-pages --file book.pdf --pages "1-3,7" --output ch1.pdf all4one deps # what optional extras are installed ``` Options come from the tool's own field definitions, so the CLI can never drift from the UI. Boolean options are `--flag` / `--no-flag`. ## Optional dependencies The app and 380 of the tools run on the Python standard library alone. The rest declare what they need and light up when it is present: | Needs | Unlocks | |---|---| | Pillow | 26 image tools | | pypdf | 24 PDF tools | | FFmpeg / ffprobe | 20 media tools | | openpyxl · python-docx | 15 document tools | | Tesseract · Poppler | OCR and PDF-to-image | | 7-Zip · LibreOffice · git | archive, office conversion, git tools | | cryptography | file encryption | | pywin32 | the Windows API tools | Run `all4one deps` — or open **Dependencies** in the app — for the exact install line for each one. ## Architecture ```text main.py entry point: no arguments opens the UI, else the CLI core/ tool.py the contract — a tool is a function + a field schema registry.py discovery, validation, ranking, readiness runner.py one execution path for UI and CLI, streaming + cancel deps.py optional dependency probes and install hints cli.py argparse front-end built from the same schemas settings.py one small JSON file: theme, favourites, recents ui/ theme.py design tokens + the whole stylesheet (dark and light) icons.py line icons as inline SVG — no image files to ship widgets.py cards, chips, option editors, the output console pages.py home, category, search, tool page, settings, dependencies window.py sidebar shell, navigation history, search tools/ 16 modules; a tool is ~15 lines plus its options scripts/ catalogue + landing-page generators, release audit tests/sweep.py runs every runnable tool against fixtures docs/index.html the landing page, generated from the registry ``` A tool looks like this, and that is all it takes to appear in the app with a page: ```python @tool(id="gst-calc", name="GST Calculator", category="Numbers", summary="Add or remove GST at any rate, and split CGST/SGST or IGST correctly.", fields=[F.number("amount", "Amount (₹)", 10000.0, minimum=0.0), F.choice("rate", "GST rate", ["5", "12", "18", "28"], "18")]) def gst_calc(v, ctx): ... ``` The UI renders the fields, the CLI turns them into flags, and the catalogue is generated from the same metadata. There is no registration step and no plugin manifest. ## Building the binary ```powershell pip install -r requirements-build.txt python build.py # audit → tests → PyInstaller onefile → zip ``` Output in `dist/`: `All4one.exe` and `All4one--windows.zip`. PyInstaller cannot cross-compile a Windows binary, so the real `.exe` is produced by GitHub Actions on a `windows-latest` runner — every push to `main` builds one, and a `v*` tag publishes it as a release. The Linux job runs the audit and the full tool sweep on every push. ## Verification ```bash python scripts/audit.py # catalogue integrity, versions, hygiene, imports python tests/sweep.py # executes every runnable tool against real fixtures ``` Both are wired into CI and must pass before a build is published. The audit rejects duplicate ids, duplicate summaries, unknown dependency keys, undocumented tools and version drift; the sweep is what stops a tool from quietly becoming decoration. ## Documentation | Document | For | |---|---| | [USER_GUIDE.md](USER_GUIDE.md) | Using the app: search, tool pages, options, output, shortcuts | | [INSTALLATION.md](INSTALLATION.md) | Portable build, from source, optional dependencies, troubleshooting | | [TOOL_CATALOG.md](TOOL_CATALOG.md) | Every tool, its options and what it needs — generated from the registry | | [DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md](DEVELOPER_GUIDE.md) | The tool contract, adding a tool or a category, testing | | [BUILDING.md](BUILDING.md) | The build pipeline, CI workflows, releasing | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | What changed in 4.0 and why | | [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md) | Reporting, and the safety design | | [docs/index.html](docs/index.html) | The landing page served at drsamonline.github.io/All4ONE | The catalogue and the landing page are generated from the live registry (`scripts/catalogue.py`, `scripts/landing.py`), and the audit fails if either drifts from the code — so the numbers in these pages are the numbers in the app. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence Released under the **PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0** — free for personal and other noncommercial use; # BlinkTransfer ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Send a file with light. No internet, no Bluetooth, no cables.** Animated QR codes, **rateless-coded** so a missed frame never breaks the transfer — the receiver only needs *enough* frames, not every one. [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-7c3aed)](LICENSE) [![Commercial licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/commercial-licence%20available-22c55e)](COMMERCIAL.md) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/commits) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/stargazers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/total)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases) [![Top language](https://img.shields.io/github/languages/top/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER) [![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-6366f1)](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/play/) **[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/play/)**  ·  **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/BLINKTRANSFER/)**  ·  **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases/latest/download/BLINKTRANSFER-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER/releases/latest/download/BLINKTRANSFER.apk)
--- BlinkTransfer moves files between two devices using **only a screen and a camera**. One device shows an animated QR code; the other points its camera at it. Nothing leaves the room — there is no server, no network and no pairing. It is the **universal** member of the optical-transfer family: monochrome QR only, standards-based, and deliberately dependency-light, so it works on the cheapest phones and in the worst light. ## Why it is different - **Rateless (fountain) coding.** Frames are LT-encoded symbols, not an ordered list. Miss one, or twenty, and the transfer still finishes — you just need about *k* good frames out of the loop. This is the feature the previous version promised and did not ship. - **Any-scanner compatibility mode.** A small text file can be sent as a single plain QR that *any* third-party scanner can read — no app needed on the other side. - **Truly offline.** Fully installable PWA; after first load it never touches the network. - **Light on dependencies.** Two small, well-known libraries (`qrcode-generator` to draw, `jsQR` to read) and nothing else at runtime. ## How it works ``` files ─▶ gzip ─▶ split into k blocks ─▶ LT fountain symbols ─▶ QR frames (loop) │ files ◀─ gunzip ◀─ reassemble ◀─ LT belief-propagation decode ◀─ jsQR ◀ camera ``` Each QR carries a 22-byte self-describing header plus one fountain symbol, so the receiver can lock on to **any** frame — there is no header QR to catch first. A header CRC-16 drops mis-read frames; the QR's own Reed-Solomon handles bit errors; a CRC-32 on the whole payload confirms the finished file. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/BLINKTRANSFER.git cd BLINKTRANSFER npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm test # run the test suite npm run build # production bundle into docs/play/ ``` Open the dev URL on both devices (or install the PWA). On one, **Send** and pick files; on the other, **Receive** and point the camera. ## Performance Throughput is roughly `frame bytes × frame rate`. Defaults: ~1.4 KB per frame at 12 fps ≈ 17 KB/s, and larger files loop. | What | Note | |------|------| | Per frame | ~1.4 KB (balanced), ~0.8 KB (robust), ~1.8 KB (dense) | | Frame rate | 2–24 fps, your choice | | Limits | 20 MB total per transfer | | Overhead | ~5–15% extra frames for the fountain decoder | Bigger files work, but for anything over a few MB a network would be faster — this is for when there is no network, or when you would rather there were not. ## Compatibility mode Tick **Compatibility mode** to send one small text file (≤ 1.2 KB) as a single plain QR. Any phone camera app will read it — useful for links, addresses, Wi-Fi passwords and quick notes, with no second device running BlinkTransfer. ## Browser support Chrome 80+, Edge 80+, Firefox 114+, Safari 16+. Requires `getUserMedia` (camera), `CompressionStream` (gzip) and — for the sender — the Wake Lock API (optional). `jsQR` and `qrcode-generator` are bundled, so nothing is fetched at runtime. ## Project layout ``` src/ index.html styles.css main.js sw.js lib/ fountain.js LT fountain codes (encoder + belief-propagation decoder) frame.js frame header, presets, CRC codec.js multi-file container + gzip qr.js QR encode (qrcode-generator) / decode (jsQR) utils.js CRC-16/32, PRNG, helpers public/ manifest + icons tests/ node --test suite (fountain, frame, codec, optical loopback) tools/ build.mjs, dev.mjs, serve.js docs/ landing page + built demo (GitHub Pages) ``` ## Testing ```bash npm test ``` The suite includes a full **optical loopback**: files → gzip → fountain frames → rendered QR pixels → jsQR → fountain decode → files, with binary data. No browser required. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence BlinkTransfer is **free for personal, academic, hobby and non-profit use** under the [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](LICENSE). **Commercial use needs a paid licence** — see [COMMERCIAL.md](COMMERCIAL.md) for what counts as commercial and how to get one (by email invoice). Third-party components and their licences are listed in [NOTICE](NOTICE). > Note: earlier versions were published under the PolyForm Noncommercial licence. That grant stands > for copies already distributed; this and future versions use the dual model > above. ## Credits Built by **Dr Sohil Momin** ([@drsamonline](https://github.com/drsamonline)). # CLDR — Command Line Dispatch & Route **A single tiny Rust binary that sits in your tray, pops up on a keystroke, and runs whatever you type — a sum, a path, an app, a search.** [![Build & Release](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/actions/workflows/build-release.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/actions/workflows/build-release.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/CLDR?include_prereleases&style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux-blue?style=flat-square)](#-download) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-orange?logo=rust&logoColor=white&style=flat-square)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [![License: MIT + attribution](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT%20%2B%20attribution-yellow?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) ### [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/CLDR/) · [Download the latest release](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) · [User guide](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) · [Setup guide](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md) · [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
--- --- ![CLDR command window](docs/screenshots/01-main.png)
Type anything. CLDR routes it — math, unit conversion, a path, an app, or a web search.
--- ### `/cmd` — run it and read the answer `/run` spawns detached and shows nothing, which is right for opening an editor. `/cmd` is for the other question: *what does this print?* ```text > /cmd lumen stats $ lumen stats → exit 0 index /home/you/.local/share/lumen/lumen.db photos 131 favourites 3 with GPS 0 folders 4 > /cmd lumen search "harbour at dawn" --json > /cmd git status --short > /cmd uname -a ``` - Arguments are split the way a shell would, so quotes work: `/cmd lumen search "harbour at dawn"`. - stdout and stderr are both captured, capped at `max_results` rows; a single line longer than 500 characters is truncated and says how many characters were dropped (`… (+39412 chars)`). - The exit code is shown on the summary line. - **It gives up after five seconds.** A launcher that freezes is worse than one that says "still running", so a command that outlives the cap is reported and left running in the background — use `/run` for anything long. ## 📌 What is CLDR? CLDR is a **single-binary command launcher** for Windows and Linux. Bind it to a desktop shortcut or global hotkey; it stays resident in the background and **summons its command window** when you press the key. Type anything — CLDR *routes* it to the right action instantly and shows the result inline. ```text > 2*(3+4)/7 → [CALC] 2*(3+4)/7 = 2 > 10 km in mi → [CALC] 10 km in mi = 6.213712 mi > notes.md → [OK] opened /home/you/notes.md > code → [RUN] spawned `code` (detached) > rust lifetimes → [WEB] browser → https://duckduckgo.com/?q=rust+lifetimes ``` ## ✨ Features | | | |---|---| | 🪟 **Tray-resident, one keystroke** | Lives in the background; the shortcut **summons** the existing window instead of opening a duplicate | | 🧠 **Smart routing cascade** | math → unit conversion → existing path → PATH binary → web search | | 🧮 **Zero-dep calculator** | `+ - * / % ^ ( )` with unary minus, right-associative power, div/mod-by-zero guards | | 📐 **Unit conversion** | `10 km in mi`, `2 h in min`, `10 GB in MB` — ten dimensions: length, mass, time, volume, area, speed, data, pressure, energy, temperature | | 🗂️ **Slash commands** | `/run` `/cmd` `/open` `/ls` `/find` `/web` `/calc` `/sys` `/help` `/clear` | | ⏱️ **Command history** | `↑`/`↓` (or `Ctrl+P`/`Ctrl+N`), persisted between runs | | 📋 **Copy without a clipboard crate** | `Ctrl+Y` copies the last result via OSC 52 — works over SSH | | ⚙️ **Config + aliases** | `~/.config/cldr/config.toml` — search engine, caps, and `alias.g = /web` | | 🩺 **Hardware diagnostics** | `/sys` — cores, OS, hostname, user, no external tools | | 🪶 **Near-idle** | Redraws only on change; idle cost is one `poll()` every 250 ms | | 🔒 **No clipboard, no telemetry, no network daemon** | The only socket is loopback-only, for summon | ## 📥 Download Grab the latest from the [**Releases**](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR/releases) page. | Platform | Portable | Installer | |---|---|---| | **Windows 10/11 x64** | `cldr-windows-x86_64.zip` — extract & run `cldr.exe` | `cldr--setup.exe` | | **Linux x86_64** | `cldr-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` — extract & run `./cldr` | `./install.sh` | | **Linux ARM64** (Pi 4/5) | `cldr-linux-aarch64.tar.gz` | `./install.sh` | Every release ships a `SHA256SUMS.txt` and SLSA build provenance. ### Portable (no install) ```powershell # Windows Expand-Archive cldr-windows-x86_64.zip -DestinationPath $env:LOCALAPPDATA\cldr & "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\cldr\cldr.exe" --summon ``` ```bash # Linux tar -xzf cldr-linux-x86_64.tar.gz ./cldr-linux-x86_64/cldr --summon ``` ### Installer ```powershell # Windows — run the setup, or from a portable folder: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts\install-shortcut.ps1 ``` ```bash # Linux — installs to ~/.local/bin + menu entry + tray autostart + Super+Alt+C ./install.sh ``` ## 🏁 Build from source ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR && cd CLDR cargo build --release # → target/release/cldr(.exe) cargo test # engine + IPC + extras unit tests cargo run -- --self-test # 14 headless checks (exit 0 = pass) ``` No system libraries, no C toolchain beyond what Rust already needs. ## 🗂️ In-window commands | Command | Description | |---|---| | `/run ` | spawn detached via the OS shell | | `/open ` | open a file/folder in the default viewer | | `/ls [path]` | list a directory (row-capped) | | `/find ` | recursive search (depth-capped) | | `/web ` | search in your default browser | | `/calc ` | arithmetic `+ - * / % ^ ( ) unary-` | | `/sys` | hardware diagnostics | | `/help` · `/clear` | cheat sheet · clear pane | | *(no prefix)* | auto: math → units → path → PATH app → web | ### Keyboard | Key | Action | |---|---| | `Enter` | submit | | `↑` `↓` | history (empty input) / scroll results | | `Ctrl+P` `Ctrl+N` | history prev / next | | `PgUp` `PgDn` `Home` `End` | scroll results | | `Ctrl+Y` | copy last result (OSC 52) | | `Ctrl+L` | clear pane | | `Del` | clear input | | `Esc` / `Ctrl+C` | quit | ![Routing examples](docs/screenshots/02-routing.png) ## ⚙️ Configuration `cldr --config` writes a commented starter file to `~/.config/cldr/config.toml` (Linux) or `%APPDATA%\cldr\config.toml` (Windows). Everything is optional. ```toml # search engine — {q} is replaced by the URL-encoded query search_url = "https://duckduckgo.com/?q={q}" # search_url = "https://www.google.com/search?q={q}" max_results = 50 # /ls and /find row cap find_depth = 4 # /find recursion depth # aliases: "name = replacement"; "name arg" appends arg alias.g = /web alias.gh = /web github.com alias.n = /run nvim ``` ## 🧲 How the tray + summon works ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant U as User (shortcut / hotkey) participant S as cldr --summon participant I as Loopback IPC (127.0.0.1, ~/.cldr/port) participant W as Running window U->>S: press shortcut S->>I: connect, send "SUMMON" I->>W: accept, reply "OK-WINDOW" W->>W: raise_window() (Win32 / xdotool) S-->>U: exits (no duplicate window) ``` Loopback-only control channel — no clipboard, no privileged APIs, no firewall prompt. A detached daemon (`--daemon-start`) services queued `open`/`run`/`sys` requests from atomically-published per-request files in a private, per-user state directory. ![Help cheat sheet](docs/screenshots/03-help.png) ## 🎯 Design goals | Goal | How | |---|---| | **Small** | 4 crates total (`crossterm`, `ratatui`, `open`, `walkdir`); full LTO, one codegen unit, symbols stripped, `panic=abort` | | **Fast** | Redraw only on change; a single 250 ms `poll()` when idle; no async runtime | | **Dependency-free at runtime** | One binary; nothing to install, no DLLs, no Python | | **Private** | Never reads or writes the clipboard; no telemetry; the only socket is loopback | > **Why a terminal window, not a native GUI?** A native toolkit (winit/egui/Qt) > would add tens of MB of dependencies and binary size. The terminal *is* the > smallest possible GUI here — on Windows the console is auto-shrunk to a > compact ~92×26 box; on Linux your terminal emulator sizes it. ## 🏗️ Project layout ```text src/ ├─ main.rs CLI router (foreground / --summon / --tray / daemon / --self-test) ├─ engine.rs dispatcher, calc parser, smart cascade (+ unit tests) ├─ extras.rs config, aliases, history, unit conversion, base64, self-test ├─ ipc.rs loopback-TCP summon control channel ├─ tui.rs ratatui command window (dirty redraw, history, compact window) ├─ summon.rs window raising, autostart, tray loop └─ daemon.rs detached background worker packaging/ Windows installer (Inno Setup), Linux install/uninstall, portable notes scripts/ shortcut installers (PowerShell + sh) docs/ user guide, setup guide, shortcut recipes, screenshots ``` ## 📚 Documentation | Document | Contents | |---|---| | [docs/USER_GUIDE.md](docs/USER_GUIDE.md) | walkthrough, keys, examples, troubleshooting | | [docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md](docs/SETUP_GUIDE.md) | build, install, shortcuts, autostart, releases | | [docs/SHORTCUTS.md](docs/SHORTCUTS.md) | per-DE / per-tool hotkey recipes | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | version history | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | dev workflow, code style, PR rules | ## 🚀 Releases Releases are **tag-driven** and fully automated: ```bash # bump version in Cargo.toml + CHANGELOG.md, then: git tag v1.3.0 && git push origin v1.3.0 ``` CI builds Windows + Linux (x86_64 and aarch64), packages portable archives and the Windows installer, generates `SHA256SUMS.txt`, attests build provenance, and publishes the GitHub Release. ## ⚖️ License & attribution © **2026 Dr. Sohil Momin ([drsamonline](https://github.com/drsamonline))** — [PolyForm Noncommercial licensed with a mandatory attribution clause](LICENSE). HCS: # Holistic Compression Sources (HCS) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) Canonical, offline, vendored source vault for the **CHCE** engine (Chimera Hybrid Compression Engine) and all CHIMERA-family projects (`heavenzip`, `ziptastic`, `compfactory`). Every third-party compressor, preprocessor, recompressor, and entropy-coder reference used by CHCE lives in [`/old`](./old), pinned at a known-good revision. Consumers pull this repo with `git subtree` and build from the pinned tree. **Design constraints (non-negotiable):** 1. **Offline-only.** No neural networks, no model files, no GPU runtimes. Context-mixing (CM) compressors like `zpaq`, `paq8px`, `lpaq` are pure algorithms — they are **not AI** and are fully offline. 2. **Single source of truth.** One copy of each source, no nested `.git` directories. Sources are vendored flat, with one deliberate exception: 23 of them are **git submodules** pinned to an upstream commit, because copying another project's history would make this vault a fork of it rather than a mirror. See [Vendored sources and submodules](#vendored-sources-and-submodules). 3. **License-audited.** Every source is listed with its licence identifier in `SOURCES`. The full licence texts are **not yet collected** — see [Known gaps](#known-gaps). --- ## Integration Model | Consumer | How it uses HCS | |---|---| | `ziptastic` (native engine) | `git subtree` of `HCS` into `vendor/` | | `heavenzip` (orchestrator) | Consumes **prebuilt binaries** released by `ziptastic` — does not build from `/old` | | `compfactory` (workshop) | Full checkout; edits propagate back to HCS via PR | > **Rule:** `heavenzip` must never contain algorithm code; `ziptastic` must > never shell out to external executables. HCS exists to feed `ziptastic`. --- ## Repository Layout HCS/ ├── README.md # this file ├── SOURCES # machine-readable manifest (id, url, pin, licence, integration) ├── .gitmodules # URL mapping for the 23 pinned sources ├── LICENSES/ # PLANNED: one .txt per source (see Known gaps) ├── old/ # vendored sources (the vault) │ ├── xz/ │ ├── zpaq/ │ ├── srep/ │ └── ... └── (future) └── chimera/ # Treat it as an **external process** invoked by `heavenzip`, or drop JPEG recompression for now. - **`advancecomp` is GPL-3.** Same rule: external process, not linked. - **`upx` is GPL-2.0.** Same rule. - **`lzo` is GPL / commercial dual.** Do not link unless CHCE is GPL. - **`paq8px` is GPL-2.0.** Treat as an **external process** in `heavenzip` for the `--max-ratio` tier, not a linked library. All other listed sources are permissive (MIT, BSD, Apache-2.0, zlib, PD, 0BSD) and safe to link into a closed-source CHCE core. --- ## 🏆 The Offline Ratio Ladder CHCE selects a tier per block based on the joint parser's cost model. This is the target performance envelope across the sources in `/old`: | Tier | Backend(s) | Ratio vs xz | Speed vs xz | |---|---|---|---| | **Max ratio** | `paq8px` / `LPAQ9` | 0.70–0.80× | 0.001× | | **High ratio** | `zpaqfranz -m5` / `zpaq` | 0.80–0.85× | 0.01× | | **Strong** | `bzip3` / `libbsc` / PPMd (`7z`) | 0.90–0.98× | 0.5–2× | | **Baseline** | `xz` (LZMA2) | 1.00× | 1.00× | | **Balanced** | `zxc` / `zstd -19` / `brotli -q11` | 1.05–1.15× | 3–10× | | **Fast** | `density` / `lz4` / `csc` / `lizard` | 1.3–1.5× | 20–50× | | **Ultra-fast** | `heatshrink` / `brieflz` / `snappy` | 2× | 100×+ | Plus these orthogonal transforms that operate **before** the entropy tier: - **Semantic recompression** — `preflate`, `preflate-rs`, `precomp-cpp`, `aqueous`, `rhefo` (DEFLATE, JPEG, PNG, PDF, PE, SQLite, ~20 formats) - **Text tokenization** — `parmar` (+7–9.6 % on LZMA2 over raw text) - **Numeric bit-transpose** — `bitshuffle`, `pcodec` (2–10× on typed arrays) - **Short-string coding** — `shoco`, `smaz` - **Long-range dedup** — `srep` (matches beyond LZMA's 64 MB window) - **Executable packing** — `upx`, `zelf` --- ## Bumping a Source 1. `cd old/` and check out the desired revision. 2. Update the `pin` in `SOURCES`. 3. Confirm the licence from the source's own `LICENSE`/`COPYING` file and correct the `SOURCES` row if it moved. (`LICENSES/` is planned, not present — see [Known gaps](#known-gaps).) 4. Regenerate any integration tests in `ziptastic` that consume this source. 5. Open a PR titled `bump: → `. --- ## Adding a New Source 1. `git clone --depth=1 old/` **inside this repo**. 2. `rm -rf old//.git` — **critical, do not skip**. 3. Add a row to `SOURCES`. 4. Record the licence identifier in the `SOURCES` row. Full licence texts are not collected yet — see [Known gaps](#known-gaps). 5. Add a row to the appropriate section of this README. 6. Commit: `add: ()`. --- ## Quick Verification To check that `/old` contains no nested `.git` folders (the most common mistake when vendoring): ```bash find old -name .git -type d # should print nothing ``` (The 23 pinned submodules are the exception and are expected to carry `.git`; the check above is about *copied* sources.) The equivalent for the pins is `./scripts/check-vendor.sh`, below. ## Vendored sources and submodules Most of `old/` is plain vendored source. 23 entries are **git submodules** — they pin one commit of an upstream repository rather than copying its history, so the mirror stays a mirror and HCS never claims authorship of code it did not write. ```bash git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/drsamonline/HCS # or, in an existing clone: git submodule update --init --recursive ``` **Verify at any time:** ```bash ./scripts/check-vendor.sh # exit 0 = every source present and mapped python3 tools/check-sources.py # exit 0 = every directory recorded, every id resolves ``` The second one exists because the first never reads `SOURCES`. A directory can materialise and still have no recorded upstream, licence or integration, and an id can point at a directory name the vault does not use (`xz` for `xz-master`). `tools/check-sources.py` reads both sides and says which rows and which directories disagree. It runs in CI, advisory until the findings it currently reports are settled. ### Why the guard exists Until this was fixed, `old/` carried those 23 gitlinks with **no `.gitmodules` file at all**. That state is unrecoverable: git records a commit SHA for each submodule but has nowhere to fetch it from, so `git submodule update --init` could not work, and every clone — HCS, and every repo that vendors a copy of it — silently got 23 empty directories. Nothing failed until a build or a benchmark reached for one of them, and then it looked like a missing source rather than a broken mirror. The repair was to add the URL mapping that was always missing (the recorded pins were all valid — 20 resolve by ref, and the remaining 3 fetch fine by SHA). The guard is the part that makes it not happen again: `scripts/check-vendor.sh` fails if any directory under `old/` is empty, if a gitlink has no `.gitmodules` entry, or if a `.gitmodules` entry points at a directory that does not exist. CI runs it on every push with `submodules: recursive`, so a mirror that cannot materialise goes red instead of going quiet. ## Known gaps - **Licence texts.** `SOURCES` records an SPDX identifier and an integration verdict per source, which is what `ziptastic` needs to decide whether a source may be linked. The full texts are not in the repository: there is no `LICENSES/`. Nothing in the tree is broken by this, but a downstream user shipping a binary cannot audit a licence from this vault alone, and the "copy the text before linking" rule has never had a directory to copy into. - **`MANIFEST.json`** records a producer and class per file for the files it knows about, and was last written on 2026-11-04. It is not regenerated on every push, so treat it as a snapshot rather than an index. `tools/manifest.py` is what writes it. - **The HCS `LICENSE` is PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0**, which covers the files this repository authors (the manifest, the catalogue, the tooling). The vendored sources under `old/` keep their own licences, which are the ones that govern them; the PolyForm terms cannot relicense code HCS did not write. That distinction is worth stating plainly because the badge at the top of this file reads as if it covers everything. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # 🏥 HHMS — Homeopathic Hospital Management System ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **A LAN-based hospital management system purpose-built for homeopathic hospitals and clinics.** Runs entirely on the local network with a server-owned database — *no internet dependency, no cloud lock-in.* [![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/landing%20page-live-1d4ed8?logo=githubpages&logoColor=white)](https://drsamonline.github.io/HMS/) [![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-1d4ed8?logo=githubpages&logoColor=white)](https://drsamonline.github.io/) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-0.0.1-informational)](VERSION) [![License: Proprietary](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-Proprietary-red.svg)](LICENSE) [![Tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-569%20passed-brightgreen)](backend/tests) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20LAN-lightgrey)](docs/DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) **Landing page:** · **Demo build:** · **Demo data guide:** [docs/DEMO_DATA.md](docs/DEMO_DATA.md) HHMS is a LAN application, so there is no hosted web demo — a fresh install seeds a full demo dataset automatically on first run.
--- ## 📐 Architecture at a Glance ```text ┌──────────────────┐ ┌──────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │ HHMS-Client.exe │ ─────► │ LAN HTTP/JSON │ ─────► │ HHMS-Server.exe │ │ (WebView2 UI) │ │ │ │ (server-owned SQLite) │ └──────────────────┘ └──────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────┘ ``` | Layer | Description | |-------|-------------| | 💻 **Client** | Lightweight HTML/CSS/vanilla-JavaScript interface hosted in WebView2 | | 🔌 **Transport** | HTTP/JSON over the hospital LAN with automatic server discovery | | 🗄️ **Server** | The only component that touches the shared SQLite database — the client never opens it directly | 📖 Details: [DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE](docs/DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [BACKEND_ARCHITECTURE](docs/BACKEND_ARCHITECTURE.md) · [FRONTEND_ARCHITECTURE](docs/FRONTEND_ARCHITECTURE.md) --- ## 📁 Repository Layout | Path | Contents | |------|----------| | [`backend/`](backend) | Python server: API routers, services, models, Alembic migrations, tests | | [`frontend/`](frontend) | Client UI: HTML, CSS, and vanilla JavaScript modules | | [`client/`](client) | Native Windows client host (WebView2 shell) | | [`docs/`](docs) | Full specification, architecture, workflow, and batch documentation ([index](docs/INDEX.md)) | | [`.ai/`](.ai) | Project constitution, coding rules, decisions, and state tracking | | [`data/`](data) | Runtime data directory (server-owned database and secrets) | --- ## ✨ Features **Clinical** — patient registration & search, OPD queue with token system, homoeopathic case records, diagnosis/ICD-11, prescriptions, IPD admission with ward/bed management, investigations/laboratory/X-Ray, annual case rollover and archival. **Operational** — billing & payments with live-derived invoice balances, pharmacy stock ledger with dispense integrity, procurement/goods receipt, department/service/designation masters, role-based dashboards (outstanding billing, bed occupancy, pending investigations, OPD queue, discharge audit). **Reporting & printing** — statistics engine, 16 screen/paper-parity print envelopes (receivables aging, collection summaries, receipt continuity, settlement/refund audits, ward occupancy, investigation billing reconciliation), PDF generation, report scheduling, batch printing. **Release-ready infrastructure** — LAN server discovery (UDP port 38541), single-file Windows/Linux server binaries, Inno/NSIS installers, automatic dual-platform GitHub releases (rolling `nightly` prerelease on every push to `main`, stable Release on `v*.*.*` tags), backup/restore workflows, login rate limiting, JWT hardening, secret-key rotation runbook. **569 backend tests passing.** --- ## 🚀 Quick Start ```bash cd backend pip install -r requirements.txt python -m app.server ``` The server runs migrations automatically, creates the default administrator (`admin` / `admin` — change it immediately; disable with `HHMS_BOOTSTRAP_DEFAULT_ADMIN=false`), seeds a full **2025 demo dataset** on first run (no commands needed — see below), serves the built-in web GUI at `http://localhost:8000/`, and listens on the configured LAN port. See [SERVER_STARTUP](docs/SERVER_STARTUP.md) and [DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE](docs/DEPLOYMENT_ARCHITECTURE.md) for production setup. ### Demo data (automatic on first run — no commands) On a brand-new install the server seeds a full year of realistic demo data by itself at startup — patients, OPD tokens, cases, prescriptions, dispenses, lab results, admissions, invoices and payments — so the GUI is populated the moment you open it. Portable builds (folder or EXE) work out of the box: copy → run → log in as `admin` / `admin`. - The seed runs **only** when the database is pristine; any install that already contains real data is never touched. - Opt out with environment variable `HHMS_SEED_DEMO_DATA=false` (recommended for production deployments). - Optional manual commands (not required): `python -m app.server seed-demo-data` supports `--year` and `--force`. Details: [docs/DEMO_DATA.md](docs/DEMO_DATA.md). --- ## 🔧 Development Workflow 1. Use the latest verified repository ZIP as the source of truth. 2. Rubrics support a parent heading and a note. | | **Marking system** | Define the grading scale yourself. Four presets ship in, and you can edit any of them or add your own schemes. | | **Author & branding** | Your name, credentials, clinic, email, website, book title, edition, year, copyright line and licence — stamped into every PDF, HTML file and workbook you export. | | **Cases** | A private case logger: log a case, track the outcome (Cured / Improved / No Change / Aggravated / Suppressed) and review the history. | | **Help** | The full how-to guide lives inside the app, plus a first-run tour and print-to-PDF. | | **About** | The dedication, the maker, and the licence it is released under. | Everything is stored **locally in your browser** (IndexedDB). Rubrics everywhere use the active scheme, and every export renders the grades accordingly. --- ## 📖 How to use it The same guide is built into the app — open the **Help** tab, or press **Take the tour**. **Getting started** 1. Open the **Materia Medica** tab and add your first remedy (or edit the three starter remedies). 2. Give it an abbreviation — short forms like `Acon` or `Nat-m` are what the repertory shows. 3. Add symptoms to it: pick a chapter (Mind, Head, Stomach…), write the symptom, set a grade. 4. Open the **Repertory** tab, add a chapter, then add rubrics inside it. 5. Inside a rubric, type a remedy abbreviation and press Enter to attach it, then choose its grade. 6. Fill in your **Author** details, then go to **Data** and export your book. **Building the repertory.** A rubric is a symptom heading such as *Anxiety, about health*. It may also have a parent heading (so *Morning* under *Sweat of the feet* reads as *Sweat of the feet, Morning*) and a note. **Backups.** Your work lives only in this browser. Export a JSON backup regularly, and import it on another device to carry your project across. --- ## 📤 Export & import | Format | Contents | |---|---| | **JSON — full backup** | Everything, re-importable here to restore the project. | | **JSON — OMM** | Repertory and/or materia medica in the reader-app schema (v1.1). | | **CSV** | All datasets as a zip, or one dataset at a time. | | **Excel (.xlsx)** | A workbook: Info, Remedies, Symptoms, Repertory, Cases, Marking. | | **PDF** | A printable book with your author block and copyright. | | **HTML** | A self-contained, styled document you can open or host. | | **SQL (.sql)** | Portable `INSERT` statements for SQLite, Postgres or MySQL. | | **SQLite (.sqlite)** | A real database file (`meta`, `remedy`, `symptom`, `rubric`, `remedy_link`, `case_log`). | **Import** accepts a full JSON backup, an OMM repertory or materia-medica file, or CSV — with **Merge** or **Replace** mode. --- ## 🔧 Under the hood All writers are dependency-free and run entirely in the browser: the `.xlsx`, `.pdf` and `.sqlite` files are generated byte-by-byte in JavaScript, so the app never needs a network connection or a library from a CDN. --- ## 🔗 Compatibility with the OMM reader app The JSON exports use the same envelope the reader app reads (`schema_version: "1.1"`, `type: "repertory"` / `"materia_medica"`, a `book` provenance block, and `sections → rubrics → remedy_table` / `remedies → symptoms`). A repertory built here drops straight into that collection, and a book extracted by the OMM pipeline can be imported here for editing. --- ## 🛠️ Running it locally ```bash python3 -m http.server 8080 # then open http://localhost:8080 ``` Deploy anywhere static — GitHub Pages, Netlify, Cloudflare Pages. # NOVA — Semantic Programming Platform [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-green)](LICENSE) **A statically-typed, compiled systems programming language.** Its compiler lowers NOVA source through a semantic pipeline — lexer, parser, semantic analyser, SIR, lowerer — to four backends: **C, JavaScript, Rust and WebAssembly**, with a runtime, package manager, language server and debugger alongside. **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/NEO/)** · **[Examples](examples/)** · **[Language spec](docs/language/)** · **[Development plan](DEV_PLAN.md)** · **[Architecture](ARCHITECTURE.md)** · **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** Live demo: not yet available — the project is pre-release (Phase 4 in progress).

The compiler transforms NOVA source code into multiple target languages (C, JavaScript, Rust, WebAssembly) through a robust semantic analysis pipeline. ## Current Status **✅ Phase 1: Compiler Core - COMPLETE** - Full lexer, parser, semantic analyzer implemented - SIR (Semantic Intermediate Representation) defined - Lowerer converts AST to SIR - 4 backends: C, JavaScript, Rust, WebAssembly - Total: ~3,500+ lines of compiler code **✅ Phase 2: Runtime System - COMPLETE** - ✅ Memory management (192 lines, arena allocation, GC foundation) - ✅ Type system (260 lines, type registry, dynamic values) - ✅ Error handling (297 lines, panic handling, backtraces) - ✅ FFI support (332 lines, C interop, FFI arrays) - ✅ Core runtime library (139 lines, initialization, stats) - ✅ Garbage collection (315 lines, mark-and-sweep implementation) - ✅ I/O runtime (535 lines, file I/O, streams, directories) - ✅ Threading primitives (314 lines, mutexes, RW locks, condition variables) - Repertorium-Publicum: # Repertorium Publicum Explorer ![offline: no network](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![deps: 0 runtime](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) ![tests: 14 passing](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![rubrics: 74,480](docs/assets/badge-rubrics.svg) ![payload: 1.9 MB, one file](docs/assets/badge-size.svg) ![licence: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg) **A repertory you can search like a ledger.** 74,480 rubrics and 735,460 graded remedy links from **Repertorium Publicum** (2008) — the printed three grades intact, a case builder, and grade-weighted repertorisation — in one HTML file that runs with no server, no account and no network. **[Open the repertory →](https://drsamonline.github.io/kent-repertory-explorer/play/index.html)** · [the landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/kent-repertory-explorer/) · [the data](https://github.com/drsamonline/homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json) · [the source](pipeline/) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) --- ## What it is, precisely The data is **Repertorium Publicum** by **Vladimir Polony (2008)**, published as part of the [OpenRep](https://github.com/nondeterministic/oorep) source code and licensed **GPL v3**. It is **not** Kent's *Repertory of the Homoeopathic Materia Medica*, 1897 first edition. It has its own chapter structure — separate *Clinical*, *Appetite*, *Blood* and *Heart & Circulation* chapters, which Kent does not have — and its own additions. Earlier releases of this app described it as Kent 1897; that was wrong, and it has been corrected throughout: this README, the page, the app's own footer and both manifests. ## What's inside | | | |---|---| | Rubrics | **74,480** | | Graded remedy links | **735,460** | | Remedies | **669** | | Chapters | **41** | | The whole app | **one 1.9 MB HTML file** (gzip + base64, decompressed in the browser) | | The dataset itself | **1.35 MB gzipped**, down from 1.46 MB after re-encoding | Every link carries a grade, taken from the typography of the printed repertory: | grade | meaning | links | |---|---|---| | **3** | strongest association | 71,582 | | *2* | moderate | 198,591 | | 1 | least | 465,287 | ## Features - **Search in repertory language** — `anxiety night`, `thirstless`, `weeping consolation`. Results are ranked **narrowest first**, because the rubrics with three remedies are the ones that narrow a case. - **Chapter browse** across all 41 chapters, with rubric counts. - **Filters** — narrow-only with an adjustable threshold, sort by narrowest / broadest / A–Z / chapter. - **Named cases** — keep several at once: switch, rename, delete. Each holds its own rubrics and notes. - **Case builder** — add rubrics, attach a note to each, remove or clear. **Undo/redo** with `Ctrl+Z`. - **Scoring you can see** — three weightings (3·2·1, 1·1·1, 9·4·1) and an eliminative filter that keeps only grade-2-or-better coverage. The formula is printed under the control and every export says which one produced the numbers. - **Analysis** — remedies ranked by the sum of grades and rubrics covered; minimum-grade filter; "cover all rubrics"; exclude a remedy (it stays visible, struck through, and can be brought back). - **Matrix** — remedy × rubric grid showing each grade. - **Why a remedy ranks** — click it in the analysis to see every rubric of *this* case it covers, at which grade, and which it misses. - **Remedy → rubrics** — click any remedy chip to see every rubric it appears in, by chapter and grade. - **Chapter drill-down** — browse a chapter, then its branches, then search inside one. - **"Did you mean"** — a spelling that finds nothing is matched against the repertory's own vocabulary. - **Export** — plain text, CSV, JSON, copy to clipboard, and a clean print/PDF sheet. - **Deep links** — `#q=anxiety+night`, `#tab=analysis`, `#demo=case`, `#remedy=Ars`, `#rubric=`. No router, no dependency; this is what drives the live demo on the landing page. - **Themes** — dark, light, high-contrast. **Keyboard-first** with `/`, `↑ ↓`, `Enter`, `c`, `a`, `m`, `t`, `Esc`. - **Offline-first** — one self-contained HTML file, a manifest at the right path and a service worker that precaches the app and serves the HTML network-first, so a release lands on the next visit. The header says `Offline ready` once the app is cached, and offers `New version — reload` when one lands. - **A print sheet that is the case** — rubrics, notes, analysis and matrix, without the interface. - **A build stamp in the footer**, so "am I on the new one?" is answerable from inside the app. - **Case persists** in local storage; notes included. ## Using it 1. Search in **repertory language** — not the patient's words. 2. Prefer **narrow** rubrics; a rubric with 250 remedies tells you little, one with three is gold. 3. **Add** the rubrics that survive to your case. 4. Open **Analysis** to rank remedies across them. 5. Treat the ranking as a **shortlist to study in the materia medica** — the repertory narrows, the materia medica decides. ## Screenshots | landing page | the app | |---|---| | ![Landing page](docs/assets/landing-desktop.png) | ![The app](docs/assets/app-desktop.png) | Both are taken from the real pages by `scripts/shot.sh` — headless Chromium, no mock-ups. Accent Oracle

It listens to four seconds of speech and guesses which accent it heard —
on device, with a band on how sure it is.

Open the app →  ·  Landing page  ·  User guide  ·  The twelve  ·  The rule  ·  Support

the oracle, having just heard four seconds of someone reading a sentence

--- One HTML file, no build step, no dependencies, no model download — which is also why it works with the network switched off. The page carries a `Content-Security-Policy` with `connect-src 'none'`, so a fetch or a WebSocket is refused by the browser itself rather than by a promise in the footer. The recording is decoded into eight numbers and dropped. A service worker makes the second visit work with the radio off, and the app installs to a home screen like any other app. ## What it does It measures, then compares. Pitch is found by autocorrelation, the first two formants by cepstral smoothing of the spectrum, syllable onsets by positive spectral flux, and the vowel space by the spread of formant values in Bark. Those eight numbers are scored against twelve accent profiles, and the result carries a band rather than a percentage of certainty. | | | |---|---| | accents in the set | **12** | | measurements per sample | **8** | | runtime dependencies | **0** | | network requests at runtime | **0** | | engine tests | **23** | The result screen names an accent and the region that accent is usually heard in, shows the runners-up, and hands you a card: where it is heard, what it is commonly confused with, and one thing worth knowing. There is a challenge mode where the room records a round, the oracle guesses out loud, and the room settles the score. ### The four bands The band is the most important thing on the screen, and two of the four are the app declining to answer. | Band | Meaning | |---|---| | **clear enough** | one profile fits noticeably better than the next — the best case this app offers | | **narrow-ish** | two profiles are close; the winner is a coin that landed your way | | **too close to call** | the top profiles are effectively tied, and it says so instead of picking | | **wide open** | nothing in the set fits this sample well | ### The honest caveat The eight measurements are real. The **profiles they are compared against are hand-set starting values**, not values measured from a labelled corpus — they are ordered the way the literature would lead you to expect, but they are not measurements, and the app says so on screen. [`ACCENTS.md`](ACCENTS.md) has the twelve cards and the exact procedure for replacing the priors with real centroids from Common Voice or VoxCommunis. Until that pass happens, this is a game with a real microphone and honest measurements behind it. That is what the [spec](SPEC.md) asked for. ## The rule The idea this was built from said it in one line, and it is the first requirement rather than a footnote: > Frame it as a fun game, never as a judgment about a person. So the app names an accent, never a nationality; it reports on the speech in that one sample, never on you; and it says which of those it is not doing, on the result screen, every time. A wrong guess has to be cheap and funny, which is a design constraint on the result screen rather than a disclaimer in a footer. ## Run it ```bash node test/engine.test.js # 23 passing, 0 failing python3 -m http.server 8000 # then open http://localhost:8000/docs/play/ ``` Every feature, step by step, is in **[USER-GUIDE.md](USER-GUIDE.md)** — recording, clips, reading the band, challenge mode, installing, microphone troubleshooting, and the release checklist. The app is a single file, so `docs/play/index.html` also opens directly from disk. A microphone needs a secure context, so `http://localhost` works and `file://` may not — the clip button covers that case, and it decodes the file in the page like everything else. ## Platforms Windows, Linux and Android. There is no macOS or iOS build — the app is a web page, and the same page is the product on all three. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page docs/play/index.html the app — engine, interface, cards, support panel docs/play/sw.js the offline shell; bump CACHE on every release docs/play/manifest.webmanifest installable, with the icons beside it docs/play/icon.svg the mark docs/assets/ screenshots, generated badges, the UPI QR, the portrait USER-GUIDE.md every feature, step by step, and the release checklist ACCENTS.md the closed set of twelve, the card copy, the calibration path SPEC.md where this came from and what it must not do test/engine.test.js the engine, lifted out of the page and run in Node tools/ the estate's presentation checks ``` ## Built with Vanilla JavaScript and the Web Audio API. No framework, no bundler, no package manager, no build step — `docs/play/index.html` is the source and the artefact. The engine does its own maths: a radix-2 FFT, cepstral liftering for the formants, normalised autocorrelation for the pitch, spectral flux for syllable onsets, and a Bark-scale vowel space. The tests lift that block out of the HTML and run it in Node against synthesised voices with known pitch, formants and syllable gating. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. It ships as **engine only**: a small, generic sample world (four chapters, eight locations, a handful of classes, races, enemies and gear) so you can see it run and then build your own RPG on top. > **The engine is MIT.** The *Aethelgard* games' story, characters and artwork are > a separate work, © Dr. Sohil Momin, all rights reserved — free to play, not > open source, and **not contained in this repository**. Play it here: **[drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/chronicles/](https://drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/chronicles/)** Both Aethelgard games live in **[drsamonline/aethelgard-games](https://github.com/drsamonline/aethelgard-games)**. The visual novel runs on its own engine, [Saga](https://github.com/drsamonline/saga-vn-engine). ## Run it The engine is plain ES modules with no build step and no page of its own: this repository ships the **engine**, while the page, the mods folder and the two playable games live in **[drsamonline/aethelgard-games](https://github.com/drsamonline/aethelgard-games)**. To try the engine, serve this folder and import `js/boot.js` after the data files from a page of your own (ES modules need http, not `file://`): ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 ``` No install, no dependencies. The one test suite runs in plain Node: ```bash node test8.js && node test9.js ``` ## Project layout ``` style.css the look manifest.json the PWA manifest (the page it names lives in aethelgard-games) sw.js the offline cache; its precache list is pinned to this repo by test9.js js/core.js state, saves, settings, attributes js/combat.js turn-based combat and statuses js/world.js the map, travel, dungeons and events js/quests.js the story engine (chapters, choices, quests) js/mods.js the drop-in mod loader js/views/ one file per tab (hero, atlas, forge, market, ...) js/data/ THE SAMPLE WORLD <- your game's data goes here gamedata.js elements, statuses, items, buildings, locations classes.js classes, skills and class missions races.js playable races and genders enemies.js enemies and bosses gear.js weapons, armour and crafting recipes quests.js the sample story ... companions, events, gems, music, reactions, wiki, i18n docs/ the landing page + design notes tools/ build and simulation scripts test8.js, test9.js the suites CI runs (static audit; service worker) ``` Everything under `js/data/` is a **generic sample** — replace it with your own game's world. ## Making it yours The engine ships a small generic sample. # AI Bridge [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-3f7a52?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **Your browser's AI, inside VS Code. No API key, no second subscription.**
--- You are already signed in to ChatGPT in Chrome. You already pay for it. AI Bridge attaches to that tab over the Chrome DevTools Protocol and drives it from inside VS Code — reading answers, writing edits into your workspace, and keeping a project state that survives a new chat. By default it never launches a browser — it uses the tab you opened. It never asks for an API key. If you would rather it started one for you, `browser.mode: "launch"` does that, with a profile of its own so your normal browsing is untouched.

Chat panel — streamed answers, and edits you accept hunk by hunk

## Why it exists - **No API keys.** Nothing to paste, nothing to leak, nothing to bill. - **Your subscription, your session.** It drives the page you already use, with the model you already chose. - **Edits you can refuse.** Every change arrives as a proposal with a diff; untick what you don't want, accept the rest in one undo step. - **It survives the limit.** When ChatGPT says *"you've reached your limit"*, the context moves to Claude or Gemini and the conversation continues.

Providers — health dots, the model list, and any provider you configure yourself
Router — priority, cooldowns, failover, and a preview of the chain it would try

## Install **From a build:** download the `.vsix` from [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/ai-bridge/releases), then: ```bash code --install-extension ai-bridge-0.20.4.vsix ``` **VSCodium, and any other VS Code fork:** the same `.vsix` installs. Once published, it is also on **Open VSX** — `codium --install-extension ai-bridge`. One difference is worth knowing: VSCodium ships no Copilot, so the chat model picker stays empty there. That is not a fault — use the panel at `Ctrl+Alt+A`, which is the primary interface anyway. And with no Copilot, a **local model** becomes the natural choice: `AI Bridge: Add Local Model` finds Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp or vLLM on this machine and registers it in one click — no browser, no key, nothing leaving the machine. **From source:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/ai-bridge.git cd ai-bridge npm install && npm run build && npm run package code --install-extension ai-bridge-0.20.4.vsix ```
## Five steps to first use 1. **Open your browser with the debug port on** — close it first, then: `chrome --remote-debugging-port=9222` 2. **Sign in to ChatGPT** in that window, normally. 3. **Attach:** `Ctrl+Shift+P` → *AI Bridge: Attach Browser*. 4. **Check the dot:** `Ctrl+Shift+P` → *AI Bridge: Adapter Health*. Green means the selectors matched. 5. **Ask something:** `Ctrl+Alt+A` opens the chat panel. Try *"rename oldName to normalise in src/format.ts"*. If a dot is red, the site changed its page — press **AI Bridge: Export Breakage Report** and send that file. It contains no conversation text.
## How it works ``` ┌──────────────┐ loopback WS ┌──────────────┐ CDP ┌────────────────────┐ │ VS Code │◄────────────────►│ Bridge │◄────────►│ your browser tab │ │ extension │ 127.0.0.1 only │ (Node) │ 9222 │ ChatGPT / Claude │ └──────┬───────┘ └──────┬───────┘ └────────────────────┘ │ │ edits, state, adapters, router, settings, panel RAM watchdog ``` - The **bridge** is a separate Node process on loopback. It holds the CDP connection and the adapters. - The **extension** owns everything that touches your workspace: files, diffs, state, settings. - **Adapters** are selector maps — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, or one you add in settings. - A **router** picks the provider, honours cooldowns, and fails over carrying only what changed.
## What it does about tokens Measured, not claimed (`docs/compression-bench.md`): | input | tokens | saved | |---|---|---| | polite one-liner | 34 → 21 | ⇣38% | | terse one-liner | 8 → 8 | ⇣0% | | verbose spec paragraph | 113 → 80 | ⇣29% | | pasted stack trace | 83 → 71 | ⇣14% | | code request | 68 → 59 | ⇣13% | | boot prompt | 975 → 974 | ⇣0% | | repo bundle | 588 → 370 | ⇣37% | Compression helps on verbose prose and repo context, and does nothing for terse prompts. The bigger saving is **not sending context that isn't needed**: repo context is attached only when the question names a file, a symbol or a code term, which avoids a 500–900 token bundle on chatty prompts.
## Features | | | |---|---| | **Three providers, plus your own** | ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini out of the box; any other web chat via a selector map in settings | | **Streaming panel** | Virtual-scrolled, first token measured (~471 ms in testing) | | **Reviewable edits** | Diff card with **per-hunk** accept/reject, one `WorkspaceEdit`, sha-verified, drift-refusing | | **Project state** | Gzipped, encrypted, snapshotted; a ≤4k boot prompt restores DOING/TODO in a fresh chat | | **Locked decisions** | "Never do X" is held even in auto mode, with an explicit override flow | | **Compression** | T0 always (protected spans, glossary), T1 opt-in local model, T2 opt-in provider-side | | **Session rotation** | On a usage limit: boot → new page → inject, with an editable preview first | | **Router** | Priority, per-provider cooldowns, exponential backoff + jitter, pre-warm at 80%, free-model preference | | **RAM watchdog** | 3 s poll, 80% evict + GC, 100% block; low-end mode for 8 GB machines | | **Settings** | Six tabs, every field, inline validation, a live preview on each tab | | **Keyboard first** | `Ctrl+Alt+A` chat · `Ctrl+Alt+,` settings · `Ctrl+Alt+R` rotate · `Ctrl+Alt+S` state · `Ctrl+Alt+C` compression |
## Free-tier API endpoints Besides the three web chats, the bridge can talk to any endpoint that speaks `POST {baseUrl}/chat/completions` — OpenRouter's free pool, Groq, Google AI Studio, Cerebras, GitHub Models, or a local Ollama. These need no browser and no selectors, so they cannot break when a site changes its page. - **Model discovery** from `GET {baseUrl}/models`, or a pinned list when the catalogue is hundreds of models long. - **Structural tool calls** where the endpoint supports them; the prompt protocol where it does not, scrubbed out of the answer either way. - **Real usage numbers.** These endpoints report prompt and completion tokens, so a remaining count is measured rather than guessed. - **Keys stay off disk.** They live in memory for the life of the bridge, or in `AI_BRIDGE_API_KEY_`. Configured over the control plane (`ctl.api.providers.set`); the batch records, including what was taken from where, are in [`docs/batch8/`](docs/batch8/). Two suites cover it: `npm run test:api` (32 checks) and `npm run test:tools` (34 checks). ## What is actually proven This is an experimental project and it would be dishonest to imply otherwise. **Proven** — 942 checks across 35 suites, run on every push: - The bridge, the CDP controller, the watchdog, the router and the state layer. - All three adapters and a fourth custom one, driven end to end **against fixtures**. - Per-hunk edits, the locked-decision guard, drift refusal, one-undo applies. - The boot prompt staying under 4k with every delta present across five failovers. - A deliberately broken fixture failing the contract suite — the suite detects breakage. - The breakage report containing no chat content, checked against known fragments. **Not proven** — and you should know before relying on it: - **Live selectors.** No adapter has run against the real ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini. Fixtures only. - **The free-tier line** — API transport, tool layer, the fast-path cascade, per-feature routing, the Copilot provider: 196 checks across 9 suites. - **The one-hour memory soak.** Three minutes passes flat; an hour needs real hardware. - **T1 and T2 quality.** Built, guarded, tested for safety — never run against a real model. - **Windows.** The code paths exist; only Linux has been exercised.
## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Privacy - The bridge listens on `127.0.0.1` only, with a token in `~/.ai-bridge/lock.json` (`0600`). - No telemetry, no analytics, no phone-home. Nothing leaves your machine except the prompts you send to the site you are signed in to. - State is encrypted at rest by default and redacted before it is written. - The breakage report is built from an allow-list: host only (no paths, no conversation ids), selectors tried, and tag/attribute **names**. A guard refuses to write it if any chat text appears.
## Development ```bash npm install npm run build # tsc across shared, bridge, extension npm run test:all # 626 checks, 21 suites npm run test:bench # token-savings report npm run soak # idle memory soak npm run package # bundles and builds the .vsix ``` ## Releasing Releases are automatic and version-gated — pushing code alone publishes nothing. ```bash npm run version:bump patch # or minor / major, or an explicit 1.2.3 git commit -am "release" && git push ``` Every push to `main` publishes **two** things: | release | when | what | |---|---|---| | **Latest build** (pre-release) | every push | a fresh `.vsix` from that commit, replaced each time | | **vX.Y.Z** (latest) | only when the version changes | the tagged, tested release | So there is always a downloadable `.vsix`, and version numbers stay meaningful. `docs/` deploys to GitHub Pages on any change to the landing page. Layout: `shared/` contracts and wire types · `bridge/` the CDP process, adapters, router · `extension/` the VS Code side · `test/` fixtures and suites · `docs/` evidence and the landing page.

You can also serve the folder with any static host (GitHub Pages, Netlify, `python3 -m http.server`) — that is exactly how the [hosted copy](https://drsamonline.github.io/ambient-sound-studio/play/) above is deployed. > **First click starts audio.** Browsers require a user gesture before playing sound, so press the ▶ button (or a preset) to begin. --- ## 🎛 Using it | Step | What to do | |---|---| | 1 | Tap a **preset** for an instant mood, or **Surprise me** for a random one | | 2 | Raise individual **layer faders** to build your own mix | | 3 | Use **mute** / **solo** to isolate layers, and watch the **meters** | | 4 | Press **▶** to play; the **Sleep** timer and **Pomodoro** are in the dock | | 5 | Open **⋯ (More)** for reverb, binaural beat, breathing, mixer view, sounds, extras and settings | | 6 | **Export** from the download icon | Double-tap any fader to reset it to zero. The bar under the title always shows the current mix and its layers. ### ⌨️ Keyboard shortcuts | Key | Action | |---|---| | Space / K | Play or pause | | M | Mute everything | | R | Surprise me (random mix) | | S | Silence all layers | | B | Breathing guide | | V | Toggle mixer view | | 1–9 | Apply preset 1–9 | | Ctrl/⌘+Z | Undo | | ? | Help | | Esc | Close panels | | ← → ↑ ↓ | Move a layer, when its drag handle has focus | --- ## 🎚 Exporting | Format | Speed | Notes | |---|---|---| | **WAV** 16-bit / 24-bit | Instant | Lossless. A 10-minute stereo file is ~115 MB (16-bit) or ~173 MB (24-bit). | | **Opus** (Ogg) | Fast, not instant | Small and high quality. Needs a **one-time ~230 KB encoder download** (see below), then it is cached and reused offline forever. | Exports are capped at **10 minutes**, peak-normalised, and assembled from several distinct crossfaded tiles so nothing audibly repeats. Playback pauses during the export (optional) and resumes afterwards. > **About the Opus encoder.** The app asks before downloading it, tells you why, and stores it on your device. After that one download it works offline for good. If you decline, or you are offline, the app falls back to the browser's own recorder, or to WAV. --- ## 🎵 Your own sounds **More ⋯ → Add sound files…** turns any audio file into a first-class layer: it gets a card, fader, mute, solo, meter and reverb send, and it is stored on your device and restored on every later visit. Remove one with the small × on its card. This is also the honest answer to "can it ship with recorded samples": every **built-in** layer is synthesised in the browser (no audio files, no network), while recorded audio is whatever **you** add. --- ## 📴 Offline & PWA - **Every built-in sound is generated in the browser** — there are no audio files and no network requests. Open the file with the network switched off and it works completely. - The app ships a full **web app manifest**, maskable icons and an **Install app** button, so it installs to your home screen and opens without browser chrome. - **iOS installs it as-is.** For Chrome/Edge/Android to offer a full install prompt, host the folder and make sure `sw.js` (included in this repo) sits next to `index.html` — the app registers it automatically when served over http(s). --- ## 🔒 Privacy - **No analytics, no telemetry, no accounts, no cloud.** Nothing is ever uploaded. - Everything you create — mixes, custom sounds, the cached encoder — is stored **on your own device**. - The only network request the app can ever make is the **optional, user-confirmed** Opus encoder download. - Microphone access is only requested if you explicitly turn on the microphone layer, and that audio never leaves the page. --- ## 🧩 Zero dependencies - **One HTML file.** HTML, CSS and JavaScript in a single document. - **No framework, no build step required, no CDN** for the app itself. - The minified build is **137 KB**; the readable source is 164 KB (the Hindi and Gujarati strings are multi-byte, so the byte count is higher than the character count). - Third-party code is limited to the optional Opus encoder, downloaded at your request and cached locally — see [docs/THIRD-PARTY.md](docs/THIRD-PARTY.md). --- ## 🌐 Browser support | Browser | Playback | WAV export | Opus export | |---|---|---|---| | Chrome / Edge / Brave | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Ogg) | | Firefox | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Ogg) | | Safari (macOS / iOS) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ (Ogg) — requires the encoder download | | Any browser without Web Audio | ❌ | — | — | Requires the **Web Audio API** (every current browser). The app detects its absence and shows a clear message instead of failing silently. --- ## 📁 Project layout ``` ambient-sound-studio/ ├── index.html ← the app (minified, ready to serve) │ live at drsamonline.github.io/ambient-sound-studio ├── sw.js ← optional service worker for a full PWA install ├── src/ │ └── ambient-sound-studio.src.html ← readable source (edit this one) ├── assets/ ← banner + screenshots used by this README ├── docs/ │ ├── ARCHITECTURE.md ← how the audio engine and app fit together │ ├── BUILD.md ← regenerating the minified build │ ├── FAQ.md ← common questions │ └── THIRD-PARTY.md ← third-party components and licences ├── tools/ │ └── build.js ← the minifier ├── .github/ ← issue templates, PR template, Pages workflow ├── CHANGELOG.md ├── CONTRIBUTING.md ├── CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md ├── SECURITY.md └── LICENSE ``` --- ## 🛠 Development You can edit the app with nothing but a text editor — **`src/ambient-sound-studio.src.html` is the source of truth**, and it runs directly in a browser. To rebuild the minified `index.html`: ```bash npm install # installs html-minifier-terser (dev only) npm run build # writes index.html from src/ ``` The build is optional. There is no framework, no bundler, no transpiler and no test dependency — the app is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and it is meant to stay that way. See [docs/ARCHITECTURE.md](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md) for a guided tour of the code and [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) before opening a pull request. --- ## 🗺 Roadmap - [x] 25 layers, 36 presets, reverb, binaural beats, ducking - [x] WAV + Opus export with multi-tile crossfading - [x] Fully offline, installable PWA - [x] Your own audio files as layers - [x] **Sound packs** — export your custom sounds + mix as one shareable file - [x] **Seasonal and regional presets** — Monsoon Evening, Dawn Chorus, Winter Night, Temple Bells… - [x] **Localisation** — English, Hindi and Gujarati More ideas are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). --- ## 📄 Licence **Free for personal, non-commercial use.
