app-builder: # app-builder **A shared build kit that turns a static web app into two offline deliverables: a portable Windows EXE and an Android APK.** [![Landing page](https://img.shields.io/badge/landing%20page-open-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-builder/) [![All projects](https://img.shields.io/badge/All%20projects-hub-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/) [![Offline](https://img.shields.io/badge/offline-yes-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) [![Type: shared build kit](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-shared%20build%20kit-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-builder/) [![Tech: Python + Kotlin](https://img.shields.io/badge/tech-Python%20%2B%20Kotlin-3572A5?style=flat-square)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](LICENSE) **Landing page:**  ·  **All projects:** A small, reusable kit that turns a **static web app** into two double-clickable, offline deliverables: * a **single-file portable Windows EXE** (`-portable.exe`) — a tiny Python launcher bundled with the app that serves it locally and opens the browser; and * an **Android APK** (`.apk`) — a dependency-free WebView wrapper of the same app. Both work fully offline. A consuming app repo adds **one workflow file** and gets freshly-built artifacts attached to a GitHub Release on every push. --- ## What's in here ``` exe/ launcher.py # serves the bundled app/ on 127.0.0.1 and opens a browser build.py # PyInstaller --onefile build -> dist/-portable.exe requirements.txt # pyinstaller apk/ settings.gradle.kts build.gradle.kts # AGP 8.x + Kotlin plugin (apply false) gradle.properties app/ build.gradle.kts # compileSdk 34 / minSdk 24 / targetSdk 34, signed release src/main/AndroidManifest.xml src/main/java/com/drsamonline/appbuilder/MainActivity.kt src/main/res/values/strings.xml # app label (placeholder, replaced by the workflow) src/main/assets/www/ # <-- the app's HTML is copied here by the workflow keystore/ debug.keystore # shared debug-grade signing key (see below) tools/ verify_exe.py # inspects the built EXE: valid PE, executable, size budget, imports examples/ build-apps.yml # the workflow a consuming repo drops into .github/workflows/ README.md ``` --- ## How a repo uses the kit Add `examples/build-apps.yml` as `.github/workflows/build-apps.yml` in your app repo and set the three values under `with:` to match your layout: ```yaml jobs: app: uses: drsamonline/app-builder/.github/workflows/build.yml@main with: app_name: my-app # -> my-app-portable.exe and my-app.apk app_src: docs/play # folder containing your index.html (+ any assets) deploy_path: docs # folder to publish to Pages ("" = do not deploy) ``` **Call the workflow; do not copy it.** The build, release and deploy live in the reusable workflow, so a fix there reaches every app at once. An earlier hand-copied version of this file drifted and kept `if: always()` on the release job, which *deleted* the published release before recreating it. The reusable workflow runs, on every push to `main` (and on manual `workflow_dispatch`): 1. **`exe` job** (`windows-latest`) checks out your repo **and** this kit, copies `app_src/` into `exe/app/`, runs `python exe/build.py`, and uploads `-portable.exe`. 2. **`apk` job** (`ubuntu-latest`) checks out both, installs the Android SDK packages, copies `app_src/` into `apk/app/src/main/assets/www/`, and runs `gradle assembleRelease` to produce a signed `.apk`. 3. **`version` job** consumes any `changes/` files and bumps `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md`. 4. **`release` job** publishes both artefacts on a single fixed-tag release (`app-latest`) — created **only if it is missing**, then uploaded with `--clobber`. It never deletes the release first, so a failed build leaves the previous one intact. 5. **`pages` job** deploys `deploy_path` after the release lands. A push that touches only root docs/meta (`*.md`, `LICENSE`, `.gitignore`, …) is skipped entirely by `paths-ignore`, so a docs-only commit does not run the builder. ### Stable download URLs Because the tag is always `app-latest` and is recreated each run, these URLs are permanent: ``` https://github.com///releases/latest/download/-portable.exe https://github.com///releases/latest/download/.apk ``` Link your landing page to those and the download always tracks the latest build. --- ## The EXE launcher `launcher.py`: * picks a free port on `127.0.0.1`, * serves the bundled `app/` folder with `http.server`, * opens the user's default browser at the URL, prints it, and * runs until the console window is closed / `Ctrl+C`. It resolves its bundled data via `sys._MEIPASS` when frozen by PyInstaller, and falls back to the script directory when run as a plain script. `build.py` builds the EXE with `--onefile`, names it `-portable`, and bundles the app folder as `app`. It uses the correct `--add-data` separator for the platform (`;` on Windows, `:` elsewhere). Set `APP_NAME` in the environment before running it. Every build **inspects the EXE before it ships it.** `tools/verify_exe.py` reads the PE and asserts it is a valid PE, an executable, within a size budget, and imports nothing unexpected — then prints the machine, subsystem, size and imports to the build log, so the record shows what actually shipped. `MAX_EXE_MB`, `REQUIRED_IMPORTS` and `FORBIDDEN_IMPORTS` (and `SIGNED_REQUIRED=1`) tune the assertions per app. --- ## The Android APK The `apk/` project is deliberately minimal and dependency-free (platform framework only — **no AndroidX**): * `compileSdk 34`, `minSdk 24`, `targetSdk 34`, AGP 8.x. * `MainActivity` is a full-screen `WebView` with JavaScript and DOM storage enabled, loading `file:///android_asset/www/index.html`. * The hardware back button navigates the WebView history first. * `INTERNET` permission is declared (some wrapped apps fetch remote assets). The app's HTML lives in `app/src/main/assets/www/` — the workflow copies your `docs/play/` folder there before building. The app label comes from `res/values/strings.xml`; the workflow replaces the `APP_NAME_PLACEHOLDER` token with `APP_NAME`. --- ## Signing key (read this) `keystore/debug.keystore` is a **debug-grade** key (alias `androiddebugkey`, store/key password `android`, CN=Android Debug, validity ~10000 days). * Its only purpose is so that **successive builds can be installed over each other** during sideloading/iteration. * It is **NOT** a Play-Store signing key. Do **not** publish to Google Play with it. It is public in this repository, so it provides no security. * To use your own key, add repository **secrets** and pass them through in the `apk` job's environment: | secret | meaning | | --- | --- | | `KEYSTORE_FILE` | path to the keystore file you stage in the job | | `KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` | store password | | `KEY_ALIAS` | key alias | | `KEY_PASSWORD` | key password | `app/build.gradle.kts` reads those env vars and falls back to the committed debug key when they are unset. --- ## Caveats * The APK is **debug-signed** (see above) — fine for sideloading, not for Play. * The EXE is unsigned, so Windows SmartScreen may warn on first run ("More info" → "Run anyway"). Code-signing is out of scope for this kit. * Each run costs ~2 GitHub-hosted runner-minutes (Windows + Linux). A cold Android build is the slower half (SDK + Gradle download). ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. # Clip Loom ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Clean it before you paste it — with programs you can read.** [![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-clean%20a%20link-b4482f?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=231d16)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=231d16)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-clip-loom?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16&color=b4482f)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/releases/latest) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-4f7a5c?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-b4482f?style=flat-square&labelColor=231d16)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [**Open the tool →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/)
![Clip Loom](docs/shot.png) A link with eleven tracking parameters. Text pulled out of a PDF with three spaces between every word. A paragraph going into a field that will not wrap. Clip Loom does those jobs with **programs you can read in full** — twenty lines of Weft-8 assembly each, running on a machine that lives in the page. ## The five programs | Program | What it does | The idea it uses | |---|---|---| | **Strip the query string** | cut a URL at the `?` | compare each byte with `0x3F`, stop when it matches | | **Squeeze runs of spaces** | `a b` → `a b` | remember the *previous* byte in a register and compare | | **Wrap at 40 characters** | insert a newline every 40 | count down in a register and refill it — the same code for any length | | **Strip query and fragment** | cut at `?` and at `#` | two terminators instead of one | | **One line per sentence** | newline after every `.` | one more comparison in the copy loop | Every program reads one byte at a time from the `CLIPBOARD` port, decides, and writes. No regular expressions, no library, nothing you cannot follow with a pencil. ## Built on the Loom This app does not carry its own computer. `docs/play/weft8.js` is the **Weft-8** from [Jacquard (the Loom)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — byte for byte the same engine, the same one its 102 assertions cover. What this repository adds is a host: a clipboard that hands the machine one byte at a time and collects what it writes. That is the whole design. The machine is shared; the job is a peripheral. ## Run it Open `docs/index.html`, or use the [live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/). The Windows EXE and Android APK are on the [rolling release](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-clip-loom/releases/latest). Your text never leaves the tab: the machine reads it in the page, and the clipboard buttons use the browser's own clipboard API with a plain "select and copy" fallback if the browser refuses. ## Test it ``` npm install node test-node.js # 66 assertions — the machine and every program node tests/page-smoke.js # 9 assertions — the page, driven in jsdom ``` The program suite runs **every example each program ships** on the real machine, then the edges: the empty clipboard, text with no `?`, a run of five spaces, and a 120-character paragraph that must wrap into four lines with no character lost. It also checks the programs **bite**: delete the `?` comparison from program 01 and the example that says the query must go starts failing. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | **Clip Loom** (you are here) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. app-companion-forge: # Companion Forge ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) [![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-companion-forge/) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) [![download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-companion-forge **The drsamonline Forge system in your pocket.** The build queue, the state, the kit dependency graph and the repo fleet — in one offline page. No accounts, no network, no telemetry. Built with **Forge** on the shared **web-kit** (storage, i18n EN/HI/GU, CSV, theme, a11y). ## What it does Open the console and you get the whole system at a glance: - a **summary** — items done, queue remaining, kits live, fleet size, average conformance score, blocked items; - the **build queue** — every item with its kit dependencies, status and whether it is runnable right now; - the **kit graph** — each kit with its consumer apps; - the **repo fleet** — role, conformance score and visibility. Search any view, export it to CSV, switch language (English / हिन्दी / ગુજરાતી) and theme. Everything is local; the app never calls the network. ## Run it Open `docs/play/index.html` in a browser. That's the whole app — the engine (`docs/play/forge.js`), the bundled snapshot (`docs/play/data.js`) and the shared runtime (`docs/play/web-kit.js`) sit next to it, so it works from `file://` and from GitHub Pages. ``` node test-node.js # 30 passed, 0 failed ``` ## How it is built The app is **thin**: all the common behaviour (storage, languages, CSV, theme, accessibility) comes from **web-kit**; the only app-specific code is - `docs/play/forge.js` — a small, pure, zero-dependency engine that reads the snapshot: `statusOf`, `isRunnable`, `nextRunnable`, `summarize`, the row builders, `search` and `toCSV`. It runs unchanged in the browser and under Node, so it is unit-tested headlessly; - `docs/play/data.js` — a read-only snapshot generated from `forge` and `registry` by `gen_data.py`. It is bundled, never fetched. ## Build the EXE and APK This repo calls the shared build workflow. On every push, GitHub Actions builds a portable Windows EXE and a signed Android APK from `docs/play` and attaches them to the `app-latest` release. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. app-encrypted-case-log: # Encrypted Case Log [![Live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/play/) ![Crypto](docs/assets/badge-crypto.svg) ![Offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![Tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![Dependencies](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) [![Licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE) **Per-patient clinical notes, encrypted on the device. Offline. No account, no server.** Everything lives on the device, encrypted at rest with **AES-256-GCM** (Web Crypto), in **IndexedDB**. The page carries `connect-src 'none'`, so an outbound request is impossible even by accident — there is nothing to send your notes to. | | | |---|---| | **Landing page** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/ | | **Live app** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/play/ | | **Demo vault** (sample records, memory only) | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-encrypted-case-log/play/index.html?demo=1 | | **Source** | https://github.com/drsamonline/app-encrypted-case-log | | **Changelog** | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | | **All projects** | https://drsamonline.github.io/ | ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) The landing page embeds the real app in a frame, driven by guided buttons (`#patients`, `#note`, `#search`, `#locked`) rather than four static pictures. Screens of the app itself, at both widths, live in `docs/assets/app-desktop.png` and `docs/assets/app-mobile.png`; both are produced by `scripts/shot.sh app`, the icon set by `scripts/icons.py`, and the badges by `scripts/badges.py`. `docs/play/icon.png` is committed so the release build picks up the real icon rather than a generated monogram — an offline-first app should not fetch an image service to describe itself. Built with Forge, composing five shared kits: `crypto-kit` (AES-GCM, PBKDF2, key wrap), `case-kit` (the record shape), `search-kit` (ranked search), `export-kit` (save a file) and `web-kit` (shell, storage runtime, PWA). The app is English only, deliberately: it is a clinical tool used in one language, and a half-translated record screen is worse than an English one. ## Run it `docs/play/index.html` is the whole app. No build step, no install. ``` node tests/self-tests.js # 21 tests, no browser needed python3 scripts/icons.py # the PWA icon set, rendered locally ``` Append `?demo=1` to open the sample vault — real crypto over real records, but held in memory, so nothing is written to your device. ## The vault, and what it means for you - You set a **passphrase**. A key-encryption key is derived from it with **PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256, 600,000 iterations, a random 16-byte salt**. - A random **data-encryption key (DEK)** encrypts the records. The passphrase only **wraps** the DEK — so changing the passphrase never re-encrypts a record. - A **verifier** (a known constant encrypted with the DEK) makes a wrong passphrase fail cleanly instead of silently producing garbage. - A **24-word recovery code** wraps the same DEK, so a forgotten passphrase is survivable. It is shown **once**; rotating it invalidates the old one immediately. > **Without the passphrase or the recovery code, the data is unrecoverable.** There is no > server to reset it, and that is the point — not an oversight. A header written with fewer KDF rounds than the current target is re-wrapped at the higher count on its next unlock. That is the only place the passphrase exists, so it is the only place an upgrade can happen. ## The records One record per blob, a **fresh 96-bit IV every time**, and the record id as **AAD**, so a record cannot be swapped or replayed. The self-tests prove that: a swapped record fails to decrypt, no IV is ever reused, and the ciphertext never contains the plaintext. A patient carries a **short label — initials or a code, not a full name**. The device may be shared, and the label is the field most likely to be seen. Each note carries a **severity from 1 to 4**, and the patient view draws that as a line — inline SVG, no chart library. Deleting is a **tombstone** you can undo until you lock; purging happens on lock. Every save keeps up to **five previous versions**, as the old ciphertexts themselves, so a restore is a decrypt and never a rewrite of history. ## Search, and its ceiling **You cannot search ciphertext.** On unlock the app decrypts every record into memory and builds a transient index with `search-kit`; the index is thrown away on lock. A plaintext index on disk would leak exactly what we encrypted, so there isn't one. The index is built **once per data change**, not once per keystroke, and unlock decrypts in **batches of 250** so a large vault paints early instead of blocking on one pass. Filters for **tag** and a **date range** sit beside the search box. **The honest ceiling is about 50,000 records** — the decrypt-everything-on-unlock step is linear, and past that the unlock becomes slow on a phone. It is not unlimited, and the app does not pretend it is. ## Export and import - **`.ecl`** — a single encrypted archive (the vault header and every encrypted record). It is already encrypted, so it is safe to keep anywhere. The app prints a **SHA-256 of the archive** when it writes one, so a restore can be checked. - **Plaintext CSV** — behind a clear warning, for when you must hand something over, and **CSV import** with a column preview for the reverse direction. - **Import merges by default**: a dry-run count of *new / newer / identical* records, then a merge keyed on record id and timestamp. Replacing the vault is a second, explicit question. - **Print** with a print stylesheet hands a single record over on paper — offline, no PDF library. - A double-clicked `.ecl` opens the app through `file_handlers`, still with no network. The round-trip is tested: **export → wipe → import → identical data.** ## Safety Never persists the DEK; it is held in memory only and cleared on lock. **Auto-locks after 5 minutes idle** (configurable) and on demand, and can lock the moment the tab is hidden. Requests `navigator.storage.persist()` so the database is not evicted, and shows the quota it is using. Optional, and off by default: **destroy the vault after N wrong passphrases**, for a device you expect to be taken. A **decoy vault** is also available — a second passphrase opening a separate, empty vault with its own key. Nothing marks it as a decoy, because a marker would defeat it. A **vault health** panel decrypts every record and reports anything that fails, and the self-tests can be run from the page. The service worker serves the **HTML network-first** (the cache is only the offline fallback) and asks the registration to update on every load, so a shipped release is not hidden behind a stale cache. The footer prints a **version and build stamp**, so "am I on the new one?" is answerable from the page itself. ## Keyboard and type `N` new patient · `/` search · `Ctrl`+`S` save · `L` lock · `S` settings · `Esc` close · `?` the list. Text size, and a **redaction curtain** for a shared screen, live in Settings. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page — its own design, not the app's docs/play/ the app: index.html plus the kits, sw.js, manifest docs/play/icons/ the PWA icon set, generated by scripts/icons.py docs/play/icon.png the icon the RELEASE build rasterises (EXE + APK) docs/assets/ app screenshots and the generated badges docs/shot.png the pipeline's own screenshot (do not hand-edit) scripts/badges.py draws the badges into docs/assets/badge-*.svg scripts/icons.py renders the icon set from icon.svg / icon-maskable.svg scripts/shot.sh headless Chromium screenshots, desktop and phone widths index.html, *.js a mirror of docs/play/ kept at the repo root ``` ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # app-endpoints

<!-- shot:start -->

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-endpoints/)
[![download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-endpoints?label=download&color=blue)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-endpoints/releases/latest)
[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-101%20assertions-3f7a52)](test-node.js)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-informational)](LICENSE)

**Find the right free API for a job — offline, with the CORS and auth answers a directory usually
makes you guess** — no accounts, no telemetry, no network at runtime.

Open it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-endpoints/play/> · About it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-endpoints/>

## Why it exists

Every API directory is a list you read. But three questions decide whether an API is usable before
you write a line — **does it need a key**, **can a browser call it at all** (CORS), and **is it
HTTPS** — and in most lists those are footnotes. Here they are filters. The filter is the product.

The idea surfaced three times independently (the open-data survey, the learn-to-code survey, the
productivity-tools survey) before it was built, which is the strongest signal the queue has. It is
**master list #134**; the first commit's message cites #154, which is wrong — this app was already on
the list with a spec, and the backlog's P5 line for it was a duplicate.

**What this is not.** The spec asked for a rate limit on every entry. The source does not state rate
limits, so none are recorded — the app says "listed as free in public-apis" and links out rather than
inventing one. There is no "try it" call, and no URL was checked for liveness: this is a directory,
not a monitor. `QUEUE/app-endpoints.md` in forge records each of these as not built.

## What is here

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/play/endpoints.js` | the engine — `validate`, `search`, `stats`, `savePins`, `loadPins`; pure, no DOM, no request |
| `docs/play/app.js` | the UI — wires inputs to the engine and nothing else |
| `docs/play/data.js` | the bundled directory, **generated** from `data/apis.json` by `tools/build-data.py` |
| `data/apis.json` | the record: 2,214 entries plus the source, licence and fetch date in `meta` |
| `data/SOURCE.md` | where the data came from, its licence, and every curation step with its count |
| `docs/play/search-kit.js`, `export-kit.js` | the kits, copied in, so it runs from `file://` |

## The dataset

2,214 public APIs from the **public-apis** README table — **MIT**, fetched **2026-11-10**.
1,103 need no key; 943 allow CORS; 51 categories. `data/SOURCE.md` records the source, the licence,
the fetch date and every change made to the table, with counts. No free-tier terms are recorded,
because the source does not state them — the app links out and says so rather than inventing them.

`docs/play/data.js` and `data/apis.json` are checked to agree entry for entry by the test suite, so
the bundle cannot drift from the record it claims to be.

## What it does when things go wrong

- **Bad input** — an unknown `auth`, `cors`, `https` or category is refused with the vocabulary it
  accepts, and no result set is produced, so the screen keeps its previous list. A search that
  matches nothing names the filters that emptied it.
- **No network** — nothing changes: the directory is in the page and there is no request to fail.
- **Storage full or unavailable** — a pin that cannot be written is reported as **not kept**, with
  the reason, and still works for the session.
- **Corrupt saved state** — reported as corrupt with an excerpt and a reset; never rendered as
  "you have no pins".

## Test it

```sh
node test-node.js      # 101 assertions, no dependencies, no browser
```

The suite is mutation-tested: removing the auth filter turns 6 red, reporting a corrupt save as
empty turns 3 red, reporting a full disk as saved turns 1 red, and swallowing a bad filter turns 7
red.

# Image Toolkit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**Resize, compress, convert, crop and strip the GPS out of a photo — on your device, with nothing uploaded.** **[Open the app →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-image-toolkit/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-image-toolkit/) · [The rule](#what-it-refuses-to-do) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) Every other "compress my image" page uploads the photo first. This one cannot: there is no server, no account and no network request. The file is read into memory, processed by the code in this repository, and written back out. No build step, no runtime dependency — what is in `docs/play/` is what runs. It installs as an app, it speaks English, Hindi and Gujarati, and `python3 scripts/bundle.py` folds the whole thing into one HTML file that opens from a USB stick. ![The app, after the sample photo has been through it](docs/assets/app-desktop.png) ## What it does | | | |---|---| | **Resize** | contain inside a box, aspect kept, never upscaled, never rounded to zero | | **Crop and turn** | square, 4:3, 3:4, 16:9, 9:16; 90°/180°; mirror — and the EXIF orientation is read before the strip, so a portrait photo is not written out sideways | | **Compress** | the highest quality that still fits a byte budget — a binary search, seven encoder calls at the very worst, drawn as a curve | | **Convert** | JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF and BMP in; JPEG, PNG or WebP out — or Auto, which encodes two and keeps the smaller (a source that may carry transparency is compared against WebP alone, because JPEG would flatten it) | | **Strip** | EXIF, XMP, IPTC, JPEG comments; PNG `eXIf`/`tEXt`/`iTXt`/`zTXt` — the colour profile is kept unless you say otherwise, and “every metadata block” takes the maker notes too | | **Check** | the *output* bytes are read back: "checked: nothing left" means the file that will be written really has nothing identifying in it | | **Inspect** | before anything is removed, the queue shows what the file says about itself: camera, model, date, and whether there is a GPS block | | **Batch** | paste a screenshot in, queue as many as you like, give any one of them its own settings, leave with one ZIP, one A4 PDF, or a per-file report saying exactly what was done | The pixels are never touched by the strip: everything from the JPEG scan onwards is kept byte for byte, and the PNG colour and image chunks are copied whole. A first visit has no photo to work on, so the app paints one — a 3200 × 2400 landscape, grained so it compresses like a photograph, with a real EXIF block carrying a real GPS fix (19°04′N 72°52′E). It is generated from code by `docs/play/sample.js`: there is no sample file to fetch and nothing bundled as bytes. The sample goes through exactly the path a dropped photo takes. ## The done-means, as the spec states it > A 4 MB photo is resized and compressed to under 500 KB without any network request. `node test-node.js` proves it in pieces rather than asserting it whole: the budget search is driven by a fake encoder whose output shrinks with quality (the way a real one does), so "4 MB → under 500 KB" is a real assertion about the search; and every file that ships is scanned for an external reference, a `fetch(`, an XHR and a remote `@import`, so "no network request" is a fact about the code. What the test cannot prove is how a real browser's canvas encoder sizes a real photo — that is the browser's answer, and the app reports the size it actually got. On the sample it reports **3.29 MB → 286 KB**, 1600 × 1200, GPS gone, checked. ## What it refuses to do, and does not - No upload, no endpoint, no `fetch`, no XHR — asserted across every shipped file, not promised in prose. - No account, no sign-in, no analytics, no telemetry. - No runtime dependency: `imgtool.js` is one file of plain JavaScript with no imports, and the `deps` badge is counted from the files that ship rather than typed. - No build step, no bundler, no framework. - No silent failure: a file that is not an image is refused with the type it reported; a HEIC is named as something a browser cannot draw, with the way out; unreadable metadata is reported as unreadable; a download that cannot be written says so. - A footer counter watches for any request that leaves this origin and stays at zero. ## Run it ```bash node test-node.js # the proof: 206 assertions, no dependencies python3 -m http.server -d docs 8000 # then open http://localhost:8000/play/ python3 scripts/version.py # one version, in every place it is written python3 scripts/icons.py # the icon set, from assets/icon.svg python3 scripts/badges.py # badges, with the counts computed python3 scripts/bundle.py # the whole app as one HTML file python3 scripts/uitest.py # the app in a headless browser: 30 checks python3 scripts/shot.py --help # screenshots of pages that have settled ``` There is no build step. `docs/play/` is the app. `RELEASING.md` is the six-step release. The rolling release carries four things built from the same commit: the portable EXE, the Android APK, the Linux binary, and `image-toolkit.html` — the whole app as one file, which opens from a USB stick with no server at all. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page — its own design, not the app's docs/play/index.html the app docs/play/app.js the view: queue and per-photo settings, results, preview, chart, ZIP docs/play/imgtool.js the engine — sniff, dimensions, EXIF, orientation, strip, check, fit, budget, ZIP, PDF docs/play/i18n.js English, Hindi and Gujarati, one table docs/play/sample.js the sample photo, painted on a canvas when it is needed docs/play/sw.js the offline worker — network-first HTML, cache bumped per release docs/play/manifest.webmanifest docs/play/icons/ generated from assets/icon.svg docs/play/web-kit.js vendored, unmodified — hashed in NOTICE.md and checked docs/play/export-kit.js vendored, unmodified — hashed in NOTICE.md and checked docs/assets/ screenshots and generated badges assets/icon.svg the one master mark scripts/ version, icons, badges, bundle, shot test-node.js the proof ``` Both surfaces are light by default, follow the system preference on first paint, and carry a toggle that is remembered — under separate keys, so setting one never changes the other. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — free for personal, hobby and educational use; commercial use needs a paid licence. # Jacquard ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **The loom you program — an 8-bit machine you can hold in your head.** [![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-drsamonline.github.io%2Fapp--jacquard-d98324?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-jacquard/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=1a1610)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-jacquard/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=1a1610)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-jacquard?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610&color=d98324)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/releases/latest) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-3f7a52?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](LICENSE) [![Offline](https://img.shields.io/badge/network-none-3f7a52?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](#-what-it-refuses-to-do) [![No runtime dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-d98324?style=flat-square&labelColor=1a1610)](package.json) [**Open the loom →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) · [Reference card](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/play/#card) · [What it refuses](#-what-it-refuses-to-do) · [Tests](#-the-proof)
--- Automation usually hides behind coloured boxes. Jacquard puts a **real machine** underneath it: a fictional 8-bit CPU, the **Weft-8**, programmed in assembly, with the clock, the calendar, the clipboard and the accelerometer exposed as **memory-mapped peripherals**. You read a register, you act on it — and you can watch every register, flag and byte change while it runs. The whole app is one page and two files it carries with it. No build step, no framework, no network, no account.
``` IN OFFICE_INSIDE ; read the machine's senses CMP R0, R15 JNZ done ; already at the office -> say nothing IN NEXT_EVENT_MIN CMP R1, R2 ; ten minutes or less? JG done OUT NOTIFY ; leave now done: HLT ```
## Contents | | | |---|---| | [The machine](#-the-machine) | the ISA, the flags, the memory map | | [What a program looks like](#-what-a-program-looks-like) | `leave-now`, end to end | | [The proof](#-the-proof) | 118 assertions: 102 for the engine, 16 that drive the page | | [What it refuses to do](#-what-it-refuses-to-do) | the failure behaviour, asserted not promised | | [Run it](#-run-it) | from a USB stick, a laptop, a phone | | [One honest note on the count](#-one-honest-note-on-the-count) | 27 opcodes, not 28 | ## The machine | | | |---|---| | **Registers** | 16 × 8-bit. `R0` is the accumulator — `LDI`, `LOAD` and `IN` all fill it, `MOV` moves it. | | **Flags** | `Z` zero · `C` carry/borrow · `N` negative · `V` signed overflow | | **Instructions** | fixed **two bytes**, little-endian: the opcode, then the operand | | **Operand** | an 8-bit value, address or port — or two registers packed as `a << 4 \| b` | | **Address space** | 256 bytes: ROM `0x00`–`0x7F`, RAM `0x80`–`0xBF`, peripherals `0xC0`–`0xFF` | | **Stack** | 16 deep, with overflow and underflow reported rather than crashed | Because the operand byte carries both registers, `ADD R12, R5` is literally `04 C5`. A program with a known listing assembles to exactly that listing, byte for byte — which is the first thing the tests assert. The peripherals are host callbacks, so the machine is testable with no browser at all: ``` CLOCK 0xC0 LAT 0xC1 LON 0xC2 OFFICE_INSIDE 0xC3 NEXT_EVENT_MIN 0xC4 NOTIFY 0xC5 CLIPBOARD 0xC6 ACCEL 0xC7 RNG 0xC8 AUDIO 0xC9 HALT 0xCA ``` ## What a program looks like `leave-now` ships with the app: notify ten minutes before the next calendar event, unless you are already at the office. It exercises a peripheral read, a comparison, a signed branch and an output — and all four of its paths are asserted. ``` IN OFFICE_INSIDE CMP R0, R15 ; R15 is 0 here JNZ done ; already there -> say nothing IN NEXT_EVENT_MIN MOV R1, R0 ; R1 = minutes to the event LDI 10 MOV R2, R0 ; R2 = 10 CMP R1, R2 JG done ; more than 10 minutes -> wait LDI 1 OUT NOTIFY ; leave now done: HLT ``` The page shows you the registers, the four flags, the program bytes, scratch RAM, and a **weave strip** that lights up the instruction the program counter is standing on. ## The proof ``` node test-node.js # 102 assertions, no dependencies — the engine node tests/page-smoke.js # 16 assertions — the page, driven in jsdom ``` The tests run the **real** engine — `docs/play/weft8.js`, the same file the page loads. Nothing is mocked except the peripherals, which are callbacks by design. - the encoding, byte for byte, including `ADD R12,R5` → `04 C5` - **all 27 opcodes** assembling and running in one program - **five hand-checked branch traces**, including signed `JL` at `-1` vs `1` and `JG` at `127` vs `-1`, where the subtract overflows - carry, overflow, zero and negative — from `ADD`, `SUB`, `SHL`, `SHR` **and `CMP`'s own borrow** - `CALL`/`RET` nesting, `PUSH`/`POP` order, the 16-deep overflow and the empty-stack `RET` - the peripherals, the ROM write refusal, the step limit, an opcode that does not exist - every refusal in the assembler, with the line number it refuses on - **the page itself**: that it loads the engine, that its script parses, and that every example it offers assembles on the machine it ships And `tests/page-smoke.js` boots the real page in jsdom, clicks the real buttons and reads the real DOM: run, step, reset, the weave strip, the device sliders reaching the machine, and a program that does not assemble being refused instead of run. That test exists because a page bug no engine test could see — `vm.h` where it should have been `vm.peripherals`, which made **Assemble & run** throw — shipped once and was caught only by driving the page. jsdom is a **test-only** dependency; the app has none. **Checked to bite**, not just to pass: rewrite `JL` to test `Z` and two branch traces fail; suppress `CMP`'s borrow and the carry assertion fails. ## What it refuses to do | Situation | What happens | |---|---| | The program does not assemble | it is **never run**; the error names the line and the reason — an undefined label, `R16`, an immediate of 300, a program past the 128-byte ROM | | The program loops forever | it stops at the step limit, and the page says it stopped there | | `RET` with an empty stack | an error, not a crash | | A write into ROM | refused **and reported**, rather than silently doing nothing | | Storage is full or unavailable | Save says so, and tells you to export instead; the editor keeps your program | | No network | nothing changes — there is nothing to fetch. The peripherals are simulated on the device | ## Run it Open `docs/index.html`. That is the whole app; `web-kit.js` and `weft8.js` sit next to it, so it works from `file://` and from GitHub Pages. | Where | How | |---|---| | **Browser** | [drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | | **Windows** | the portable EXE on the [rolling release](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard/releases/latest) | | **Android** | the signed APK on the same release | | **Anywhere** | copy the folder; there is nothing to install | ## One honest note on the count The spec asks for "a program using all **28** opcodes" and then names twenty-seven: `LDI MOV LOAD STORE ADD SUB AND OR XOR NOT SHL SHR CMP JMP JZ JNZ JG JL CALL RET PUSH POP IN OUT RAND NOP HLT`. The machine has **27**, and this README says so rather than inventing a twenty-eighth to satisfy a number. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | **the Loom** (you are here) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | [Weft Puzzles](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence **PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0** · © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin. # Lantern [![live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live%20demo-open%20the%20library-f0b429?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-lantern/demo/) [![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-lantern/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-lantern/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![audit](https://img.shields.io/badge/audit-in%20the%20suite-f0b429?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](tools/audit.mjs) [![licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-f0b429?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](LICENSE) [![dependencies](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-5fbf8a?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](package.json) [![network](https://img.shields.io/badge/network-none-5fbf8a?style=flat-square&labelColor=0b0e12)](#what-it-does-when-things-go-wrong) **A whole library, served over your own Wi-Fi, with no internet at any point.** One device — a laptop, a Raspberry Pi, a phone that runs Node — becomes a local content server. Everyone else on the same network opens the address it prints, in a **plain browser**, and browses, searches and reads a bundled library. Nothing leaves the host unless you export it. *Internet-in-a-Box, as an app.* A school, clinic or village gets a searchable library for the cost of one device and none of the connectivity. **[Open the live demo →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-lantern/demo/)** — the real client and the real search code, running in your browser over a pre-built copy of the starter pack. ![Lantern](docs/icon-512.png) ## Get it **[Download Lantern →](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-lantern/raw/main/dist/lantern.zip)** — one `.zip`, about 55 KB. Inside: `start-lantern` for Windows and for Linux, the server, and a starter library. There is no installer and nothing to fetch afterwards. Every tagged release also carries the same bundle as an attached asset, built by `.github/workflows/release.yml`. ## Run it Three steps, no terminal, no account. 1. **Install Node.js** — open [nodejs.org](https://nodejs.org), click the big green **LTS** button, keep clicking **Next** until it finishes. It is the only thing you install. 2. **Start Lantern** — double-click **`start-lantern.bat`** on Windows, or **`start-lantern.sh`** on Linux. A window opens and stays open; that window *is* Lantern running. Leave it open. 3. **Tell people the address** — the window prints one, like `http://192.168.1.24:8080/`. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi types it into their browser. Nothing to install on their side. Nothing is sent anywhere, and no internet is used at any point. ## Add your own books A book, a set of notes, or a whole shelf is one JSON file — a **pack**. There is no editor and no build step; the file is the format. 1. **Copy the sample.** Open [`examples/starter-pack.json`](examples/starter-pack.json) in any text editor and save a copy under a new name. It already has the shape: an `id`, a `title`, and a list of `docs`. 2. **Put your text in it.** Each document is a `path`, a `title`, and the text as simple HTML inside `content`. One entry per chapter. ```json { "id": "my-library", "title": "My Library", "docs": [ { "path": "chapter-1.html", "title": "Chapter 1", "content": "

Chapter 1

The text of the chapter goes here.

" } ] } ``` 3. **Import it.** Open the address the host printed, find the **Packs** card, choose your file and press **Import pack**. It is saved on the host, hashed, and searchable immediately. A second pack later is searchable alongside the first — the search box covers the whole library, not one pack. ## Settings There are two, and neither usually needs changing. | | | |---|---| | **the port** | `node server.js 9000`, or edit `8080` in `start-lantern.bat`. Change it when something else already owns 8080. | | **where the library lives** | the `packs/` folder next to `server.js`, one folder per pack with a manifest. Remove a pack from the Packs card or delete its folder; the index drops it on the next start. | ### If you use a terminal ```bash node server.js # or: node server.js 8080 ``` It prints the addresses to open: ``` Lantern is serving 3 document(s) on port 8080 Open on any device on this Wi-Fi: http://192.168.1.24:8080/ No internet is used at any point. ``` Then, on the host, open the Packs card and import `examples/starter-pack.json`. Anyone on the Wi-Fi can now read and search it. There is nothing to build and no dependencies: the host is one Node file with **no runtime dependencies**, and the client is one page with no build step. Node.js itself is the one thing a person has to install, which is why the two launchers exist — they are for people who do not want to see a terminal. ### Or copy one file `dist/lantern.js` is the **whole app in one file** — server, search index and client, with the page and icon carried inside it. Copy it to a machine with Node and run it; there is no folder to keep beside it. ```bash node lantern.js 8080 ``` ## The three parts | | | |---|---| | **the host** | one Node file, zero dependencies: serves the page, the library and the search index | | **the packs** | content, hashed on import and re-verified on every load | | **the reader** | a plain browser on the same Wi-Fi — no app, no account, no internet | ## What it does - **Host mode.** Import content packs into the host; it serves them on the LAN. - **Client.** Anyone on the network opens the address in a browser — no app, no account, no internet. - **Search.** A full-text index over every document in every pack, built on the host. A document containing the whole query as a **phrase** outranks one that merely contains its words. - **Pack manager.** Each pack's **true byte size**, its document count, and one button to remove it — which removes its documents from search at once. - **Usage stays local.** No analytics, no call home, no third-party request in either the host or the page. ## A pack A pack is one JSON file: ```json { "id": "my-pack", "title": "My Pack", "docs": [ { "path": "notes.html", "title": "Notes", "content": "

Notes

" } ] } ``` On import Lantern writes each document and records its **SHA-256 and byte length** in the pack's own `manifest.json`. It re-checks both every time it loads a pack. ## What it does when things go wrong | Situation | What Lantern does | |---|---| | A document path tries to leave the pack (`../`, an absolute path) | The import is refused and the path is named. A request for such a path is refused with 403. | | A file cannot be written (no space, read-only disk) | The pack is **not** added, the files that did not land are named, and nothing half-written is left behind — a reader cannot tell a missing page from a missing chapter. | | A pack's files no longer match its manifest | The pack is moved to `.quarantine/`, reported in the Packs card, and is neither served nor searchable. | | A bundle that is not JSON, or has no documents | Refused with the reason shown. | | No peers, no internet | Nothing changes: the library still opens on the host, and says how many documents it holds. | ## The proof ```bash node test-node.js # 60 assertions node tools/audit.mjs # every claim in this README, checked against the repo node tools/build.mjs # the demo library, the single file and the bundle ``` The suite runs **over real HTTP against a real host**, because the point of a LAN app is that a browser on the network can read it. It uses Node's `http` rather than `fetch`, so the test never depends on the internet's plumbing. What it covers: the host taking a port and answering; the client page being served; import, and the true byte size read back off disk; a document read over HTTP; phrase-first ranking **ahead of documents that only carry the words**; search after a pack is removed; traversal refusal at request and at import; a bundle that is not JSON; a write that fails with `ENOSPC`; a checksum mismatch being quarantined; **the builds** (a second build changes nothing, the bundle carries every file, and the single file copied alone into an empty folder still serves the page and the icon); and the audit itself. **Checked to bite**, not just to pass: with the phrase bonus removed and both traversal guards removed, 10 assertions fail. ## Layout ``` server.js the host — zero dependencies lib/search.js the index and the ranking, shared by the host and the demo page public/ the client: index.html, lan-kit.js, icon.svg docs/ the landing page, the demo, the icon docs/demo/ the live demo (search + reader, over a built copy of the pack) examples/ a starter pack to import tools/build.mjs demo library → dist/lantern.js → dist/lantern-.zip tools/audit.mjs the claims, checked dist/ the built single file and the portable bundle ``` The demo page loads **the same `lib/search.js`** the host runs. A demo that re-implements the search would drift from the app, and a demo that drifts is a lie with a nice font — so `tools/audit.mjs` fails if the demo ever stops using it. ## Built on - [lan-kit](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit) — vendored as `public/lan-kit.js` for the LAN address helpers (`Lan.hostUrl`), so the page and the host agree on what address a phone should open. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — see [LICENSE](LICENSE). © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin.

# OPD Register [![Live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/play/) ![Offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![Tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![Dependencies](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) ![Single file](docs/assets/badge-size.svg) [![Licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE) **The daily OPD register, on one page, at typing speed — offline, no account, no server.** Every day of the month is laid out and ready to type into. Counts, department splits and the daily trend update as you write. Print the register for the file, export a day-wise sheet to Excel, and keep several OPD centres apart in the same app. All of it lives in the browser on your device; the page makes no network request at all. | | | |---|---| | **Landing page** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/ | | **Live app** | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/play/ | | **Demo** (sample month, memory only) | https://drsamonline.github.io/app-opd-register/play/index.html?demo=1 | | **Single HTML file** | [`dist/opd-register.html`](dist/opd-register.html) — ~130 KB, opens from a USB stick | | **Windows EXE / Android APK** | [releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-opd-register/releases/latest) | | **Source** | https://github.com/drsamonline/app-opd-register | | **Changelog** | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) · [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) | | **All projects** | https://drsamonline.github.io/ | ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) Screens at both widths: [`docs/assets/app-desktop.png`](docs/assets/app-desktop.png), [`docs/assets/app-mobile.png`](docs/assets/app-mobile.png), [`docs/assets/app-sheet.png`](docs/assets/app-sheet.png) (the phone editor), [`docs/assets/app-history.png`](docs/assets/app-history.png) (history in the editor), [`docs/assets/app-week.png`](docs/assets/app-week.png) (the week as seven columns), [`docs/assets/app-slip.png`](docs/assets/app-slip.png) (the printed visit slip), [`docs/assets/app-followups.png`](docs/assets/app-followups.png) (follow-ups due, by department), [`docs/assets/app-search.png`](docs/assets/app-search.png) (the patient list and its sort), [`docs/assets/app-digest.png`](docs/assets/app-digest.png) (the printable digest) and [`docs/assets/app-stats.png`](docs/assets/app-stats.png). Badges are drawn locally by `scripts/badges.py`; the icon set by `scripts/icons.py`. Nothing here is fetched from a badge service, because an offline-first app should not need the internet to describe itself. ## Run it `docs/play/index.html` is the whole app. No build step, no install, no dependencies. ``` node tests/self-tests.js # 101 checks, no browser needed python3 scripts/build.py # the single-file build -> dist/opd-register.html python3 scripts/badges.py # the README badges ``` Append `?demo=1` for a generated month — real screens, real arithmetic, held in memory so nothing is written to your device. ## What is in it | View | What it does | |---|---| | **Dashboard** | Five KPIs (total, male, female, new, follow-up) with share-of-total; department bars; sex donut; a bar per day of the month; the last days with data (click to open); **follow-ups due in the next 14 days**, with the mobile number; a short "reading" panel — busiest day, new-vs-follow-up, working days with no entry, female share, gyn share. | | **Register** | The month calendar with day statuses and per-day counts; then one section per day: status dropdown, free-text note, patient count, add-row, print-day and clear-day. **Month or week scope** — the week as seven columns you can compare, with a weekly total — a **row filter** across the visible days (or **inside one day**), and a **range of days** marked in one go. Print prints whatever is on screen: the month, or the week on one A4. On a desktop a sticky, column-aligned grid; on a phone a card per patient and a full-screen editor. | | **Statistics** | Day-wise, month-wise or any date range, with 17 selectable columns (summary, departments, sex-within-department, activity). Print, Excel (.xls), CSV — and a **one-page digest** per month: totals, departments, every day in two columns, every week, a note on entries missing a diagnosis, and a signature line. | | **Patients** | Ranked substring search over every month — name, OPD no., age, department, diagnosis, treatment, address — optionally across all locations, sorted newest / oldest / name / OPD. A hit opens that patient in the editor. | | **About & help** | Storage used, patient and month counts, locations, backup and restore, keyboard reference, the counting rules, privacy and licence. | Open a patient and the editor leads with **their previous visits** — date, department, diagnosis, prescription, how long ago the last one was, and one button to copy that prescription into today's row. **Print slip** turns those visits into half a page for the file or the patient. A row can also repeat the last prescription with one click. Clicking a row number opens it; the OPD field offers the **next number in your series** (offered, never applied) and the department field offers the departments this location actually uses. Each patient row also carries a **mobile number** and a **follow-up date** — neither of them makes a row a patient, so a stray date can never inflate a total. Rows duplicate with **Ctrl+D** for the next member of the same family, `01/01/1990` typed into Age becomes 35 years, the department field offers the departments this location actually uses, a **range of days** can be marked holiday in one go (and undone), **one day** can be printed on its own, and ages read the way they are said: `8 mo`, not `0`. Smaller things that earn their place: automatic OPD autofill for returning patients, recent patient chips, undo on delete (row, patient, whole day) and on import, dark mode, a save indicator, a storage-full fallback that prunes empty days rather than losing the entry, install-as-app, and a single-file build for a USB stick. ## The counting rules, written down A report nobody can explain is worse than no report, so the rules are in the app (About & help) and here: - **A row is a patient** when any of OPD no., department, name, age, address, diagnosis or treatment is filled. A half-typed row is still saved — nothing is ever thrown away for being incomplete. - **Gynecology is female-only.** Any department containing *gyn*, *obs* or *obstet* is counted as female whatever the sex field says, and is counted once — not twice. - **Under 15 also counts as Pediatrics.** A child entered under Medicine appears in both the Medicine and Pediatrics buckets. Age accepts `5`, `5y`, `1.5`, `6 mo`, `3 days`. - **Day status is a label, not a filter.** Holiday, non-working and no-activity days are excluded from "per active day" averages, but their patients still count in the totals. ## Keyboard `/` search · `N` new patient · `Ctrl`+`D` duplicate · `T` today · `D` dark mode · `1`–`5` sections · `Alt`+`←`/`→` month · `Enter` next row (adds one on the last row) · `Ctrl`+`Enter` add row · `↑`/`↓` move within a column · `Esc` close. ## Your data One `localStorage` key (`dailyEntryRegister.v2`) holds every location and every month. No account, no analytics, no cookie, no network call. Clearing site data erases it, so **export a backup weekly** — the import restores everything, including the location names. The file format is plain JSON and is compatible with the earlier v2 release of this app. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page — its own design, not the app's docs/play/ the app: index.html, assets/, sw.js, manifest, icons/ docs/play/assets/ app.css · store.js · register.js · dashboard.js · stats.js · search.js · app.js docs/shot.png the screenshot the pipeline captures docs/assets/ screenshots and the generated badges dist/opd-register.html the single-file build (generated) scripts/build.py inlines css + js into the single file scripts/badges.py draws docs/assets/badge-*.svg scripts/icons.py renders the PWA icon set from icon.svg tests/self-tests.js 101 checks over the real source, no browser ``` The app is six classic scripts in one namespace, not ES modules — so it also runs from `file://` inside a WebView and from the EXE's bundled server without a build step. ## Builds One push to `main` builds the portable EXE and the APK, publishes the rolling `app-latest` release and deploys the demo to Pages, all from the same commit — so the live demo and the released binary can never disagree. The pipeline lives in the public [`app-builder`](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) kit; this repo only calls it. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Attribution - **Licence text** — [PolyForm Project](https://polyformproject.org/licenses/noncommercial/1.0.0), PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0. - **Icons** — drawn for this app as inline SVG paths and one `icon.svg`. No icon font, no Font Awesome, no Lucide dependency. - **Fonts** — the system UI font stack. Nothing is downloaded. - **Charts** — a donut of two `` elements and a row of `
` bars. No chart library. - **Patient data in the screenshots** — generated by the app's own `?demo=1` month; the names are invented. - **Clinical conventions** (gynecology as female-only, under-15 as pediatrics) follow how the paper OPD register in an Indian district hospital is tallied; they are documented in the app so a reader can disagree with them explicitly. ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). © 2026 Dr Sohil Momin.
app-organon-reader: # Organon Reader [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) **The Organon of Medicine in two editions — Boericke\u2019s sixth (1922) and Dudgeon\u2019s fifth (1849) — searchable, bookmarkable and readable with the network off, and switchable while you read.** No account, no server, no telemetry. Open the page and read. - **App:** - **The text — sixth edition:** *Organon of Medicine*, 6th edition (completed 1842), translated by William Boericke, 1922 — public domain. The reading text comes from the **Médi-T transcription** (homeoint.org) of that translation; it is corroborated, section by section, against **three OCR scans** of the printed book, and `tools/extract.py` refuses anything that fails either test. **All 291 sections are present.** - **The text — fifth edition:** *Organon of Medicine*, 5th edition (1833), translated by R. E. Dudgeon, 1849 — public domain. Built by `tools/build-organon5.py` from the **same fifteen Médi-T pages**, which print both editions side by side; the sixth-edition parser skips the fifth-edition blocks by design, and this one keeps them. Corroborated against **three Dudgeon scans** (Wellcome 1893, Internet Archive 1849, Google 1849): median **0.979**, minimum **0.745**, every one of its **294 sections** above the 0.60 floor. **They are different books:** 74 sections are worded differently and §292–§294 exist only in the fifth. - **Built with:** `web-kit`'s storage model, and nothing else. No CDN, no build step, no dependencies. ## What it does **Two editions, and it never confuses them.** The edition selector in the header switches the whole book — text, section list, search and bookmarks. Every section says how the two editions stand: *only in the fifth edition*, *wording differs from the sixth edition*, or *same wording in both editions*. Each edition keeps its own bookmarks and notes, because a note on §153 means a different paragraph in each. It is a reader, not an interpreter. It presents the text, finds a phrase in it instantly, and keeps your bookmarks and notes on your own device. It does not summarise, advise, or explain Hahnemann. Search is phrase search over the bundled text. Type `vital force` and every section that contains it is listed, best match first, each with its section number and the line it matched. Every section is in the left-hand list — click one, or type a number into the § box to jump. In the text you can walk the book with **Next / Previous**, or the ← and → keys, and the reader steps over a section it does not carry rather than stopping dead at the gap. Open a section and you can bookmark it or write a note; both are stored locally and both come back on the next visit. Under each section number the reader names the scan that section was read from. ## What it refuses to do - **It does not merge the editions.** The two bundles are separate files with separate provenance; nothing is blended into one "best" text, and a section is never silently swapped for its counterpart in the other edition. - **It does not renumber the book.** A section exists only where a section mark can be read, and every section records where its text came from. OCR alone reached 255 of 291 — three scans of the same printing lose *different* marks — so the remaining 36 come from the transcription, each accepted only because its wording is found verbatim in the scans (median 98% of its word-runs). Nothing was renumbered, nothing was reconstructed, nothing was taken from another edition or another translation. - **It does not invent a section to fill a gap.** Nothing in the text is paraphrased, reconstructed or generated. - **It does not fetch anything.** No `fetch`, no `XMLHttpRequest`, no beacon, no socket, no off-origin `

# Panchang [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**A daily Indian almanac that computes the day on your device** — and tells you the minute each limb changes. Tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana with their end times; sunrise, sunset, moonrise and moonset; Rahu Kaal, Gulika, Yamaganda and Abhijit; day and night choghadiya; the twenty-four hora; the lunar month in both reckonings, Vikram and Shaka Samvat; the moon's sign and phase; an eclipse flag; festivals resolved from tithi rules; a muhurat finder. No network, no account, no telemetry. **[Open the app →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-panchang/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-panchang/) · [Method](#how-the-panchang-is-computed) · [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-panchang/releases) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) The landing page is not a picture of the app — it embeds the real `docs/play/` in a frame and drives it to a day worth seeing. The app is two scripts and three data files, all in this repository: a shared runtime (`web-kit.js`), the engine (`panchang.js`, self-contained), and the bundled names, cities and festival rules. No build step, no bundler, no package install, no server. ## What it does Pick a date and a place — search a city, tap **Use my location**, or type coordinates. The app computes the day and shows, for each limb, **when it began and when it ends**: ``` Tithi Krishna Amavasya 11:27 → 12:31 Nakshatra Swati pada 1 05:51 → 07:23 Yoga Ayushman 03:25 → 03:01 Karana Chatushpada 11:27 → 23:56 Rahu Kaal (Sunday) 16:37 → 18:02 ``` Every day is addressable, so a panchang can be linked or shared: `docs/play/index.html#d=2026-11-08&lat=19.0760&lng=72.8777&zone=Asia/Kolkata&lang=gu`. | | | |---|---| | headless assertions, `node test-node.js` | **204 passing, 0 failed** | | runtime dependencies | **0** — two in-repo scripts and three data files | | sun–moon elongation vs an independent ephemeris | **better than 0.05°** | | limb boundary accuracy | **a minute or two**, stated rather than hidden | | cities bundled, with real time zones | **118** | | languages | **3** — English, हिन्दी, ગુજરાતી, values translated too | | engine | `panchang.js` 0.4.0 | ## What it must not do, and does not - **No account, no profile, no sync.** There is nothing to sign into. - **No network at runtime.** A test scans every shipped file for a script, link or fetch pointed at another origin; a second test renders the app in Chromium with every host unresolvable. - **No telemetry, analytics or error reporting.** Nothing leaves the device. - **No external font, icon or badge service.** Type is the system face; badges and every icon size are generated in this repository. - **No geocoder.** The city list is a data file. Reverse geocoding offline is not possible without a dataset this app should not carry, so "use my location" snaps to the nearest bundled city. - **No silently stale page.** Every asset is version-tagged and the service worker's cache is named after the release, so a new page cannot pair with an old engine; if it somehow does, the page says so and offers a reload instead of sitting there frozen. - **No silent precision.** Lunar longitude from a reduced series puts a tithi or nakshatra boundary within a minute or two of time, and local tradition differs on ayanamsa and on where a day begins. The day can be read at noon (default), sunrise, or midnight — the app says which. ## How the panchang is computed Entirely on-device, from first principles: - apparent **solar and lunar longitudes** from Meeus, *Astronomical Algorithms* (ch. 25 and 47) — the moon with its E-factor, the additive planetary terms (A1, A2) and its latitude from the largest ch. 47 terms; **ΔT** by the Espenak–Meeus polynomial, so the series are given TT while the API takes UT; - **tithi** and **karana** from the moon–sun elongation, **nakshatra** and **yoga** from the sidereal positions after a **Lahiri ayanamsa** (linear precession from its J2000 value); - **limb boundaries** by bisection on those angles — which is what turns "which tithi is today" into "the tithi changes at 14:52"; - **sunrise and sunset** from the standard sunrise equation with altitude and refraction, plus civil twilight; **moonrise and moonset** by sampling the moon's altitude and bisecting the crossings, using GMST and the moon's own latitude; - **Rahu Kaal, Gulika, Yamaganda, Abhijit** as segments of the real sunrise-to-sunset day, and **choghadiya** and **hora** from the weekday tables; - **the lunar month** amanta and purnimanta, named from the solar sign at the new moon that begins it, and the **samvat** years from the Gregorian date; - **eclipses** from the distance of the moon to the nearer node at the syzygy — "possible", never "visible here", which would need a horizon model this app does not claim; - **festivals** from `{masa, paksha, tithi, at}` rules in `docs/play/data/festivals.js`, not from a table of dates that goes stale. `test-node.js` checks six elongations against an independent ephemeris, the March equinox, Mumbai's sunrise and sunset, Holi and Diwali, the karana table, a 1000-day sweep, polar latitudes, daylight saving in Sydney and London, four published eclipses, ten festivals against their conventional dates, the choghadiya and hora tables, the names tables, the cities, the page's own wiring, and an offline guard. `scripts/offline-check.js` then renders the page in Chromium with every host unresolvable and looks for the day's tithi in the DOM. ## Run it ```bash open docs/play/index.html # the whole app, no install node test-node.js # 204 passed, 0 failed node scripts/offline-check.js # renders with no network (skips if no browser) node scripts/stamp.js # after a VERSION bump: record what shipped ``` ## Download it Every push builds the binaries from the same commit as the demo and attaches them to the rolling `app-latest` release; tagged releases carry the same assets with the changelog. The icon is [here](docs/play/icon-512.png) — `scripts/icons.py` renders every size from `docs/play/icon.svg`, including a Windows `.ico` and the Android adaptive layers, so no hand-made PNG can drift. | | | | |---|---|---| | | **Windows** | `panchang-portable.exe` — no installer, no registry writes | | | **Android** | `panchang.apk` — signed, sideload; no store | | | **Linux** | `panchang-linux` — `chmod +x` and run | ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page — night sky, gold, its own design docs/play/index.html the app docs/play/panchang.js the engine: astronomy, limbs, windows, months, eclipses docs/play/web-kit.js the shared runtime: storage, i18n, CSV, theme, a11y docs/play/data/names.js tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana, masa, rashi in three scripts docs/play/data/cities.js 118 places, each with an IANA zone docs/play/data/festivals.js observances as tithi rules, not dates docs/play/sw.js offline shell — HTML network-first, assets cache-first docs/assets/ screenshots and generated badges scripts/badges.py draws the badges, reading the count from the suite scripts/icons.py renders every icon size from the SVG master scripts/shot.py screenshots the landing page and the app scripts/offline-check.js renders the app with no network, in a real browser scripts/stamp.js records what shipped in BUILD.json, and refuses a stale tag BUILD.json the SHA-256 of every file a browser can fetch ENHANCEMENTS.md what is worth doing next, and what it would cost ``` ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way.
