app-poets-studio: # Poet's Studio ![live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg) ![tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg) ![licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg) ![offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg) ![deps](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg) ![dictionary](docs/assets/badge-dict.svg) **Rhyme, metre and fixed forms — a workshop that measures what you actually wrote.** Offline, no accounts, no telemetry, no generator. The whole 124,926-word pronouncing dictionary travels inside the app. [Live app](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-poets-studio/play/) · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-poets-studio/) · [What it refuses to do](#what-it-refuses-to-do) · [Sources](#the-dictionary-and-its-size) · [Enhancements](ENHANCEMENTS.md) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) Master list **#130** · built from `QUEUE/app-poets-studio.md`. ## What it does - **Rhyme finder** — perfect, near and slant rhymes, found by *sound* from a pronouncing dictionary, with a syllable filter. Spelling is not consulted, so `though` and `cough` are correctly told apart and `say` rhymes with `away`. - **Syllable and metre counter** — every line, with its stress pattern shown as a running bar. When the line is regular the metre is named; when it is not, it is not named, and the message names the **foot** that broke and which way the beat falls there. - **The scheme as you are making it** — the gutter letters each line ending A, B, C … in order of first appearance, so you see the rhyme you are actually writing rather than the one you meant to write. - **Fixed forms as constraints that check you** — Shakespearean sonnet, blank verse, terza rima, rubaiyat quatrain, haiku, tanka, limerick, ghazal, and a custom stanza with your own syllable counts and scheme. Each is a live pass/fail with the reason, per line. - **A ghazal in Devanagari or Gujarati** — measured in *mātrā*, not in English phonemes. Every line of a couplet must share the same count, which is the practical test of a shared beher; the script is named under the form. - **Two readings where a word has two** — `record`, `present`, `wind`, `read`, `blessed`, `learned` and their kind keep both pronunciations, and the metre picks the one the line asks for. - **Samples to load** — a sonnet that passes, a haiku, a tanka, a ghazal with a radif, a ghazal in Devanagari, and one haiku that is a syllable long in its first line so you can see the app say so. They live in `docs/play/samples.js`, and the tests assert the verdict each one is there to demonstrate. - **My words** — teach it a name, a dialect form or an invented word by giving its sounds in ARPAbet. It is appended to the dictionary text before parsing, so the metre and the rhyme finder treat it like any other word. It stays on the device. - **Writing journal** — drafts, versions and notes on the device, kept in IndexedDB rather than localStorage so a journal of versions is not up against a 5 MB ceiling: import a journal as well as export it, diff two versions line by line, rename, copy, and undo a delete. Two tabs on the same journal tell each other when one of them saves, so neither silently reverts the other. Export one poem, the whole journal as JSON, or every draft as a ZIP. - **Print** — `Ctrl/Cmd+P` gives the poem and its measure, without the furniture. ## The three rhyme strengths | | | | |---|---|---| | **Perfect** | the same sound from the last stressed vowel | `wall` / `fall`, `day` / `grey` | | **Near** | the same consonant frame, a different vowel | `cat` / `cot`, `love` / `move` | | **Slant** | the same stressed vowel, a different ending | `cat` / `cap` | ## The dictionary, and its size `docs/play/dict.js` carries the **CMU Pronouncing Dictionary** — **124,926 words** and **133,971 pronunciations** — inside the app, so rhyme and metre work with no network and no model. Every pronunciation is kept, not one per word: 8,383 words have more than one reading, and those are the words a poet notices. `fire` measures as one syllable or two, `read` as *reed* or *red*, depending on the line. It ships in a single-character ARPAbet encoding (each phoneme is one printable character at `33 + its index in Poetry.ALPHABET`), which is about half the bytes of the plain text and decodes in one pass. Extra readings of the same word follow the first on the same line, separated by `|`. The derivation is reproducible: `python3 scripts/build-dict.py path/to/cmudict.dict`. The tab that separates the word from its phonemes is what marks a line as encoded, so a plain `word P1 P2` dictionary can still be pasted in by hand — which is exactly how **My words** works. Around thirty elided and archaic forms the dictionary has never met — `dimm'd`, `ow'st`, `grow'st`, `wander'st`, `ne'er`, `o'er`, `'tis`, `heav'n` — carry a hand-written pronunciation in `poetry.js`, so a real sonnet is not marked inexact for its apostrophes. The dictionary is BSD-2-Clause and its licence travels with it in [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md). ## The mātrā counter A syllable in Devanagari or Gujarati is a written unit, not a vowel phoneme: a consonant carries its inherent *a* (1 mātrā), a mātrā sign replaces it with its own weight, and a halant kills it — so `कल` is 2, `काल` is 3, and `क्` is 0. Anusvara and chandrabindu nasalise the vowel they follow and add nothing. The ghazal uses that count directly. Two lines that share a beher share a mātrā count, so that is what the form checks, line by line, and reports. Urdu script is deliberately **not** counted: its short vowels are not written, so a mātrā count there would be a guess dressed up as a measurement. ## What it refuses to do - **Write the poem.** There is no generator, no prompt box, no suggestion engine. - **Guess at a word it does not know.** An unknown word is named in the line and counted as one syllable, and the line is marked inexact — a metre count that is quietly wrong is worse than one that says it is unsure. - **Call an irregular line regular.** A metre is only named when at least 60% of its feet fit; otherwise the pattern is shown and the name is left off. - **Reach the network.** No `fetch`, no `XMLHttpRequest`, no socket, anywhere in the app — and a test asserts it. ## Run it Open `docs/play/index.html`. That is the whole app — the kits, the samples and the dictionary sit next to it, so it works from `file://` and from GitHub Pages. ``` node test-node.js # 136 assertions, no dependencies node test-ui.mjs # the page in a real DOM (needs jsdom, harness only) node scripts/build-single.mjs # one self-contained dist/poets-studio.html bash scripts/icons.sh # the icon set, from docs/icon.svg python3 scripts/badges.py # the badges, drawn locally bash scripts/shot.sh app sonnet bash scripts/release-notes.sh --dry-run ``` Over http(s) the app also **installs itself**: `sw.js` caches the six files once, so afterwards it opens from an icon with the network off. The page is served network-first and the cache name is bumped on every release, so a new build is never hidden behind a stale cache; the footer prints a build stamp so "am I on the new one?" is answerable from the page itself. Keyboard: `Ctrl/Cmd+S` save, `Alt+R` rhyme finder, `Alt+1…9` pick a form. ## How it is built | | | |---|---| | `docs/index.html` | the landing page — its own design, with the app embedded live | | `docs/play/index.html` | the app — one page, no build step | | `docs/play/poetry.js` | the engine: syllables, stress, rhyme, metre, forms. Works in the browser and in Node, so the tests test the app | | `docs/play/dict.js` | the bundled dictionary | | `docs/play/samples.js` | the poems the app can load, with the verdict each one demonstrates | | `docs/play/web-kit.js` | shell, storage, theme, i18n, CSV | | `docs/play/export-kit.js` | files and ZIP off the device | | `docs/play/sw.js` | the service worker: network-first HTML, cache-first assets | | `docs/play/manifest.webmanifest` | install metadata and the icon set | | `docs/icon.svg`, `docs/icon-glyph.svg` | the mark, and the mark without its ground | | `docs/play/icon.png` | the icon the release builds take: the kit reads it from the app directory | | `scripts/` | badges, icons, the dictionary, screenshots, release notes and the single-file build — all local | | `packaging/app-poets-studio.desktop` | the Linux launcher entry, with its icon | | `docs/play/icon*.png` | the icon the builds take — launcher PNGs, and the adaptive layers Android masks | | `changes/`, `VERSION` | the changelog is written with the change, not reconstructed later | | `ENHANCEMENTS.md` | what is shipped, what is left, and why the rest is not done | Deep links open a case directly: `play/#/sonnet`, `#/tanka`, `#/haiku-off`, `#/ghazal`, `#/ghazal-hindi`, `#/rhyme/though`. The landing page drives the embedded app with the same slugs over `postMessage`, so switching sample never reloads the dictionary. The form checks are deliberately honest about the difference between a *dictionary* stress and a *verse* stress: CMUdict marks `is` and `a` as primary stressed, which no one beats in a line, so a line is allowed to depart from the ideal pattern in up to 20% of its syllables rather than being held to a perfection no real sonnet has. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # app-story-engine

<!-- shot:start -->

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-story-engine/)
[![download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-story-engine?label=download&color=blue)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-story-engine/releases/latest)
[![tests](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-141%20assertions-3f7a52)](test-node.js)
[![license](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-informational)](LICENSE)

**A book the reader moves through: choices, carried state, and a map of where you have been** — offline, no accounts, no telemetry.

Read it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-story-engine/play/> · About it: <https://drsamonline.github.io/app-story-engine/>

## Why it exists

A "choose your own adventure" app usually forgets what you chose: the branches are a tree of
screens and the reader is a click. This one makes **the state the story**. What you pick changes
what you carry; what you carry decides which doors are still open; and the trail shows every
passage you have been through, in the order you went through them — return visits included.

## What is here

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `docs/play/story-engine.js` | the engine — `compile`, `newGame`, `choicesFor`, `advance`, `trail`, `save`, `load`, `createStore` |
| `docs/play/book.js` | *The Fifth Mile* — the book that ships with it, as data |
| `docs/play/index.html` | the reader — passage, choices, closed doors, the trail, the state you carry |
| `docs/index.html` | the landing page |
| `test-node.js` | `node test-node.js` — 141 assertions over the real engine and the real book |

## The four things it promises

1. **A choice leads to a different passage.** Two choices at one passage go to two different
   passages. A choice that does not exist is refused **with the passage shown**.
2. **The same choices produce the same ending.** The engine has no clock, no dice and no `eval`.
   Replay and you get the same state, the same trail, the same ending.
3. **The trail is every passage, in order.** A return visit is recorded again, not collapsed into a set.
4. **A failure is reported, never smoothed over.** A full disk stops the *saving*, not the reading.
   A corrupt save is reported with the passage it claims and offered for export — the app never
   resumes at the beginning and calls it your place.

## Run it

Open `docs/play/index.html`. That is the whole app — the two kits it uses sit next to it, so it
works from `file://`, a USB stick, or GitHub Pages.

```bash
node test-node.js          # 141 assertions
```

# Thermals [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**What each classical source actually says about a remedy's thermal reaction — in its own words, with the source named — and where those sources do not say the same thing.** **[Open the app →](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-thermals/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-thermals/) · [The rule](#the-extraction-rule) · [Sources](#the-three-sources) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) *The pipeline above keeps this screenshot of the live demo current. A curated set — desktop, phone, landing page — lives in [`docs/assets/`](docs/assets) and is what the landing page uses.* Light and dark, toggled from the header and remembered; the system preference decides the first paint. Offline, no accounts, no server, no network at any point. One page, no build step, no runtime dependencies — the four kits it uses are vendored. ## What it does Look up a remedy and read what every bundled source says about its thermal reaction, each statement quoted verbatim against the source that wrote it. Above the quotes sits a summary **computed from those quotes**: | Summary | When | |---|---| | `sources agree (n)` | two or more bundled sources speak, and all of them point the same way | | `sources disagree` | two or more speak and they point opposite ways | | `one source only` | exactly one bundled source speaks. **This is the common case and is never agreement** | | `unclassified` | no bundled source carries a thermal statement for that remedy. It carries no quote and no summary | A **dated note** is a temporary shift — an acute fever, a pregnancy, a proving — with an end date. When the date passes the note stays visible, marked expired, and the constitutional quotes are untouched. | | | |---|---| | quoted sentences (rows) | **164** | | remedies in the index | **366** | | remedies with at least one statement | **115** | | remedies with no statement in any source (`unclassified`) | **251** | | sources | **3** | | remedies carried by two sources | **12** | | remedy names unresolved | **0** | | quotes repaired from the page image | **6** |

## What it must not do, and does not - It never assigns, derives, averages or infers a thermal state. One row is one remedy, one source, one verbatim sentence. - It never derives a classification from rubric counts or grades. - It never selects or prescribes a remedy, and it does not decide anyone's thermal state. - `ambithermal` is not a state this app looks for: no bundled source uses the word. - A remedy no source speaks about is `unclassified` — no quote, no summary. ## The extraction rule It ships with the data, because the row count is a property of it. A **thermal statement** is a sentence in a source's own words containing one of these phrases, as whole words, case-insensitively: `chilly` · `chilliness` · `always cold` · `feels cold` · `feels hot` · `cold feeling` · `cold-blooded` · `warm-blooded` · `always warm` · `cold constitution` · `hot constitution` · `warm constitution` · `cold patient` · `hot patient` 1. **Modality lines and modality sections are excluded** — a modality is what changes a state, not what the state is. 2. **Fragments under 12 characters and paragraphs over 400 are excluded.** 12 and not 20 because *"Chilly disposition."* — Jahr 1847, Cistus — is 19 characters and is exactly the statement this app exists to show. 3. **The sentence is kept verbatim.** Whitespace is normalised; nothing else is paraphrased, reordered, merged or trimmed. 4. The set is deliberately narrow: a bare *cold* or *heat* is not in it, because in this corpus those words are overwhelmingly water, air, a room, a modality or a fever. `tools/extract.py` applies the rule; `tools/make-bundle.py` turns the result into the bundle the page loads; `node test-node.js` checks the output. ## The three sources | Source | Gives | Notes | |---|---|---| | **Open Materia Medica** — © Dr. Sohil Momin, BHMS, 2026 | 109 rows across 82 remedy pages | the estate's own plain-language materia medica, quoted with the copyright holder's permission | | **Manual of Homoeopathic Medicine** — G. H. G. Jahr, trans. P. F. Curie, 1847 | materia medica text | public domain, via `homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json` | | **Homoeopathic Therapeutics of Diarrhoea** — James B. Bell, 7th ed., 1906 | materia medica text | public domain, checked against a [second scan of the same edition](https://archive.org/details/in.ernet.dli.2015.94901) | `repertory/repertorium-publicum-2008/` in the JSON repository is GPL v3 and is **not** bundled. ## Correcting the names The transcribed books are OCR. Some remedy names arrive damaged (`NTJX VOMICA`), some merged with the next remedy, and some are really chapter headings. `tools/names.py` corrects what an authority confirms and says so where none does. **Authorities**, all free and named in `data/reference-names.json`: Open Materia Medica's 344 curated names, the repertory remedy index, and the Internet Archive's numbered index of Jahr's *Manual* (1847). | outcome | entries | |---|---| | confirmed — the printed name is already a known name | **79** | | corrected from a named authority (26 of them readings the owner confirmed directly) | **47** | | settled by a second scan of the same book, from the entry's own symptoms | **10** | | readable, kept as printed (a remedy the reference does not carry) | **132** | | **not bundled** — two remedies the transcription ran together | **27** | | **not bundled** — not a remedy (chapter heading, page artefact, fragment, duplicate) | **7** | Every correction carries its evidence in `data/name-overrides.json`, and the app shows the name the transcription printed next to the correction, so a reader can check it rather than trust it. ## Repairing the texts `text_damage` marks a quote that carries a swallowed page number, a broken word or a stray mark. Where the damage can be repaired **from the page itself**, it is: `tools/text-repair.py` pulls the scan's page-level OCR, finds the page carrying the sentence, and repairs only what the page witnesses — `sen-` + `sitiveness` → `sensitiveness`, `alw'ays` → `always`, and a page number swallowed into the prose. Six quotes are repaired this way, each keeping the transcription's own words beside it and showing its page number. **No quote currently carries a damage flag**, and the ones that were never damaged no longer say they were. ## Run it ```bash node test-node.js # 567 assertions python3 -m http.server -d docs 8000 # landing page + app, or just open docs/index.html ``` Regenerating the data needs the two source repositories side by side: ```bash python3 tools/names.py --fetch # rebuild the name reference (needs archive.org) python3 tools/names.py # apply it -> data/name-map.json python3 tools/text-repair.py --fetch # page-level OCR of the Bell scan python3 tools/text-repair.py # repair damaged quotes -> data/text-repairs.json python3 tools/extract.py src/open-materia-medica src/materia-medica-json data python3 tools/make-bundle.py python3 tools/badges.py # the local SVG badges node test-node.js ``` ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page (this project's own design) docs/play/index.html the app itself docs/play/thermals.js the logic the page and the tests both use docs/play/data/bundle.js the bundle: rows, remedies, the rule, the counts docs/play/vendor/ web-kit, search-kit, case-kit, export-kit (vendored) docs/assets/ screenshots and the generated badges data/ rows, remedies, name map, reference, text repairs tools/ extract, names, text-repair, make-bundle, badges test-node.js the suite ``` ## Kits **web-kit** (storage, and whether a write landed) · **search-kit** (ranked lookup across the quoted sentences) · **case-kit** (the dated-override record) · **export-kit** (getting the bundle and the notes off the device). ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # Weft Puzzles ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Six small programming puzzles, solved on a real 8-bit machine.** [![Live demo](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-play%20it-4fd1e0?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342)](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) [![Test](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/test.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=tests&labelColor=0a2342)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![Build + deploy](https://img.shields.io/github/actions/workflow/status/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/build-apps.yml?branch=main&style=flat-square&label=build&labelColor=0a2342)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/actions/workflows/build-apps.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342&color=4fd1e0)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/releases/latest) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-5ee0a0?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342)](LICENSE) [![Built on the Loom](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20on-the%20Loom%20(app--jacquard)-ffb454?style=flat-square&labelColor=0a2342)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) [**Play it →**](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/) · [The machine it runs on](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard)
![Weft Puzzles](docs/shot.png) A robot on a grid, five puzzles, and a machine with sixteen registers, four flags and twenty-seven instructions — **and no `if` statement**. So you build one, out of `CMP` and `JZ`. That is the whole point of the puzzles: the constraint is the lesson. ## The six puzzles | # | Puzzle | What it teaches | |---|---|---| | 01 | **First thread** | `LDI` puts a number in the accumulator, `OUT MOVE` hands it to the machine | | 02 | **Step around** | four moves, three directions — a straight line is not always the answer | | 03 | **Until you stand on it** | `LOAD` reads a port; `CMP` + `JZ` are how a machine decides | | 04 | **Feel for the wall** | `BUMPED` is the machine's own feedback — a loop that reacts | | 05 | **The whole weave** | a level can ask for more than arrival: collect both flags first | | 06 | **The long way round** | three bump loops in a row — a program is a shape you repeat | Each puzzle ships a **working solution**, and the test suite runs every one of them on the real machine. A puzzle nobody has solved is a puzzle nobody knows is solvable — so that is asserted, not assumed. ## Built on the Loom This app does not carry its own computer. It runs the **Weft-8** from [Jacquard (the Loom)](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-jacquard) — `docs/play/weft8.js` is that engine, byte for byte the same file, and the same one its 102 assertions cover. What this repository adds is a *world*: `docs/play/world.js` puts the machine inside a grid and hangs seven ports off it, at `0xD0` and up so they never collide with the Loom's own `0xC0`–`0xCA`: ``` POS_X 0xD0 POS_Y 0xD1 UNDER 0xD2 MOVE 0xD3 BUMPED 0xD4 DONE 0xD5 BEEP 0xD6 ``` So the machine is unchanged, and the puzzle is a peripheral — which is exactly how a real 8-bit computer met the world. ## Run it Open `docs/index.html`, or play the [live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-weft-puzzles/). Windows EXE and Android APK are on the [rolling release](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-weft-puzzles/releases/latest). ## Test it ``` npm install # jsdom, test-only node test-node.js # 69 assertions: the machine, the world, and every level's solution node tests/page-smoke.js # 12 assertions: the page, driven in jsdom ``` The engine suite asserts that the machine is still the Loom's (two-byte encoding, 27 opcodes), that the world obeys its own rules (walls refuse a move and set the bump flag, flags are taken once, the checker knows a level with a flag left is not solved), that **every level's reference solution solves it in under 400 steps and fits the 128-byte ROM**, and that wrong answers are refused — walking into the wall, stopping one square short, and guessing a corridor's length blind. The page suite boots the real page, picks puzzles, runs programs, peeks at the solution and checks the page says *Solved* — because a page that does not work is not a puzzle. ## The Weft-8 family One machine, seven faces. Every one of these runs `weft8.js` from the Loom, byte for byte — learn it once and you have learned all seven. | | what it is | |---|---| | [the Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-jacquard/) | the machine and its editor — where it all starts | | **Weft Puzzles** (you are here) | five puzzles solved in assembly, a robot on a grid | | [Clip Loom](https://drsamonline.github.io/app-clip-loom/) | clipboard programs you can read: strip, squeeze, wrap | | [Weft-8 on hardware](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-hardware/) | the same machine in C, three-way parity with the JS one | | [weft8-kit](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-kit/) | rules small enough to sign off | | [Weft-8 Classroom](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-classroom/) | eight exercises that teach how a computer works | | [Weft-8 beside x86 and ARM](https://drsamonline.github.io/weft8-compare/) | the same four jobs in three machines | ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # art-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) **The art primitives Forge was missing.** Zero dependencies, one file, no assets. palette · pixel canvas · draw ops · undo · dithering · median-cut · sprite sheets · isometric · sketch loop
--- ## The two halves - **STATIC pixel art** — an indexed palette, a pixel canvas that scales with **nearest-neighbour** (smoothing off by default — the classic trap), draw ops, a delta undo stack, dithering, median-cut quantisation, sprite sheets, and the isometric mapping. - **LIVE generative visuals** — a frame loop (`Art.sketch`) you can run on its own or drive from `game-kit`'s fixed timestep, so a sketch is reproducible from a fixed step. Both, from one kit. ## What's in it | | | |---|---| | `palette` | an indexed palette from a Lospec-style list, with `swap`, `cycle` and `nearest` | | `canvas` | an indexed pixel buffer: `set`, `line`, `rect`, `ellipse`, `fill`, `mirror` | | `scale` | nearest-neighbour upscaling (never smooths) | | `history` | a bounded undo/redo stack that stores **deltas, not whole frames** | | `dither` | ordered (Bayer) and Floyd–Steinberg | | `quantize` | median-cut to N colours, so a photo becomes pixel art | | `spriteSheet` / `sliceSprite` | a sheet + JSON atlas, with a slicing round-trip | | `tilemap` | a grid of tile ids (`-1` = no tile, so tile `0` stays legal): `get`/`set`, pixel→tile by **floor**, `fillRect`, a capped iterative `floodFill`, 4-bit `autotile` masks, and `toCanvas(tiles)` | | `anim` | a timeline over frames: `at(t)` is a **pure function of time**, `pingpong` without repeated endpoints, `fps 0` frozen instead of `NaN` | | `generate` | a **seeded** sprite generator (`Art.rng`, mulberry32) that is mirror-symmetric by construction, never empty, and rebuilds an asset folder from one number (`generateSet`) | | `iso` | the cartesian ↔ isometric coordinate mapping | | `sketch` | a setup-once / draw-every-frame loop | ## Usage ```js var Art = require("./art-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.Art var pal = Art.palette("1a1c2c 5d275d b13e53 ef7d57"); // a Lospec-style list var c = Art.canvas(32, 32, pal); c.rect(4, 4, 24, 24, 2, true).ellipse(16, 16, 10, 10, 3, true); var big = Art.scale(c, 8); // nearest-neighbour, crisp var hist = Art.history(c, { limit: 100 }); // undo/redo over deltas hist.begin(); c.set(0, 0, 1); hist.commit(); hist.undo(); var pal2 = Art.palette(Art.quantize(pixels, 16)); // median-cut a photo var sheet = Art.spriteSheet([frame0, frame1]); // sheet + atlas // 1.1.0 — a level, its timeline, and a seeded creature to put in it var map = Art.tilemap({ w: 20, h: 12, tileW: 16, tileH: 16 }); map.floodFill(0, 0, 1); // lay a floor var walls = map.autotile(); // N=1 E=2 S=4 W=8 per tile var level = map.toCanvas(tileCanvases); // compose it into one canvas var hero = Art.generate({ seed: 2026, w: 16, h: 16, density: 0.8 }); var walk = Art.anim([hero, Art.generate({ seed: 77, w: 16, h: 16 })], { fps: 8, pingpong: true }); walk.at(0.3); // the frame for that moment, always ``` ## Licence position (read this) Everything here is **reimplemented from published technique**; permissive reference projects are named only in comments, and **no code is copied**. In the survey behind this kit: Aseprite is not open source (learn, never copy); Data-Pixels and pixel8 carry **no licence**; six tools are copyleft — none of their code is used. The permissive references (piskel, Pixelorama, PixelCraft, poxi, and the isometric mapping from isometric-contributions) are cited as ideas. ## Tests ``` node test-node.js 86 passed, 0 failed ``` Covers the spec's required cases — a **nearest-neighbour scaling** case, a **dithering pattern** case, a **median-cut** case with a known input, a **sprite-sheet export round-trip**, a **tilemap** case (floor, flood-fill bounds, autotile masks), a **timeline** case (pure `at(t)`, pingpong without repeated endpoints) and a **procedural sprite** case (same seed, same sprite; mirror symmetry; never empty) — plus the palette, every draw op, the bounded delta undo stack, the isometric mapping and the sketch loop. All headless. The 1.1.0 additions were **mutation-tested ten ways** and all ten are caught by an assertion (floor→truncate in `at`, a flood fill that re-fills, swapped E/W autotile bits, `toCanvas` ignoring the tile id, pingpong repeating its endpoints, rounded instead of floored time, mirroring only on even widths, dropping the non-empty guarantee, ignoring the body shape, and `Art.version` drifting from `VERSION`). ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. The primitives a **panchang** (Indian almanac) needs — and nothing app-specific: - **Julian day**; **solar** and **lunar longitude** (Meeus); - **ayanamsa** (Lahiri, approximate); **sunrise / sunset / solar transit**; - **moon phase** and illumination; - the derived **tithi, nakshatra, yoga, karana** — from the sun–moon longitude. ```js const p = Astro.panchang({ y: 2026, m: 10, d: 23, h: 6 }, { lat: 28.6139, lon: 77.2090 }); p.tithi.name; // "Shukla Dwadashi" p.nakshatra.name; // "Purva Bhadrapada" p.sun.sunriseUTC; // -> add your timezone offset ``` ## Verified against published values ``` node test-node.js 13 passed, 0 failed ``` - Sun apparent longitude vs **Meeus 25.b**: `199.90894` (published `199.90895`). - Moon longitude vs **Meeus 47.a**: `133.16000` (published `133.162655`). - Delhi sunrise/sunset, midsummer: `05:24` / `19:22` IST. - Tithi/nakshatra/yoga/karana ranges and the tithi–elongation relation. ## Accuracy — read this Solar and lunar longitude are good to about **0.01–0.05°**, which puts a tithi/nakshatra boundary within roughly **a minute of time**. So panchang timings are **approximate** — do not present them as exact, and local tradition may differ. # audio-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) **Synthesis, theory, patterns and notation.** Zero dependencies, one file, no audio assets. synthesis · ADSR · filters · noise · mixer · music theory · patterns · notation · sonification · mastering
--- ## The rule this kit exists to state **Game music is PATTERNS, NOT FILES.** A Forge game ships as one file with no assets. A pattern is a few kilobytes of data and plays through WebAudio; an audio file is megabytes. `game-kit` should adopt this rule: generate the music, do not ship it. ## What's in it | | | |---|---| | `music` | notes, intervals, transposition, 12 scales, 11 chords — the arithmetic every musical feature needs | | `synth` | a pure **ADSR** envelope, an oscillator voice with an optional filter, a noise source, and a small mixer | | `seq` | a **pattern sequencer**: rows × channels of notes, flattened to timed events and scheduled through WebAudio | | `notation` | a staff **layout** — each note's position, so a renderer just draws it | | `sonify` | map the bytes of any file to sound | | `master` | **honest** mastering helpers: a loudness measure, a match gain, and a peak limiter | | `time` | **deterministic time**: a seeded PRNG with stable forks, a tempo **map** (rubato, ritardando), and human timing jitter | | `sched` | a lookahead **scheduler with a watchdog** — a throttled tab must not end a song halfway | | `texture` | seven synthesised **ambient beds** (rain, wind, fire, vinyl, ocean, stream, hum) | | — | `synth.harmonics()` keeps partials under Nyquist; `synth.softClip()` is a master safety curve | Everything is generated in code or stored as pattern data. **No audio assets are shipped.** ## What changed in 1.1.0 Four things learnt building a full generative composer on this kit: 1. **Determinism is a feature, not a detail.** `A.time.seeded(seed)` gives the same stream everywhere, and `fork("drums")` is stable per label — so one track can be locked while the rest is re-rolled. 2. **Tempo moves.** `A.time.map([{beat:0,bpm:80},{beat:16,bpm:90}])` with `secondsAt`/`beatAt`/`bpmAt`. Every beat→second conversion in a real piece has to go through it, or note *lengths* drift the moment the tempo changes. 3. **Static is usually aliasing, and clicks are usually corners.** `synth.harmonics()` clamps partials under Nyquist; `synth.softClip()` is a `tanh` curve for the master, because a hard clamp is a corner and a corner is a click. 4. **A scheduler needs a watchdog.** `setInterval` stops in a throttled tab; `A.sched()` notices and keeps ticking. ## Usage ```js var A = require("./audio-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.AudioKit // Theory — no audio needed A.music.scale("C4", "major"); // -> [60, 62, 64, 65, 67, 69, 71] A.music.chord("A4", "minor"); // -> [69, 72, 76] A.music.parse("A4").freq; // -> 440 // Synthesis — on a user gesture (the browser rule) var ctx = new AudioContext(); var v = A.synth.voice(ctx, { type: "square", freq: 440, filter: "lowpass", cutoff: 900 }); v.play(ctx.currentTime, 0.5, { a: 0.01, d: 0.1, s: 0.7, r: 0.3 }); // A pattern: a few KB of data, not a file var pat = A.seq.pattern([ ["C4", null, null, "E4"], ["G4", null, "B4", null] ], { bpm: 120, rowsPerBeat: 4 }); A.seq.play(ctx, pat, { type: "square" }); // Notation layout A.notation.layout(["C4", "D4", "E4"]); // -> { notes: [{x, step, ...}], width } ``` ## Notes - **No autoplay.** Every node is built from a context you create on a user gesture. - **Everything is reimplemented.** References (the tracker tradition, Orca, MuseScore, matchering, binary-synth, Neothesia) are named in comments; **no code is copied**, and the copyleft ones are technique only. - **The mastering helpers are a matching aid, not a replacement for an engineer** — say so in any app that uses them. ## Tests ``` node test-node.js 42 passed, 0 failed ``` Covers the spec's required cases — an **ADSR envelope shape**, a **scale/chord construction**, a **sequencer scheduling** case (notes land on the right beats), and a **notation layout** — plus note parsing, transposition, sonification and the mastering helpers. All headless: the theory, the envelope maths and the scheduling are pure, so they test with no audio context. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # audit

[![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-3f7a52

The change log for the drsamonline fleet — **78 repositories, 105 workflow files, 10 scheduled jobs**.

Every audit, fix and correction lands here, with the evidence. Nothing in this repo is a plan for
later; if it says a thing was done, the `log/` entry that claims it carries the before-and-after.

## Why this exists

The fleet grew faster than its bookkeeping. Licence badges drifted from their LICENSE files, new
repos fell into an "Other / New" bucket, landing pages stopped offering downloads, and the audit
files that documented all of it were scattered across five unrelated repos. This repo is the single
place where the state of the fleet is measured, the change is recorded, and the next run can prove
what moved.

## Layout

    log/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD-<slug>.md   one file per session
    reports/<YYYY-MM>-<slug>/          a measurement or a plan, with its evidence beside it
    state/                             machine-readable snapshots, refreshed by tools/collect.py
    tools/collect.py                   read every repo into state/
    tools/diff.py                      compare two snapshots, print only what changed
    tools/licence_check.py             licence badge vs LICENSE file, all repos
    tools/fix_licence_badges.py        make a badge say what its LICENSE grants
    tools/presentation_audit.py        landing page, app, badges, shots, support block, per repo
    tools/verify.py                    the repo-presentation skill's gate, copied verbatim

Four report sets live here so far: `reports/2026-11-fleet-audit/` (the whole estate read end to
end), `reports/2026-11-forge-release/` (the plan to ship the control plane as one release),
`reports/2026-11-presentation-audit/` (all 100 repos against the presentation skill, with the delta
each one still needs) and `reports/2026-11-manifest-design/` (seven rounds of design and review for
per-file provenance and drift-aware healing). A report is a measurement or a plan; the log entry is
the decision. Neither
is a substitute for the other.

## The rule

**A change is not done when it is pushed. It is done when it is read back from the API and the
batch's verification passes.** The log entry records the verification, not the intention.

Every log entry uses the same six headings, in this order:

    ## What I looked at
    ## What was wrong
    ## What I changed
    ## Evidence
    ## What I deliberately did not do
    ## Next

The fifth one matters most. A log that only records what changed hides the decisions that were
made by *not* changing something, and those are the ones that get re-litigated later.

## Read state through the API, never through raw

`raw.githubusercontent.com` serves a cached copy that lags minutes to hours behind a commit. In this
fleet it has twice made finished work look broken:

- a `build.yml` that already contained the icon wiring was served without it
- 14 landing pages that had just been repaired were served in their old, broken form

Both times the API (`GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}`) showed the truth immediately.
**Use the API to decide whether something worked.** Use raw only for bulk reading of files that
have not changed in the last hour. Where a URL matters, fetch actual bytes and check the status.

## Running it

    gh auth login                      # or GH_TOKEN in the environment
    python3 tools/collect.py           # ~5 minutes for 78 repos
    python3 tools/licence_check.py     # exits 1 if any badge is wrong

`licence_check.py` runs weekly on a Monday at 03:31 UTC and commits the fresh snapshot. That cron is
deliberately clear of every other job in the fleet — the current set is:

    Mon 03:17  update-profile        Mon 03:23  skills/refresh
    Mon 03:31  licence-check (this)  Tue 03:47  dashboard/refresh
    Tue 04:00  metrics               Tue 04:12  Matneo/blog
    Tue 04:22  Matneo/store          Tue 06:00  control-panel/scan
    Wed 05:00  app-builder/kit-tests 1st+16th 03:00 store-images, 03:37 refresh-hub

## Conventions

- **One commit per repo.** Repos are independent; there is no shared release train, and a
  cross-repo change cannot be reverted per repo.
- **A script fixes a class of defect; a human decides a class of question.** Encoding a space is
  a script. "Is this repo MIT or PolyForm?" is not.
- **Never let a sweep invent a licence.** If a badge and its LICENSE disagree, the sweep stops
  and the repo goes to the decision batch.
- **Test against the real response shape and the broken state.** Two repairs in this log failed
  because they were tested against cached data and against a clean page instead of the damaged one.

# backup [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) **Snapshot a repository before it changes — so a merge can never lose the code that was there.** A reusable GitHub workflow + a zero-dependency script. Compressed, timestamped, rotated, and never full.
--- ## What it does Before a merge replaces a repository's code, `backup` takes the **state that is about to be replaced** and stores it, compressed, in a **dumps** repository: ``` dumps/ drsamonline__ml-kit/ 2026-10-24T103000Z/ ml-kit.tar.gz 2026-10-24T110000Z/ ml-kit.tar.gz drsamonline__case-kit/ 2026-10-24T103000Z/ case-kit.tar.gz ``` One folder per repository (`owner__repo`), one folder per backup named with the **date and time**, and inside it the repository as a `.tar.gz`. ## The two rules that keep it safe 1. **It never fills up.** Each repository keeps the newest **100** backups (configurable). Past that, the **oldest is deleted** to make room for the new one — so the most recent work is always present and the store stays bounded. 2. **It never stops.** When a dumps repository passes its **size cap** (800 MB by default), the next one is **created automatically** — `dumps`, `dumps-2`, `dumps-3`, … — and the backup continues there. A full repo can never block a backup. ## How to wire it in — before every merge Add this to any repository's workflow. It runs on a pull request, so it snapshots the **base commit** — the code as it is *before* the merge: ```yaml name: backup on: pull_request: jobs: backup: uses: drsamonline/backup/.github/workflows/backup.yml@main with: keep: 100 # optional max_mb: 800 # optional secrets: BACKUP_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.BACKUP_TOKEN }} ``` One secret, **`BACKUP_TOKEN`**, is required: a token with `contents: write` on the dumps repositories and `contents: read` on the source repository. (`GITHUB_TOKEN` is scoped to a single repository, so it cannot write to the dumps repo.) Run it by hand too: ```bash GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --repo drsamonline/ml-kit --ref main GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --repo drsamonline/forge --ref main --dumps dumps --keep 100 ``` ## Read this before you make the dumps repo public **A dumps repository holds your source code.** If *any* repository you back up is private, its dumps must be private too — a public dumps repo would publish that code. `backup.py` therefore creates new dumps repos **private by default**; pass `--public` only when every source repository is already public. ## The options | flag | default | what it does | |---|---|---| | `--repo` | — | the source repo, `owner/name` | | `--ref` | the default branch | the ref to snapshot — pass the **PR base** to capture the pre-merge state | | `--dumps` | `dumps` | the dumps repo name | | `--owner` | the source owner | who owns the dumps repo | | `--keep` | `100` | backups kept per repository; the oldest beyond it are deleted | | `--max-bytes` | `800 MB` | the dumps repo size cap before rolling to a new repo | | `--public` | off | create new dumps repos public (read the warning above) | | `--restore-test` | — | do not back up: unpack one dump and compare it with the commit it holds | | `--at` | the newest | with `--restore-test`, which snapshot to restore | | `--manifest` | — | do not back up: regenerate the dumps repo's `manifest.json` from its tree | ## The manifest is derived, not written by hand `/manifest.json` is regenerated from the dumps repository's own tree — after every backup, and on demand: ```bash GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --manifest --dumps dumps ``` It was hand-written once, on the store's first day, and never again: it went on claiming one repository was backed up while the store held 78. A derived index cannot drift, and if it is wrong then the tree it was derived from is wrong too. It is verified on the way in exactly as a dump is — the stored blob sha is compared with the sha of the bytes written — and a manifest that cannot be written **fails the run**, because a derived index allowed to go stale quietly is the defect this replaces. The one thing it does not record is the commit each dump holds. That is inside the tarball; `--restore-test` reads it. ## Proving a backup can actually be restored A backup that ran is not a backup that restores. This unpacks one dump and compares it, file for file, with the commit the dump names — every file's git blob sha against the repository's own tree at that commit. It exits 0 only on an exact match: ```bash GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --restore-test --repo drsamonline/forge GITHUB_TOKEN=... python3 backup.py --restore-test --repo drsamonline/forge --at 2026-10-27T124846Z ``` ``` read 0.69 MB; the API's stored blob sha is 81bbcaf0af unpacks clean (gzip CRC verified): 349 files, taken at 57d64d93c932 PASS EXACT RESTORE - 349 files match drsamonline/forge@57d64d93c932 file for file ``` It also fails on a truncated dump, on a dump whose top directory names a different repository, and on a tree GitHub truncated — an incomplete comparison is never a pass. Run it from the workflow by dispatching `backup` with `restore_test: true`. ## Verified ``` python3 tests/test_backup.py 50 passed, 0 failed ``` The tests cover the decisions that must be right — rotation keeps the newest N and deletes the oldest, the timestamp sorts chronologically, and a **full dumps repo rolls over to a new one**. Disabling rotation makes **4** of them fail. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # Base Bench [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**Every number base, unit and timezone on one page — with the working shown.** **[Open the bench →](https://drsamonline.github.io/base-bench/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/base-bench/) · [What it refuses to do](#what-it-refuses-to-do) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) A converter you cannot check is a converter you have to trust. Base Bench shows the arithmetic at every step, so the answer is verifiable on paper. Offline, no accounts, no server, no build step, no runtime dependencies — the app is a folder of files you can open from a USB stick. Master list **#142** · built from `QUEUE/app-base-bench.md`. ## What it does | | | |---|---| | **Bases, linked** | Decimal, hex, binary and octal are four views of one number. Type in any field and the other three follow, with no reload. Plus any base from 2 to 36, with the legal digit strip printed beside it. | | **The working, in the base you typed into** | 255 → hex is shown as `255 / 16 = 15 remainder 15 (F)`, `15 / 16 = 0 remainder 15 (F)`, then *read the remainders bottom-up: FF*. That is the sum you would do by hand. | | **Units, with the factor** | Length, mass, data and time carry their factor in the working line. Temperature is affine, so it gets its own formula rather than a factor. `KB` and `KiB` are kept apart, because they are different units. | | **Timezones, with the rollover** | Fixed offsets, stated as fixed. The day change is said out loud rather than swallowed: 01:00 IST is 19:30 UTC **the previous day**. | | **A log, on the device** | The conversions you keep live in this browser's storage and leave only when you export them as CSV. | | **Any length of integer** | The whole part is carried as a BigInt, so a 30-digit number is read and written exactly. A double would start rounding at 2^53 and print a plausible answer that is not the one you typed. | | **Three languages** | English, Hindi and Gujarati — every label, every note and every refusal. The choice is remembered on the device, and the arithmetic does not change with it. | | **Installs as an app** | A service worker keeps the shell on the device and serves the HTML *network-first*, so a new release can never hide behind a cache. Add to home screen from the browser menu — no store, no account. | ## What it refuses to do - **Not a scientific calculator.** It converts, and it shows how. Anything else is a different tool. - **No invented answers.** An illegal digit, an unknown unit, a length converted to a mass, or `0x` on base 10 each produce a sentence saying what is wrong — not a plausible-looking number. Where a double would round, the bench does not round: it carries a BigInt instead. - **No network at any point.** No fetch, no CDN, no font service, no analytics. The page carries everything it needs, and the test suite asserts it. - **No account, no sync, no telemetry.** Nothing leaves the device unless you export it. ## Take it with you | | Asset | What it is | |---|---|---| | | [`base-bench.apk`](https://github.com/drsamonline/base-bench/releases/download/app-latest/base-bench.apk) | Android WebView build, signed | | | [`base-bench-portable.exe`](https://github.com/drsamonline/base-bench/releases/download/app-latest/base-bench-portable.exe) | one portable Windows binary, no installer | | | [`base-bench-linux`](https://github.com/drsamonline/base-bench/releases/download/app-latest/base-bench-linux) | Linux binary | Every asset on the [releases page](https://github.com/drsamonline/base-bench/releases) is built from the same commit as the live page, so the demo and the download can never disagree. ## Run it ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/base-bench open docs/play/index.html # the whole app node test-node.js # 116 assertions, no installs ``` ## The proof `node test-node.js` — **116 assertions**, no dependencies. Sixteen of them are the dictionary itself: every key in every language, every refusal code the engine can emit written out in all three, and every phrase the page tags for translation actually present. The engine is `docs/play/basebench.js` and the page is a view over it, so testing the engine tests what the app does. Included are the spec's own done-means (255 shows as `FF` and `11111111` in the same view, and typing into any field updates the others), 4,004 round trips across bases 2, 8, 16 and 36, the temperature fixed-points, and the timezone day rollover. Each assertion was checked to **bite**: five mutations of the engine (lowercase digits, the day rollover removed, the `- 32` dropped from the Fahrenheit formula, the prefix check disabled, the digits reversed) each fail between 1 and 9 assertions. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page - its own design, not the app's docs/play/index.html the app docs/play/basebench.js the engine: bases, units, timezones docs/play/sw.js the offline shell: network-first HTML, cache-first assets docs/play/manifest.webmanifest what makes it installable, and its icons docs/play/icon-*.png the launcher icons, drawn locally docs/play/web-kit.js storage, theme, i18n, a11y docs/play/export-kit.js the CSV export docs/assets/badge-*.svg badges, drawn locally by tools/badges.py docs/assets/app-*.png screenshots of the real page docs/shot.png the pipeline's own screenshot (rewritten on every build) release-notes.md the release page's own notes: an icon per asset test-node.js the proof tools/badges.py regenerates the badges - no image service involved ``` The page carries a `Content-Security-Policy` of `default-src 'none'` with `connect-src 'none'`, so "no network" is enforced by the browser rather than only asserted by the suite. Bump `CACHE` in `docs/play/sw.js` and the build stamp in the footers on every release — the worker serves HTML network-first precisely so that a stale cache cannot hide a release, but the two stamps are what make "am I on the new one?" answerable from the page. The badges are drawn by `python3 tools/badges.py`, not fetched from a badge service: an offline-first app that needs the network to say "no network" has broken its own rule. If the suite stops printing 116, change the number in `tools/badges.py` in the same commit. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # BlinkCode AI ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Point your camera, get the file.** A file is compressed into a compact *File DNA* container, painted as **SpectraCode colour matrices**, and recovered by pointing a camera at the sender's screen — no server, no network after the first launch. [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-7c3aed)](LICENSE) [![Commercial licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/commercial-licence%20available-22c55e)](COMMERCIAL.md) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai)](https://github.com/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai/commits) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai)](https://github.com/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai/stargazers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai/total)](https://github.com/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai/releases) [![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-06b6d4)](https://drsamonline.github.io/blinkcode-ai/play/) [![No runtime deps](https://img.shields.io/badge/runtime%20deps-0-6366f1)](package.json) **[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/blinkcode-ai/play/)**  ·  **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/blinkcode-ai/)**  ·  **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai/releases/latest/download/blinkcode-ai-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/blinkcode-ai/releases/latest/download/blinkcode-ai.apk)
--- BlinkCode AI is the **high-capacity** member of the optical-transfer family. Where a QR code carries black-and-white modules, a SpectraCode carries **colour cells** — five bits per cell instead of one — so a single frame holds kilobytes rather than hundreds of bytes. ``` file ─▶ arithmetic coder ─▶ File DNA ─▶ frames ─▶ RS(255,223) ─▶ colour grid │ file ◀─ arithmetic decoder ◀─ CRC-32 ◀─ collector ◀─ RS ◀──────┘ ▲ camera ─▶ bullseye detect ─▶ homography ─▶ colour correction ─▶ classify ``` ## What it does - **SpectraCode transport** — a 36-colour palette, 5 bits/cell, bullseye markers and a calibration strip, rendered at two densities (120×80 and 60×40). - **Real compression** — an order-1 arithmetic coder **with a match (LZP) model**, plus a perceptual image mode. See the benchmark below. - **Reed-Solomon RS(255,223)** — repairs up to 16 damaged bytes per block, which is what lets a frame survive glare, shadow and mis-classified cells. - **Full optical decoder** — marker detection → homography → 3×4 colour correction → cell classification → RS, all in a Web Worker. - **Rateless (fountain) frame stream** — an LT code with a systematic prefix, so the receiver rebuilds the container from *any* k + a little overhead symbols. A missed frame costs one more symbol, not a whole loop. CRC-32 verifies the result. - **Offline-first PWA** — the model bundle is downloaded once and cached; after that the app never touches the network. ## Compression benchmark `npm run bench` — the arithmetic coder with and without the match model, against gzip. Measured on the project's own corpora: | corpus | orig | order-1 | + match | gzip | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | english prose (repeated) | 18 000 | 6.6× | **53.9×** | 136× | | english prose (varied) | 14 379 | 2.6× | **12.5×** | 13.3× | | JSON records | 71 556 | 4.0× | **8.6×** | 15.5× | | source code | 102 286 | 2.1× | **2.9×** | 3.3× | | already-compressed (gzip) | 156 | 1.3× | **2.0×** | 1.8× | | random bytes | 16 000 | 0.93× | 0.92× | 1.00× | | **total** | **222 377** | **2.4×** | **3.5×** | 4.2× | The match model added **~31%** overall over the original order-1 coder. It is still beaten by gzip on long repeats, and cannot beat entropy — see the honest limits below. ## Robustness `npm run robustness` pushes a simulated camera (perspective tilt, colour cast, vignetting, blur, sensor noise) until the decoder breaks. Current margins on a standard-density code: | condition | still decodes up to | | --- | --- | | sensor noise | ±32 (8-bit levels) | | blur | a 3-pixel box radius | | low light (gain) | 0.3× – 1.0× | The decoder samples each cell with a **median** (robust to edge bleed and glare), stretches the capture's contrast before binarising, and tries several thresholds when locating the bullseye markers. ## Perceptual mode The lossy image mode quantises a photo into a 64-value latent. `npm run perceptual` measures reconstruction error: | image | RMSE | PSNR | | --- | ---: | ---: | | smooth gradient | 3.9 | 36.3 dB | | photo-like | 7.7 | 30.4 dB | | 2-pixel stripes | 57.5 | 12.9 dB | The last row is the honest limit: a 64-value latent cannot represent near-Nyquist detail, and no reconstruction trick brings it back. Reconstruction now uses a **bicubic** upscale — bilinear left visible faceting on gradients and cost about 9 dB there. ## Honest limits These matter more than the pitch, so they are stated plainly here and in the app's "How it works" tab: - **One SpectraCode frame holds 5,111 payload bytes** (1,097 in robust density). Throughput is roughly `5 KB × frame rate` — about 15 KB/s at 3 fps. Frames are rateless, so a missed frame costs an extra symbol rather than a full loop. - **1000:1 lossless compression of arbitrary files is impossible.** Lossless coding cannot go below the entropy of the data. Real measured ratios are in the table above: strong on structured text, ~1× on already-compressed data. - **Extreme ratios exist only in perceptual mode**, which is genuinely lossy — an image becomes a 64-value latent and returns as a soft reconstruction. - **The "neural" model is a mock with a real interface.** The bundle format, one-time download, offline caching and the coder's model API are production shaped; the weights are trained order-1 statistics plus DCT quantiser scales (~129 KB), not a large neural net. `Order1Model` in `src/lib/arith.js`, `Order1MatchModel` in `src/lib/predict.js` and the transforms in `src/lib/image-codec.js` are the swap points. - **Camera decoding is validated in simulation**, not against physical phone optics: the tests render a code, apply perspective tilt, a colour cast and vignetting, and decode it end to end. Real-world glare, motion blur and low-end sensors may still need per-cell voting and multi-frame averaging. ## Run it ```bash npm install npm run build:model # (re)train and package the downloadable model bundle npm run serve # http://localhost:8080 npm test # codec + full optical loopback tests npm run bench # compression benchmark npm run lint ``` Open the app, pick a file (or paste text), hit **Compress**, then **Show SpectraCode** on the sender and **Start scanning** on the receiver. Without a second device, the **loopback self-test** pushes every rendered frame back through the real optical decoder. ## Project layout ``` src/ index.html app.js styles.css sw.js manifest.webmanifest lib/ arith.js arithmetic coder + order-1 model predict.js order-1 + match (LZP) model — the compression upgrade codec.js File DNA encode/decode orchestration format.js container header fountain.js LT fountain codes (rateless frame stream) image-codec.js perceptual latent encoder/decoder geometry.js linear solver, homography, colour-correction fit palette.js the 36 reference colours rs.js Reed-Solomon GF(256) spectracode.js layout, symbol packing, renderer spectra-decode.js marker detection → payload bytes storage.js one-time model download + offline persistence stream.js frame header, CRC-32, out-of-order frame collector surface.js canvas / buffer drawing targets workers/ model loader, compression, decompression, optical decode models/ucg-v1.bin downloadable model bundle tools/ build.js, build-model.js, bench.js, tune.js, robustness.js, perceptual.js, update-scales.js, serve.js tests/ codec, stream, predict + end-to-end optical loopback docs/ landing page + built demo (GitHub Pages) ``` ## The landing page embeds the app itself in a frame, driven by four guided buttons — the demo is the product, not a picture of it. --- ## What it computes | Area | Outputs | |------|---------| | **Body composition** | BMI with category and gauge, body-fat % (Deurenberg), lean body mass, body surface area (Mosteller), ideal body weight (Devine), adjusted body weight, waist-to-height ratio, waist-to-hip ratio, ideal weight range and target weight | | **Energy** | BMR (Mifflin–St Jeor), TDEE (activity multipliers), calorie targets (maintain / lose / gain) and projected weekly weight change | | **Macros** | Protein, fat, carbohydrate and fiber; protein per meal; macro split (% of calories) | | **Fluids** | Daily fluid requirement (30 mL/kg baseline, adjusted for climate, exercise, fever and breastfeeding), shown in mL / L / glasses | | **Renal** | Creatinine clearance (Cockcroft–Gault) from a serum creatinine, with its formula and limits | | **Dosing** | Weight-based (rate × weight) and surface-area-based (rate × BSA) dose, with the unit shown at every step | | **Risk scores** | CHA₂DS₂-VASc — stroke risk in non-valvular atrial fibrillation, with its source and intended population | | **Risk & flags** | Indian/Asia-Pacific **and** WHO BMI cut-offs; cautions for renal/hepatic disease, heart failure, athletes and paediatric patients | ## The working, shown Every result is printed with its formula and your own values substituted, in a "Show the working" panel: ``` BMI = 23.3 weight ÷ height² = 69 ÷ 1.72² BMR = 1600 10×wt + 6.25×ht − 5×age + 5 = 10×69 + 6.25×172 − 5×34 + 5 TDEE = 2480 BMR × activity = 1600 × 1.55 CrCl = 101.6 (140 − age) × wt ÷ (72 × Scr) = (140 − 34) × 69 ÷ (72 × 1.0) ``` A number you can check is worth more than a number you must trust — and it makes the app teachable and auditable without reading JavaScript. ## Features - **Responsive layout** — a single mobile column on phones, and a two-column desktop view (inputs and saved entries on the left, a sticky results panel on the right) from 960 px up. - **Real-time** recalculation as you type, and **unit conversion that preserves values** — cm / m / ft+in and kg / lbs switch without losing what you entered. - **Saved entries** in `localStorage`, each with an optional patient name/ID and a timestamp; delete with undo, filter, load back into the form, and a **BMI trend chart** across saved entries. - **CSV export and import** (with formula-injection protection) and **print / PDF** output. - **Copy / Share** a formatted text summary of the current result. - **Trilingual UI** — English, हिन्दी and ગુજરાતી. - **Light / dark theme**, respecting the system preference. - **Accessible** — ARIA radiogroups, live result region, keyboard navigation, focus-visible states, hover definitions on every metric, and a print stylesheet. - **Installable** — a web app manifest and a service worker (document network-first, assets cache-first, cache name stamped from the version), so "Add to Home Screen" installs an app rather than a bookmark, and a shipped update cannot hide behind a stale cache. A build stamp in the footer answers "am I on the new one?". - **A printed clinical note** — the print stylesheet produces a note, not a print of the dashboard: patient, age, sex, measurements, BMI and date in a header, the results in three columns, the working underneath in small type, and a signature line. The form is not printed; the record is. - **Change since the last entry** — for a returning patient the results panel states the difference from their previous saved entry (weight, BMI, waist, body fat) with the interval, matched on the patient name/ID. - **Readable in the consulting room** — three text sizes and a high-contrast mode, both remembered; `lang` follows the interface language so a screen reader pronounces Hindi and Gujarati. - **Keyboard-first entry** — Enter advances through the form and saves at the end; Alt+1…5 jump to age, height, weight, waist and activity; Ctrl/⌘+S saves, Ctrl/⌘+Enter saves and clears. - **Batch mode** — paste rows from a spreadsheet (patient, age, sex, height, weight, waist) and compute the whole list, then export it as CSV. Each row goes through the same form and the same functions as a single patient, so there is no second implementation to drift, and your own entries are left untouched. - **Encrypted export** — AES-256-GCM with a passphrase (PBKDF2-SHA-256, 150 000 iterations, fresh salt and IV), using the browser's own `crypto.subtle`. A CSV on a shared laptop is a plain list of patients; this is not. - **A sealed log** — every saved entry carries the SHA-256 of the one before it, and "Verify log" names the first entry that no longer matches. It detects an edit, not an attacker holding the whole file. - **Fully offline** — self-contained, no external requests; install it, or add it to a home screen on mobile. ## Usage - **Online:** open the [live calculator](https://drsamonline.github.io/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/play/). - **Offline:** download [`index.html`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/drsamonline/bmi-bmr-tdee-macros-fluid-calculator/main/index.html) and open it in any modern browser. - **On mobile:** open the file or link, then "Add to Home Screen". ## Repository contents | Path | Purpose | |------|---------| | `index.html` | Production build — the minified single-file app. | | `src/clinical-health-calculator.html` | The same app, un-minified and commented, for editing. | | `docs/index.html` | The landing page — this project's own design, not a copy of the app. | | `docs/play/` | The app as GitHub Pages serves it: the build, the manifest, the worker and its icons. | | `docs/assets/` | Generated: badges, app icons, platform glyphs, screenshots, social card. | | `scripts/build.js` | Minifies `src/` into `index.html` and `docs/play/index.html`, and stamps the service worker's cache name from the app version. `npm run build`. | | `docs/play/manifest.webmanifest` | The install manifest: standalone, `start_url`, icons that live inside the app folder because that is all the EXE and APK bundle. | | `docs/play/sw.js` | The service worker. Documents network-first, assets cache-first, cache name stamped at build time. | | `scripts/badges.py` | Draws the badges. Run it after a change that alters a claim. | | `scripts/make_icons.py` | Draws the app icon at every size, including the one the release pipeline stamps into the EXE and APK. | | `scripts/shot.py` | Takes the screenshots with headless Chromium, over a throwaway local server. | | `scripts/release_notes.py` | Builds the release notes from the changelog section for the version in `package.json`. | | `.github/workflows/release-extras.yml` | After the build: `SHA256SUMS.txt`, the hand-carry `-web.zip`, and those notes, attached to the rolling release. | | `test/crypto.test.js` | The encryption and log checks, in their own process — a runtime without WebCrypto must not take the suite down. | | `ROADMAP.md` | Offline-only enhancements, ordered by clinical value. | | `export-kit.js` | The shared export kit (CSV writer and download helper), inlined into the source above. | | `LICENSE` | PolyForm Noncommercial licence. | To rebuild after editing the source: ``` npm install npm run build # src/ -> index.html + docs/play/index.html, and the worker's cache name npm test ``` The build compresses but does not rename: the shipped file is the file a colleague is meant to be able to audit, so `function calculate` stays `function calculate`. ## Tests The app carries its own known-value self-tests — one per calculator, plus a units-consistency check. The suite is 74 checks in total: the calculators, the working panel, the CSV writer, the manifest and its icons, the service-worker cache name, the text-size and contrast controls, the change-since-last-entry line, the printed note's header, the Enter-key flow, batch mode and the limits panel. Eleven more live in `test/crypto.test.js` — the encrypted export round-trip, and the sealed log including that an edited record breaks the chain at the right entry. Those need `crypto.subtle`; where a runtime cannot start WebCrypto the suite prints `SKIP` and says so rather than pretending they passed. Open `index.html?selftest=1` and read the console, or run them headlessly: ``` npm install npm test ``` `test/selftest.js` loads the built `index.html` in a headless DOM, runs the self-tests, and drives the calculator (creatinine clearance, the "Show the working" panel, dosing, CHA₂DS₂-VASc). `.github/workflows/test.yml` runs it on every push. ## Changelog **2.7.0 — 2026-11-01** - **Batch mode** — paste a list and compute it; every row goes through the same form and functions as a single patient, and your own entries are restored afterwards. - **Encrypted export and restore** — AES-256-GCM with PBKDF2-SHA-256 key derivation (150 000 iterations, fresh salt and IV) through the browser's own `crypto.subtle`. - **A sealed log** — each entry carries the SHA-256 of the one before it; "Verify log" names the first entry that no longer matches. It detects an edit, not an attacker who can rewrite the file — the limit is stated rather than implied. - **When these numbers do not apply** — a limits panel under the definitions, covering BMI, the body-fat estimate, Mifflin–St Jeor, Cockcroft–Gault, the dose arithmetic, CHA₂DS₂-VASc and the fluid baseline. - **Release extras** — `SHA256SUMS.txt` beside every asset, a hand-carry `-web.zip`, and release notes generated from this changelog. The artwork now lives where the pipeline looks, and `scripts/make_icons.py` regenerates it at every size. - **Badges are files, not requests.** `scripts/badges.py` draws them into `docs/assets/`; the README and the landing page reference them by relative path, so nothing on either surface fetches from an image service. - **A landing page of its own.** Paper, serif and amber against the app's pale teal instrument panel — the two surfaces no longer read as one product twice. Accessibility, trilingual UI, light/dark theme, minified single-file build. ## Formulas & references - **BMR** — Mifflin MD, St Jeor ST, et al. *Am J Clin Nutr* 1990;51:241–7. - **TDEE** — standard activity multipliers (1.2 / 1.375 / 1.55 / 1.725 / 1.9). - **BMI cut-offs** — WHO international and WHO Asia-Pacific / ICMR Indian cut-offs. - **Protein & fiber** — IOM Dietary Reference Intakes; ACSM/NSCA protein range 0.8–2.0 g/kg. - **Fluid** — 30 mL/kg/day adult baseline (EFSA / IOM general guidance). - **Ideal body weight** — Devine BJ. *Drug Intell Clin Pharm* 1974. Adjusted BW = IBW + 0.25 × (actual − IBW). - **BSA** — Mosteller RD. *N Engl J Med* 1987;317:1098. - **Body fat** — Deurenberg P, et al. *Br J Nutr* 1991;65:105–14. - **Waist** — IDF / WHO Asia-Pacific cut-offs (men >90 cm, women >80 cm); waist-to-hip >0.90 (men) / >0.85 (women). - **Creatinine clearance** — Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. *Nephron* 1976;16:31–41. Adults 18+; needs steady-state renal function and a steady-state serum creatinine; not valid in pregnancy or at extremes of body size. - **Dosing** — weight-based (rate × actual weight) and surface-area-based (rate × BSA, Mosteller). Arithmetic only; not a prescribing decision. - **CHA₂DS₂-VASc** — Lip GYH, et al. *Chest* 2010;137:263–72. **Intended population: non-valvular atrial fibrillation.** Not a general risk score; it does not decide treatment. ## Disclaimer This is a **decision-support aid only**. Boericke, M.D. (1927)* [**Landing page**](https://drsamonline.github.io/boericke-repertory/)  ·  [**Live app**](https://drsamonline.github.io/boericke-repertory/play/)  ·  [**Releases**](https://github.com/drsamonline/boericke-repertory/releases/latest)  ·  [**Roadmap**](docs/ROADMAP.md)  ·  [**Licence**](LICENSE) [Windows `.exe`](https://github.com/drsamonline/boericke-repertory/releases/latest/download/boericke-repertory-portable.exe)  ·  [Android `.apk`](https://github.com/drsamonline/boericke-repertory/releases/latest/download/boericke-repertory.apk)  ·  [`index.html`](https://github.com/drsamonline/boericke-repertory/raw/main/docs/play/index.html)

--- ## What it is Boericke's *Repertory* is the index to a homeopathic practice: a symptom path, a rubric, and the remedies that belong to it, graded. This is that book as **one 903 kB HTML file** — the stylesheet, the script and the whole dataset inline. Open it in a browser and it runs; there is no install, no build step, no server and no account. It is built for the consulting room, which is why it is offline-first rather than offline-tolerant: once the page has loaded it never opens a socket. No CDN, no web font, no analytics, no telemetry, no badge service — **including on the landing page that advertises it.** ## What it does **Search like a query.** Instant results across 6,110 rubrics with real operators — `"exact phrase"`, `-exclude`, `a or b` — and typo tolerance that only kicks in when nothing at all matched. Remedy aliases mean *Gelsemium* finds the source's own *Gels*. `/` focuses the box, `↑` `↓` move, `Enter` adds to the chart. **Browse the book.** A **Browse** toggle walks the repertory by chapter and sub-rubric, expanded lazily, so you can navigate the way the book is laid out instead of guessing at words. **Repertorise, then eliminate.** Every selected rubric scores its remedies — grade 2 counts two points, grade 1 counts one, and you can change both weights (the scale is printed on the chart and in the print sheet, so a chart stays auditable). Mark a rubric **must-have** and every remedy that misses one is faded, or filtered out entirely. Filter the table by name; tap any remedy to see every rubric that lists it. **Keep the case.** Patient details, notes and prescription sit alongside the selection and the chart, grouped by patient. Cases can be **locked with a passphrase** — AES-256-GCM, key derived with PBKDF2-SHA256 (200,000 rounds) in the browser and never stored. Print a one-page A4 case sheet, export the chart as CSV, export every case as JSON, or save straight to a file you choose. **Work fast.** A command palette on `Ctrl`/`Cmd + K`, undo on `Ctrl`/`Cmd + Z`, saved searches, per-rubric notes, and computed "similar rubrics" for a rubric you are unsure about. **Cite it.** Every rubric has a `❝` button that produces a citable reference — path, chapter, edition, and the remedies split by grade — ready to paste into a case note. The author's own 1927 prefatory note is quoted in full in About, because it explains the arrangement better than any summary could. **Checked against the source.** Every rubric was aligned to a complete transcription of the 1927 text and compared remedy by remedy, grade by grade: **5,319 of 5,415** are identical, and the **96** that differ are listed in the app with the source's own line and the exact disagreement. About → Source check shows the totals; the ⚠ mark on a row means "look here". See [`SOURCES.md`](SOURCES.md). **Refuses to phone home.** No account · no server · no network after load · no external assets · no telemetry · no silent updates. ## What's new in 1.6.0 English-only interface · elimination by repertory section · patient visit history with a "New visit" action · a versioned release strip on the landing page. ## What's new in 1.5.1 A final audit as a script (`scripts/audit.py`, 29 checks) · the second-repertory plan removed · dead code removed. ## What's new in 1.5.0 Every rubric verified against the 1927 text · the 96 disagreements published, not hidden · the verdict shown in the citation sheet. ## What's new in 1.4.0 A citation for any rubric · the author's prefatory note quoted in full · [`SOURCES.md`](SOURCES.md) recording what came from where, and what could not be obtained. ## What's new in 1.3.0 The interface briefly shipped in three languages (removed in 1.6.0 — English only) · `?lang=` deep links · the release pipeline now embeds the real icon (`docs/play/icon.png` is the file `app-builder` looks for first). ## What's new in 1.2.0 Query operators and typo tolerance · browse-by-chapter · must-have rubrics · configurable grade weights · chart filter · encrypted vault · patient grouping and case search · command palette · undo · saved searches · per-rubric notes · similar rubrics · one-page case sheet · CSV export · backup reminder · service worker and installable manifest · text-size and high-contrast settings · data audit · remedy alias table. See the [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and the [roadmap](docs/ROADMAP.md) for what is deliberately not done. ## Use it | | | | :-- | :-- | | **Online** | [drsamonline.github.io/boericke-repertory/play/](https://drsamonline.github.io/boericke-repertory/play/) | | **Offline** | download [`index.html`](index.html) and open it — that is the whole installation | | **Windows / Android** | the portable `.exe` and the signed `.apk` on [Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/boericke-repertory/releases/latest) | | **Self-host** | fork the repo, enable GitHub Pages, deploy from the default branch | ## The data | | | | :-- | --: | | Rubrics | **6,110** | | Unique remedies | **1,461** | | Chapters | **25** | | Graded entries | **48,385** (15,737 at grade 2) | | Remedies with no rubric | **0** | | Runtime dependencies | **0** | The dataset is cleaned, not copied: OCR variants of a remedy name are merged into one canonical name, duplicate rubrics are merged, and remedy-less category headings are kept for structure but never appear in search results — so every rubric shown carries at least one remedy. The **About → Data audit** panel recomputes these numbers in the app, so the cleaning can be checked rather than trusted. ## The repository ``` docs/index.html the landing page (its own design, not the app's) docs/play/index.html the app as deployed docs/play/sw.js service worker: network-first HTML, cache-first assets docs/play/manifest.webmanifest docs/play/icon.png the mark app-builder embeds in the .exe and .apk docs/assets/ screenshots, local SVG badges, generated icons docs/ROADMAP.md the offline-only enhancement list SOURCES.md provenance: what came from where, how it was verified, what could not scripts/badges.py draws docs/assets/badge-*.svg — no image service scripts/icons.py rasterises the icon: PNG sizes, .ico, adaptive layers scripts/social.py draws the 1280x630 social card scripts/shot.sh headless-Chromium screenshots of both surfaces scripts/check.sh syntax check + self-test + vault test, one command scripts/audit.py every claim in this repo, checked against this repo tools/selftest.html 28 assertions driving the app through its own API scripts/vault_test.mjs 6 assertions on the encryption round trip ``` ```bash bash scripts/check.sh # syntax + 28 browser assertions + 6 crypto assertions python3 scripts/audit.py # 29 checks: offline promise, versions, counts, links python3 scripts/badges.py # regenerate the badges python3 scripts/icons.py # regenerate the icons, .ico and adaptive layers bash scripts/shot.sh landing # screenshot the landing page bash scripts/shot.sh app app '?q=burning%20headache' ``` The build pipeline (`.github/workflows/build-apps.yml`) builds the `.exe` and the `.apk` from `docs/play`, publishes the rolling release and deploys `docs/` to Pages — all from one commit, so the live demo and the released build can never disagree. ## Credits - **Content** — *Repertory* by **Oscar E.
