canteen-lan: # Canteen LAN [![live](docs/assets/badge-live.svg)](https://drsamonline.github.io/canteen-lan/) [![tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg)](test-node.js) [![deps](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg)](docs/play/) [![offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg)](#what-it-refuses-to-do) [![licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE) [![protocol](docs/assets/badge-protocol.svg)](docs/play/canteen.js) **Order from your table over the room's own Wi-Fi.** One laptop hosts the canteen and serves the board itself; every phone on the network joins it, orders from its seat, and the kitchen watches each table move from *placed* to *served*. No internet, no accounts, no telemetry, no dependency at runtime — and the board speaks English, one language, so nothing can drift out of sync with itself. **[Open the board](https://drsamonline.github.io/canteen-lan/play/)** · **[The landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/canteen-lan/)** · **[Run a room](#run-a-room)** · **[Adding a menu item](#adding-a-menu-item)** · **[Licence](LICENSE)** ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) ![The kitchen board, orders grouped by table with the running bill and how long each has waited](docs/assets/app-desktop.png) ## What it does A guest picks a table and a name, searches or filters the menu, picks **priced modifiers** (*Elaichi +₹5*), adds items to a cart that survives a reload, and places the order with a note — then taps *Show my bill* for an itemised slip with a QR the counter can read. The kitchen sees every open order grouped by table with the running bill and the minutes each has waited, or as a **floor** of tiles it can tap; marks one *preparing*, *served* or *cancelled*, **undoes** a wrong tap, **splits a table's bill** across heads in exact paise, prints a KOT or bill, edits the menu with its **stock counts**, **modifiers** and **serving windows**, prints the **menu board for the wall** on A3, reads the **shift report** — as a screen or an **A4 sheet** — and exports the day as CSV. The shift downloads as a file and can be put back from the board, so a backup needs no shell. It keeps working when the Wi-Fi does not: a service worker holds the shell, and anything sent while the room is unreachable waits in an outbox and is re-sent on reconnect — with idempotent order ids, so a re-send can never double-charge a table. The landing page embeds the real board in a frame (`play/?demo=1`) seeded with a shift's worth of orders, so you can move an order along, open the menu editor and add a dish before you install anything. The demo runs the same code as the app, from a pure engine function (`Canteen.demoDoc()`) the tests cover — there is no second demo build. ## Adding a menu item Three ways in, all ending in one `menu` message every device applies. There is no admin panel to log into and no database to migrate. 1. **From the board.** Kitchen → *Menu* → name, price in rupees, optional SKU and tags → *Save item*. It appears on every phone at once. Edit, *Sold out* and *Delete* sit on the same row. 2. **At startup, from a file.** `node host/room.js --menu my-menu.json` — a JSON array of `{ "sku", "name", "price", "tags", "names" }`, price in **paise**. Once the room has run, the journal wins, so a kitchen edit is never overwritten by a restart. 3. **By protocol.** `{ t: "menu:set", item: {…} }`, with `menu:del` and `menu:sold` beside it. SKUs, prices and tags are re-validated on arrival, so a hostile peer cannot post a ₹1 thali. Two rules make it safe to edit a live board: a placed order keeps the name and price it was ordered at, so changing the menu never rewrites an old bill; and a sold-out item leaves the guest menu while staying on the bills already open. A dish can carry **priced modifiers** (`Extra chutney:10, No sugar:0`, set as `name:price` pairs) and a **serving window** (`from` 6, `to` 11 — it may wrap past midnight). The guest menu follows the clock and says how many dishes are off it at this hour; the window is a display rule, so an order already placed is never re-priced or refused by the clock. A modifier's price always comes from the dish's own list, never from the message, so a peer on the LAN cannot price its own extra. A dish can also carry a **count** — twelve thalis, not "sold out". An order can only be placed as far as the count goes, the count comes off the menu as the order goes on the board (so a replay of the same messages lands on the same numbers), and at zero the dish leaves the guest menu while staying on open bills. `{ t: "stock:set", sku, stock }` sets it; a blank count means unlimited. ## Run a room One machine — a laptop, a Pi, anything with Node: ``` node host/room.js # room "canteen", port 8080 node host/room.js --pin 4821 # a stranger on the Wi-Fi is refused node host/room.js --print 192.168.1.50:9100 # every order prints a KOT node host/room.js --menu my-menu.json # seed the menu node host/room.js --data .canteen # where the journal lives node host/room.js --mirror 192.168.1.21:8080 # keep a second host in step ``` `--mirror` forwards every broadcast to a peer host, so the counter keeps running if the laptop dies; forwarded messages are marked and never re-forwarded, so two hosts cannot loop at each other. `--mirror-pin` is for a peer that does not share the room's PIN. It serves the board itself at `/`, prints the LAN address, and draws a QR in the terminal for a guest to scan — the code carries the room PIN, so scanning joins in one step. Also on offer: `/join` (a scannable page), `/qr.svg`, `/state`, `/report`, `/print`, and `/journal` (GET the shift as a `.jsonl`, POST it back to restore). The journal is `.canteen/room-.jsonl` — one JSON object per message. A restart replays the shift instead of losing it, and the menu comes back as the kitchen left it. ``` node test-node.js # 247 passed — engine, transport, page node scripts/smoke-host.js # 29 passed — the real host, across a restart and a mirror node scripts/link-check.js # 34 passed — every local link and anchor resolves ``` No host at all? `docs/play/index.html?solo=1` runs the whole canteen on one device, with the board persisted locally. ## How it is built The app is thin on purpose, and every part it stands on is **in the repository**: - `docs/play/canteen.js` — the engine: the board (menu, orders, table calls, audit log) and the twelve-message protocol (`menu`, `menu:set`, `menu:del`, `menu:sold`, `stock:set`, `order`, `status`, `cancel`, `undo`, `clear`, `call`, `ack`), plus priced modifiers, serving windows, the floor plan, the bill slip and the split. Pure, zero-dependency, identical in the browser and under Node, so the whole mechanic is tested headlessly. - `docs/play/web-kit.js` — the slice of the shared web-kit the app uses (storage, i18n EN/HI/GU, CSV, theme, seo, ui), shipped locally. It used to be *assumed* rather than shipped, which meant the page threw before it painted: 78 green engine tests and a dead screen. A test now reads `docs/play/index.html` and fails if any script it references is missing or remote. - `docs/play/lan-kit.js` — the room transport: SSE for server→client, plain POST for client→server, with the optional room PIN riding on every POST. - `docs/play/sw.js` + `manifest.webmanifest` — the offline shell: HTML network-first, assets cache-first, cache name bumped per release, and a build stamp in the footer so "am I on the new one?" is answerable from the page itself. - `docs/play/index.html` — the menu, the cart, the join panel, the kitchen, the floor, the menu editor, the report (screen and A4) and the guest's slip. English only, by decision: one language is easier to keep honest than three, and it is the one the thermal roll can print. The engine still stores an optional `names` field, so a Hindi board would be a UI job later rather than a data migration. - `host/lan-host.js` — the room: SSE, POST, a PIN check, the journal (including `/journal` download and restore), an optional mirror, and static serving. - `host/room.js` — the canteen host: journal replay, `/join`, `/qr.svg`, `/state`, `/report`, `/print`, and a KOT to a thermal printer on every order. - `docs/play/qr.js` — a real QR encoder (byte mode, versions 1–4, ECC L): bit stream, Reed–Solomon parity, function patterns, mask chosen by penalty score. It lives in the app folder because two surfaces need it — the host's join code and the guest's bill slip — and `host/qr.js` is the Node door to the same file. `scripts/qr-verify.py` checks the finished matrix module-for-module against the reference `qrcode` library — 4/4 exact — because a hand-rolled encoder is exactly the code that looks right and scans wrong. - `host/print.js` — ESC/POS over a TCP socket, 32 columns, no driver and no CUPS. - `scripts/smoke-host.js` — starts `host/room.js` as a real process, drives its routes over HTTP, kills it, starts it again and checks the shift and the menu came back, then brings a mirror up beside it and round-trips the journal. - `scripts/link-check.js` — every relative link, image and in-page anchor on the landing page and the README resolves; it runs in CI, so a renamed file cannot break a badge quietly. Every message is sanitised on arrival (SKUs, quantities, tables, statuses, tags, languages and calls are validated and clamped) and **prices are taken from the room's menu, never from the message**, so a buggy or hostile peer on the LAN cannot mis-price an order or break the board. Money is integer paise, so a running bill never drifts — including a bill split seven ways. The landing page at `docs/index.html` is its own object — a kitchen pass of thermal tickets and hairline rules on butcher paper, deliberately unlike the app's rounded, warm interface. Its badges are generated locally by `scripts/badges.py`; nothing on either surface is fetched from an image service or a CDN. ## What it refuses to do No cloud, no accounts, no internet, no telemetry, no CDN or external font, no app store, no runtime dependency, no database or migrations, no printer driver — and no price that came off the wire. ## Build the EXE and APK On every push, GitHub Actions runs the suite, builds a portable Windows EXE and a signed Android APK from `docs/play`, publishes them to the `app-latest` release with the app icon attached, and deploys the demo to Pages. All from the same commit, so the live demo and the download can never disagree. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. One file. Sections, dated symptoms, follow-ups, a timeline and a summary — the shared logic extracted from the drsamonline apps that repeat it. ## Use it See `case-kit.js` for the full API and `test-node.js` for worked examples. ## What it does - sections (history / habits / mapping) - dated symptoms with severity - follow-ups (remedy / potency / response) - timeline + summary + JSON - a plain-JSON interchange record (patient + version + cases) ## Interchange record A case (or a set of cases) can be handed to another app in the family as **one plain-JSON file** — no server, no network: ```json { "format": "case-kit/record", "version": 1, "exported": "2026-01-07T10:00:00.000Z", "patient": { "id": "p-001", "label": "S.M." }, "cases": [ { "id": "c…", "title": "Skin case 12", "sections": { … }, "symptoms": [ … ], "followUps": [ … ] } ] } ``` ```js var text = Case.exportRecord(caseOrCases, { id: "p-001", label: "S.M." }); var rec = Case.importRecord(text); // { version, patient, cases: [...] } ``` - **`patient`** is an opaque `id` and a short `label` (initials or a code) — **never a name**. Nothing identifying is carried by default. - **`version`** lets the shape evolve: older records still import (migrated at `importRecord`), and a *newer* version is refused rather than guessed. - The family mapping: a case's `followUps` are the **encounters**, and its `symptoms` / `sections` are the **notes** — a case-kit record expresses both. - Where a record is encrypted (the **Encrypted Case Log**), encrypt the whole envelope — the interchange file must be the encrypted archive, not plaintext. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 26 passed, 0 failed ``` ## Consumers skin-case-tracker, HMS, whispering-body-first-aid, gentle-pediatrics-companion ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # Chalk [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**A shared whiteboard for the room.** Everyone on the same Wi-Fi draws on the same board, live. No accounts, no internet, no telemetry — the strokes travel across your own network and nowhere else. **[Open the board →](https://drsamonline.github.io/chalk-lan/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/chalk-lan/) · [The rule](#what-it-must-not-do-and-does-not) · [Releases](#releases) · [What is in it](#what-is-in-it) ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) One person starts a room on a laptop in the room. The host prints a QR code and serves the board itself, so anyone who scans it is on the shared board with the room already joined — and anyone who prefers to type can enter the address or press **Find a room**. Draw with a finger, a mouse or a stylus; the strokes cross your own network and stop there. A late joiner gets one snapshot of the board, not a replay. ## What it does The app is **thin**: storage, languages, theming and accessibility come from **web-kit**; the room — SSE for server→client, plain POST for client→server, a room code, a snapshot for late joiners — comes from **lan-kit**. The only app-specific code is - `docs/play/chalk.js` — the engine: the board document, the message protocol, the geometry a board needs (hit testing, shapes, SVG export) and the demo scenes the landing page draws. Pure, zero-dependency, and it runs unchanged in the browser and under Node, so the whole mechanic is tested headlessly; - `docs/play/index.html` — the canvas, the toolbar, the join panel, the note editor, the QR panel; - `docs/play/qr.js` — a zero-dependency QR encoder, so a room can be joined by pointing a phone at a terminal; - `host/room.js` + `host/lan-host.js` — the room host, which also serves the board. Every message is sanitised on arrival (colour, size, text and points are validated and clamped, strokes bounded at 5000), so a buggy or hostile peer on the LAN cannot break the board. | | | |---|---| | runtime dependencies | **0** | | tests | **127 passing** — 115 engine, 12 host | | message types on the wire | **7** — `point`, `stroke`, `note`, `undo`, `clear`, `cursor`, `snapshot` | | languages | **6** — English, हिन्दी, ગુજરાતી, मराठी, বাংলা, தமிழ் | | snapshot for a late joiner | **one message**, not 500 | ## What is in it Everything that was on the list is built, and none of it costs a network call or a dependency. **On the board** - **Pressure and three nibs** — a point carries its pressure; chalk is soft and pressure-led, a marker is flat, a pen is thin and crisp. - **Shapes that snap** — line, box and circle drag out as a preview and commit as one stroke; the corners overshoot the way a hand does. - **Sticky notes** — a fifth message type carrying text items; notes move and edit by id. - **Laser pointer** — a cursor that is drawn, fades, and is never stored in the document. - **Four surfaces** — plain, dotted paper, a grid, a blackboard; all drawn on the canvas, no image fetched. - **Three chalk sets** — default, Okabe–Ito colour-safe, and high contrast. - **Undo anyone** — a mode where clicking a stroke or a note removes it, using a segment-aware hit test. **Into the room** - **Join by QR or room code** — the host serves the board, so its QR lands a phone in the room; the code sits beside the status dot. - **Find a room** — `Lan.scan()` probes the device's own /24 for a Chalk host. No DNS, no internet. - **Snapshot instead of replay** — one `snapshot` message, rebuilt through the engine on the host. - **Draw through a dropped host** — messages that fail to send are queued and flushed in order on reconnect. - **Named cursors** — every author's pointer, drawn with their name, fading on its own. - **Several boards in one room** — every message carries a board id; the engine ignores other boards. **Kept on the device** - **Save and reopen** — `.chalk.json` out and in, through the tested codec. - **SVG and PDF** — a vector export and print-to-PDF, both offline. - **Autosave** — the board is written to IndexedDB and comes back after a reload. - **Replay a session** — record the message log, then play it back with the gaps squeezed. **Installed, and for everyone** - **PWA** — a manifest and a service worker: HTML network-first, assets cache-first, cache name bumped per release, so a new build is never hidden behind the old one. - **A single-file board** — `scripts/bundle.py` inlines everything into `docs/play/chalk-single.html`. - **Keyboard drawing** — arrows move the point, space starts and ends a stroke. - **Six languages.** What is *not* there, and is not pretended otherwise: no mDNS/Bonjour (browsers cannot broadcast on the LAN, so discovery is a subnet probe instead), no cloud, no iOS-native build, no voice or image import. ## What it must not do, and does not - **No internet.** The app is four local scripts; the room is a socket on your own LAN. Unplug the WAN cable and the board keeps working. - **No accounts.** A name for the author label, stored on the device, and nothing else. - **No server of ours.** The host is a file you run yourself; there is no service to sign up to. - **No telemetry.** There is no analytics call in this repository to disable. - **No build step and no packages.** `npm install` is not part of running it. ## Releases Every push to `main` builds the three downloads below from `docs/play`, publishes the rolling `app-latest` release and deploys the page — all from the same commit, so the live demo and the released build cannot disagree. | | download | what it is | |---|---|---| | **Android** | [chalk-lan.apk](https://github.com/drsamonline/chalk-lan/releases/download/app-latest/chalk-lan.apk) | signed WebView build | | **Windows** | [chalk-lan-portable.exe](https://github.com/drsamonline/chalk-lan/releases/download/app-latest/chalk-lan-portable.exe) | portable, no installer | | **Linux** | [chalk-lan-linux](https://github.com/drsamonline/chalk-lan/releases/download/app-latest/chalk-lan-linux) | single binary | **2.0.0** — 1 November 2026 Every enhancement on the list, built: pressure and nibs, snapping shapes, notes, a laser, four surfaces, a colour-safe chalk set, undo-anyone, QR and room-code joining, a LAN scan, snapshots, a reconnect queue, named cursors, several boards, save and reopen, SVG and PDF, autosave, session replay, a PWA, a single-file build, keyboard drawing and six languages. The host now serves the board itself. Tests 50 → 127. **1.1.1** — 1 November 2026 The landing page stopped advertising the roadmap, and the colour swatches show their own colours again. **1.1.0** — 1 November 2026 A landing page of its own, the app moved to `docs/play/`, demo scenes drawn by the engine, a theme toggle and a build stamp. Tests 38 → 50. **1.0.0** — 25 October 2026 PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 everywhere, stated the same way in the licence, the headers and the README. **0.1.0** — 23 October 2026 First pass: the canvas board, the protocol with sanitisation, the zero-dependency room host, the build workflow. ## Run it **Start the room** (on one machine — a laptop, a Pi, anything with Node): ```bash node host/room.js # room "chalk", port 8080 ``` It prints the room code, the LAN address and a QR code. That address serves the board, so any device on the same Wi-Fi can open it — or scan the code — and be in the room. **Or open the board with no host at all:** ```bash docs/play/index.html # the app, from file:// docs/play/chalk-single.html # the same board in one email-able file ``` ```bash node test-node.js # the engine: 115 passed node test-host.js # the room: 12 passed ``` `?demo=lesson|erase|join` opens the board on a demo scene and `?theme=dark|light` pins the look for that visit — both are how the screenshots and the landing page's frame are made. ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page docs/play/index.html the app — canvas, toolbar, join panel, note editor, QR panel docs/play/chalk.js the engine: document, protocol, geometry, scenes docs/play/qr.js the QR encoder docs/play/web-kit.js shared runtime: storage, i18n, theme, a11y, ui docs/play/lan-kit.js the LAN transport, the health probe and the subnet scan docs/play/sw.js the offline shell (network-first HTML, cache-first assets) docs/play/manifest.webmanifest docs/play/chalk-single.html the whole board in one file, built by scripts/bundle.py docs/assets/ screenshots, generated badges and icons host/room.js the room host you run host/lan-host.js SSE down, POST up, snapshots, static board scripts/badges.py draws docs/assets/badge-*.svg and checks each claim scripts/icons.py draws docs/assets/icons/*.svg scripts/bundle.py builds chalk-single.html scripts/shot.sh screenshots the landing page and the app test-node.js the engine suite test-host.js the host suite, over real HTTP ``` The badges, the icons and the QR code are all **generated, not fetched** — an offline-first board that needs the network to describe itself would have broken its own rule. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. compfactory: # compfactory [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) Development workspace for the **CHCE** multi-repo compression project — the repository that coordinates `ziptastic`, `heavenzip` and the shared compression sources (`HCS`) rather than shipping an app of its own. Three repositories and this coordinator; there is no fourth. `preflate` is not a repository: it lives inside ziptastic as `src/precompressors/preflate_wrap.cpp`. ## What this repository is for CHCE (Holistic Compression Sources) is four things that have to agree: a source vault (`HCS`), the engine built from it (`ziptastic`), the orchestrator that chains prebuilt binaries (`heavenzip`), and this coordinator. It holds the phase plan, the hard rules all of them follow, and the per-repo agent prompts that keep the work in order. ## The rules that matter - **Keep each repository single-purpose.** If a file does not belong here, it does not go here. - **Follow the phases in order.** Each repository's `AGENT_PROMPT.md` lists them, and a phase's exit tests must pass before the next one starts. - **A failed gate is a commit, not a silence.** `phase-: FAILED — `, then stop and report. - **`vendor/hcs/` is read-only.** - **Offline at runtime.** No network calls, no downloads, no models. ## Why the architecture looks like this `heavenzip` never opens a compressor. It spawns processes — which is why it can stay GPL-safe while driving GPL tools: there is no linking, only process boundaries. The full plan is in [PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md](PROJECT_OVERVIEW.md); the per-repository instructions are in each repository's `AGENT_PROMPT.md`. The workspace itself is documented in [docs/WORKSPACE.md](docs/WORKSPACE.md) and a working day in [docs/WORKFLOW.md](docs/WORKFLOW.md). ## Phases `AGENT_PROMPT.md` §8 is the six-phase plan. Apps never bundle a compression library: ```js const gz = await Compress.gzip(bytes); // -> Uint8Array const raw = await Compress.gunzip(gz); // -> Uint8Array const b64 = await Compress.compressString("lots of text…"); const txt = await Compress.decompressString(b64); ``` ## API | Call | Does | |---|---| | `Compress.gzip` / `gunzip` | gzip (with header). | | `Compress.deflate` / `inflate` | zlib deflate. | | `Compress.deflateRaw` / `inflateRaw` | raw deflate (no header) — smallest. | | `Compress.compressString` / `decompressString` | Text ⇄ base64, any format. | | `Compress.ratio(original, compressed)` | Compressed/original, for a UI. | | `Compress.human(n)` | "12.4 KB" style formatting. | | `Compress.bytes` | text/base64 helpers. | ## Why not a library Compression Streams are built into modern browsers and Node 18+, so a compression library is dead weight. This wrapper is the one place the plumbing lives — and it reads the stream directly, so it needs no `Response`/`Blob` and runs everywhere the streams exist. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js PASS gzip round-trip PASS deflate round-trip PASS deflate-raw round-trip PASS repetitive data compresses well PASS string round-trip PASS unicode survives 6 passed, 0 failed ``` ## Environment Needs **Compression Streams** — Chrome 80+, Firefox 113+, Safari 16.4+, Node 18+. `Compress.available()` reports it. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

Conqueror OS

A private, offline resilience workspace that lives in a single HTML file.
Read · reflect · journal · track · review — no server, no account, no build step required to run it.

Landing page  ·  Live demo  ·  Download for Windows (.exe)  ·  Download for Android (.apk)  ·  Source  ·  Features  ·  Changelog  ·  All projects

--- Conqueror OS is a self-contained personal application for building mental resilience. It ships a short book (*The Resilience Protocol*), a Markdown journal, daily trackers, fillable worksheets, structured challenges, a spaced-repetition review queue, and local-only analytics — all wrapped in one file you can open from disk, email to yourself, or host anywhere.

--- ## Table of contents - [Highlights](#highlights) - [Screenshots](#screenshots) - [Quick start](#quick-start) - [Single-file by design](#-single-file-by-design) - [Zero dependencies](#-zero-dependencies) - [Features](#features) - [Keyboard shortcuts](#keyboard-shortcuts) - [Data & privacy](#privacy) - [Building from source](#building-from-source) - [Testing](#testing) - [Browser support](#browser-support) - [Project structure](#project-structure) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Roadmap](#roadmap) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [License](#license) - [Disclaimer](#disclaimer) --- ## Highlights - **One file, zero infrastructure.** `dist/conqueror-os.html` is the entire application. Open it and it runs. - **Offline by construction.** After the page loads there are no network requests at all — enforced with a Content-Security-Policy that forbids outbound connections. - **Private by default.** Your journal, notes and moods never leave the device. No analytics, no telemetry, no accounts. - **A real reading system.** Multi-book library with parts/chapters, inline highlights in three colours, notes, bookmarks, favourites, focus mode, read-aloud and dwell-time tracking. - **A practice system, not just a reader.** Journal, trackers, worksheets, challenges, and a spaced-repetition review queue. - **Resilient storage.** Schema migrations, undo on every destructive action, encrypted backups, JSON/Markdown/Word/CSV export, and an import that can merge instead of overwrite. - **A real icon system.** A single inline SVG sprite (~50 symbols) drives the whole interface — crisp at any zoom, colour-matched to every theme. - **Accessible.** Keyboard-first, focus-trapped dialogs, ARIA live regions, radiogroup semantics, high-contrast theme, and reduced-motion support. ## Screenshots | Library (multi-book, parts) | Reader (highlights, notes, related) | |---|---| | ![Library](docs/images/library.png) | ![Reader](docs/images/reader.png) | --- ## Quick start **Use it online (nothing to install):** **[drsamonline.github.io/conqueror-os/play/](https://drsamonline.github.io/conqueror-os/play/)** **Or run the file yourself (no tooling required):** 1. Download [`dist/conqueror-os.html`](dist/conqueror-os.html). 2. Open it **directly in a browser tab** (double-click it, or *File → Open*). 3. That's it — the app runs entirely in your browser. > **Important:** open the file in a real browser tab. If you view it inside an in-app preview pane, an email client or a document viewer, JavaScript may be blocked and you'll see an empty shell. The app shows an explicit message when that happens. **Run it locally with a server (optional, for install/PWA-style use):** ```bash npm run serve # serves the repo at http://localhost:8080 ``` ## ⚡ Single-file by design Everything — HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and all book content — is inlined into one document. That gives you: - Trivially portable: a single file to keep, copy, back up or host. - No CDN, no bundler required at runtime, no supply-chain surface. - Works from `file://`, a USB stick, a static host, or an intranet share. - The readable source (`src/index.html`) is the same file, just unminified. ## 🪶 Zero dependencies The **runtime has no dependencies** — no framework, no library, no external asset. The only `devDependencies` are for the maintainer toolchain (a minifier and a headless DOM for tests). `npm ls --prod` is empty by design. --- ## Features ### Reading - **Multi-book library** with parts and chapters, progress pips and per-book completion. - **Inline highlights** in amber / blue / green with per-highlight notes; click any highlight to edit or delete. - **Selection quick-actions** — highlight, copy, or send the selection straight to a new journal entry. - **Notes** per chapter with Markdown and `[[wiki links]]` to other chapters. - **Bookmarks with labels**, a dedicated Bookmarks page, and a Favourite-quotes page. - **Inline SVG diagrams** — a themed, hand-built diagram for every chapter, drawn to adapt to the current theme. - **Focus mode**, line-spacing / width / font / weight controls, and **read-aloud** (Web Speech API). - **Themes:** light, dark, sepia, high-contrast, OLED black, and Auto (follows the OS). - **Resume banner** and dwell-time tracking (minutes per day and per chapter). ### Journal & reflection - Six entry types, **tags**, and filters by **type, tag, date range and free text**. - **Edit** entries, **draft autosave**, **voice dictation**, and a rotating daily prompt. - **"On this day"** resurfacing of past entries. - **Attachments** (images) stored in IndexedDB. ### Trackers & analytics - Built-in trackers (mood, sleep, exercise, meditation, habits) plus **custom trackers**. - **Trend line + 7-day moving average**, **calendar heatmap**, and **correlation** (Pearson r) between any two trackers. - Local-only **insights** and printable / exportable reports. ### Challenges & review - Structured 7/21/30/45/90-day programs plus **custom challenges**. - **Pause/resume**, **reminders**, a **shareable progress card** (canvas → PNG). - **Spaced repetition** (SM-2 lite) over each chapter's key idea and reflection. ### Worksheets & knowledge - Reusable fillable sheets with saved history (Daily Check, Weekly Review, Setback Ledger). - **Knowledge graph** of chapters, worksheets and challenges by shared concepts. - **Glossary** auto-built from chapter tags. ### Data, safety & privacy - **Undo** on every delete; # control-panel

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE)

**Every workflow in every repository — what runs, when, what calls what, and what is connected to nothing.**

Nothing in this system knew its own shape. There were ~112 workflows across ~64 repositories: reusable
ones, callers, schedules, dispatches — and no single place that answered *"what runs, and what calls
what?"*. This is that place.

It is also the control surface: **every workflow has a Run button**, and they are grouped into the four
stages they actually form — from an idea to a shipped app to the system repairing itself.

## What it holds

| file | what it is |
|---|---|
| `docs/inventory.json` | every workflow, parsed: its triggers, cron, jobs, `needs`, steps, permissions, and every reusable call it makes |
| `docs/plan.json` | the four stages, the routes through them, and the workflows that fit in no stage |
| `docs/index.html` | the panel — the pipeline, the routes, the Run buttons, and what is broken |
| `tools/fetch.py` | pull every repo's workflows into a tree (no secret needed for public repos) |
| `tools/scan.py` | parse the tree into the inventory, and work out who calls whom |
| `tools/plan.py` | turn the inventory into the stages and the routes |

## The four stages

1. **Scratch** — an idea becomes a repo. `intake`, `new-app`, `adopt`.
2. **Build** — a repo becomes an artefact. Every `test`, `ci`, `lint`, and the app pipeline.
3. **Deliver** — an artefact becomes public. `release`, `pages`, `shot`, `app-deliver`, the refreshers.
4. **Repair** — the system keeps itself honest. `self-diagnose`, `self-heal`, `health`, `audit`, `backup`,
   `repo-learning`, `backlog-status`.

## The routes — how little you have to do

| route | you do | then, on its own |
|---|---|---|
| **A new app** | describe it in one line | spec → repo → guards → landing page → three-platform build → release → demo → screenshot |
| **Change an app** | push, or merge a PR | test → build → release → demo → screenshot |
| **Repair** | nothing | diagnose → heal → audit → learn → back up |
| **Ship on demand** | press Run | three builds → release → demo → screenshot |

**The everyday routes ask for at most one thing, and usually nothing.**

## How Forge embeds

Three layers, three jobs:

- **Forge** (private) is the **brain** — the memory (backlog, run log, registry, rules), the tools, and the agent's workspace.
- **This panel** (public) is the **map** — what runs, what calls what, what is missing, and the routes.
- **The dashboard** (public) is the **vitals** — what the system *is*: the products, their health, the conformance scores.

One-way and checkable: **Forge writes the memory → the tools derive the facts → the panel and the dashboard publish them.**
Anyone can run the tools and get the same numbers.

## Why this is the commercial product

You are not selling an app. You are selling **a system that governs itself and can prove it** — one that audits its own
drift, catches its own silent failures, backs up before every merge, and shows its work in public, with the numbers
generated from the repositories rather than typed into a slide. The licence sells **Forge**; the apps stay free, which is
what makes the map worth reading.

## What is missing (tools/gaps.py)

Every check is a rule with a reason — `permissions`, `timeout-minutes`, `concurrency`, drift, orphans, un-runnable
workflows. **DRIFT is the one that already cost a release.**

## The chosen routes (tools/simulate.py)

Candidates are **scored**, not asserted: inputs, hand-actions, how many things must go right, **the chance the output is
wrong**, stage coverage, resumability, and whether the route leans on a hand-copied workflow. The winner per scenario is
the one the numbers choose.

## The Run buttons

Each opens that workflow's page on GitHub — the real dispatch. Nothing here needs a token in a browser,
which is why the panel can be public.

## How it stays true

`scan.yml` runs daily: it re-fetches every workflow, rebuilds the inventory and the plan, runs both
tools' own tests first, and commits the fresh data. The page reads that data, so it cannot drift from
what the workflows actually are.

# CoreFit MD [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)

**A five-minute morning core routine where every set opens on the demonstration, not the intro.** **[Open the app →](https://drsamonline.github.io/corefit-md/play/)** · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/corefit-md/) · [The rule](#the-rule) · [Backlog](BACKLOG.md) ![The landing page](docs/shot.png) No account, no server, no build step, no dependencies. `docs/play/` is the entire application — eight small scripts on one namespace, one stylesheet, three self-hosted fonts. It runs from `file://` by opening `index.html`, and installs as a PWA when served over HTTPS. ## The rule Most workout apps embed a video and press play, so the set begins with a channel ident and a presenter explaining the move. Here the clip window is data: ```js { videoId: 'ASdvN_XEl_c', clip: { start: 30, end: 55 } } ``` The player is created with `start=30`, seeked again the moment it reports ready, and re-seeked whenever playback passes the window end — so fifty seconds of plank keeps showing the plank. During each rest interval the next exercise is preloaded with `cueVideoById`, which removes the black frame at the top of the following set. Every window is editable in the app's Library: scrub, hit **now** on either field, save. ## Where the motion comes from `Settings → Clip source` decides: - **YouTube** (default) — the 0:30 clip window plays when the embed loads. Four of the five original IDs are alive; Bird Dog was replaced after the original 404'd. - **Local** — no network request of any kind. Motion comes from `assets/media/` if a clip exists there; otherwise the still is shown. Either way, every move has a **local still** in `assets/media/` (watermarked, 1280×720), so a blocked embed, a dead video or a flight turns the workout into a slideshow rather than a black box. Animated SVG figures remain underneath that as the final fallback. On the first visit over HTTPS the service worker caches every media file in the manifest, so one session online makes the stills available offline afterwards. ## When there is no network Every move ships an **animated SVG figure** drawn for this app (`docs/play/assets/demo/`, 1.5–2.2 KB each). It replaces the player automatically when: - the clip is dead — one of the original five IDs had been deleted, which is what started this; - the embed is blocked or errors; - the device is offline (`navigator.onLine === false`); - the clip is shorter than its window (the player clamps the window to the real duration); - you flip the **Clips / Figures only** switch at the top of the Library (also in Settings → Video). Tapping any library card opens the sheet even with no video at all: it shows the animated figure, a link to open the clip on YouTube, and a search for a better one. The figures are original drawings, not frames from the videos: the clips are other people's work, so they are embedded and credited — the channel name sits under the player and every source is listed in the app's *Sources and credits* sheet. Nothing is copied into the repo. ## Generated assets `PROMPTS.md` is the brief for replacing the figures with AI-generated stills and video loops: a shared style block, a character-lock strategy, ten per-move prompts (image and motion), negative prompts, an acceptance checklist, and the watermark spec. All ten moves now have a generated still in `docs/play/assets/media/` — watermarked, 1280×720, 68–127 KB each. The animated SVG figures remain as the fallback for anything missing, and as the source for the `scripts/figures.py` pipeline. Drop more into `docs/play/assets/media/` and run `python3 scripts/media_manifest.py`. The app prefers them over the figures everywhere, per exercise, falling back for anything missing — so a partial set is fine. `scripts/watermark.py` stamps the CoreFit MD mark onto stills (Pillow) and clips (ffmpeg). ## What it does | | | |---|---| | Moves per session | **5**, plus warm-up and cool-down | | Session length | **6:15** at week 1, **7:10** at peak | | Progression | **6 weeks**, 45 → 60 s work, deload at week 4, driven by sessions logged | | Languages | **English · हिन्दी · ગુજરાતી**, locale-aware dates | | Storage | `localStorage` — history, clips, settings, profile | | Offline figures | **10** animated SVGs, 19 KB total | | Runtime dependencies | **0** | | App size | **363 KB**, 31 files | Sessions carry pause, skip, restart, ±10 s, per-side splitting for unilateral moves, an optional rep-counting mode, and resume-after-interruption. Logging carries streaks with a one-day grace, a weekly goal, 30-day consistency, post-session RPE, a pain flag and a note. Export is CSV, JSON backup/restore, or a printable summary. ## What it must not do, and does not - **No account, no sign-in, no sync.** There is no server to sync with. A backup file is the whole sync story. - **No analytics, no third-party scripts.** The only network requests are the video embed and its thumbnail. - **No streak mechanics that punish rest.** One missed day is forgiven anywhere in the chain; two in a row end it. - **No medical claims.** It screens for contraindications, offers an easier variation, and tells you to stop if a move hurts. It is a training aid. ## Run it ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/corefit-md cd corefit-md python3 -m http.server 8080 # then open localhost:8080/docs/ # or just the app, straight from disk: open docs/play/index.html # regenerate the committed assets python3 scripts/badges.py bash scripts/shot.sh . app ``` ## Layout ``` docs/index.html the landing page (its own design; serif, cobalt, dark demo band) docs/play/index.html the app — markup only docs/play/assets/css/ one stylesheet, light + dark + big-text + landscape docs/play/assets/js/ config · data · store · i18n · video · session · ui · main docs/play/assets/i18n/ en / hi / gu string tables docs/play/assets/demo/ 10 animated SVG demonstrations (offline fallback) docs/play/sw.js offline shell: HTML network-first, assets stale-while-revalidate docs/assets/ screenshots + badges generated by scripts/badges.py scripts/ badges.py, figures.py, shot.sh BACKLOG.md everything next that needs no server — and what is refused ``` ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0 — see `LICENSE`. Video embeds belong to their creators. --- ## Author **Dr Sohil Momin** — [@drsamonline](https://github.com/drsamonline) Built as a personal morning routine and published so it can be forked. The clinical screening, contraindication flags and regression notes are written from a doctor's viewpoint, not scraped from a fitness blog; the training content is ordinary core work anyone can do on a mat. crypto-kit: # crypto-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) [![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/crypto-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/crypto-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml) **The shared crypto core for drsamonline apps.** One file, no dependencies, built on the Web Crypto API. Apps should never hand-roll cryptography. This is the one place it lives — the browser-side counterpart to what `lockhtml` does on the command line: - **AES-256-GCM** — authenticated encryption, so tampering is detected; - **passphrase keys** via **PBKDF2-SHA256**; - a portable **sealed envelope** (`salt + iv + ciphertext`) as bytes or base64; - a **one-time-view** helper (seal with a random key, delete it after first open); - byte / text / base64 helpers. ## Use it ```js // passphrase-sealed note const b64 = await CryptoKit.sealString("meet me at 7", "correct horse"); const text = await CryptoKit.openString(b64, "correct horse"); // -> "meet me at 7" // or a key you manage yourself const key = await CryptoKit.newKey(); const box = await CryptoKit.encrypt(key, CryptoKit.bytes.fromText("hi")); const back = await CryptoKit.decrypt(key, box); ``` ## API | Call | Does | |---|---| | `CryptoKit.seal(bytes, passphrase, opts)` | Returns the sealed envelope (Uint8Array). | | `CryptoKit.open(envelope, passphrase, opts)` | Decrypts; **throws** on wrong passphrase or tampering. | | `CryptoKit.sealString` / `openString` | The same, as base64 strings. | | `CryptoKit.deriveKey(pass, salt, iters)` | A PBKDF2 AES-256 key. | | `CryptoKit.encrypt` / `decrypt` | AES-GCM with a key you hold. | | `CryptoKit.newKey` / `exportKey` / `importKey` | Random keys, for one-time view. | | `CryptoKit.randomBytes(n)` | Cryptographically random bytes. | `opts.aad` adds associated data (bound to the ciphertext, not encrypted). `opts.iterations` sets the PBKDF2 cost (default 250,000). ## One-time view Seal with a random key, give the key out-of-band, and delete it after the first `open`. `crypto-kit` gives you the primitives; the app owns the "used once" state. ## Secure context Web Crypto needs **https or localhost**. GitHub Pages is https, so deployed apps are fine; opening a page from `file://` may not be. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 7 passed, 0 failed ``` Covers: round-trip, wrong passphrase rejected, tampering detected, AAD mismatch rejected, base64 round-trip, key export/import, and unicode. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # Dance Fight ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Every fight move is a dance move.** A single-file browser rhythm game — load your own track, the beat is analysed up front, and every attack you throw is a dance move. Land it in time with the music and it becomes a **PERFECT** hit worth 60% extra damage. **🔗 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/dance-fight/)**  ·  **🎮 [Play the live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/dance-fight/play/)**  ·  **[Source](https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight/releases/latest/download/dance-fight-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight/releases/latest/download/dance-fight.apk)
---

Every fight move is a dance move.

Load a track from your device and the character dances to it. The beat is analysed up front, the whole arena pulses on the pulse, and every attack you throw is a dance move — land it in time with the music and it becomes a PERFECT hit worth 60% extra damage.

▶ Play it in your browser

--- ## What it is A single-file browser game. No build step, no dependencies, no install, no server. ``` index.html # the entire game — HTML, CSS, JS, ~78 KB ``` Open it, pick a song, fight. It works offline and from `file://` too. ### Highlights - **The music drives everything.** Your track is analysed for its real beat grid, and the character's dance is locked to the audio playhead — so it can't drift, and it doesn't depend on frame rate. - **Every move is a dance move.** Arm Wave, Spinning Kick, Body-Roll Uppercut and a 720° Body-Roll Finisher. Spins are real rotations, not pose swaps. - **The character never stops dancing.** Attack poses are layered *over* the ongoing groove rather than replacing it. - **Rhythm is the combat system.** Moves landed on the beat hit 60% harder and build a bigger combo. Shuffle-stepping in time charges your finisher meter. - **Keyboard and touch.** On-screen controls appear automatically on phones. - **One file, zero dependencies.** No framework, no bundler, no CDN. --- ## How to play Pick an audio file (or just press Start and it plays a default 128 BPM groove). | Key | Move | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | `A` `D` | Shuffle step | Dance-walk. Stepping in time charges your finisher meter | | `W` | Leap | Arabesque | | `S` | Dip | Guards and dodges — hold to block | | `J` | **Arm Wave** | Fast, low damage | | `K` | **Spinning Kick** | Medium — a full 360° turn | | `L` | **Body-Roll Uppercut** | Heavy — rolls through a full turn | | `SPACE` | **Body-Roll Finisher** | Needs a full meter — a 720° spin | | `P` | Pause / resume music | | **Land moves on the beat.** A move thrown within ~80 ms of a beat lands as a PERFECT: 1.6× damage and a bigger combo multiplier. The gold `· ON BEAT` tag on the move name tells you when you nailed it. **On a phone:** on-screen controls appear automatically. Hold a direction with one thumb and tap attacks with the other. Rotate to landscape — the arena is wider than it is tall. --- ## How the beat sync works The interesting part. The usual approach — polling an `AnalyserNode` every frame — ties beat detection to the render frame rate, which falls apart on a slow device. This game does it **offline instead**, on the decoded audio buffer, before the fight starts: 1. **Low-pass** the signal to ~180 Hz with a one-pole filter (kick-drum territory). 2. Build a **per-10 ms RMS envelope**, then take its **positive flux**. 3. **Peak-pick** onsets against an adaptive threshold. 4. **Autocorrelate** the flux over lags of 0.30–0.75 s to find the tempo, refined to sub-sample accuracy. 5. Search every phase offset for the **grid that lines up with the most onset energy**. The result is a beat grid. During play the dance phase is read *straight off the audio playhead* — `(playhead − phase) / period` — so the groove cannot drift, and it is completely independent of frame rate. On test tracks at 100, 128 and 150 BPM the detected tempo was exact, and **97% of kicks landed within 30 ms of a grid beat** (median offset 5–9 ms, which is just the 10 ms hop resolution). Everything else is drawn on a forward-kinematic skeleton. Moves are keyframed joint angles blended *over* the ongoing dance groove rather than replacing it, so the character keeps dancing while it fights. Spins are faked as a horizontal squash that mirrors past 90°, with the near and far limbs swapping — and every attack leaves additive ghost trails of the last few poses, which is what makes a rotation read as motion. --- ## Run it locally ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/dance-fight.git cd dance-fight open index.html # macOS (xdg-open on Linux, start on Windows) ``` No toolchain needed. To serve it instead: ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 # then visit http://localhost:8000 ``` --- ## Known limitations Being straight about what this is and isn't: - **Autoplay.** Browsers block audio until you interact with the page, so the first tap or click unlocks sound. If you ever hear nothing, a **live level meter** under the BPM readout shows whether audio is actually flowing — and a banner appears if it isn't. That meter reads real signal, not a flag. - **Tempo lock is at load.** A track with a long ambient intro, or one that drifts tempo, gets a grid based on the overall character of the song. If no clear pulse is found it falls back to a steady 128 BPM. - **Mobile is landscape.** It's playable in portrait, but the arena is 16:9 and it will be cramped. - **Feel is unverified at 60fps.** The geometry, timing and beat grid were verified programmatically, but I could only test in a headless browser rendering a few frames per second. How the spins and trails feel in motion is the part you're the judge of. ---

# dashboard — the live status of the drsamonline system

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE)

A **public** status page for the whole fleet, served from **GitHub Pages** (public
repo = free Pages, no paid plan). It shows every repo, its build health, its
download links, and the store.

## How it stays current (free, no PAT)

A static page cannot read private repos from a browser. So the data is
**pre-rendered**: the Forge agent (which has admin access) generates `data.json`
from the `registry`, the `knowledge` index and the GitHub API, and commits it here
on a schedule. `index.html` is a plain static app that just renders `data.json`.

```
registry + knowledge + GitHub API
        │  (Forge agent, scheduled)
        ▼
   data.json  ──▶  index.html  ──▶  GitHub Pages (public, free)
```

No PAT, no secrets, no server. Sensitive internals (quota detail, the commercial
plan) stay in the private repos and are reported to the owner directly, not here.

## Where it lives

**https://drsamonline.github.io/dashboard/play/** — that is the whole site.

The console is the app; there is **no landing page**, by design (`PAGES.json`:
`landing` is null, `app` is `docs/play/index.html`). So the site ROOT answers
**404**: `docs/` has no `index.html` and must not gain one. If you are looking at
a 404, you are one path short — add `play/`.

## Files

- `docs/play/index.html` — the console (no CDN, no build step).
- `docs/404.html` — the not-found page; its only link goes to the console.
- `data.json` — the rendered data (regenerated by the agent).
- `generate.py` — the reference generator the agent runs.

I write software that keeps working when the connection drops.

I'm a practising homeopathic physician in Vadodara. Everything here is built on one premise: the app should be the whole app — no server to reach, no account to create, nothing phoned home. It turns out that covers most of what I want to make, from a clinician's repertory to a browser game that runs from a single file.

# drsamonline.github.io

The personal project index for **Dr Sohil Momin**, served by GitHub Pages at
**https://drsamonline.github.io/**.

[![Live site](https://img.shields.io/badge/live%20site-drsamonline.github.io-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![Projects: 41](https://img.shields.io/badge/projects-41-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![Offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/offline--first-yes-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![No trackers, no cookies](https://img.shields.io/badge/no%20trackers-no%20cookies-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![Type: project hub](https://img.shields.io/badge/type-project%20hub-586069?style=flat-square)](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=flat-square)](LICENSE)

**Live site:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/>  ·  **Source:** <https://github.com/drsamonline/drsamonline.github.io>

A single static page that lists every project. The data is **built ahead of
time and committed**, so the page never depends on a rate-limited third-party
call to render — it fetches one same-origin JSON file and falls back to an
embedded snapshot if that is unavailable.

## How it works

1. A scheduled GitHub Actions workflow (`.github/workflows/refresh-hub.yml`)
   runs daily at 03:17 UTC and on `workflow_dispatch`, with
   `permissions: contents: write`.
2. It calls the GitHub API **with the runner's authenticated token** (never the
   60-requests/hour unauthenticated limit), drops forks and the
   `drsamonline` / `drsamonline.github.io` repos, and merges the rest with the
   `CURATED` map inside `index.html`. A repo that is **not** in the map still
   appears, under the automatic **Other / New** category, using its GitHub
   description.
3. `tools/build_hub.py` writes the merged data to **`repos.json`** and
   regenerates the embedded snapshot in `index.html` (so the offline fallback
   always matches) plus the JSON-LD `ItemList` and `sitemap.xml`.
4. `tools/capture_shots.py` loads every project landing page at 1200×750,
   downscales to 600×375 and encodes **WebP** into `assets/shots/<repo>.webp`.
   Images that already exist, are recent and were a successful capture are
   skipped; failures fall back to a branded placeholder and are retried.
5. Everything is committed back to the repository.

At runtime the page:

* renders instantly from the embedded snapshot, then
* fetches **`repos.json`** (same origin, no rate limit, fast) and re-renders.

No third-party screenshot host, no runtime GitHub API call, no analytics.

## Design

* Calm, professional palette built on CSS custom properties in `:root`, with a
  full override under `[data-theme="dark"]`. Body text meets WCAG AA (4.5:1)
  and UI borders meet 3:1 in both themes.
* A **theme toggle** in the navigation that respects `prefers-color-scheme` on a
  first visit, persists the choice in `localStorage`, applies the stored theme
  **before first paint** via a tiny inline `<head>` script, updates its
  `aria-label` / `aria-pressed` and icon, and works with the keyboard.
* `prefers-reduced-motion` is honoured throughout.
* Self-contained: inline CSS/JS, no external JS libraries, inline SVG icons.

## Layout

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html` | The hub. Contains the `CURATED` map (source of curated fields) and the embedded snapshot. |
| `repos.json` | Build-time data the page fetches at runtime. |
| `tools/build_hub.py` | Fetches the API, merges with `CURATED`, writes `repos.json` + snapshot + JSON-LD + sitemap. |
| `tools/capture_shots.py` | Captures and encodes the local thumbnails. |
| `tools/placeholders.py` | Branded fallback thumbnail. |
| `assets/shots/` | Locally served thumbnails (`<repo>.webp`) + `_manifest.json`. |
| `.github/workflows/refresh-hub.yml` | The scheduled build. |

## Customising

Everything configurable lives in the small block at the top of the inline
`<script>` in `index.html`:

| Setting | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `CURATED` | Per-repo `cat`, `desc`, `demo`, `feat`, `rel`, `kicker`, `tag`. |
| `CAT_LABEL` / `CAT_ORDER` | Category names and display order. |
| `FEATURED` | Repo keys pinned to the top of the Featured section. |

## Local preview

```bash
python3 -m http.server 8080
# then open http://localhost:8080/
```

To regenerate the data locally without the API:

```bash
HUB_REPOS_FILE=repos_raw.json python3 tools/build_hub.py
```

Works on a phone. | | | | :-- | :-- | | **Source** | [github.com/drsamonline/eon-commando](https://github.com/drsamonline/eon-commando) | | **Download** | [index.html](https://github.com/drsamonline/eon-commando/raw/main/index.html) (109 KB, self-contained) | | **Landing page** | [drsamonline.github.io/eon-commando](https://drsamonline.github.io/eon-commando/) | --- ## 📸 Screenshots
**Title** — three eras, one commando

**Era I · Ashen Dawn** — the burning city, turrets on the rooftops

**Era II · Glacier Eon** — ice shelves over open air

**Boss — The Warden** — spread fire, shoulder cannons, ground shockwave

**Boss — The Eon Heart** — a spiral that closes from every angle

**Widescreen** — the view widens from 16:9 to 21:9 instead of letterboxing
--- ## 🆕 What's new in 4.6.2 **Cross-audit with [neon-runner](https://github.com/drsamonline/neon-runner), and two things adopted from it.** - **The next frame is scheduled before any work runs.** neon-runner has always done this; it's a stronger guarantee than scheduling afterwards, because the following frame is booked even if the error guard itself fails. - **Pad opacity**: a `FADE` button in the pad editor cycles 100% → 70% → 45%, so the on-screen controls can stop covering the play area. The audit also confirmed what neon-runner does *not* need: it has no undefined-variable bugs (the class that froze Eon for two releases), and it already wraps text by measured width. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.6.1 **Cutscene and perk text now stays inside its panel.** Text was wrapped by *character count*, which is only correct for one font size in one panel width — on a 220 px portrait view a 26-character line is wider than the dialogue column, so it ran past the panel edge. Both now wrap by measured pixels. The cutscene panel is also anchored inside the play band rather than straddling into the letterboxed ground, and the three perk cards **stack full width on a phone** instead of being squeezed into ~49 px columns.
 
## 🆕 What's new in 4.6 **A HUD that reads, and pickups that show what they are.** - The HUD is **one panel**, sized to its own content: hearts, power gauge, grenades, lives and the weapon, instead of five things scattered across three corners — with the weapon chip no longer clipped against the bottom edge. - **Lives and combo used to both render as `X2`.** Lives now has its own glyph and row. - **Pickups have icons**: a rifle silhouette, a diverging fan for spread, three stacked rounds for machine, a sparked beam for laser, a teardrop for flame — and each box takes the weapon's colour, so it says which gun before you read anything. - Hearts are solid rather than thin outlines; foreground silhouettes are a tint with a rim instead of 82% black shapes that read as holes in the ground; the boss bar no longer overflows the portrait view. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.5.1 **Hotfix — the game froze the first time you got hit.** `playerHurt` referenced a variable that didn't exist (a mistake from the AEGIS perk in 4.4), so the first hit threw, and the throw killed the animation loop: a permanent freeze on the last rendered frame. Fixed. Two structural changes came out of the audit: **the animation loop can no longer die** — the whole frame is wrapped and the next frame is always scheduled, so any future error costs one frame instead of the game — and **endless mode no longer opens on the campaign cutscene**, which had been stopping the first wave from spawning. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.5 **LAN co-op.** Two players, same Wi-Fi, no internet, no accounts. ```bash node server.js # prints the address to open on both machines ``` Both players open the printed URL, player one picks **HOST**, player two picks **JOIN**. It runs on [`lan-kit`](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit) (SSE + POST, zero dependencies). It is **lockstep**: both machines run the same seeded simulation and exchange only 9-bit input masks per frame, with a 12-frame delay line. No world state is ever sent — which works because the simulation was already deterministic and the replay system had already proven that masks reproduce a run exactly. Verified with two independent headless browsers against a real host: same frame, same score, same position for both players, frame delta 0. **Honest limits.** In this 2-core sandbox a two-browser session without LAN runs at 30 fps and with LAN at roughly 8–17 fps — lockstep is correct but lossy under CPU and round-trip pressure. I have not been able to measure it on real hardware over a real Wi-Fi LAN, so I can't promise a smooth 60. Pause is disabled in LAN (it would desync) and cutscenes are skipped. ## 🆕 What's new in 4.4 **A perk after every era.** Eight of them, one pick from three, and the run gets shaped by your choices instead of just getting longer.
| Perk | Effect | | :-- | :-- | | **Overcharge** | all weapons hit 25% harder | | **Rapid** | weapons cycle 20% faster | | **Vitality** | +1 max health, and a full heal now | | **Scavenger** | +1 grenade capacity, and 2 in hand | | **Momentum** | the power gauge fills 35% faster | | **Phantom** | dash recovers 35% sooner | | **Aegis** | take 20% less damage | | **Reserve** | +1 life | They stack, they are never offered twice, and they carry across every era — so a run that picked Overcharge three times plays differently from one that took Aegis and Vitality. ## 🆕 Earlier releases - **4.3** — the touch pad layout editor: drag and resize both clusters, remembered per device. - **4.2** — three new bosses: The Drowned Relay, Orbit Wreck, The Last Second. - **4.1** — per-era weather, one jump button, every heading auto-fits the screen. - **4.0** — three more eras, story cutscenes with an in-engine renderer, power gauge and combo, controls rebuilt around auto-fire, a credit roll. - **3.1** — Windows EXE and Android APK built by CI through `app-builder`, a redesigned landing page, a separate demo page. - **3.0** — endless mode: escalating waves, a boss every fifth wave, a rising score multiplier. - **2.8** — auto-fire, on by default on touch, with a wider portrait view. - **2.7** — every menu tappable, pause as a real menu. - **2.6** — rebindable controls, per player, persisted. Full detail for every version is in [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md). ## 🆕 What's new in 2.3 **74% fewer draw operations per frame** — 2,210 down to 573, measured by counting canvas calls rather than trusting a stopwatch. Same pixels, a quarter of the work. - **Ground is baked, not redrawn.** Each stage's floor, speckles and props are rendered once into 1024 px chunks and blitted from there. The live path is still in the file behind `?legacyground=1` so the two can be compared — the baked version matches it to within one pixel on 0.24% of pixels (sub-pixel rounding at chunk edges). - **Text is cached.** Every HUD string used to be drawn as dozens of `fillRect` glyphs each frame; now each unique string is rendered once into a tiny canvas and blitted. That alone was 1,400 of the 2,210 operations. - **Broad-phase bullets** skip enemies they cannot reach before doing box maths. - **A seed you can pin.** `?seed=4242` makes a run reproducible end to end — cosmetic randomness now routes through the seeded stream too, which is the groundwork for replays. - **A frame meter.** `?fps=1` overlays fps, frame ms and entity counts; `?bench=600` times 600 update+render pairs and prints the average into the title bar. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 2.2 **Bosses fight back with three attacks each, on their own clocks** — not one scripted loop.
- **The Warden** now drops **ceiling debris** on your position — three rocks (five in phase 2), each telegraphed for 42 frames by a shadow on the ground and a falling marker line, so you always know exactly where not to stand. - **The Glacier Wraith** summons **swarm darts** on its own timer, separate from its ice-shard fan. Kill them or eat them. - **The Eon Heart** fires **rotating beams** — a 70-frame dashed telegraph, then a live beam that sweeps across the arena for 150 frames. Phase 2 sends two, counter-rotating.
**A weak point that rewards aiming.** The Warden's core takes **double damage** — a body shot does 4, a core shot does 8, with a `CORE` popup when you find it. Bosses are no longer a matter of holding fire at the biggest rectangle on screen. Every hazard is a real entity with its own telegraph, damage box and lifetime, so they work in co-op too and can be dodged with the dash's i-frames. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 2.1 **Two players, one screen.** Press **2** on the title screen. Player one takes the arrows and `Space`/`Z`; player two takes `WASD` and `,` `.` `/` `;` `'`. Two gamepads also work — the second pad becomes player two automatically.
- **Shared camera** frames both players and follows their midpoint. - **Soft leash** — wander too far and you are nudged back toward your partner at 3 px a frame. No teleporting, no rubber-banding snap. - **Revive instead of death.** Go down and you have six seconds; a partner standing close for about a second brings you back at one heart. If nobody reaches you, you bleed out. - **A life is only lost when nobody is left standing** — both down means the run restarts at the last checkpoint together. - Enemies, turrets and bosses all target **whichever commando is nearest**, and contact damage is checked against both. Also in this release: the **brute's shoulder charge** is now telegraphed and on a 150-frame cooldown instead of firing whenever it is close, and **downed players no longer fall through the floor** (they were unreachable, so revive could never trigger). --- ## 🆕 What's new in 2.0 **New verbs.** **Dash** (Shift) with i-frames and a 42-frame cooldown, **melee** (V) — a short arc that finally solves "enemy standing on top of me" — and **grenades** (G), three per life, thrown with an arc, bouncing, five-damage in a 42-pixel radius. All three have touch buttons. **Four new enemy archetypes.** **Sniper** paints a laser sight on you for 42 frames before firing. **Swarm** darts fly straight at you. **Brute** is armoured, heavy and shoulder-charges. **Shielder** carries a front plate that stops your fire dead — you have to flank or jump it. **Telegraphs.** Every shooter now winds up for 16–42 frames before it fires, with a visible cue, so a death is something you could have read. **Hit-stop.** Three frames of frozen world on melee and grenade hits — the world stops, you do not, so a press during the freeze is never swallowed. **Difficulty tiers.** Recruit (6 hearts, 5 lives, half damage), Commando (as before), Eon (2 hearts, 1 life, 1.5× damage taken, tougher enemies). **A settings screen** (O or from pause): difficulty, colour scheme, reduce motion, flash intensity, HUD size, music, sound effects, auto-fire. Every option persists. **Accessibility.** Three colour schemes including deuteranopia and high contrast, which recolour hostile fire — the thing that actually matters in a bullet-hell moment. Reduce-motion kills shake, flashes and scanlines. Flash intensity is a slider, for photosensitivity. **Local leaderboard and lifetime stats** — top five runs on the title screen, runs/kills/time kept in `localStorage`. **Installable.** A service worker and manifest ship alongside the game: install it once and it launches with the network off. Sharp pixels on retina via a DPR-aware backbuffer, plus fullscreen (F) and a screen Wake Lock while you play. --- ## 📱 On a phone
  
**The canvas fills 100% of the screen in both orientations**, measured at 390×844, 360×640, 412×915, 768×1024, 844×390, 640×360 and 1440×810. Landscape keeps the 16:9-to-21:9 view and fills the screen edge to edge. Portrait switches to a **square logical view (270×270)** — a 16:9 band on a phone held upright is only a quarter of the screen and the sprites end up tiny. The canvas then takes the full screen height, the play area sits at the top where your eyes are, the earth continues below it with strata and grit, and the thumb pads overlay that lower band so nothing is wasted. The play area is 78% larger than it was in 1.2 (219 px tall → 390 px on an iPhone), and the title and settings screens reflow for the narrow view instead of overflowing. If you want the widest possible view, rotate: landscape shows 584 world pixels of width against portrait's 270. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 1.2 - **Phone support, properly.** The canvas is now `position:fixed; inset:0` and owns the viewport. On a 390×844 phone the game used to be a 215-pixel band floating in page padding with a desktop keyboard hint beneath it; it now fills the screen in landscape and lays out as band-plus-thumbs in portrait. - **Pause moved out of the play area** — bottom centre in landscape, a thin strip at the top in portrait, so it never covers the game. - **Visual-viewport sizing** — the layout listens to `visualViewport` resize and scroll, so the address bar collapsing no longer leaves the game mis-scaled. - **Whole-number scale snapping** when it costs less than 12% size, for crisper pixels. - Desktop keyboard hint now fades after nine seconds instead of sitting over the game. --- ## 🆕 What's new in 1.1 - **Curved, hand-drawn sprites.** Every character was rebuilt from stacked rectangles into rounded caps, arcs, ellipses and bezier limbs — helmets, visors, shoulders, knees and boots all have real silhouettes now, while the game stays pixel-pure on the 480×270 grid. - **Enemy variation.** One rig, many looks: each era reskins the same enemy silhouette (ember → frost → core), spawns get ±6% scale jitter, and roughly one in eight is an **elite** in gold with ~1.8× health. - **Widescreen.** The logical viewport follows your window's aspect ratio from 16:9 up to 21:9, so ultrawide and 16:10 screens fill properly instead of letterboxing. Boss arenas keep a fixed 16:9 footprint and the camera centres them, so a wide screen sees the walls rather than the void. - **Readability pass.** Enemy bullets got dark rims, glow and motion trails; screen-edge arrows point at enemies you cannot see; the background dims 18% during boss fights. - **Better feel.** Corner correction — you now slide around a ledge instead of bonking your head on it — plus rounded platforms and ground edges that no longer read as knife cuts. --- ## Contents - [Play it](#-play-it) — **[live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/eon-commando/play/)** - [Screenshots](#-screenshots) - [Why it is interesting](#-why-it-is-interesting) - [Controls](#-controls) - [The three eras](#-the-three-eras) - [Weapons](#-weapons) - [Enemies and bosses](#-enemies-and-bosses) - [How it works](#-how-it-works) - [Project layout](#-project-layout) - [Build and test](#-build-and-test) - [Roadmap](#-roadmap) - [License](#-license) --- ## ✨ Why it is interesting - **One file, no network.** `index.html` is the game. No CDN, no fetch, no `localStorage` requirement — high scores simply save if storage is available. - **No assets at all.** Every sprite is drawn from rectangles and paths at runtime. Every sound is synthesised from oscillators and noise buffers. The HUD font is a 5×7 bitmap defined as strings. - **Manual fire, classic rules.** No auto-aim, no regenerating health. Four hearts, three lives, and you lose your weapon when you die — back to the rifle. - **Coyote time and jump buffering.** Six frames of coyote time, seven of buffered input, variable jump height. It feels like a 16-bit game, not a web demo. - **Three stages, three bosses, two phases each.** Half health changes the fight: wider spreads, summoned drones, faster spirals. - **Fixed 60 Hz simulation.** An accumulator drives physics, so a 144 Hz monitor does not make the commando run faster. - **Touch and keyboard, same code.** On-screen pads appear only on touch devices; gamepads work through the Gamepad API. --- ## 🎮 Controls | Action | Keyboard | Touch | Gamepad | | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | | Move | `←` `→` / `A` `D` | Left D-pad | D-pad / left stick | | Aim up | `↑` / `W` | D-pad up | D-pad up | | Aim down (mid-air) | `↓` / `S` | D-pad down | D-pad down | | Duck | `↓` while standing | D-pad down | D-pad down | | Jump | `Space` `X` `K` | **A** | A / cross | | Fire | `Z` `J` `Ctrl` | **B** | X / square | | Dash | `Shift` `L` | **»** | RB / R1 | | Melee | `V` `C` | **M** | X / square | | Grenade | `G` `B` | **G** | B / circle | | Settings | `O` | from pause | — | | Daily run | `D` (title) | — | — | | Unleash | `E` | ⚡ (when ready) | Y / LB | | Jump (auto-fire on) | `↑` or `Space` | ▲ | A | | Duck (auto-fire on) | `↓` | ▼ | down | | Rebind keys | `O` → Controls | — | — | | Watch last run | `R` (title) | — | — | | Fullscreen | `F` | — | — | | Pause / menu | `P` `Esc` | ❙❙ button | Start | | **Player 2** | `WASD` + `,` `.` `/` `;` `'` | — | second pad | | Mute | `M` | — | — | Hold jump for the full arc, tap it for a short hop. Always with you, always reliable. | | **SPREAD** | slow | 1 ×3 | Three pellets in a fan. | | **MACHINE** | very fast | 1 | Jittery, forgiving, melts anything static. | | **LASER** | slow | 3 | Punches through three targets. | | **FLAME** | fastest | 1 | Short reach, wide cloud, burns through crowds. | Pickups float in capsules: **weapons**, **repair** (2 hearts) and **Eon shards** (+500). A fatal hit drops you back to the rifle — the classic run-and-gun tax. --- ## 👾 Enemies and bosses | Enemy | Behaviour | | :-- | :-- | | **Grunt** | Patrols, stops to shoot, reverses at ledges | | **Runner** | Charges when it sees you, leaps the gaps | | **Drone** | Hovers on a sine wave, drifts over your head, drops bombs | | **Turret** | Fixed, tracks you, fires aimed shots | | **Jumper** | Hops toward you, shoots mid-leap | | Boss | Phase 1 | Phase 2 (below half health) | | :-- | :-- | :-- | | **The Warden** | Walks the arena, 3-way spread, ground shockwave | 5-way spread, faster cadence, quicker stomps | | **Glacier Wraith** | Flies, aimed bursts, fan of ice shards | Calls in drones, wider shard fan | | **The Eon Heart** | Four-armed spiral, aimed volley | Six-armed spiral, faster, summons runners | --- ## ⚙ How it works | System | Implementation | | :-- | :-- | | **Loop** | Fixed 1/60 s step with an accumulator; render once per animation frame | | **Rendering** | One 480×270 canvas, integer-scaled with `image-rendering: pixelated` | | **Art** | Rectangles and paths — the commando, enemies, bosses, skylines, props | | **Text** | A 5×7 bitmap font defined as `#`/`.` strings, drawn pixel by pixel | | **Audio** | Web Audio: square/saw/triangle oscillators, noise buffers, a look-ahead sequencer | | **Music** | Per-era tracks — bass, lead and noise drums — scheduled against the audio clock | | **Input** | One action set merged from keyboard, pointer pads and the Gamepad API | | **Camera** | Lerped horizontal follow, clamped to the stage, locked during boss fights | | **Save** | `localStorage` for high score and mute, wrapped so private mode never throws | ### Zero dependencies There is no `package.json` to install, no bundler, no framework, and no asset pipeline. The shipped `index.html` makes **no network requests of any kind** — not for fonts, not for images, not for analytics. Load it once, unplug the network, keep playing. --- ## 🗂 Project layout ``` eon-commando/ ├── index.html ← the game (built, self-contained, ~100 KB) ├── build.py ← src/ → index.html ├── src/ │ ├── 00_head.html ← document, CSS, touch pad markup │ ├── 10_core.js ← constants, maths, storage, URL params │ ├── 20_audio.js ← chiptune synth + the era tracks │ ├── 30_input.js ← keyboard / touch / gamepad, canvas scaling │ ├── 40_art.js ← 5×7 font, the commando, enemies, bosses │ ├── 50_content.js ← weapons, enemy stats, the three stages │ ├── 60_entities.js ← physics, AI, bullets, particles, boss patterns │ ├── 70_game.js ← state machine, stage flow, camera, scoring │ ├── 80_render.js ← parallax eras, world, HUD, screens │ ├── 90_main.js ← canvas setup, fixed-step loop, demo harness │ └── 99_tail.html └── docs/ ← GitHub Pages root ├── index.html ← landing page ├── play/index.html ← the game, served live └── shots/*.png ← screenshots ``` --- ## 🛠 Build and test The build is a concatenation — no toolchain, no dependencies, Python 3 only: ```bash python3 build.py # src/ -> index.html ``` That is the entire build. To check a change without opening a browser, the game exposes a deterministic demo harness through URL parameters: ```bash # 400 simulated frames of era I, then freeze the frame index.html?shot=1&stage=1&demo=400 # drop straight into a boss fight index.html?shot=1&stage=3&warp=2520&demo=320&right=0 ``` `?demo=N` runs N fixed steps with scripted input, `?warp=X` teleports the commando, `?shot=1` strips the page chrome for screenshots, and `?debug=1` writes the game state into the document title. Every screenshot in this README was captured with those flags in headless Chromium. --- ## 🗺 Roadmap ### Shipped - [x] Six eras with distinct palettes, hazards and parallax - [x] Five weapons, nine enemy archetypes, three bosses with second phases and arena hazards - [x] Dash, melee and grenades; hit-stop; attack telegraphs - [x] Chiptune music and sound effects, synthesised at runtime - [x] Keyboard, touch pads and gamepad, with rebindable keys per player - [x] Two-player local co-op with revive - [x] Difficulty tiers, settings, colour schemes, reduce-motion, HUD scaling - [x] Curved sprite art, per-era palettes, scale jitter, elite variants - [x] Widescreen 16:9 → 21:9; portrait fills the screen with a closer view - [x] Readability pass: bullet rims and trails, threat arrows, background dimming - [x] Performance: 573 draw ops/frame, down from 2,210 - [x] Replays (196 chars for 900 frames) and a daily seed - [x] Auto-fire with a ±31° assist, on by default on touch - [x] Installable PWA, offline, zero dependencies ### Next, in order - [x] **Endless mode** — escalating waves, boss every fifth wave, rising multiplier - [x] **Touch pad layout editor** — drag the pads anywhere, resizable, persisted - [x] **Perks between eras** — 8 perks, one pick from three after each era, stacking - [ ] **Android APK / Windows EXE** via [`app-builder`](https://github.com/drsamonline/app-builder) - [ ] **LAN co-op** via [`lan-kit`](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit) (SSE + POST, local host) - [ ] Optional CRT shader toggle --- ## 🤝 Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome.
