# Feather

![Feather opening a comic](docs/assets/app-comic.png) **A read-only document viewer that opens before you blink.** Small, portable, cross-platform, summoned by a keystroke. No editing, no annotation, no cloud, no plugins. One window, one document, nothing else. [![CI](https://github.com/drsamonline/feather/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/feather/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/built%20with-Rust-orange?logo=rust)](https://www.rust-lang.org/) [The plan](docs/plan.html) · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/feather/) · [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)
--- ## Status This repository is at **M0 — the spike**. The engine path is being proven before any window code is written, because the plan's first question is not "does it look good" but "how long does it take to open a document and draw page one". | Piece | State | |---|---| | Format router (extension + magic bytes) | done, tested | | `Document` trait — the contract every format implements | done | | Byte-budgeted LRU tile cache | done, tested | | PDF pipeline (hayro, pure Rust, Apache/MIT) | done — renders real pages | | Image pipeline — one picture, one page | done | | Comic pipeline — CBZ, natural page order | done | | XLSX workbooks — grid, not pages | done | | DOCX documents — read as blocks, reflowed | done, approximate | | PPTX decks — text at the file's own coordinates | done, text only | | ODT / ODS / ODP — OpenDocument, same pipelines | done | | Six Office formats, three pipelines | docx/odt · xlsx/ods · pptx/odp | | PSD — the composite a layered file ends with | done, 8-bit RGB and greyscale | | CBR (RAR comics) | in-process, no helper needed — via the UnRAR decoder, see `LICENSE-UNRAR` | | EPUB pipeline — reflowed text, its own layout engine | done, first cut | | Text and Markdown — same engine, one file | done | | `feather` CLI — `info` and `render` | done — measures the budget | | Scroll model — page geometry, visible range, zoom anchoring | done, tested | | Window — open, fit to width, scroll, zoom, page | done — first light | | Tile cache in the draw path, render thread, stale-work cancellation | done | | Pages as a grid of tiles, with a raster ceiling for huge pages | done | | Session model — tabs, pinning, dedupe, per-tab reading position | done, tested | | Single instance — a second launch becomes a tab, not a window | done | | Tab strip — labels, active chip, click to switch | done | | Multiple windows | next | | Desktop integration — .desktop, registry, MIME candidates | done (Linux, Windows) | | Global shortcut — Ctrl+Alt+F summons the window | done | | Tray icon | deferred — see below | | EPUB, images, comics, Office read mode | later | | Desktop integration — .desktop, registry, MIME candidates | done (Linux, Windows) | | Global shortcut — Ctrl+Alt+F summons the window | done | | Tray icon | deferred — see below | | EPUB, images, comics, Office read mode | later | ## Try it ```sh cargo build --release ./target/release/feather info some.pdf ./target/release/feather render some.pdf 1 -s 2.0 -o page1.png ``` And the window itself: ```sh cargo run --release -p feather-app -- some.pdf ``` | Key | Does | |---|---| | `↓` `↑` / `PgDn` `PgUp` / wheel | scroll | | `←` `→` | previous / next page | | `+` `-` | zoom around the centre of the screen | | `1` | fit to width | | `Home` `End` | first / last page | | `]` `[` | next / previous tab | | drop a file on the window | open it (several files → several tabs) | | click a tab | switch to it | | `Ctrl+Alt+F` (anywhere) | summon the window | | `o` | open a document — the system picker, starting where you were | | `n` | open this document in a window of its own | | drag over text | select it (EPUB today) | | `c` | copy the selection | | `/` | search the document · `Enter` next · `Esc` closes | | `p` | pin or unpin the current tab | | `w` | close the current tab (refused if pinned) | | `Esc` `q` | quit | There is no toolbar. There is nothing on a toolbar. The window never rasterises. A worker thread owns the document and draws pages into a byte-budgeted cache; the window only blits what is already there, so a 400-page PDF scrolls without freezing and a fast flick drops the pages it has already left behind instead of queueing them. Text is selectable where a pipeline can say where the words are — drag to select, `c` to copy. EPUB can; PDF cannot yet, because hayro hands back a page image and extracting positioned words from it is the next piece of work. A viewer that pretends to select in a PDF it cannot read would be worse than one that does not. The tab strip is the only permanent chrome: one chip per document, the active one lit, a pin marked with `*`. Labels are drawn with the system's own sans face — fontdb finds it, fontdue rasterises it — so no font is embedded and the binary does not grow. Latin only for now; a real shaper is its own block. Open a second file while the viewer is running and it becomes a tab in the running window rather than a second window — the first launch owns a loopback port and later launches hand their path to it. Pinned tabs sort left and refuse to close. Tiles are keyed by document as well as page, so two tabs of the same PDF can never share a bitmap. Pages are cut into a grid of 512-pixel tiles, so the cache can evict a corner rather than a page. And a page whose raster would exceed 32 megapixels — a 20,000-pixel scan, a poster-sized vector drawing — is rendered at a lower rung of the zoom ladder and stretched on screen: you lose sharpness, not the process. `render` prints its own timings to stderr: ``` read 1.2 ms · open 0.4 ms · render 38.1 ms · total 39.7 ms page 1 of 412 · 1190×1684 px at 2.00x · 214633 bytes png → page1.png ``` A one-page fixture lives at `tests/fixtures/minimal.pdf`, and CI renders it on every push — so the first green build is proof that the engine works on Windows, Linux and macOS, not a claim in a README. Those four numbers are the project. §8 of the plan sets the ceiling: first page of a 50 MB PDF in under 150 ms, binary under 20 MB, cold start under 300 ms. CI prints the binary size on every push so the number cannot drift quietly. ## The shape of the code ``` crates/ feather-core/ Document trait · format router · tile cache · scroll model · session (zero dependencies) feather-pdf/ PDF pipeline on hayro (pure Rust) feather-image/ still images, CBZ and CBR — the last through UnRAR C++, the only C++ in the tree feather-text/ glyph rasterisation, shared by the window and the pipelines feather-epub/ reflowable text: strip, wrap, paginate (EPUB, Markdown, txt, DOCX) feather-sheet/ workbooks: XLSX read as a grid, one sheet to a page feather-slide/ decks: PPTX slides drawn at their own coordinates feather-cli/ the spike: info + render, with timings feather-app/ the window: winit + softbuffer + two font crates ``` `feather-core` has **zero dependencies** and does not know what a pixel looks like on screen. The UI will hold a `Box` and never match on a file extension again — that single rule is what stops a fourteen-format viewer from becoming fourteen special cases in the window code. Adding a format means one enum variant, one router arm, one `Document` impl, and one line in the `open_document` factory. Nothing else in the tree changes — `feather-image` was added to prove it, and the window did not learn what an image is. ## Why hayro and not MuPDF MuPDF would give more formats in one binary, but it is AGPL — the only such dependency in this estate, and awkward beside a licence whose point is a retained attribution. hayro is Apache/MIT, pure Rust, read-only by design, and cross-compiles to Windows ARM64 without a second machine. The cost is that EPUB reflow is ours to write. §12 of the plan argues this properly. **One exception, stated rather than buried:** `feather-image` compiles RARLAB's UnRAR C++ so that CBR opens without a helper installed. That is the only C in the tree, it means the workspace is no longer pure Rust, and it carries a non-OSI licence — see [LICENSE-UNRAR](LICENSE-UNRAR) and [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md). ## Picking up where you left off Close the window and the tabs, their pins and your place in each one come back next time. The file lives where the platform expects — `$XDG_STATE_HOME/feather` on Linux, `%APPDATA%\Feather` on Windows, `Application Support` on macOS — so an application installed read-only can still remember. A document that has since been deleted is dropped quietly rather than stopping the viewer from opening. ## Multiple windows `n` opens the current document in a window of its own, and `feather-viewer --new-window file.pdf` does the same from a shell. That is a second *process*, not a second window in the running one — the window state (surface, viewport, selection, cursor) is owned by the application rather than by a window, so an in-process second window is a refactor of all of it rather than a flag. The trade is explicit: a separate window pays for its own cache and render thread, and its global shortcut registration fails because the first process already holds the key. ## Summoning `Ctrl+Alt+F` from anywhere brings the window up — un-minimised, focused, on top. That is the honest version of "open the document selected in the file manager": no desktop exposes the shell's selection to a third party, so the shortcut raises the viewer and the path can be pasted or dropped into it. On Wayland the registration fails and Feather says so once, rather than silently doing nothing. **The tray icon is deferred, on purpose.** `tray-icon` needs GTK on Linux, which would pull a few hundred megabytes of development libraries into a build that currently needs none — for a status icon. The right Linux answer is a StatusNotifierItem over D-Bus (`ksni`), which is a self-contained piece of work rather than a dependency swap, and it is not in this milestone. ## Roadmap What is released, what is next, and what each thing is waiting on: [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | https://ko-fi.com/matneo | | PayPal | https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN | | Books | https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc | | Everything else | https://drsamonline.github.io/ | | Email | sohilmomin2000@gmail.com | ## Format engines Why Office, slides, PSD and CAD are not in the viewer yet, which of the ArtCraft engines would change that, and what each costs: [docs/format-engines.md](docs/format-engines.md). ## Decisions The choices that were not obvious, and the evidence that settled them — shaping, PDF text, CBR, the tray, in-process windows — live in [docs/decisions.md](docs/decisions.md). ## Your own typeface ```sh FEATHER_FONT=/path/to/YourFont.ttf feather-viewer document.pdf ``` The viewer sets a page in whatever face you name, instead of asking the system for one. A bad path prints what it could not read and falls back to a system face rather than leaving you with a blank page and no explanation. It exists for two reasons: a reader may prefer a different face, and a rendering test needs one fixed face — the same page scored 0% against a baseline rendered on one machine and 14% on another whose fonts differed, which is no way to run a regression check. ## Looking at it without a display ```sh feather-viewer --screenshot out.png document.pdf feather-viewer --screenshot page41.png --page 41 comic.cbr ``` `--page` is 1-based, like every page number a person says. Builds the frame through the same function the window uses — the surface is taken out of the application for the duration of a frame — and writes it as a PNG. No window, no display, so it works in a container. CI renders two screenshots on every push and keeps them as artifacts; a frame that comes out suspiciously small fails the build, because that is what a blank page looks like. ## Download Prebuilt binaries are attached to [releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/feather/releases): Linux x86-64, Windows x86-64 and macOS arm64, each with a SHA-256 beside it. The archives contain the single binary, the licence and this README — there is nothing else to install. ## Registering with the desktop ```sh packaging/linux/install.sh # ~/.local/bin + a .desktop entry ``` ```powershell powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging\windows\install.ps1 ``` Both register Feather as a *candidate* for the formats it can open — PDF, EPUB, CBZ/CBR and images — and neither seizes the default. Choosing the default is the user's job, in their own settings, where they can also undo it. macOS is not automated yet; [packaging/macos/README.md](packaging/macos/README.md) says what a bundle would need and why notarisation is the real blocker. ## Read the plan first [docs/plan.html](docs/plan.html) — sixteen sections: the engine decision, the requirement ledger, the format matrix, Office and ODF in five honest tiers, the ecosystem sweep, the crate picklist, the performance budget, the audit log of what earlier drafts got wrong, and a triage of twenty reference projects. ## Licence MIT. form-kit: # form-kit [![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/form-kit/) [![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/form-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/form-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) **24 form controls for offline apps.** Zero dependencies. One file. The controls every app in this fleet hand-rolls — inputs, selects, a date picker, OTP boxes, uploads, checkboxes, switches, sliders, rating, toggles, colour pickers — with one API and one validation pass. ## Use it ```js var F = require("./form-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.Form var name = F.input({ label: "Name", required: true }); document.body.appendChild(name.wrap); // label + control + help + error line name.value(); // read name.set("Ada"); // write, without firing a change name.on("change", fn); // listen F.bind(name, someSignal); // two-way with a ui-kit signal ``` ## What it does - **Text** — `input`, `textarea`, `password`, `search`, `number` (reads as a number or `null`), `date`, `datePicker` - **Choice** — `select`, `autocomplete` (type to filter, click to pick), `checkbox`, `switch`, `radioGroup`, `slider`, `rate`, `toggleGroup` (single or multiple), `otp` - **Wider** — `calendar` (Monday-first month grid, ISO dates), `upload`, `colorSwatches`, `colorPicker`, `imageSelect`, `editableText`, `hotkey` - **Layout** — `field` wrappers with label, help text, required marker and an error line wired by `aria-describedby`; `group` as a `fieldset`; `submitFooter` - **`F.validate(values, rules)`** — `required`, `min`, `max`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `pattern`, and a custom `validate` that returns `true` or a message. Errors are messages, because the message is what the user has to read - **`F.showErrors(controls, result)`** — paints those messages onto the controls and sets `aria-invalid` - **`F.values(controls)`** — collect a named set of controls into one object - **`F.bind(control, signal)`** — two-way binding to anything callable with `.update()`, so `ui-kit` stays optional rather than a dependency Every control returns the same shape — `el`, `wrap`, `value()`, `set()`, `on()`, `disable()`, `invalid()` — so a form can be built, validated and reset without special-casing any of them. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 108 passed, 0 failed ``` The tests run against a small DOM written inside `test-node.js` (createElement, appendChild, setAttribute, addEventListener, dispatch), so the kit exercises the same code paths in Node that it does in a page. They cover each control's structure and ARIA attributes, value round-trips, change events, the calendar's Monday-first grid and year wrap, OTP focus flow, autocomplete filtering and selection, multi-select toggles, every validation rule, and binding in both directions. ## Consumers None, by design — no app in the fleet is modified by this pass. The measured case for it: date pickers appear in 18 files across 5 sampled apps, checkboxes and switches in 14 files across 5, sliders in 2. frame-kit: # frame-kit [![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/frame-kit/) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) **The shared transfer-frame core for drsamonline apps.** One file, no build step, no dependencies. `optical-kit` moves bytes; `frame-kit` *wraps* them. It is the layer the optical-transfer apps (`helioprism`, `blinkcode-ai`, `BLINKTRANSFER`) were each re-implementing: a self-describing frame, the rateless collector that locks onto a stream, and the byte/checksum helpers underneath. ## What it gives you - **A 22-byte self-describing header** — magic, version, transferId, k, blockSize, totalLength, a payload CRC-32, the symbol id, and a header CRC-16. A receiver can lock onto *any* frame, mid-stream, with no separate header code. - **Strict validation of untrusted input** — a decoded frame is bytes from a camera; a corrupt or crafted header is dropped, not allowed to allocate. - **A rateless `FountainCollector`** — absorbs symbols in any order, tolerates duplicates, restarts when the transfer id changes, and verifies the payload checksum when it assembles. - **Byte/checksum utilities** — CRC-16/CCITT, CRC-32, a seeded PRNG, XOR/concat helpers and size formatting. ## Use it Drop `frame-kit.js` next to your code and load it, then use the global `Frame`: ```html ``` The collector sits over a fountain decoder (the codec lives in `optical-kit`). Pass the decoder factory, or omit it to use `optical-kit`'s decoder if it is loaded: ```js const rx = new Frame.FountainCollector(LTDecoder); // your decoder rx.add(Frame.parse(bytes, { magics: [0xb7] })); rx.progress; // 0..1 rx.assemble(); // Uint8Array, checksum verified — or throws ``` ## API | | | |---|---| | `Frame.pack(opts)` | Build a frame from `{ magic?, transferId, k, blockSize, totalLength, payloadCRC\|checksum, symbolId, data }`. | | `Frame.parse(bytes, opts?)` | Parse and validate; `opts` = `{ magics?, label? }`. Throws on anything malformed. | | `Frame.FountainCollector(Decoder)` | The rateless collector. `.add(frame)`, `.assemble()`, `.complete`, `.progress`, `.received`, `.count`, `.symbols`, `.transferId`, `.magic`, `.reset()`. | | `Frame.crc16`, `Frame.crc32` | CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE and CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3). | | `Frame.createPRNG(seed)` | Mulberry32 seeded PRNG. | | `Frame.xorInto`, `Frame.concatBytes`, `Frame.formatSize`, `Frame.generateUUID`, `Frame.guessType` | The small helpers the apps share. | | `Frame.HEADER_SIZE`, `Frame.VERSION`, `Frame.MAX_CONTAINER`, `Frame.DEFAULT_MAGIC`, `Frame.frameBytes`, `Frame.blockCount` | Frame geometry. | ## Verified `test-node.js` proves the frame, its validation and the collector: ``` node test-node.js ... 19 passed, 0 failed ``` ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # Helioprism ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **One app. Two kinds of light.** Move a file between two devices using only a screen and a camera — no network, no cables, no pairing. Helioprism carries the same rateless frame stream over **two physical transports** and picks the right one for the job. [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-7c3aed)](LICENSE) [![Commercial licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/commercial-licence%20available-22c55e)](COMMERCIAL.md) [![Last commit](https://img.shields.io/github/last-commit/drsamonline/helioprism)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/commits) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/helioprism)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/stargazers) [![Downloads](https://img.shields.io/github/downloads/drsamonline/helioprism/total)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/releases) [![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-06b6d4)](https://drsamonline.github.io/helioprism/play/) **[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/helioprism/play/)**  ·  **[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/helioprism/)**  ·  **[All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/)** **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/releases/latest/download/helioprism-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism/releases/latest/download/helioprism.apk)
--- ## The two transports | | **QR** | **SpectraCode** | |---|---|---| | Physical layer | monochrome QR modules | 36-colour cells, 5 bits each | | Per frame | ~1.4 KB | ~5.1 KB | | Strength | any camera reads it; any scanner reads a tiny file | far more capacity per frame | | Best for | small files, cheap optics, maximum compatibility | larger files | Both carry the **same** frame format and the **same** rateless fountain stream, so a missed frame costs one more symbol rather than a whole loop. The magic byte in each frame says which layer carried it, so the receiver **auto-detects** — point one receiver at either code and it works. ## How it works ``` files ─▶ container ─▶ fountain symbols ─▶ frames ─▶ QR or colour matrix │ files ◀─ container ◀─ collector ◀─ frame ◀─ camera ─┘ ``` - **Selection engine** — auto-picks QR for small payloads and the colour transport for large ones, or you choose. - **Compatibility mode** — a small text file can go out as one plain QR that any third-party scanner reads. - **Offline-first PWA** — installable; after first load it never touches the network. ## Quick start ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/helioprism.git cd helioprism npm install npm run dev # http://localhost:3000 npm test # both transports, end to end npm run build # production bundle into docs/play/ ``` Open the dev URL on both devices (or install the PWA). On one, **Send** and pick files; on the other, **Receive** and point the camera. ## Project layout ``` src/ index.html styles.css main.js sw.js transports/ index.js registry + selection engine qr.js QR transport (monochrome) spectra.js SpectraCode transport (colour) lib/ container.js shared multi-file container fountain.js shared LT fountain codes frame.js shared frame format + collector (per-transport magic) qr/ QR encode (qrcode-generator) / decode (jsQR) spectra/ arithmetic coder, match model, Reed-Solomon, colour matrix, optical decoder workers/ optical decode worker for the colour transport tests/ frame, fountain, selection + both transport loopbacks tools/ build.mjs, dev.mjs, serve.js docs/ landing page + built demo (GitHub Pages) ``` ## Testing ```bash npm test ``` Both transports are tested end to end in Node: files → the transport's real `render()` (into a mock canvas) → pixels → the transport's `decodeFrame()` → collector → files. ## Support | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | ## Licence Helioprism is **free for personal, academic, hobby and non-profit use** under the [PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0](LICENSE). **Commercial use needs a paid licence** — see [COMMERCIAL.md](COMMERCIAL.md). [![License: Free to use, attribution required](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Free%20to%20use,%20attribution%20required-yellowgreen)](LICENSE)

## Repertorium Publicum (2008) — complete, graded


![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)
`repertory/repertorium-publicum-2008/` holds a **complete, fully graded** open
repertory: **74,480 rubrics**, **735,460 remedy links**, **669 remedies**, 41 chapters.

Unlike the `kent-1897/` extraction, every remedy link carries a grade (1–3):

| grade | links |
|---|---|
| 1 | 465,287 |
| 2 | 198,591 |
| 3 | 71,582 |

Sourced from the [OOReP](https://github.com/nondeterministic/oorep) open repertory
database (repertory token `publicum`).

**Please note:** this is *not* Kent's 1897 first edition. It is *Repertorium Publicum*
by Vladimir Polony (2008), a Kent-derived repertory with its own chapter structure
(separate *Clinical*, *Appetite*, *Blood* and *Heart & Circulation* chapters) and its
own additions. It is licensed **GPL v3** as part of the OpenRep source code — not
public domain. See the dataset README for details.

## The Organon, in two editions

`treatise/` holds the *Organon of Medicine* as a **treatise** — numbered paragraphs, no
rubrics, no remedies — in both public-domain English translations:

| file | edition | translation | paragraphs |
|---|---|---|---|
| `organon-6th-1922.json` | sixth (completed 1842) | William Boericke, 1922 | 291 |
| `organon-5th-1849.json` | fifth (1833) | R. E. Dudgeon, 1849 | 294 |

Each paragraph carries its text, its printed footnotes, the source it was read from and
the fraction of its 12-letter sequences found verbatim in OCR scans of **that edition**
(median 0.976 for the sixth, 0.979 for the fifth; floor 0.60). The two are different
books — 74 paragraphs are worded differently and §292–§294 exist only in the fifth — and
they are kept as separate volumes, never merged.

## The public-domain collection

**70 volumes (1847–1932)** — 16 repertories, 6 materia medicas and 40 treatises:
**352,063 repertory rubrics**, **1,429,263 remedy links** of which **751,907 carry a
grade**, 39,770 materia medica symptoms and 5,392 sections of prose, every string verbatim
from its source.

Knerr's 1896 repertory (131,685 rubrics, 43 chapters) and Kent's 1897 are split by chapter
with an `index.json`; Gentry's concordance is split A-Z by concordance keyword, 25 files
plus `index.json`; the rest are single files. Each book carries a QC report under
`data/processed/<slug>/qc_report.md` with its verbatim-fidelity rate.

Two figures worth reading carefully, because they are not what they look like. **Kent's
1897 repertory is entirely ungraded** — 59,114 rubrics and 353,000 links, every grade null
— while the graded links come from Knerr and from Repertorium Publicum. And the totals in
`catalog.json` were recounted from the files themselves on 2026-11-04, having previously
omitted every split volume: remedy links were 613,588 short and rubrics 34,531 short.

# iamsingle.app — directory of single-file web apps

[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-22c55e)](LICENSE)


![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)
A curated, community-submittable catalog of apps that ship as one HTML file:
no install, no build step, no server required to run. Sparked by
[Show HN: Bento](https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49008211) and the
broader "single-file web app" (SFWA) niche (TiddlyWiki, Hyperclay, Decker,
and a growing list of GitHub projects tagged `single-file`).

Name: **iamsingle.app** (pun on "single-file app" / "I am single").

## What's here

```
index.html                          the site itself — build_pages.mjs inlines entries.json/stars.json/sizes.json into
                                     every generated page, so it's self-contained (works over file://, no fetch needed);
                                     falls back to fetching data/*.json if that inline data is ever missing
vercel.json                         rewrites /entry/:slug to index.html for the client-side detail-page router
api/submit.js                       serverless function: POST here to open a submission PR directly
data/entries.json                   the directory's data — never touched directly by a submission PR, see below
data/pending/                       one file per open submission PR — see "How submissions merge without conflicting"
data/stars.json                     GitHub star count + repo creation date snapshot, refreshed daily — not hand-edited
data/sizes.json                     byte size of each entry's live URL response, from scripts/screenshot.mjs — not hand-edited
og/                                 generated per-entry share card (name, stars, size, score over the app's own screenshot),
                                     used as each entry page's og:image/twitter:image — from scripts/screenshot.mjs
assets/favicon.svg, logo.svg         vector source (edit these, not the PNGs)
assets/favicon-16/32/180/512.png     rendered favicon sizes
assets/logo.png                      rendered logo, 720×160
scripts/collect_pending.py          gathers data/pending/*.json into a list for the review scripts
scripts/security_scan.py            heuristic security checks (see below)
scripts/merge_checks.py             writes results into each matching data/pending/*.json as a `checks` array
scripts/promote_pending.py          folds a merged data/pending/*.json file into data/entries.json
scripts/snapshot_stars.py           fetches star counts, writes data/stars.json
scripts/check_hn_featured.py        heuristic Hacker News coverage lookup (see below) — leads only, never auto-applied
.github/workflows/review-submission.yml   wires the review scripts into a manual PR-review flow
.github/workflows/promote-pending.yml     runs promote_pending.py after a submission PR merges
.github/workflows/snapshot-stars.yml      runs snapshot_stars.py daily, plus on every push to main that touches data/entries.json
package.json                        marks this a Node/Vercel project (api/submit.js needs it)
```

## How submissions merge without conflicting

Early on, every submission PR contained a full rewritten copy of
`data/entries.json` (the new entry appended to the end). That meant two
PRs open around the same time would both edit the same lines of the same
file — a textbook git merge conflict, every time, requiring the same
manual fix (rebuild the entry on top of current `main`, force-push,
re-merge) by hand.

Now a submission PR only ever adds one new file, `data/pending/{slug}.json`,
holding just that one entry. Two PRs can never collide, because they're
never editing the same file. The actual fold into `data/entries.json`
happens after a PR merges, via `promote-pending.yml` — it always reads
`data/entries.json` fresh off current `main`, appends the entry, and
deletes the consumed pending file. If two merges land close together, the
workflow's `concurrency` group queues the second run to start only after
the first finishes, so there's no race on the shared file either.

## How the site works

- Static, three files at runtime: `index.html` + `data/entries.json` +
  `data/stars.json`. No backend.
- **Star ranking + GitHub pill**: for entries with a `repo` field, star
  count and repo creation date come from `data/stars.json`
  (`{repo: {"stars": N, "created": "YYYY-MM-DD"}}`), a snapshot refreshed
  daily (and right after any merged submission) by the `snapshot-stars.yml` workflow
  (`scripts/snapshot_stars.py`, authenticated with the default
  `GITHUB_TOKEN` for a 5000/hr rate limit). The site does not call the
  GitHub API live per visitor — that was the original design and it
  doesn't scale past a handful of concurrent visitors sharing an IP. Each
  card shows a small pill with a GitHub icon (links to the repo), the
  star count, and the repo's creation month/year.
- **Sort options**: stars, "date created" (the repo's own GitHub creation
  date, from `data/stars.json`), "date added" (when the entry was added to
  *this* catalog, from each entry's `added` field), or name. `added` is
  stamped automatically by `api/submit.js` at submission time; entries from
  before this field existed keep whatever date was backfilled from git
  history when it was introduced.
- **Submission form**: POSTs directly to `api/submit.js`, which opens the PR
  itself via the GitHub API — see "Submission backend" below. A manual
  "file it as an issue" link is kept as a fallback if the API is down.
- **Featured badge**: an entry with a `featured` field
  (`[{"platform", "url", "title", "points"}]`) shows a badge next to its
  category tags. For `"platform": "Hacker News"` this renders as an
  orange HN-branded pill (Y mark, ▲ point count) linking to the thread;
  `points` is a static snapshot from when the entry was added, not
  live-refreshed — HN scores are effectively frozen once a story ages off
  the front page, so there's no daily-refresh job for this the way there
  is for stars. Other platform values fall back to a plain text badge.
  Nothing sets `featured` automatically — see `scripts/check_hn_featured.py`
  below for how a maintainer finds candidates to confirm.
- **Check badges**: each card shows `passed/total` from the entry's `checks`
  array, if present. Click the badge to expand the itemized pass/fail/skip
  list. Entries with no `checks` (hand-curated, never gone through a PR)
  show no badge — that's intentional, not a bug.
- **Detail pages**: clicking an entry's name goes to `/entry/{slug}` (a
  slugified version of its name) instead of straight to the live demo — a
  client-side view, still rendered by `index.html`, with a bigger header,
  Share/Visit buttons, stat cards (GitHub stars, created date, repo, security
  audit score), and the full checks list. `vercel.json` rewrites any
  `/entry/:slug` request to `index.html` so a hard refresh or a shared link
  works, not just in-app navigation. There's no server-side rendering, so a
  shared link's social-preview card falls back to the generic site-wide
  `og:image`/description, not per-entry content — the page itself renders
  correctly once loaded, this only affects unfurled link previews.

## Submission backend (`api/submit.js`)

A Vercel serverless function. Validates the form POST, then opens a PR
adding one new file under `data/pending/` directly via the GitHub API —
no GitHub account needed on the submitter's end, and no manual
issue→PR conversion by a maintainer. It still reads `data/entries.json`
once, read-only, to reject an obvious duplicate URL before opening the PR.

Needs one env var set on the Vercel project (not committed anywhere):

- **`GITHUB_BOT_TOKEN`** — a fine-grained PAT scoped to *only* this repo,
  with **Contents: write** and **Pull requests: write** permissions. Don't
  reuse a broad personal token here — this one lives in Vercel, not a CI
  job gated by manual review, so it should carry the least privilege that
  still works.

Also enforces a 100/day submission cap (`DAILY_SUBMISSION_CAP` in
`api/submit.js`), counted via GitHub's own PR history — no extra
infrastructure needed. Caps PR/branch spam from a public, unauthenticated
endpoint.

The heavier checks (`security_scan.py`: repo clone, `detect-secrets`,
`semgrep`) are *not* run here — too slow for a synchronous request. Those
still require a maintainer to manually run "Review submission" from the
Actions tab before merging. A honeypot field (`hp`) provides basic bot
resistance on top of the daily cap.

## How the review pipeline works

**Manually triggered** by a maintainer (Actions tab → "Review submission" →
Run workflow, entering the PR number) — not automatic on every incoming PR.
This is deliberate: the script below runs with `contents: write` /
`pull-requests: write`. Automatically checking out an untrusted PR's own
branch and running its scripts with that access is a classic GitHub Actions
"pwn request" — a submission PR could modify `scripts/*.py` itself and
exfiltrate the token. Instead the workflow always runs the scripts from the
base branch, and pulls only the PR's `data/pending/*.json` file(s) as plain
data via `git show` — the PR's own code is never checked out or executed.

Per pending entry:

1. **`collect_pending.py`** — gathers every `data/pending/*.json` file the
   PR added into a single list for the scripts below.
2. **`security_scan.py`** — heuristic only, not a guarantee:
   - if `repo` is set: shallow-clones it, runs `detect-secrets` (leaked
     credentials) and `semgrep` (`p/security-audit`, `p/javascript` rulesets).
     Only `ERROR`-severity semgrep findings that aren't explicitly
     low-confidence fail the check: `p/security-audit` is a high-recall audit
     ruleset meant to surface things for human review, so a raw finding count
     is noise rather than a verdict. Lower-severity hits are still counted in
     the check's detail text, so a noisy entry isn't presented as spotless.
   - always: fetches the live `url` (http/https only; internal/private hosts
     refused, and re-checked on every redirect hop) and regex-tests the raw
     HTML/JS for the literal presence of `eval(`, `new Function(`, decode→eval
     chains, decoded content written into the DOM, `sendBeacon` calls — these
     are presence checks on fetched text, not argument/taint analysis, so a
     `fail` means "found, needs a human look," not "confirmed dangerous"
   - a page over the 20 MB read cap is reported `skip`, never `pass` — a
     truncated body matches no patterns and would otherwise be
     indistinguishable from a clean result
   - each test reports `pass` / `fail` / `skip` individually — no prose summary
   - `scripts/test_security_scan.py` covers the above (`python3
     scripts/test_security_scan.py`, stdlib only)
3. **`merge_checks.py`** — writes the results into a `checks` array on the
   matching pending file (matched by `url`, not `name`, which isn't unique)
   and rewrites that `data/pending/*.json` file in place — never
   `data/entries.json` directly, see "How submissions merge without
   conflicting" above.
4. **`check_hn_featured.py`** — searches HN's free Algolia API
   (`hn.algolia.com/api`, no auth) for stories matching the entry's
   repo/URL/name. Common project names produce false positives (e.g.
   searching "Bento" also surfaces an unrelated Steam Deck keyboard), so
   results are only ever *candidates* in the PR comment — nothing writes
   to the entry's `featured` field automatically. A maintainer confirms a
   real match and adds it by hand.
5. The workflow commits and tries to push that change back to the PR branch
   — this only works for PRs from branches in this repo; `GITHUB_TOKEN` can't
   push to a fork's branch, so fork PRs rely on the PR comment instead.
6. A PR comment posts the same pass/fail list per entry, plus any HN
   candidates, for reviewers who don't want to open the diff.
7. Once the PR merges, `promote-pending.yml` folds the (now checks-annotated)
   pending file into `data/entries.json` and deletes it — see above.

### Known limitations worth reviewing

- `security_scan.py`'s pattern tests are regex-based and will miss anything
  even lightly obfuscated. Treat every `pass` as "nothing obvious found,"
  not "verified safe." `semgrep`/`detect-secrets` versions aren't pinned in
  the workflow — consider pinning once this is stable, so results don't
  shift silently on a tool update.
- GitHub's unauthenticated API rate limit (60/hr/IP) applies to the live
  star-ranking calls from visitors' browsers. Fine at current scale.
- The SSRF guard re-checks every redirect hop, but it validates a host by
  resolving it and then reconnects by name — so a DNS record that changes
  between those two steps (rebinding) could still slip through. Closing that
  means pinning the connection to the validated IP, which `urllib` can't
  express without reimplementing TLS hostname verification.
- Nothing re-scans an entry *automatically* after its PR merges. A live URL is
  checked once and never again, so a project that fixes its dependencies keeps
  its old verdict until someone asks for a re-check:

      node scripts/screenshot.mjs --refresh <slug>[,<slug>]   # re-measure some
      node scripts/screenshot.mjs --refresh-all               # re-measure everything

  That re-does the screenshot, size, QR eligibility and network profile for
  those entries, then `build_pages.mjs` regenerates their badges. A scheduled
  version still wants a guard against a network blip flipping a certified
  entry to failed — see the note on downgrades below.
- There's no check for whether an app phones home. `sendBeacon` is
  pattern-matched, but `fetch(`/`XMLHttpRequest`/WebSockets/remote
  `<script src>` are not, and regex is the wrong instrument for it anyway —
  intercepting requests in the headless browser that already loads every
  entry (`scripts/screenshot.mjs`) would be both more accurate and a more
  meaningful badge than anything in the current set.

## If you rename the site

Update in one pass:
- `<title>` and `.kicker` / `<h1>` text in `index.html`
- the wordmark text in `assets/logo.svg` (re-render `logo.png` after editing)
- `OWNER`/`REPO` constants at the top of `api/submit.js`, and the fallback
  issue link in `index.html`'s submit-section, if the repo name changes too

## Deploying

Needs Vercel (or another host that runs `api/*.js` as serverless functions)
— `api/submit.js` means this is no longer a pure static site. Set
`GITHUB_BOT_TOKEN` as a project env var (see "Submission backend" above)
before the submission form will work; the catalog itself renders fine
without it.

lan-kit: # lan-kit [![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/lan-kit/) [![test](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lan-kit/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE) **The shared LAN core for drsamonline apps.** Zero dependencies. A local room with a real-time channel, for apps that run on a Wi-Fi network with **no internet**. The transport behind the LAN apps (`Chalk`, `Canteen`, `Blackboard`, `Rally`) — extracted from `HMS` so it isn't re-implemented per app. ## Why SSE + POST (not WebSocket) A WebSocket needs a framing library. Server-Sent Events and plain POST are built into every browser and Node, so a room needs **no dependencies at all**: - **server → clients:** `GET /events` (SSE) - **clients → server:** `POST /send` - **health:** `GET /health` ## Use it **Host (Node, zero deps):** ```js const { createHost } = require("./lan-host.js"); const host = createHost({ room: "canteen", app: "canteen", pin: "4821", history: 50 }); const port = await host.listen(0); // 0 = any free port host.onMessage((m, board) => console.log("got", m, "on", board)); host.broadcast({ hello: "room" }); // everyone host.broadcast({ line: "x" }, "board-2"); // one board host.snapshot("board-2", { doc: [] }); // catch a joiner up ``` **Client (browser):** ```js const c = Lan.client({ url: Lan.hostUrl(8080), board: "main", // optional: which board to join pin: "4821", // optional: the room's PIN onOpen: h => console.log("joined", h.room), onSnapshot: s => console.log("caught up", s.doc), onMessage: m => console.log("got", m) }); c.send({ from: "me", text: "hello room" }); c.send("a bare string is a message too"); ``` `Lan.roomCode()` makes a short code (no 0/O/1/I/L); `Lan.hostUrl(port)` builds the URL for the current LAN (and still works from `file://`, where there is no hostname); `Lan.health(url)` asks a host who it is; `Lan.scan()` looks for rooms on the subnet. ### Boards A client that names a board hears **that board plus the room-wide messages**. A client that names none hears everything — which is what every app already got, so nothing that worked before changes behaviour. `board` is routing, not content: it is stripped from the message before broadcast. ### The PIN Set `pin` on the host and every `POST /send` must carry it or it is refused with `403 {"ok":false,"error":"pin"}`. The client sends it automatically when given one. **The PIN never reaches the room.** It rides on every POST, so the host deletes it from the message before broadcasting — otherwise the secret is published to exactly the people it was meant to keep out. `/health` reports `pin: true` or `false`, never the value. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 42 passed, 0 failed ``` Covers the transport (listen, SSE connect, client count, POST broadcast, the hello event, the observer callback, the health endpoint, a clean close), boards (a message reaches its own board, not another, and reaches a client that named none), snapshots, the PIN (refused without it, refused with the wrong one, accepted with the right one, **and never broadcast**), and the client against a stubbed browser (a bare string becomes a text message, an object is sent as it is, the pin rides on every POST, `hostUrl` survives `file://`). `Lan.health` and `Lan.scan` are tested against real sockets, including a dead host, which must resolve to `null` rather than throw. The suite is mutation-tested: removing `delete msg.pin` turns 1 red, ignoring the board filter turns 1 red, and removing the pin check turns 4 red. ## What it is not Not a security boundary. The PIN keeps a stranger on the same Wi-Fi out of a room; it is not authentication, it is not encrypted, and it travels in clear text on the POST that carries it (which is why it is stripped before the broadcast, and why the host never echoes it). Anyone who can watch the network can read it. Do not send secrets over a LAN room. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. LEXORA

Layered EXact-text Repository & Adaptive compression architecture
Canonicalize text conservatively, then compress it with guaranteed byte-exact recovery — decode(encode(C)) == C for every input.

--- > **Project status: Phase 1 prototype in development.** Documentation (Batches A–E) complete/drafted; > early implementation code exists (canonicalization, Zstd core baseline, `.lxz` v0 container, benchmark harness, > CLI app, experimental PySide6 GUI milestones M1–M3). > Nothing here is a shipped or released feature. See [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) for the verified state. > **Badge honesty note:** the CI badge reflects the real workflow in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, but > **GitHub Actions runs are paused by owner decision 2026-10-17** (free-tier minutes exhausted; OQ-15) — > the badge shows the last historical run, not current state; verification gate is local (`pytest -q` + linkcheck > before every commit). The *Tests* badge is a > static snapshot of the locally verified suite (101 passed, re-verified 2026-10-17), not a live measurement. > **Last verified:** 2026-10-17 against the current working branch (see git history). --- ## What is LEXORA? LEXORA is a text-cleaning and **exact-compression** system for document collections (TXT, PDF, optionally OCR'd scans). It: 1. **Ingests** TXT and PDF files (OCR optional for scanned pages). 2. **Canonicalizes** the extracted text conservatively into deterministic UTF-8 bytes (this step *may* be lossy relative to the source, by design). 3. **Compresses** those canonical bytes with **guaranteed byte-exact recovery**: `decode(encode(C)) == C` for every input. The core invariant: **canonicalization may lose information relative to the original source; compression after canonicalization must never lose a single byte.** ## Why? Generic compressors (Zstandard, XZ, Brotli) treat text as opaque bytes. Document collections contain structure — repeated boilerplate, templates, records, multilingual text (English, Hindi, Gujarati) — that a compressor can exploit if it is allowed to *learn* representations safely. LEXORA's goal is to beat frozen generic baselines on total stored size while preserving strict correctness and running on low-resource hardware (~4 GiB RAM). ## Goals - Byte-exact losslessness after canonicalization — always, provably, via round-trip verification. - Conservative, versioned canonicalization with golden test vectors. - Cost-driven codec/candidate selection: every candidate competes against pinned baselines, and **every serialized byte counts** in the cost model. - Operate within a ~4 GiB RAM budget with bounded, streaming/block-based processing. - Multilingual support: English, Hindi (Devanagari), Gujarati. ## Non-goals (current scope) - Reconstructing original OCR output or source PDF layout bit-for-bit. - Claiming any performance advantage over Zstd/Brotli/XZ/PPMd before reproducible benchmark evidence exists (**no LEXORA-vs-baseline evidence exists**; the only published numbers, Revision R1, are baseline-vs-baseline on a Tier-1 smoke corpus — see [docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md](docs/BENCHMARK_RESULTS.md)). - Being a general-purpose archive format. ## Features by maturity | Status | Capability | |---|---| | **Implemented** | Conservative canonicalizer (`src/lexora/canonicalize.py`), Zstd core baseline (`src/lexora/zstd_core.py`), `.lxz` v0 container (`src/lexora/container.py`, ADR-0007), **nine CLI verbs** (`canon`/`zround`/`pipe`/`pack`/`unpack`/`verify`/`inspect`/`batch`/`doctor` — see [docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md](docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md)), benchmark harness (`benchmarks/harness.py` + `corpus.py`, reproducible per [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md)), test suite (**492 passed, 1 skipped**, verified 2026-10-29). **Every core path streams** — encode, decode and canonicalization are flat in document size (measured: 126 MiB / 35 MiB / 35 MiB peak) | | **In progress** | GUI milestones M1–M3 landed & offscreen-tested but **not released**; ADR-0011 decided the GUI becomes a *client of the CLI* (process separation) and that implementation has not started — it needs a Qt-capable machine. Corpus **meets** the ≥1 GiB benchmark requirement (2395 files / 1.054 GiB, OQ-8); what is missing is a protocol-scope run and owner sign-off. GitHub Actions paused by owner (OQ-15) — local gate is `pytest -q` + linkcheck | | **Planned** | TXT/PDF ingestion; experimental candidates (dictionaries, Re-Pair, bounded token PPM, numeric/record coding, template+residual); `.lxdb` database mode; optional encryption profile; GUI stretch items (batch queue, drag-and-drop, shortcuts) | ## Architecture overview (proposed) ``` TXT/PDF ──▶ Extraction (optional OCR) ──▶ Canonicalization (versioned, deterministic) ──▶ Compression (byte-exact, cost-selected codec) ──▶ .lxz archive (.lxdb later) ◀── decode ◀── verify: decode(encode(C)) == C enforced at build time ``` A normative specification (`docs/SPECIFICATION.md`) and detailed architecture documents exist as drafts (Batch B). To contribute, see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md); the release process is documented in `docs/RELEASE_PROCESS.md` (no releases exist yet). ## Supported inputs & current limitations - **Design targets:** `.txt` (UTF-8/other encodings), `.pdf` (text-layer first; OCR for scanned pages), scripts: Latin, Devanagari, Gujarati. - **Current reality:** byte-level canonicalization of raw text streams is implemented (rules CAN-R01/R02/R05 of the v0 rule set); TXT/PDF *file ingestion* is not implemented yet. Build scope is English-only per owner directive 2026-10-16 (Hindi/Gujarati deferred, not blocking). ## Installation / Quick start Install from a source checkout (no published package exists): ```bash pip install -e . # core (Qt-free): zstandard pinned range, Python >=3.12,<4.0 pip install -e ".[dev]" # + pytest for the test suite pip install -e ".[gui]" # + PySide6 for the experimental GUI (opt-in extra, ADR-0008) ``` Then try the CLI — `lexora --help` for the eleven subcommands, all documented in [docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md](docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md): ```bash lexora doctor # install health, incl. a live round-trip self-test printf 'alpha\r\nbeta\r\n' > in.txt lexora canon --in in.txt --out canon.txt lexora pack --in canon.txt --out a.lxz # default zstd level 9 (ADR-0012) lexora verify --in a.lxz # audit: structure + every block's SHA-256 lexora inspect --in a.lxz --verify # readable summary + accounting identity lexora unpack --in a.lxz --out back.txt lexora batch --in DIR --out-dir OUT --op canon # a whole tree, per-file JSON report lexora zdecode --in frame.bin --out back.txt # raw zstd frame, the mirror of zround ``` ### Query it like a database The archive is also a **searchable, compressed store** — SQLite holds the index, lexora holds the compressed text, and only the documents you ask for get decoded: ```bash lexora db init --root myarchive lexora db add --root myarchive --in book.txt --path "books/book.txt" --meta lang=en lexora db add --root myarchive --in paper.pdf --path "papers/paper.pdf" # PDF text layer lexora db add --root myarchive --in scan.pdf --path "scans/scan.pdf" --ocr # scanned lexora db search --root myarchive --query whale --filter lang=en lexora db get --root myarchive "books/book.txt" --out back.txt ``` Measured on 19 Gutenberg books (19.4 MB): payload **6.5 MB** (ratio 0.335), index **7.6 %** of the text, query **0.34 s**, single-document retrieval **0.47 s**. Design and trade-offs: [ADR-0016](docs/ADR/ADR-0016-queryable-archive.md) · usage: [docs/QUERY_ARCHIVE.md](docs/QUERY_ARCHIVE.md). There is a GUI for it: `lexora-gui`, then **Query archive…** in the ribbon. The GUI launcher `lexora-gui` requires the `[gui]` extra and exits 2 with guidance without it. ## Build & test commands Verified in-container (2026-10-29): ```bash python3 -m pytest -q # 492 passed, 1 skipped (~30 s; includes fuzz + interruption suites) QT_QPA_PLATFORM=offscreen python3 -m pytest -q # same, incl. offscreen GUI widget tests (needs pyside6 + libegl1) python3 scripts/linkcheck.py # docs integrity gate — ALL INTERNAL LINKS OK ``` ## Benchmarks **LEXORA has now been measured against both frozen baselines — at smoke scope, not verdict scope.** The acceptance gates are defined in the blueprint (Pass ≥ 10%, Partial ≥ 3% smaller total stored size vs. the best frozen baseline) and formalized in `docs/BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL.md`. R4, three splits, 172 files / 78.6 MiB, 3 reps (draft, awaiting owner review): | system | ratio | |---|---| | `lexora` (shipped default, level 9) | 0.3352 | | `lexora19` | **0.3090** | | `zstd19` (baseline) | 0.3109 | | `xz9` (baseline) | **0.3068** | So the pipeline sits **between** the two baselines: a small, consistent advantage over zstd-19 (167 of 172 files smaller) and a small, consistent deficit against xz-9 (xz wins every file). **Neither is a gate verdict**: the corpus now meets the ≥1 GiB requirement but no protocol-scope run has been done, and the honest reading is in [docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md](docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md). Reproduce it from [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md). ## Security & privacy notes - No security guarantees are claimed and no formal review has been performed. - **What is tested:** deterministic fuzz suites throw truncations, byte flips, end-drops and random blobs at seven reader entry points and assert that every mutant either decodes to the original bytes or raises `ContainerError` — never another exception and never a wrong answer; the reader enforces absolute limits (LIM-01/LIM-02) rather than trusting a header's declared caps; the atomic-write guarantee is verified against real SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGKILL. - Design intent: decoders enforce resource limits (bounded blocks, memory caps) to survive hostile archives; sensitive/clinical corpora must not train shared dictionaries by default. - Vulnerability reporting instructions live in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ## Documentation index - [docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md](docs/RELEASE_NOTES.md) — what this unreleased tree contains, its limits, and what a release would need - [benchmarks/README.md](benchmarks/README.md) — reproduce every measurement from a clean checkout - [docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md](docs/R4_SMOKE_DRAFT.md) — LEXORA vs both baselines, and what the numbers do not say - [docs/DEPENDENCY_LICENCE_REVIEW.md](docs/DEPENDENCY_LICENCE_REVIEW.md) — third-party obligations under PolyForm Start at **[docs/index.md](docs/index.md)**. Key entry points: | Document | Purpose | |---|---| | [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) | Current verified project state | | [docs/NEXT_SESSION.md](docs/NEXT_SESSION.md) | Resume card for the next work session | | [docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md](docs/PROJECT_CHARTER.md) | Problem, scope, constraints, success criteria | | [docs/PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md](docs/PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md) | Numbered requirements (`REQ-*`) | | [docs/GLOSSARY.md](docs/GLOSSARY.md) | Terminology | | [docs/DECISIONS.md](docs/DECISIONS.md) | ADR index & open decisions | | [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) | Ground rules, workflow, PR guidance | | [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) | Change history | | [LEXORA_Full_Blueprint_Design_Master_Prompt.md](LEXORA_Full_Blueprint_Design_Master_Prompt.md) | Approved master design blueprint (source of truth) | ## Roadmap (summary) 1. **Phase 0 (complete):** Documentation foundation, canonicalization decisions & test vectors, open conflicts resolved via delegated ADRs. 2. **Phase 1 (current):** Core Zstandard baseline + corpus manifest + benchmark harness — code landed; closure evidence awaiting owner verdict. > A curated list of tools and software that embrace the **local-first** philosophy: your data lives on your device, works offline by default, and syncs only when you choose.

## Why Local-First?

**Local-first** software keeps your data on your own hardware. The network is optional, not required. This means:

- **Privacy** -- Your data never has to leave your device. No third-party servers scanning your notes, files, or conversations.
- **Speed** -- No round-trips to a remote server. Everything loads instantly from local storage.
- **Ownership** -- You control your data. If a company shuts down, your files are still right where you left them.
- **Offline** -- Works on a plane, in a cabin, or anywhere without Wi-Fi. The internet is a feature, not a dependency.

This list collects the best tools that respect these principles -- from note-taking apps and office suites to encryption utilities and developer libraries.

# 🔒 LockHTML ![Screenshot](docs/shot.png) **Turn any file into a PIN-protected document — optionally viewable only once.** AES-256-GCM · PIN-protected · one-time view · cross-platform · offline · nothing leaves your device. [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/drsamonline/lockhtml?style=for-the-badge&logo=github&color=22d3ee&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/stargazers) [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](LICENSE) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/lockhtml?style=for-the-badge&color=22d3ee&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases) [![PyPI](https://img.shields.io/badge/PyPI-not%20published-lightgrey?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml) [![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-Windows%20%7C%20Linux%20%7C%20macOS-22d3ee?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](#) [![CLI + GUI](https://img.shields.io/badge/interface-CLI%20%2B%20GUI-22d3ee?style=for-the-badge&labelColor=0a1024)](#) ### 🌐 [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/lockhtml/)  •  🚀 [Live demo — open the app](https://drsamonline.github.io/lockhtml/play/)  •  🧭 [All projects](https://drsamonline.github.io/) **Download:** [Windows (.exe)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases/latest/download/lockhtml-portable.exe)  ·  [Android (.apk)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml/releases/latest/download/lockhtml.apk)
--- **LockHTML** takes an ordinary file — an HTML page, a PDF, a photo, anything — encrypts it with a key derived from a PIN, and gives you back a single self-contained `.html` file. Anyone who opens it is asked for the PIN; enter it and the document appears. Choose **one-time view** (or a view limit, or an expiry date) and it stops opening once the conditions are met. No server. No accounts. No uploads. The locked file is a normal web page you can email, message or put on a USB stick — and the GUI works **offline** once loaded. ## ✨ Features - 🔐 **Argon2id** (memory-hard) by default, with **PBKDF2-SHA256** as a lighter alternative. - 🔑 **Recipient mode (X25519)** — lock a file to someone's *public key* so only they can open it, with no shared secret; add a PIN on top if you want two factors. - 🕳️ **Hidden volume** — a second PIN that opens entirely different content, so the file has a plausible cover story. - 🎛️ **Auto-calibrated KDF** — `--auto-kdf` times this machine and picks the strongest Argon2id cost that still unlocks quickly. - 🐢 **Constant-memory save** — for large streaming files, decrypt straight to disk chunk-by-chunk (Chromium), instead of building the whole file in memory. - 🔄 **age interop** — read and write ordinary [age](https://age-encryption.org/v1) files (X25519 recipients), so you can open a file the `age` tool encrypted and vice versa. - 🧩 **Shamir secret sharing** — split the key into *n* shares so any *k* holders (and no fewer) can open it. Give five people a share; any three can open it. - 🧂 **Keyfile support** — optionally require a second file in addition to the PIN. - ✍️ **Ed25519 signing** — sign a locked file so recipients can verify it came from you and wasn't altered. - 🎭 **Duress PIN** — a second PIN that opens a harmless decoy document instead. - 👁️ **View limits** — one-time, *N* views, a "do not open before" time, and an expiry time. - 💧 **Watermarking** — overlay recipient-specific text to trace a leaked copy. - 📦 **Any file type** — HTML renders inline; everything else is offered as a download. - 🗂️ **Two containers** — a single self-contained file for documents, or a chunked **streaming bundle** for very large files (video, disk images) at constant memory. See [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md). - 🌐 **Browser GUI** — a single self-contained HTML file, installable as a PWA, fully offline. - 🖥️ **Cross-platform CLI** — one command on Windows, Linux and macOS. - 🔁 **Reversible** — `lockhtml unlock` recovers the original with the PIN. - 🌍 **Localised viewer** — English, हिन्दी and ગુજરાતી unlock screens. - 🧩 **Zero runtime for the recipient** — any modern browser opens a locked file. ## 🚀 Quick start ### GUI (no install) Open the live app → **** — or run it locally with the CLI. Drag in your file, set a PIN, download the locked copy. It works offline after the first load. ### CLI ```bash pip install lockhtml ``` ```bash # Lock one file with a PIN lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 # One-time view, Argon2id, with a watermark lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --one-time --watermark "For A. Sharma" # Expire it and cap the views lockhtml lock plan.pdf --pin 4821 --max-views 3 --expires 2026-12-31T00:00:00Z # Require a keyfile as a second factor lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --keyfile team.key # Sign it so the recipient can verify authenticity lockhtml keygen -o sign.pem lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --sign sign.pem # Lock to a person's public key (no shared secret) lockhtml keygen --type x25519 -o alice.pem # writes alice.pem + alice.pub lockhtml lock report.html --to alice.pub -o report.locked.html lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --key alice.pem # Add a duress PIN that opens a decoy page lockhtml lock report.html --pin 4821 --decoy-pin 0000 # Split the key: 5 shares, any 3 open it lockhtml lock report.html --shares 5:3 lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --shares report.locked.shares.txt # Hide the real file behind a cover, and tune the KDF to this machine lockhtml lock cover.html --pin 4821 --hidden-pin 0000 --hidden-file real.html --auto-kdf lockhtml unlock cover.locked.html --pin 0000 # opens the hidden content # Lock a whole folder lockhtml lock ./contracts --recursive --pin 4821 --outdir ./locked # Read and write standard age files (interoperates with the `age` tool) lockhtml keygen --type age -o key.txt lockhtml age-encrypt report.pdf -r age1abc… lockhtml age-decrypt report.pdf.age -i key.txt -o report.pdf # Large file: streaming container (viewer + sidecar .bin, constant memory) lockhtml lock holiday.mp4 --pin 4821 --stream # Recover the original lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --pin 4821 -o report.html # Open the browser GUI lockhtml gui ``` > **Tip:** share the PIN (and keyfile) over a *different* channel than the file. ## 🖥️ The GUI One self-contained HTML file (`lockhtml/gui/index.html`) — no server, no build step, works offline: - **Lock tab** — drop in any files, set a PIN (or generate a passphrase), and use the advanced panel for the KDF, view limits, expiry, watermark, keyfile and duress PIN. - **Unlock / Verify tab** — open a locked file with its PIN to preview and recover it. Because it's plain HTML + Web Crypto (+ a bundled Argon2 WASM), it runs identically in Chrome, Edge, Firefox, Safari and on Windows, Linux, macOS, Android and iOS. The hosted copy is a **PWA** — installable, and cached for offline use. ## 📸 Screenshots
**The GUI — every option, straight from your browser**

**A locked file asks for the PIN before revealing anything**
## 🔬 How it works 1. Your file is encrypted with **AES-256-GCM**. 2. The key is derived from your PIN with **Argon2id** (or PBKDF2-SHA256) and a random 16-byte salt. 3. If a **keyfile** is used, it is mixed in as a pepper (a post-KDF HMAC), so the PIN alone is not enough. 4. If you **sign**, an Ed25519 signature over the ciphertext is embedded with your public key. 5. The salt, IV and ciphertext are embedded as JSON inside a small *viewer* page. 6. Opening the file runs the viewer, which asks for the PIN and decrypts **in the browser**. The plaintext never leaves the device. ``` locked.html = viewer shell + { kdf, params, salt, iv, AES-256-GCM(ciphertext), limits, watermark, sig } ``` The full format is documented in [`docs/FORMAT.md`](docs/FORMAT.md). The CLI (Python) and the GUI (JavaScript) implement the same format, so files lock and unlock interchangeably across both — enforced by CI on every push. ### 🔑 Recipient mode Instead of a shared PIN you can lock a file to someone's **X25519 public key**, so only the holder of the matching private key can open it. A fresh ephemeral keypair is generated per file, the ECDH secret goes through HKDF-SHA256, and the result encrypts the file with AES-256-GCM. Because the shared secret is already 256 bits of entropy, no slow KDF is applied on top — and you can still layer a PIN (and a keyfile) on top for two factors. It works in the streaming container too. ```bash lockhtml keygen --type x25519 -o alice.pem # private (keep) + alice.pub (hand out) lockhtml lock big.mp4 --to alice.pub --stream ``` ### 🔄 age interop LockHTML reads and writes standard [age](https://age-encryption.org/v1) files, so it interoperates with the `age` tool. Supported: the v1 header and its MAC, `X25519` recipients and identities, the 64 KiB STREAM payload, and multiple recipients per file. Not supported: `scrypt` passphrases, the ML-KEM hybrid and P-256 tagged recipients, and ASCII armor. ```bash lockhtml keygen --type age -o key.txt # an age identity; prints the recipient lockhtml age-encrypt report.pdf -r age1abc… # -> report.pdf.age lockhtml age-decrypt report.pdf.age -i key.txt -o report.pdf ``` age uses ChaCha20-Poly1305, which Web Crypto does not expose, so this is **CLI-only** — the HTML viewer and GUI cannot open age files. Interoperability is verified against the reference implementation in both directions; see [docs/AGE.md](docs/AGE.md). ### 🧩 Shamir secret sharing Split a file's key so that any *k* of *n* holders can open it and no fewer can. A random 32-byte seed is split with Shamir's scheme over **GF(256)**; the seed feeds HKDF-SHA256 to produce the AES key. The shares are written to a `.shares.txt` file that you distribute **separately** — the locked file alone cannot be opened. It works in the streaming container and can be combined with a PIN and a keyfile. ```bash lockhtml lock report.html --shares 5:3 # writes report.locked.html + report.locked.shares.txt lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --shares some-three.txt lockhtml unlock report.locked.html --share --share --share ``` ### 🚀 Launchers (no install needed) The repo ships small launcher scripts that run the CLI straight from the checkout — handy on a machine where you have not `pip install`ed anything: | Platform | CLI | GUI | | --- | --- | --- | | Linux / macOS | `./lockhtml.sh …` (or `sh lockhtml.sh …`) | `./gui.sh` | | Windows | `lockhtml.bat …` | `gui.bat` | They find Python 3.9+, prefer a local `.venv`, check the two dependencies, and give a clear message if something is missing. On Windows the `.bat` files are directly runnable; on Unix, mark them executable once with `chmod +x lockhtml.sh gui.sh` (or just run them through `sh`). ### 🕳️ Hidden volume A locked file can carry more than one payload. The **cover** content opens with the main PIN, and a second PIN opens **hidden** content — different bytes entirely, with no indication in the file that it exists. This is the same idea as the duress PIN, generalised: you can add several hidden slots. ```bash lockhtml lock cover.html --pin 4821 --hidden-pin 0000 --hidden-file real.html ``` A hidden volume is **plausible deniability, not proof of absence**: someone who knows the format can see that extra encrypted slots exist, they just cannot read them. See [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). ### 📦 Containers and size limits The default **embedded** container puts the ciphertext inside the HTML as base64. That is the most convenient form — one file the recipient can just open — but memory use is roughly **3–4× the file size**, so it is comfortable to about 50 MB and breaks somewhere around 250–300 MB (the browser's single-string limit is ~512 MB, and base64 inflates by 33%). For bigger files use `--stream`, which writes the ciphertext to a sidecar `.bin` in fixed-size chunks. Reading and decryption then cost **~O(chunk size)** instead of O(file size), so multi-gigabyte files work. The trade-off is that the recipient receives **two files**. | | Embedded (default) | Streaming (`--stream`) | | --- | --- | --- | | Files the recipient gets | 1 | 2 (`.html` + `.bin`) | | Practical size ceiling | ~250–300 MB | Limited by disk | | Memory to encrypt/decrypt | ~3.7× file size | ~O(chunk size) | | Size overhead | ≈33% (base64) | ≈16 bytes per chunk | Neither mode touches the network — "streaming" here means *memory*, not the internet. Full reasoning, the memory arithmetic and the chunk format are in **[docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md)**. ## 🛡️ Security model — read this **The PIN (and keyfile) gives you real encryption.** Without them the file is unreadable even if someone opens it in a text editor. Wrong PINs are rejected cryptographically (AES-GCM authentication), not by a string comparison. Signatures are verified before the content is shown. **The view limits, watermark and one-time view are browser-enforced deterrents, not server guarantees.** Since there is no server, the view counter lives in the browser's IndexedDB. A determined recipient can copy the file first, use another browser or profile, clear their storage, or screenshot the decrypted page. These features stop casual re-sharing and help you trace a leak; they are not a hard guarantee. **This is not a substitute for end-to-end tools** when the stakes are high (medical records, credentials, legal documents). Once a recipient decrypts, the content is on their screen and in their memory. For genuinely enforced single-view delivery, use a server that deletes the document after the first fetch. | Property | Guarantee | | --- | --- | | Content unreadable without PIN | ✅ Strong (AES-256-GCM + Argon2id) | | Content unreadable without the private key | ✅ Strong (X25519 + HKDF) | | Content unreadable with fewer than k shares | ✅ Strong (Shamir over GF(256)) | | Wrong PIN rejected | ✅ Strong (authenticated encryption) | | Keyfile required as a second factor | ✅ Strong (pepper) | | Authenticity (sender identity) | ✅ Strong when signed (Ed25519) | | Works offline / no upload | ✅ Yes | | Truly view-once / expiry | ⚠️ Best-effort (client-side) | | Survives a determined recipient | ❌ No | See [`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md) and the self-audit in [`docs/AUDIT.md`](docs/AUDIT.md). ## 📂 Project layout ``` lockhtml/ ├── lockhtml/ │ ├── core.py # crypto + payload format v2 │ ├── cli.py # command-line interface │ ├── templates/ │ │ ├── viewer.src.html # viewer source (generated files below) │ │ ├── viewer.html # PBKDF2-only viewer (small) │ │ └── viewer-argon2.html # viewer with Argon2id WASM inlined │ └── gui/ │ ├── app.html # GUI source │ ├── index.html # generated, self-contained GUI │ ├── manifest.webmanifest, sw.js, icon.svg # PWA ├── tools/ │ ├── build.py # builds the viewer variants + GUI │ ├── minify.mjs # minifies the generated assets │ ├── check_gui_compat.mjs # cross-implementation check (run in CI) │ ├── e2e_fixtures.py # builds fixtures for the browser test │ ├── e2e_browser.mjs # end-to-end browser test (embedded + streaming) │ ├── e2e_gui.mjs # locks files with the GUI code path │ └── e2e_gui_verify.py # verifies those with the Python core ├── docs/ # design notes, format spec, audit ├── tests/ # crypto + CLI tests ├── examples/ # sample.html and its locked twin └── .github/workflows/ # CI + GitHub Pages deploy ``` ## 🤝 Contributing Issues and pull requests are welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). Planned work lives in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md). ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/lockhtml cd lockhtml pip install -e ".[dev]" npm install # build tooling: minifier + Argon2 WASM make test # run the test suite make build # regenerate + minify the GUI and viewers ``` ## 📜 License [PolyForm Noncommercial](LICENSE) © Dr Sohil Momin
Built for the web. Runs on any OS. Nothing leaves your device.
