# Lofi Studio Pro **A lofi beat machine that runs entirely in your browser.** Six tracks, sixteen steps, nine ambience layers and a live tape chain — all synthesised on the fly, no samples, no account, no server. [**▶ Open the app**](https://drsamonline.github.io/lofi-studio-pro/) · [Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/lofi-studio-pro/landing.html) · [Report a bug](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/issues) [![Licence](https://img.shields.io/badge/licence-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-4c6ef5)](LICENSE) [![Version](https://img.shields.io/badge/version-2.10.0-e94560)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/releases) [![PWA](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-installable%20%C2%B7%20offline-5a0fc8)](manifest.webmanifest) [![Tests](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/actions/workflows/tests.yml) [![139 browser checks](https://img.shields.io/badge/browser%20checks-139%20passing-2ea44f)](docs/TEST-REPORT.md) [![Build](https://img.shields.io/badge/build-none%20required-informational)](.) [![No trackers](https://img.shields.io/badge/trackers-zero-brightgreen)](.)
--- ## What it is Open the page, press play, and you have a beat. Tap pads to change the pattern, drag the tempo, roll the tape chain until it sounds like a dusty cassette. Every kick, hat and chord is generated by an oscillator in your browser — nothing is downloaded or streamed, and after the first visit the whole thing works with the network switched off. It was built for the ninety seconds between two tasks: no login, no library, no "start a project". One screen, one sound, immediate. ## Features **Sequencer** — six tracks (kick, snare, hat, bass, keys, melody) across sixteen steps, with ten ready patterns, twelve four-bar chord progressions, swing from straight to lazy, and an optional snare fill every fourth bar. Tap a pad to switch it on, **hold it** to cycle normal → accent → ghost, **drag** across a row to draw a run. Hold a track name to empty that row. Tap a track name to mute it; the mixer has per-track faders and solo. **Tape chain** — low-pass filter, tape saturation, vinyl crackle, reverb, chorus and wow-and-flutter, all live while the beat runs. **Ambience** — nine procedurally generated layers (rain, fireplace, cafe, wind, birds, thunder, ocean, night, vinyl), each with its own volume, mixable on their own without a beat. **Ten themes** — from a near-black studio to a paper-white daytime mode, all driven by CSS custom properties so the swap is instant. **Recording** — hit the record button to capture a take as a downloadable audio file, with an optional metronome and a one-bar count-in. **Chance** — press *Chance* in the sequencer header and each step gains a probability: always, 75 %, 50 %, 25 %. A step that is on can still skip, which is where a loop starts to breathe. **Song mode** — four slots, two bars each. Capture a pattern into A, another into B, flip the toggle and the sequencer walks A → B → C → D, swapping the pattern and its chords at the bar line. While a slot plays it is the live pattern, so edits mid-song land in that slot. **Undo** — every edit is undoable, and a drag across twelve pads is one undo, not twelve. `Ctrl/⌘ Z`, or the button in the sequencer header. **Presets and files** — name a beat and save it (up to 24), or export it as a `.json` and import it anywhere — by button, or by dropping the file on the window. A preset captures the beat and its sound, never your preferences. **MIDI in and out** — play the voices from a keyboard or pad controller, or export four bars as a Standard MIDI File: drums on channel 10, bass/keys/melody on 1–3, chords already voiced, accents as velocities. It opens in a DAW with the parts separated. **Installable and offline** — a service worker precaches the shell, Tone.js included, so the app opens from the home screen with no connection at all. **Honest about your data** — no analytics, no cookies, no network calls after load. Your pattern lives in `localStorage` on your device. ## Quick start **Use it** — open and press play. **Install it** — in Chrome or Edge, use the install button in the top bar (or *Install app* from the address bar). On iPhone, Share → *Add to Home Screen*. **Run it locally** — it is a static site with no build step: ```bash git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro.git cd lofi-studio-pro python3 -m http.server 8000 # open http://localhost:8000 ``` Opening `index.html` straight from disk also works; only the service worker is skipped, because offline caching needs `http://` or `https://`. ## Controls | Action | Keyboard | Touch / mouse | | --- | --- | --- | | Play / stop | `Space` | Play button | | Move around the sequencer | Arrow keys | Tap a pad | | Accent / ghost a step | — | Hold a pad | | Draw a run of steps | — | Drag across a row | | Track menu (clear / copy / paste) | — | Hold a track name | | Mute a track | — | Tap the track name (sequencer) or `M` (mixer) | | Solo a track | — | `S` in the mixer | | Tempo | — | `−` / `+`, or `TAP` four times | | Metronome / count-in | — | Settings | | Undo / redo | `Ctrl/⌘ Z` · `Shift Ctrl/⌘ Z` | Undo button in the sequencer header | | Shortcut list | `?` | Settings → Keyboard shortcuts | | Pan a track | — | Slider under the fader | | Surprise me | `S` | Settings → Roll | | Next theme | `B` | Themes tab | | Record a take | `R` | Record button in the top bar | | Stop everything | `X` | Panic button | | Share the beat | — | Settings → Copy link | | Save / load a preset | — | Settings → My presets | | Export / import a file | — | Settings, or drop a `.json` on the window | | Export MIDI | — | Settings → Export as MIDI | | Song mode | — | Song block: tap a slot to capture, hold to clear | Knobs and faders accept a drag, a scroll wheel, and arrow keys. Double-click a knob to reset it. Hold `Shift` while dragging for fine adjustment. ## What it sounds like, and why The 2.0 engine sounded like noise because it mostly *was* noise: a bare white-noise snare, a white-noise hi-hat through a high-pass, a kick three times louder than everything else, and a reverb wired as an insert — which meant the dry signal never reached the output at all. On top of that, the bass and melody were monophonic and cut their own release on every consecutive sixteenth. 2.1 rebuilds the voice design and the gain staging. Measured on the same four seconds of the same pattern: | | 2.0.0 | 2.1.0 | | --- | --- | --- | | Peak | 0.68 | 0.54 (no clipping) | | Crest factor | 7.9 | 6.9 | | Snare | white noise burst | tuned body + band-limited crack | | Hi-hat | broadband hiss | band-passed tick with a bell | | Reverb | insert — dry signal lost | parallel send | | Bass / melody | monophonic, self-cutting | polyphonic | | Master | limiter only | 2:1 glue compressor → limiter → DC block → fades | The figure is generated from real captures of the running app, not from a mock: the top two traces are the same pattern's output, and the bottom is the spectrum of the same window. The 2.0 trace never returns to silence between hits; the 2.1 trace does. ## Screenshots | Studio | Mixer and tape chain | | --- | --- | | | | | **Ambience** | **Light theme** | | | | | **Song mode** | **Mixer** | | | | | **Settings, presets and files** | **Ambience** | | | |
## Under the hood A static site, split into five plain scripts. No framework, no bundler, no dependencies to install — the only third-party code is Tone.js, vendored in `vendor/`. ``` index.html the app shell: top bar, rail, views, transport css/app.css design tokens per theme, layout, controls js/data.js patterns, chord sets, themes, presets, ambience definitions js/state.js defaults, validation, persistence, migration from v1 js/audio.js the whole synthesis engine: instruments, FX, transport, ambience js/ui.js rendering, knobs, faders, toasts, visualiser js/main.js controller: transport, presets, recording, PWA wiring js/midi.js Standard MIDI File writer sw.js precache + navigation fallback manifest.webmanifest install metadata, icons, shortcuts vendor/tone.min.js Tone.js 15.1.22 (MIT) ``` Signal path: six instrument channels → low-pass → tape → chorus → wow → reverb → master volume → limiter → destination, with the vinyl crackle deliberately tapped in after the low-pass so the pops stay crisp, and a recorder hanging off the limiter. Three decisions worth knowing: - **Nothing blocks the first paint.** Tone.js is fetched on the first gesture, not on load: 107 KB of script before you press play, 448 KB after. The service worker still precaches it, so offline is unchanged. - **Everything is validated at the edge.** `state.js` coerces and clamps every value on load, so a corrupted or half-written save can never reach the audio engine. A save from the old single-file build is migrated automatically. - **Nothing is locked behind a timer.** The transport is guarded by a promise, not a millisecond timeout — the previous version used a 180 ms lock and a 150 ms restart, which silently swallowed every restart. - **The shell ships with its own dependencies.** Tone.js is served from `vendor/`, not a CDN, so a blocked network cannot leave a drawn but silent app. ## Testing 139 browser checks run against the real app in headless Chromium — every transport control, all ten patterns, twelve chord sets, ten themes, nine ambience layers, the six knobs, the faders, per-step velocity, drag-to-paint, hold-to-clear, presets, export and import, link sharing, the sleep timer, the media session, audio headroom, persistence, a corrupted save, migration from v1, recording, offline reload, and the layout at 360 / 390 / 768 / 1280 px. ```bash pip install websocket-client && python3 tests/run_browser_tests.py ``` Results: **[docs/TEST-REPORT.md](docs/TEST-REPORT.md)** — 88 passing, 0 failing. ## Native builds The web app is the source of truth; the wrappers are thin and live in CI, so nothing has to be installed locally and no stale binary is ever committed. | Target | How | Built | | --- | --- | --- | | **Android** | `.github/workflows/android.yml` wraps the static files with Capacitor | `lofi-studio-pro-v2.10.0.apk` (3.8 MB) — debug-signed, so sideload it | | **Windows** | `.github/workflows/windows.yml` wraps the same files with Tauri (WebView2) | `Lofi-Studio-Pro-2.10.0-x64-setup.exe` (2.1 MB) and `.msi` (2.9 MB) | | **PWA** | The live site installs to any home screen | tested — this is the build the 88 browser checks run against | All three are attached to the [latest release](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/releases/latest). Push a tag and CI rebuilds them from that exact commit. The Android build is debug-signed, so it installs from a file but cannot go to the Play Store as-is: add your own keystore as repository secrets and a `signingConfig` to `android/app/build.gradle`. The Windows binaries are unsigned, so SmartScreen will warn on first run. ## Roadmap The next round of ideas — features, offline behaviour, performance, and a short list of things deliberately left out — is in **[ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md)**. The first eight are already shipped in 2.1.0 and marked as such. Every feature in this version is catalogued in **[docs/FUNCTIONS.md](docs/FUNCTIONS.md)**. ## Licence [**PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0**](LICENSE) — free to use, change and share for any noncommercial purpose: personal projects, study, hobby work, teaching, research, charities and public institutions. Commercial use needs a separate licence; [open an issue](https://github.com/drsamonline/lofi-studio-pro/issues) and ask. > Required Notice: Copyright Dr Sohil Momin (https://github.com/drsamonline) If you would rather have a permissive or copyleft licence, the code is yours to relicense only with my permission — but do ask, I usually say yes for MIT. ## Attribution - **[Tone.js](https://tonejs.github.io/)** 14.8.49 — MIT, © Yotam Mann and contributors. The entire sound engine sits on top of it. - **Every sound is synthesised.** No samples, loops, records or third-party audio assets are included, so there is nothing to clear and nothing to credit beyond the library. - **Icons** are drawn in this repository (SVG paths in `js/data.js` and `index.html`), and the PNG app icons are generated from the same shapes. - **Type** is the system UI font stack — no webfont is loaded. - Full detail in **[ATTRIBUTION.md](ATTRIBUTION.md)**. ## Sponsor Lofi Studio Pro is free and stays free for personal use. If it earned a place in your workday: - **[Sponsor on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline)** — one-off or monthly. - **Star the repo** — it genuinely helps other people find it. - **Send a pattern** — open an issue with a screenshot of something good; good presets get shipped in the next release. ## Author **Dr Sohil Momin** — built and maintained by one person, in between other things. # Lumen

[![tests](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/lumen/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![licence](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE)
[![offline](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg)](#offline-enforced)
[![build](docs/assets/badge-build.svg)](#building-it)

**A photo library that never phones home.**

An offline library in the spirit of Picasa. Point it at the folders you already
keep your photos in; it reads them, indexes them, and computes everything else —
thumbnails, edits, faces, albums, duplicates — on your machine.

[Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/lumen/) ·
[Landing page](https://drsamonline.github.io/lumen/) ·
[The rule](#offline-enforced) ·
[Support](#support)

<!-- shot:start -->

![Lumen's LAN gallery: a grid of photos with star ratings, edited badges and a possible-duplicates strip](docs/assets/app-desktop.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

---

## What it does today (v1)

**Library**
- Folder indexing with incremental rescans — a file whose size and mtime are
  unchanged is never re-opened, so rescanning 50,000 photos after adding one
  folder takes seconds.
- Month-grouped timeline grid, exactly Picasa's rhythm, with a thumbnail-size
  slider from 100 to 300 px.
- Sort by capture date, index date or file name.
- Star ratings (0-5) and favourites, both filterable.
- Background folder watching: drop files in and they appear.

**Metadata**
- EXIF read at index time: capture date, camera make/model, ISO, aperture,
  shutter, focal length, GPS, orientation.
- The full details strip in the viewer.
- GPS is captured and stored. There is no map yet (see the roadmap) because
  map tiles are an internet feature and this app does not use the internet.

**Viewer**
- Swipe, pinch-zoom, per-photo details.
- Non-destructive editing: rotate, flip, brightness, contrast, saturation,
  warmth, a real crop tool (corner handles, rule-of-thirds guides, Free / 1:1 /
  4:3 / 3:4 / 3:2 / 16:9 presets), and a **tone curve** with draggable points and
  six presets. Stored as a small JSON recipe in SQLite; the original file is
  never modified.
- Saving an edit also re-renders the cached grid thumbnail, so the tile shows
  what the viewer shows.
- Export an edited copy as a real PNG beside the original.

**Browse**
- Month-grouped timeline with a year scrubber down the right edge — drag it to
  jump to any year, which is the only navigation that works at 10,000 photos.
- Slideshow mode: full screen, auto-advance at 3/5/8/15 s, arrows to step, space
  to pause, Escape to leave. Reachable from the library or from any photo.
- Places: photos grouped by rounded GPS coordinate, largest group first. No map,
  because map tiles are an internet feature — but the browsing people actually
  did with Picasa's Places survives.

**Multi-select**
- Long-press any photo to start selecting; tap to add or remove.
- One action bar for the whole selection: 0-5 stars, favourite / unfavourite,
  add to album, or export as a ZIP.
- Bulk edits run in a single transaction, so rating 400 photos is one write.

**People**
- Manual face tagging: drag a box on a photo, name the person. Face boxes are
  stored as normalised coordinates, so they stay correct at any resolution.

**Albums**
- Virtual albums. A photo can be in many; nothing is copied.

**Search**
- SQLite FTS5 over file name, folder, caption and tags, with a LIKE fallback on
  platforms whose SQLite lacks FTS5.
- Three-stage fallback so a search rarely returns nothing: exact, then substring
  ("each" finds "beach-sunset.jpg"), then typo-tolerant ("reciept" finds
  "receipt.jpg"). The bar says which stage answered, rather than quietly showing
  approximate results as if they were exact.
- Filter chips for favourites and star ratings.

**Image formats**
- Nothing about formats is hardcoded. Every format is a plugin, and the scanner,
  thumbnailer, viewer and LAN server all ask the registry rather than testing a
  suffix — so installing a decoder makes its formats indexable with no code
  change.
- **Built in, always:** JPEG, PNG, WebP (still and animated), GIF, BMP, WBMP.
- **Via open-source decoders, when installed:** HEIC/HEIF/AVIF (libheif,
  libavif), TIFF (libtiff), camera RAW — CR2, CR3, NEF, ARW, DNG, RAF, RW2, ORF,
  PEF and more (LibRaw, darktable), JPEG XL (libjxl), and PSD/TGA/DDS/EXR/HDR
  (ImageMagick).
- Settings shows every plugin, whether it is ready, and exactly what to install
  if it is not. Lumen never downloads or bundles a decoder.
- The LAN gallery transcodes formats a browser cannot paint, so a HEIC photo
  still opens on a TV.

**Duplicates**
- Perceptual fingerprints (64-bit dHash) computed from the thumbnails that
  already exist, so a duplicate scan costs one cheap decode per photo.
- Grouping by 16-bit band lookup, then verified by Hamming distance — no
  all-pairs comparison, so 100,000 photos is still fast.
- Each group marks the copy worth keeping (largest pixel count, then largest
  file) and totals the space the extras use. **Lumen never deletes a photo.**

**Export**
- Album → store-only ZIP, streamed straight to disk, so album size is bounded by
  free space rather than RAM.
- Edited copies are written as PNG, and the written bytes are then **read back**
  and scanned for EXIF, XMP, IPTC, PNG text and time chunks. The snackbar says
  "checked: nothing left" only when that is literally true of the file on disk.

**LAN streaming**
- Turn it on in Settings and any browser on your Wi-Fi can browse the whole
  library at `http://<your-ip>:8421` — a self-contained gallery page, no CDN, no
  fonts to fetch, works with the router's WAN port unplugged.
- A UDP beacon broadcasts the address so a phone can find the desktop.

**Offline, enforced**
- No `http`, no `dio`, no webview, no telemetry. `test/offline_guard_test.dart`
  fails the build if anyone adds an outbound network client.

---

## Borrowed from the rest of the estate

Lumen is the first non-web app in this fleet, but four of its features are
direct ports of ideas already solved elsewhere in it. `CREDITS.md` lists exactly
which repo each came from and what was actually taken.

---

## Building it

You need the Flutter SDK (3.27 or newer — Dart 3.6+).

```bash
cd lumen

# 1. Generate the platform folders (android/, windows/, linux/)
flutter create --platforms=android,windows,linux .

# 2. Fetch packages
flutter pub get

# 3. Run on whichever platform you are sitting in front of
flutter run -d windows      # or: linux
flutter run -d <device-id>  # Android
```

`tool/setup.sh` (Linux) and `tool/setup.ps1` (Windows) do steps 1 and 2 in one
go.

### Shipping builds

```bash
flutter build windows --release
flutter build linux --release
flutter build apk --release --split-per-abi
```

### Android notes

`flutter create` writes a manifest without storage permissions. Lumen needs to
read image files, so add these to `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml`
inside `<manifest>`:

```xml
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_MEDIA_IMAGES"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE"
    android:maxSdkVersion="32"/>
<!-- Required only to bind the local LAN server. No outbound use. -->
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.INTERNET"/>
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE"/>
```

Also set `android:usesCleartextTraffic="true"` on `<application>` — the LAN
gallery is plain HTTP on your own network, and nothing else in the app makes a
request at all.

On first run, tap **Use camera roll** on the setup screen; it adds
`/storage/emulated/0/DCIM`, `Pictures` and `Download` automatically.

---

## Tests

CI runs on every push (`.github/workflows/test.yml`): `flutter analyze`, then
`flutter test`, then three real compiles — Linux desktop, Windows desktop and an
Android APK. That is the evidence behind "one codebase, three platforms" — every
target this project claims is compiled on every push.

Locally:

```bash
flutter test
```

- `test/edit_recipe_test.dart` — the colour-matrix maths, JSON round-trips,
  garbage input.
- `test/db_test.dart` — indexing, paging, filters, FTS search, month buckets,
  albums, edit persistence.
- `test/offline_guard_test.dart` — proves no outbound network client exists.
- `test/format_registry_test.dart` — extension routing, plugin precedence, and
  that every shipped plugin declares its backing library and its requirement.
- `test/hash_test.dart`, `test/fuzzy_test.dart`, `test/zip_test.dart`,
  `test/metadata_check_test.dart` — the v1.1 feature logic.
- `test/crop_math_test.dart`, `test/batch_ops_test.dart`, `test/places_test.dart`
  — v1.3–v1.4 logic.
- `test/tone_curve_test.dart` — LUT generation, monotonicity, overshoot, LUT
  application, and recipe round-tripping.
- `test/scanner_test.dart`, `test/search_fallback_test.dart` — regressions found
  in the v1.4.1 audit.

---

## Where things live

Everything Lumen writes goes under one application-support directory:

```
<app support>/
  lumen.db          SQLite index (photos, albums, people, faces, edits)
  thumbs/           PNG thumbnails, sharded 1000 ids per folder
  exports/          fallback target for exported copies
```

Your photos are never copied, moved or modified.

---

## Headless CLI

The same index and scanner without the interface. Pure Dart, so it compiles to a
single native binary — `lumen-cli-linux-x64` and `lumen-cli-windows-x64.exe` ship
alongside the app in every release.

```
lumen scan [--root DIR]     index the library
lumen stats                 what the index holds
lumen search QUERY          file names, folders, captions, tags
lumen recent [N]            the N most recent photos
lumen compact [--orphans|--all] [--yes]
lumen --help
```

`--json` on `stats`, `search`, `recent` and `compact` gives stable objects, so
anything that can run a process can consume the library:

```bash
lumen search "harbour" --json | jq -r '.photos[].path'
lumen stats --json | jq .photos
```

The CLI and the app share one index file, so either can rescan what the other
indexed. Both need SQLite 3 available to the dynamic loader — present on most
Linux systems; on Windows put `sqlite3.dll` beside the exe.

### Driving it from a launcher

Any tray launcher or hotkey tool that runs a command can reach the library. In
[CLDR](https://github.com/drsamonline/CLDR) that is one line in
`~/.config/cldr/config.toml`:

```toml
alias.photos = "/run lumen search"
```

Then `/photos harbour` in the command window opens the library's index. Note the
honest limit: CLDR spawns a routed command **detached** and does not render its
stdout, so the results do not appear inside its window — use `--json` and pipe it
somewhere, or open the app itself with `alias.lumen = "/run lumen"`.

## Known limitations

- **The LAN gallery streams originals.** Edits appear in the grid thumbnail and
  in the app's viewer, but a browser on the network sees the unedited file at
  full size. Serving a rendered copy would mean a decode per request; it is on
  the roadmap rather than half-done.
- **Apple platforms are not supported**, permanently. See `ROADMAP.md`.

## Honest status

This is a working v1, not a finished Picasa replacement. What is deliberately
missing, and why, is in `ROADMAP.md`. The two you will notice first:

1. **No automatic face detection.** Face boxes are drawn by hand. Real
   detection needs an on-device ML model, which is a milestone of its own.
2. **No maps.** Picasa's geo view needs map tiles; tiles need the internet.
   The plan is bundled offline tiles or a vector basemap, not a network call.
3. **Duplicate *deletion* is not automated.** Lumen groups and ranks; removing
   the extras stays a manual act, because a wrong automatic delete is the one
   mistake a photo library cannot apologise for.
4. **Video files are not indexed.** Photos only, for now.
5. **Exotic formats need a decoder installed.** JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF, BMP and
   WBMP work out of the box; HEIC, TIFF, RAW and JPEG XL need their open-source
   tool on `PATH` (see *Image formats* above). That is deliberate — bundling
   libheif and LibRaw would multiply the binary size and the licence surface.
6. **The external decoders are CLI bindings, not FFI.** That keeps the build
   dependency-free and crash-safe, and it works on Windows and Linux. On
   Android there is no shell, so those formats stay unavailable there until an
   FFI plugin is added — the interface is already shaped for one.

One file. A language model does not send a document — it sends chunks, and half of them end in the middle of a code fence. This renders what is finished and holds back what could still change. ## Use it ```js var Md = require("./markdown-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.Md Md.render("## Hi\n\nSome **bold**."); // HTML string var s = Md.stream(); s.push("## Hi\n\nSome **bo"); // { html, complete: false } s.push("ld** text.\n\n"); // { html, complete: true } s.done(); // render the finished buffer, then reset ``` ## What it does - **CommonMark's core** — ATX headings with ids, paragraphs, hard breaks (two spaces or a backslash), emphasis, strong, strikethrough, inline code, fenced code with a language (``` or ~~~), blockquotes, ordered and unordered lists including nested ones, horizontal rules, links and images - **the GitHub extensions** — tables with per-column alignment, task lists (`- [x]`), and alerts (`> [!NOTE]`, `TIP`, `IMPORTANT`, `WARNING`, `CAUTION`) - **safe by default** — HTML in the source is escaped, never passed through; a `javascript:` link or a `data:` image is rendered as text, not as a link or image - **`Md.stream()`** — `push`, `set`, `html`, `text`, `reset`, `done`. An unterminated code fence renders as code immediately; any other unfinished block renders as text, so a list item is never briefly just a dash - **`Md.blocks(src)`** — the parse tree, if you want to render it yourself - **`Md.scale(opts)`** — the two type scales from the Go source: documents at 16px with headings growing to 2.5×, chat at 14px with headings barely larger, and the heading room curve - **`Md.toDom(src)`** — a guarded DOM helper, `null` in Node The streaming model and both type scales are ported from [lobe-mygo](https://github.com/lobehub/lobe-mygo) `pkg/markdown` (MIT), which delegates parsing to MyGo's own CommonMark renderer. The parser here is written from scratch, because there is nothing to port — the Go side uses a library and the kits cannot have dependencies. ## Verified ``` node test-node.js 92 passed, 0 failed ``` The tests cover every block and inline construct, the sanitiser (a `javascript:` link and a `data:` image are both refused), that markdown inside a fence stays literal, nested lists, alert bodies, table padding for short rows, the heading scale in both variants, and the streaming behaviour that matters: a partial heading is not a heading, half-written emphasis is not bold, an open fence is code, and a trailing blank line is what finalises a block. ## Consumers None, by design — no app in the fleet is modified by this pass. The intended first adopters are the AI-facing apps (SmartNotes, ai-bridge, Matneo), which currently render model output by hand, and that adoption is yours to decide one app at a time. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # ml-kit [![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-2e7d32)](LICENSE) **The classic algorithms, from scratch — for offline features.** tf-idf · Naive Bayes · k-NN · k-means · PCA · ID3 · linear regression · Markov chains · grammar A single file, zero dependencies, no model, no API key, no network.
--- ## THE BOUNDARY — read this first This kit is for **ranking, similarity, clustering and simple trend**. It is **NOT a diagnostic or predictive engine**, and **nothing in it may be used to claim a clinical or medical capability.** Several apps that use this kit are clinical; the algorithms here are generic maths and make no clinical claim. A model that ranks notes, groups similar cases or draws a trend line is not a diagnosis, and must never be presented as one. ## Why from scratch Forge's rule is offline, single-file, zero-dependency — so the usual ML frameworks (TensorFlow, Spark, scikit-learn) are unusable: they are hundreds of megabytes and need a runtime. But the algorithms that actually earn their place offline are the *classic* ones, and each fits in tens of lines. This is the light half of Forge's AI story: **heavy AI uses the user's own key; light AI runs on the device, from scratch.** ## What's in it | Algorithm | For | |---|---| | `tfidf` + `search` | ranked text search (tf-idf weighting, cosine similarity) | | `NaiveBayes` | a tiny bag-of-words classifier (tag a note, categorise an entry) | | `knn` | "items like this one" | | `kmeans` | clustering | | `pca2` | reduce many dimensions to two, for plotting | | `id3` + `predict` | a small, readable rules classifier | | `linearRegression` | a trend line | | `markov` + `generate` | statistical generation from a corpus (char- or word-level) | | `grammar` | rule-based generation: rules, slots, weighted alternatives | Plus `rng(seed)` — a seedable RNG, so a sampled start or a generated sentence is reproducible. ## Usage ```js var ML = require("./ml-kit.js"); // Node; in a browser it is window.MLKit // Ranked search var index = ML.tfidf(["the cat sat on the mat", "dogs bark and cats meow"]); ML.search(index, "cat"); // -> [{ i: 0, score: ... }] // Classify var nb = ML.NaiveBayes().train([ { text: "good product", label: "pos" }, { text: "terrible waste", label: "neg" } ]); nb.classify("excellent product"); // -> "pos" // A trend line ML.linearRegression([0, 1, 2, 3], [1, 3, 5, 7]).slope; // -> 2 // Reproducible generation var m = ML.markov(corpus, { order: 2, word: true }); ML.generate(m, { seed: 42, length: 12 }); // same seed -> same text ``` ## Tests ``` node test-node.js ``` A known tf-idf ranking case, a Naive Bayes classification case, a k-means convergence case, a regression line against a known slope, PCA, k-NN, ID3, and seeded-reproducibility checks for the Markov chain and the grammar. CI runs it on every push. ## Design notes - **Every algorithm is reimplemented from the idea**, not copied. Where a survey suggested a reference, only the shape was taken — the code is ours. - **Deterministic where it matters.** k-means seeds from the first *k* points; Markov and the grammar take a seed, so the same seed gives the same output. - **Small and readable.** Tens of lines each, so the maths can be read and checked. - **UMD.** `module.exports` in Node, `MLKit` in a browser — the same shape as the other kits. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. # music

[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)


![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)
Album-wise music page for Dr Sohil Momin, served at https://drsamonline.github.io/music/

Audio is **not** hosted here. Each track points at the platform that hosts it (SoundCloud, Suno,
Flow Music, Newgrounds, Freesound) and the page plays it through that platform's own player, or
opens it in a new tab where no player page exists.

## What is where

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.html`, `styles.css`, `*.js` | the page. No build step, no dependencies. |
| `data/tracks.json` | the manifest the page reads. Generated — do not hand-edit. |
| `sources/seed.json` | crawled catalogue: profiles, tracks, licences, duplicates, takes. |
| `sources/*.links.txt` | the link list per platform, one URL per line. |
| `tools/build_manifest.py` | seed + link lists -> `data/tracks.json`. |
| `.github/workflows/` | rebuild manifest on push, deploy to Pages. |

## Add a track

1. Put the track link in `sources/<platform>.links.txt`.
2. Re-crawl that platform (or paste the row straight into `sources/seed.json`).
3. Push. `rebuild.yml` regenerates `data/tracks.json` and `deploy.yml` publishes it.

## Licence rule

Two tiers only, decided at ingest, never in the browser:

* `commercial` — stream free; commercial use is permitted by the source (own work, CC-BY-SA, or a
  paid Suno download).
* `personal` — stream free; no commercial use (CC-BY-NC*, everything on Flow Music until cleared,
  Suno downloads of unverified tier).

Anything uncertain lands in `personal`. Silence never grants rights.

## Duplicates and takes

* Different platform + same title = one song. Merged; the playable copy is primary and the other
  appears under "also on".
* Same platform + same title = separate takes (Suno generates two per prompt). Never merged.

## Deploy

Pages serves the repository root. `deploy.yml` publishes on every push to `main`.

# MusicGen

**A pocket generative composer.** One tap makes a finished-sounding track — harmony, melody, drums, mix and master — from six presets and a 12-character seed. No accounts, no server, no samples. It runs entirely in your browser, offline, in a light or dark studio.

[![tests](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/actions/workflows/test.yml)
[![a11y: axe clean](https://img.shields.io/badge/axe%20wcag%202.1%20AA-clean-c6f24e.svg)](#accessibility--audit)
[![license: PolyForm Noncommercial](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-c6f24e.svg)](LICENSE)
[![dependencies: 0](https://img.shields.io/badge/dependencies-0-9aa8ff.svg)](#)
[![tempo: 20–500 BPM](https://img.shields.io/badge/tempo-20--500%20BPM-9aa8ff.svg)](#)
[![size: 108 KB gzipped](https://img.shields.io/badge/size-108%20KB%20gzipped-9aa8ff.svg)](#)
[![PWA: offline-first](https://img.shields.io/badge/PWA-offline--first-c6f24e.svg)](#)
[![web audio api](https://img.shields.io/badge/web%20audio-api-ff9f6b.svg)](#)

**[▶ Live demo](https://drsamonline.github.io/musicgen/)** · **[Open the studio](https://drsamonline.github.io/musicgen/app/)** · **[Releases](https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen/releases)** · **[Enhancement backlog](docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md)**

![The MusicGen landing page, with a live specimen of a generated song](docs/screenshots/landing-desktop.png)

---

## What it is

A generative composer that behaves like an instrument rather than a toy. Every song is a **pure function of `(presets, seed)`**: the same inputs produce a byte-identical song, so a link is a recording. Random is sampled through a compatibility table so it stays musical, and every note is checked against the key and the chord sounding under it.

The whole thing is vanilla ES modules and the Web Audio API — no framework, no build step, no audio files, no network requests at runtime.

| Dark | Light |
|---|---|
| ![Studio, dark theme](docs/screenshots/studio-desktop.png) | ![Studio, light theme](docs/screenshots/studio-light-desktop.png) |
| *Two columns of dials, live spectrum, section timeline* | *The same studio in light — canvas colours are tokens too* |

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| ![Piano roll on a phone](docs/screenshots/studio-mobile.png) | ![Waveform visualiser](docs/screenshots/studio-spectrum.png) | ![Generated cover art](docs/screenshots/cover-art.png) |
| *Phone: piano roll, chord labels, playhead* | *Waveform mode* | *Cover art from the song's own data* |

## Try it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/musicgen
cd musicgen/app
python3 -m http.server 8080
# → http://localhost:8080
```

To preview the whole site the way it is published — the landing page at `/` and the
studio at `/app/` — run `npm run build` and serve `_site/`. The site is assembled from
`docs/` (the page) and `app/` (the studio) at deploy time, so there is no second copy
to drift, and `npm run build` fails if any link in it points at nothing.

Then use your browser's **Install** / **Add to Home Screen** (iOS: Share → Add to Home Screen). The service worker precaches the whole shell, so after that first visit it launches and plays with the network switched off.

## What's inside

**The composer** — eleven stages, each testable: key and mode → harmonic grid (2nd-order Markov over style progressions, modal interchange) → voicing with a voice-leading solver → bass → drums (groove templates, Euclidean layers, phrase fills) → motif → development transforms → pad and counter-line → arp → humanise → tension curve.

**The plan** — a song is two things: the decisions and the notes they produce. `plan(presets, seed)` returns the decisions as plain JSON — key, form, the chord under every bar, the theme, the tempo map — and `render(plan)` turns them into notes. `compose()` is the two together, and the split changed not one note: 330 preset × mood × seed combinations were hashed before and after it. The **Plan** panel in the studio opens that object up: reorder a section, repeat the chorus, change how many bars the intro runs, click a chord to change its quality. Every edit re-renders from the same seed, and the seed still reproduces the original. The drum pattern of any section is editable too, in a five-voice step sequencer. An edited song carries its plan in the share link — deflated, about 1.6 KB — so the link still hands over the song you heard rather than the one the seed would have made.

**The presets** — every axis has a **None**: no genre, no mood bias, no theme, no form, plain sine tones — so you can strip the song back to the notes and add only what you want. 11 styles, 10 moods, 10 themes, 8 song types, 7 synthesis technologies, plus a compatibility table that maps styles to allowed moods and engines. Tempo is a **map, not a number**: choruses lift, verses settle, every phrase gets a little rubato and the last two bars ease off, so a song breathes instead of clicking along. The BPM dial sets the centre and *Tempo drift* sets how far it may wander (0–35%). Range: **20–500 BPM**; per-track locks freeze the drums or the melody while you reroll everything else. Every share link carries the composer version, so an old seed can tell you it will sound different instead of silently lying.

**The ambience** — eight synthesised textures (rain, wind, fire, vinyl, crickets, ocean, stream, hum) with its own **Ambience dial**: *Auto* follows the theme, *None* is silence, or you pick one outright. Sitting under the arrangement with slow LFO movement and sparse droplets/crackles. Plus section transitions: a noise riser into every lift and a soft impact on the downbeat.

**The synthesis** — subtractive, FM, chiptune (real `PeriodicWave` pulses), additive, a six-frame **wavetable with a real morph**, Karplus-Strong, a **formant/vowel** layer and noise instruments, plus two **AudioWorklet** engines (granular and a waveguide) with native fallbacks; a drum kit built from oscillators and filtered noise; generated convolution reverb, tempo-synced delay and chorus; glue compressor and limiter on the master, mono bass below 120 Hz, sidechain ducking for EDM, a filter envelope and velocity-to-timbre on every voice, analogue drift, and a stereo-width tap. A voice pool steals the quietest voice with a fade; the scheduler runs a 200 ms lookahead and skips late notes instead of firing them in a burst.

**MIDI both ways** — export the song as Type-1 MIDI, or **import a MIDI file as the theme**: the highest-register line becomes the song's idea and everything derives from it.

**The exports** — WAV (16/24/32-bit, normalised to a chosen loudness target under a −1 dBTP ceiling), per-track stems as a zip with per-stem loudness in the readme, Type-1 MIDI, **XM module**, full song JSON (export *and* import), 1024 px cover art, and seed links that reproduce the exact song elsewhere.

**The module file** — a WAV keeps the sound and loses the editability; a MIDI keeps the notes and loses the timbre. An `.XM` keeps both in about 26 KB: it opens in OpenMPT, VLC or any tracker, and it carries its own instruments. MusicGen has no samples, so they are generated — one 32-sample single cycle per pitched track, built from the harmonic series of the song's synthesis technology, and one short percussive hit per drum voice. Polyphony needs channels, so the writer allocates pools rather than one channel per track: a four-note chord voicing on a single tracker channel would lose three notes of every four. The format is written from its specification, not from any tracker's source, since the trackers are GPL-family and this app is not.

**The platform bits** — installable PWA with a real install prompt and an offline badge, MediaSession metadata with generated artwork, screen Wake Lock, gamepad and MIDI-in control, five views (piano roll, tracker grid, spectrum, waveform, generative art), a piano roll you can zoom, pan and scrub, section looping, A/B against the previous song, undo/redo, a library with search/rename/duplicate, session restore, a text song summary for screen readers, `prefers-reduced-motion` and `prefers-color-scheme` support, and a strict CSP (`default-src 'self'`) with zero runtime fetches.

## Drum editing

The Plan panel's ▦ button opens a step sequencer for one section: five voices of sixteen steps, showing the pattern that is actually playing. Click a step to take it over; **Back to generated** hands the section back to the seed.

Two rules keep it honest. The grid you see is read from the song you can hear, not from the plan — the plan only stores what was *changed*, so an untouched section still shows what the generator wrote. And the first click on a section captures the whole lane for that voice before flipping one step, so the rest of the pattern doesn't move under your hand.

A hand-written lane replaces the generated one **for that voice only**: writing kicks leaves the snares, hats, claps and toms alone. The generator still runs for every section — its random draws are part of every other voice's determinism — and the overridden voice is filtered out afterwards. Which is why a plan with no lanes still renders byte-identical songs: 330 preset × mood × seed combinations were hashed before and after this change.

## Controllers

Menu → **Controllers** maps a standard gamepad onto the transport — play, generate, random, evolve, mutate, next view, volume, loop, A/B — and connects a MIDI keyboard that auditions the lead sound as you play it.

Three details make it behave:

- **buttons are edge-triggered.** A held button fires once, not sixteen times a second. The reader keeps per-pad held state, so two pads cannot share it, and an unplugged pad does not fire a storm of releases.
- **an analog trigger counts as pressed.** Triggers report `pressed: false` with a high `value` until the browser's own threshold, so either signal is accepted — that was a real bug, caught by a test that handed the reader `{ pressed: false, value: 0.9 }`.
- **nothing is polled or requested until you ask.** The pad poll starts when the dialog opens and stops when it closes; `requestMIDIAccess()` is behind a permission prompt, so it only ever runs from the button.

## The grid

The visualiser cycles **roll → grid → bars → wave → art**. The grid is not a piano roll with different paint: it is a tracker's reading of the same song — one row per sixteenth, one column per track, notes written the way a tracker writes them (`C-4`, `F#2`) and drums written as voices (`kck`, `snr`, `hat`), with a stacked step marked `kck+` rather than quietly dropping the second hit. A roll answers *what is the melody doing*; this answers *what lands on the sixteenth*, which is the question drums ask.

The layout is computed by pure functions (`noteLabel`, `buildStepIndex`, `rowsFor`, `windowFor`) so it is tested without a canvas; `drawTracker` only paints what they return. The step index is built once per song — scanning 1,500 notes for every row of every frame would be the entire cost of the view.

## Themes

The studio ships **light and dark**, and the choice is yours, not the OS's: the ◐ button (or `T`) cycles **system → light → dark** and the choice is remembered. Every surface is a token, including the canvas palettes — the piano roll, spectrum, waveform and generative-art modes re-theme with the UI rather than staying stuck on one background.

## Accessibility & audit

`npm run audit` runs axe-core (WCAG 2.1 A/AA + best practice) over the studio in **dark, light and desktop**, and over the landing page, then adds app-level checks axe cannot know about: duplicate ids, unlabelled controls, canvases without an accessible name, missing `lang`, console errors. Current state: **zero violations, zero app-level issues, zero console errors**.

```bash
npm install --no-save axe-core puppeteer   # audit + screenshot tooling only
npm run audit
```

## Tests

```bash
npm test              # 103 unit tests, no browser needed
npm run test:browser  # 177 tests in real Chromium with real Web Audio
npm run lint          # determinism lint: no Math.random / Date.now in pure modules
npm run budget        # shell size, precache completeness, no external requests
npm run visual        # pixel-diff the studio against committed baselines
npm run shots         # regenerate docs/screenshots
npm run audit         # axe + app checks, light and dark
npm run build         # assemble _site/ exactly as GitHub Pages publishes it
```

The suite asserts, rather than claims:

- determinism — the composer run 100× on the same seed, diffed
- musicality — 330 style × mood × seed cases through the theory validator
- audio — an offline render measured for silence, clipping and LUFS against the style target
- exports — WAV byte length, MIDI header and track count, zip archive structure
- continuity — a 3-second playback run whose event cursor must keep advancing, plus a watchdog test
- anti-aliasing — partial counts asserted against Nyquist at 22.05/44.1/48 kHz
- clipping — master peak ≤ 1.0 and no sample-to-sample jump above 0.9 in a dense render
- worklets — both processors render audio and the modules load in an offline context
- tempo — 20 BPM and 500 BPM both compose, render and validate; the range is clamped at both ends
- variable tempo — the map integrates and inverts, every scheduled event matches `secondsAt(beat)`, the render length equals the song's duration, and each section can sit at its own BPM
- audio integrity — a dense render has no silent holes, no voices are dropped, the pool stays inside its cap at 7/8 and 500 BPM
- loudness regression — three styles rendered offline and checked against their LUFS target and peak ceiling
- mix balance — every track rendered solo, checked for being audible, not buried, and not letting the drums dominate
- the app — theme switching and persistence, service worker caching, visualiser modes painting, stems quieter than the mix, track locks surviving a new seed
- the landing page — composing, drawing and linking its specimen

## Mix balance (why it sounds like a mix)

Per-track loudness is measured, not eyeballed: the drum bus has its own compressor, every track has a measured trim, and `npm run test:browser` renders each track solo and fails if anything is buried more than 18 dB or if the bass sits more than 12 dB over the drums. That test exists because the bass *did* sit 18 dB over the drums in v2.2.0, and it was the difference between "a song" and "a bass solo".

## Audio health

The menu has an **Audio health** panel: context state, clock source, sample rate, base latency, voice-pool occupancy, worst tick gap, late and dropped notes, clock stalls and rebuilds. It polls only while it is open.

It exists because a browser audio app fails in ways you cannot hear in a screenshot. A phone locking interrupts the context; a Bluetooth route closing kills it; a busy audio thread freezes `currentTime` while `state` still reports `running`. All three look identical from the outside — *it went quiet* — and none of them leave anything a bug report can carry.

Two of those now repair themselves. A `statechange` to `interrupted`/`suspended` is resumed, and a clock that stops advancing while the transport says it is playing triggers a full rebuild — new context, new graph, same song, same position. The panel's **Rebuild audio** button is the same path, for the case where nothing fired. The suite proves it by freezing `currentTime` mid-song and asserting playback comes back on its own.

## Playback resilience

Seeking, regenerating and switching seeds are all covered by tests, because each one used to be able to leave the app silent:

- **A regenerate reuses the AudioContext.** It used to build a new `Player` — and therefore a new `AudioContext` — every time, and browsers cap those at a handful; after a few regenerations the constructor threw and nothing played again. `Player.setSong()` swaps the graph inside the existing context.
- **The closing fade cannot fire in the past.** Seeking near the end used to schedule the end-of-song fade *behind* the playhead, which faded the master to silence with nothing to bring it back.
- **`ensureAudible()` on every tick.** If the master is ever left at silence while the transport says it's playing, it is restored — a safety net that turns a dead app into a blip.
- **`play` is imported where it's used.** The one-line cause of "regenerate goes silent": after the UI split, `generate()` called `play()` without importing it, so every regenerate threw `TypeError: play is not a function` *after* pausing. The suite now asserts playback survives a regenerate, a seek to 97%, eight regenerations in a row, and the landing page's seed switching.

## Performance: why it stopped stuttering

Three things were fighting for the main thread, and the fix was structural rather than tuning:

- **The scheduler now runs off the audio thread.** The clock worklet had never actually attached — `AudioWorkletNode` rejects `numberOfOutputs: 0`, so the constructor threw and the app silently fell back to `setInterval`, which stutters whenever the main thread is busy. It now has one output and a silent sink, and ticks arrive from the audio thread. Lookahead went from 200 ms to 300 ms, and a note is only dropped if it is more than 150 ms late.
- **The visualisers are two layers.** Everything static in the piano roll (grid, chord labels, ~1,500 notes, drum lane) is rendered once into an offscreen canvas and blitted; only the section band and the playhead are drawn per frame. Measured cost of one visualiser frame: **0.08 ms**, down from several milliseconds. The landing page's specimen got the same treatment.
- **30 fps, not 60.** The render loop was already capped; with the blit it now has room to spare, and `prefers-reduced-motion` drops it to 10 fps.

## Performance and audio integrity

Measured, not guessed. The reverb IR is synthesised once per context and cached (it used to be rebuilt on every pause); the saturation curve is a shared `Float32Array` instead of 1024 floats per note; analyser buffers are reused across frames; the section-intensity lookup is a binary search; and pausing fades the master instead of rebuilding the graph.

Three bugs used to make sound drop out, and they are worth naming because they were invisible:

1. **The voice counter never decremented.** It ran on `setTimeout`, which is throttled in a background tab and never fires during an offline render — so `active` hit the cap and stayed there, and from then on every quiet note was silently dropped. It is now a pool pruned by time, stealing the quietest voice with a fade.
2. **Feedback loops were never disconnected.** Karplus-Strong's delay line rang forever and the noise bed's LFO kept running; over a long session that is a CPU creep that ends in dropouts.
3. **Late notes were fired in a burst.** Anything more than 60 ms late is now skipped instead of dumped into the present.

## Architecture

```
index.html            landing page (its own live specimen)
landing.css landing.js
app/                  the PWA
  index.html styles.css manifest.webmanifest sw.js icons/
  src/core/           rng algorithms theory voicing motif composer validate
  src/presets/        styles moods themes types techs compatibility
  src/audio/          engine instruments drums fx mastering lufs
  src/export/         wav midi zip artwork
  src/visual/         pianoRoll (+ bars, waveform, generative art)
  src/state.js        src/main.js
  qa/matrix.html      listening matrix (dev only)
tests/unit/ tests/browser/
scripts/              screenshots.mjs, audit.mjs
docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md  the backlog
```

## Credits and licences

Two of my own other repositories informed this one. **ambient-sound-studio** (personal-use licence) is where the idea of layered synthesised textures comes from — the eight beds here are reimplemented for this engine, not copied. **eon-commando** (same) contributed the noise-sweep primitive that became the section risers. **audio-kit** (PolyForm Noncommercial) shares the same "patterns, not files" philosophy; its code is deliberately *not* vendored here, because mixing licences in one bundle is a trap.

## Layout

Two splits, both done for editability rather than tidiness.

**The engine** is five modules behind a barrel (`engine.js`): `worklets.js` (AudioWorklet loading and fallbacks), `graph.js` (track chains, buses, master chain), `scheduler.js` (tempo map, events, automation, voice dispatch), `player.js` (live transport) and `render.js` (offline rendering).

**The UI** is six modules behind `main.js` (205 lines of wiring and nothing else): `ui/ctx.js` (the DOM map, the mutable singletons, the small helpers), `ui/dials.js` (presets, random/evolve/mutate, groove editor), `ui/generate.js` (history, compose, the three readouts), `ui/transport.js` (player lifecycle, loop, A/B, wake lock, MediaSession, install), `ui/visuals.js` (theme, five views, piano-roll gestures) and `ui/exporters.js` (WAV, stems, MIDI, JSON, art, share, library, recording).

## Contributing

`CONTRIBUTING.md` has the one rule that matters (determinism in `src/core/`) and the five checks a PR must pass. `docs/LISTENING.md` is the golden-seed log — the place where the automated tests stop and a person listens.

## Design notes

Three decisions are worth knowing about, because they were made against the obvious choice:

**The validator accepts chromatic notes when the chord owns them.** An absolute "everything in the key" rule would reject the modal interchange and borrowed chords that make the harmony interesting. The rule is *in key **or** a tone of the chord sounding at that moment*.

**Loudness targets are per style.** Lo-fi sits at −16 LUFS, EDM at −11, Ambient at −18. Normalising everything to a single streaming number would flatten exactly the character the styles are for.

**Worklets arrived last, not first.** Granular and waveguide processors exist now, but every one of them is a per-track node with a native fallback, and the app still runs with `addModule` unavailable. Building the whole synth on worklets first would have made the fallback the interesting case instead of the exception.

## Known gaps

Stems share one gain (measured on the mix) rather than being re-mixed per track — the per-stem loudness is written into the zip's readme; undo covers preset changes, not generations; note audition and a groove editor are not implemented; granular and physical modelling remain native-node approximations rather than AudioWorklets; MIDI import, microtuning, a share target and a protocol handler are still open. The full backlog, with what is done and what is not, is in [docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md](docs/ENHANCEMENTS.md).

This one asks you to **position**. The gun is fully automatic and picks its own targets, so the only decisions left are spatial ones: how close do you dare stand, when do you break line of sight, when do you spend your slide, when do you jump and when do you duck. Every mechanic below exists to make those decisions interesting rather than to add buttons. - **Three controls.** Left, right, jump, duck. That is it. There is no fire button, and there never will be. - **Range is a resource.** Your gun only fires when something is inside its circle, so damage output is a function of positioning. - **Heat punishes camping.** Firing builds heat, and heat only cools when *nothing is in range*. Standing still and spraying is impossible — you have to weave. - **The chain rewards aggression.** Kills within 2.5s stack up to ×8. Staying close is how you score; it is also how you die. - **Graze rewards nerve.** Enemy fire that passes close but does not hit charges an EMP. Getting shot at is progress. --- ## 🎮 Controls | Action | Keyboard | Touch | Gamepad | | :-- | :-- | :-- | :-- | | Run left / right | `←` `→` or `A` `D` | ◀ ▶ | D-pad / left stick | | Jump | `↑`, `W` or `Space` | ▲ | A / B | | Duck | `↓` or `S` | ▼ | D-pad down | | Slide | hold `↓` while running | hold ▼ while running | down + direction | | Pause | `P` | ⏸ | Start | | Back / close menu | `Esc` or `⌫` | ↩ | — | | Mute | `M` | — | — | Every binding is remappable from **CONTROLS** on the title screen (or the pause menu). The boot screen shows your current keys, so you can see what to press before you start. Touch button size and opacity are adjustable, and there is a left-handed pad layout. **Audio note.** Browsers refuse to start audio until the page has received a real user gesture — this is a hard browser rule, not a bug. The game unlocks its audio on the *first keypress or click*, and the boot screen says so explicitly while it is waiting. If you ever hear nothing, press any key or click once. --- ## 🦆 The duck rule Ducking is not decorative. It changes your hitbox from 42px tall to 24px tall, and several threats are tuned around exactly that: - **Turret lasers** fire flat at standing chest height. Duck and they sail over your head. - **Laser gates** span chest-to-knee. Duck and you walk straight under them. - **Flyer volleys** aimed at your centre line pass overhead when you crouch. Jumping and ducking are answers to different problems. Learning which is which is most of the skill. --- ## ⚙️ Systems | System | What it does | | :-- | :-- | | **Auto-fire** | Targets the nearest threat in range, weighted toward exploders and turrets. A reticle shows the current lock. | | **Overheat** | ~19 shots to overheat. Cools only when nothing is in range. # Neon Velocity

**Play in the browser:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/neon-velocity/play/> — it
installs as an app (PWA) and works offline after the first load.
**Landing page:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/neon-velocity/>

![Gameplay](site/assets/shots/action.jpg)

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Boss fight](site/assets/shots/boss.jpg) | ![Swarm](site/assets/shots/swarm.jpg) |
| The Core Interceptor, first of four bosses | Drone formations converging |
| ![Title screen](site/assets/shots/menu.jpg) | ![Pause menu](site/assets/shots/pause.jpg) |
| Title screen, difficulty select | Pause menu |

A retro side-scrolling shooter for **Godot 4.3** where every sprite and every
sound is generated at runtime. The repository contains no binary assets at all:
no PNGs, no OGGs, no fonts — just GDScript, three shaders and two scene files.

```
godot --path .          # or open the folder in the Godot 4.3 editor and press F5
```

There is also a **web build that installs as an app** (PWA) — see
[Play in a browser](#play-in-a-browser-pwa).

## Controls

| Action | Keys |
|--------|------|
| Move | `WASD` / arrow keys |
| Fire | `Z` or left mouse button |
| Dash (brief invulnerability) | `Space` / `Shift` |
| Switch weapon | `Q` / `E` |
| Pause | `Esc` |

On a phone or tablet the game draws its own controls: drag anywhere on the left
half to fly, `FIRE` and `DASH` sit under the right thumb, and `WPN` / pause are
in the top-right corner. Turn the device to landscape — portrait shows a
"rotate your device" screen. On the web build the first tap also asks for
fullscreen and a landscape lock.

## Play in a browser (PWA)

The project exports to Web, and the export is patched into a real installable
PWA: manifest, icons, service worker, offline page. It is single-threaded, so it
does **not** need `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy` / `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`
headers and will run on any static host, including GitHub Pages, Netlify,
Cloudflare Pages and itch.io.

```bash
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Web" build/web/index.html
python3 tools/pwa_post_export.py build/web

# local preview (service workers need http, not file://)
python3 -m http.server 8000 --directory build/web
# then open http://localhost:8000
```

The first load pulls a ~35 MB wasm bundle; after that the service worker serves
it from cache and the game starts instantly, including offline. Install it from
the browser's address bar ("Install") to get a standalone window and an icon.

Two things to know: a **keyboard is required** (there are no touch controls),
and the page must be served over **HTTPS or localhost** — service workers are
refused on plain `http://` origins.

`tools/pwa_post_export.py` does two things the raw export does not: it registers
the service worker (Godot only does that for thread-enabled builds) and it
prunes the worker's precache list, which otherwise lists `index.worker.js` in
thread-less builds — one 404 there makes `cache.addAll()` reject and silently
kills offline support.

## What is in the game

- **Six weapons** — plasma cannon, spread shot, laser lance, seeker missiles,
  railgun, nova burst. Each has five levels and gains XP from kills.
- **18 mods** — stat modifiers and named effects (chain lightning, ricochet,
  life siphon, MIRV split, EMP slow, multi-pulse nova). Picking up a mod card
  pauses the run and offers three choices.
- **Endless procedural levels** — the world is a strip of 2400-unit chunks,
  each generated from `run_seed + chunk_index`, so a seed always replays the
  same run.
- **Four bosses** on a five-chunk cycle, each with its own attack patterns and
  a phase change every quarter of its health.
- **Full loop** — title screen, difficulty select, HUD, pause menu, settings,
  run summary with accuracy and best score, local save file.
- **Adaptive music** — four synthesised layers (bass, lead, pad, drums) that
  fade in as you get deeper into a run, plus 24 procedural sound effects.

## How the "zero assets" trick works

| Thing | Where it comes from |
|-------|---------------------|
| Sprites | `scripts/core/Art.gd` rasterises every image with the `Image` API from a fixed 16-colour palette, then wraps it in an `ImageTexture` |
| Sound effects | `scripts/core/AudioManager.gd` synthesises PCM float buffers (FM, sweeps, noise, arpeggios) and packs them into `AudioStreamWAV` |
| Music | The same file builds four 6.857 s loops at 140 BPM and crossfades them |
| Level art | Starfield, nebula and mountain silhouettes are generated once and tiled by `ParallaxBackground` |

Audio generation takes roughly half a second at startup on a modest laptop, all
of it before the title screen appears.

  systems/     WeaponSystem, LevelManager, GameManager, ReplaySystem

## Testing

```bash
# headless smoke test: boots Main, plays 7 seconds of synthetic input, asserts 27 things
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/TestRunner.tscn

# 50-second soak run: chunk streaming, pooling and the first boss fight
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/tools/SoakTest.tscn

# dump every generated sprite to art_preview/ for inspection
godot --headless --path . res://scenes/tools/DumpSprites.tscn
```

The test runner exits non-zero on failure, so CI can gate on it.

## Builds and releases

`export_presets.cfg` defines four presets: Web, Linux, Windows and macOS.
Export templates must be installed first (Editor → Manage Export Templates).

```bash
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Linux/X11"      build/linux/NeonVelocity.x86_64
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Windows Desktop" build/windows/NeonVelocity.exe
godot --headless --path . --export-release "macOS"          build/macos/NeonVelocity.zip
godot --headless --path . --export-release "Web"            build/web/index.html
```

Everything is automated in `.github/workflows/build.yml`:

| Trigger | What happens |
|---------|--------------|
| any push / PR | headless smoke test + 50-second soak test |
| push to `main` | the above, then the Web build is patched into a PWA and deployed to GitHub Pages |
| `v*` tag | the above, then Linux, Windows, macOS and Web are exported and attached to a GitHub release |
| manual dispatch | same as a tag, without publishing a release |

So shipping a new version is `git tag v1.1.0 && git push --tags`.

Note on Pages: GitHub Pages needs a **public** repository on the free plan, so
the Pages job is opt-in. To turn it on, make the repository public, enable Pages
with "GitHub Actions" as the source, then set a repository variable
`ENABLE_PAGES=true` (Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables).
Every push to `main` will then publish the PWA. Until then, take
`neon-velocity-web.zip` from the release and drop the unzipped folder on any
static host — Netlify, Cloudflare Pages, itch.io and GitHub Pages all work,
because the build needs no special headers.

## Saves and replays

Settings live in `user://settings.cfg`, the last run and lifetime stats in
`user://save_game.save` (JSON, XOR-obfuscated — not encrypted, and not meant to
be), and recorded inputs in `user://replays/`.

Replays are **recorded, not yet playable**: each run writes a JSON file with the
seed, difficulty and three bytes of input per frame, which is everything needed
to re-simulate it, but no playback UI is wired up yet.
