Mobile: one thumb, bottom tabs, sheets.
--- ## Why this exists Most remedy finders are a search box over a list. A repertory is not a list — it is a weighted argument. Three things decide which remedy rises: **which symptoms you chose**, **how characteristic each one is**, and **how many remedies share it**. This app puts all three on screen at the same time. - The number beside every symptom is how many of the 178 remedies carry it. Rare symptoms discriminate; the picker tells you which are rare *before* you click. - Every symptom→remedy link carries the repertory's **grade 1–3**. Grade-3 links score higher, and ★ marks them. - Every remedy carries a **verbatim quotation** from a public-domain materia medica, labelled with book and year — so you can read the source, not a summary of it. ## What it does | | | |---|---| | **Repertorise** | 634 symptoms in 17 chapters, 5 quick packs, typo-tolerant search, live ranking in a Web Worker | | **Remedy search** | The search box also finds remedies by name, Latin name, clinical use and family — one click opens the monograph | | **Pin & watch** | Pin up to three remedies and change the symptoms around them; the pinned strip keeps showing each remedy’s live rank and score | | **Data packs** | Import a JSON pack to add remedies offline (validated against this app's symptom IDs, with a SHA-256 checksum so a tampered file is refused), or export the current data as a pack. Packs persist in IndexedDB and re-apply on load | | **Text search** | A third picker mode searches the materia medica itself — descriptions, both quoted sources and clinical uses — plus the repertory rubric paths, with highlighted snippets and one click to the monograph | | **Thermal tendency** | Per remedy: chilly / hot / mixed, derived from the thermal modality rubrics in the repertory (cold agg, warm agg, warm amel, cold bathing amel) with the evidence rubric and grade shown. 135 of 297 remedies have evidence; the rest say "not stated" | | **Remedy explorer** | Force-directed relationship map: labelled without overlap, node size by relationship count, kingdom and thermal filters, search, zoom and pan, hover to isolate a remedy's relationships. **Built for touch**: the layout is computed at the real canvas size, pinch to zoom, drag to pan, tap to open, refits on rotate | | **Sources & provenance** | In-app screen with live counts, quotations per source, licences and an explicit list of what the app does not do | | **Rare-only filter** | One toggle in Repertory mode keeps rubrics carried by three remedies or fewer — the characteristic material, not the fever rubric every remedy has | | **Full repertory** | A second picker mode: search **39,737 rubrics** from Repertorium Publicum by words — *fear of death*, *thirst small*, *worse consolation* — and repertorise directly on rubrics, alone or mixed with curated symptoms | | **Boards** | Keep several rubric sets inside one case — acute picture, constitutional picture, family history — switch between them, and compare their rankings side by side | | **Interface languages** | English, हिंदी and ગુજરાતી for the finder, results and tools. Repertory terms stay in English — they are the vocabulary of the source books | | **Symptom weight** | Mark each selected symptom strong (+) or doubtful (−); the ranking responds immediately, in both the worker and the main thread | | **Eliminative method** | Strike remedies out as you go; a struck strip lets you restore them. Undo covers removals and deletions | | **Rubric provenance** | Hover any symptom for the repertory rubric behind it; every monograph lists the rubric behind each keynote (`Mind > fear > death · 26 rubrics`) | | **Grade-weighted scoring** | Chapter weights × rarity (inverse frequency) × keynote bonus × grade 1–3 × acute/constitutional mode | | **Materia medica** | 297 remedy monographs: description, **two quoted sources side by side** (Boericke 1906, Allen 1916, Nash 1899, Clarke 1900, Guernsey 1886), rubric provenance, keynotes, mentals, generals, modalities, particulars, relationships, family | | **Cases** | Save a repertorisation as a case, add dated follow-ups with remedy and potency, status and tags, search and sort, 30-day stale flag | | **Exports** | Markdown report, CSV, cases JSON, Anki deck (TSV), print stylesheet, single-remedy monograph print | | **Full-text search** | The search box also matches materia medica text, so “ague”, “monkshood” or a phrase from a description finds the remedy | | **Study** | Spaced repetition (SM-2) from any remedy, streak, month calendar, quizzes: guess-the-remedy, differentiation, keynotes, case, narration | | **Analysis** | Comparison matrix (up to 10 remedies), shared/unique comparison, relationship graph, family explorer, potency helper | | **Data audit** | Built-in integrity panel: broken references, duplicate names, orphan symptoms, contradictory modalities, unverified sources — and it reports them instead of hiding them |
## The data Every link is traceable. Nothing is generated by a language model at runtime, and gaps are reported rather than filled. | Layer | Source | Scale | |---|---|---| | Rubric grades | **Repertorium Publicum** (2008), Vladimir Polony — GPL v3 | 74,480 rubrics, 735,460 graded links | | Symptom → remedy links | Mapped to this app's 634 symptoms by exact name, synonym and checked alias | **44,710 links** across 297 remedies | | Materia medica text | Boericke 1906 · Allen 1916 · Kent 1904 · Clarke 1900 · Nash 1899 · Guernsey 1886 · Felter 1922 · Lippe 1866 · Cowperthwaite 1885 · Bell 1906 · Hale 1897 | 132 quotations | | Source verification | Each remedy's attributed sources checked against 12 full texts | 170 / 178 remedies | | Dataset | [`drsamonline/homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json`](https://github.com/drsamonline/homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json) — 72 books, 357,762 rubrics, 1,435,488 links | CC0 / GPL v3 | **Known limits, stated plainly** - Symptom→rubric matching is automated with a hand-checked alias table. It is right at the level of *"this remedy is in this rubric"*, not *"this is the simillimum"*. - The Boericke extraction covers 379 of roughly 700 entries, so 46 remedies have no Boericke quote and 8 have no verified source text. - Grades come from *Repertorium Publicum*, a Kent-derived open repertory — not from Kent 1897, whose links in this dataset are ungraded. Full provenance: [ATTRIBUTION.md](ATTRIBUTION.md). ## Offline and install | Route | How | |---|---| | **Single file** | [`dist/remedy-finder.html`](dist/remedy-finder.html) (947 KB) — curated symptoms. [`dist/remedy-finder-full.html`](dist/remedy-finder-full.html) (3.0 MB) — same app plus the complete repertory. Double-click either; no server, no install, works from a USB stick. | | **PWA** | Open the [live app](https://drsamonline.github.io/remedy-finder/) and use *Install* / *Add to Home Screen*. A service worker caches everything; it then works with the network off. | | **Windows** | Tagged releases attach a portable launcher produced by CI ([`build-exe.yml`](.github/workflows/build-exe.yml)). | | **Android** | Install the PWA (above), or wrap the live URL into an APK with PWABuilder — see [docs/PACKAGING.md](docs/PACKAGING.md). | There is **no backend, no account, no analytics, no network request at runtime.** Case data lives in IndexedDB on your device. ## Offline, and staying offline The app never needs a network. That makes **your copy the only copy**, so there is an explicit durability layer: | Control | What it does | |---|---| | **Encrypted backup** | One file, AES‑256‑GCM with a PBKDF2 key (150,000 rounds). Written to a folder you pick once (File System Access API) or downloaded. **Verified by decrypting it back before it is called saved.** | | **Restore from file** | Reads a `.rfb.json`, decrypts locally, shows a **preview** (exported date, data edition, record counts) before writing. Merges by record ID; a wrong passphrase fails closed. | | **Plain JSON export** | Same payload, unencrypted, for interoperability — labelled as patient data. | | **Download everything for offline** | Pre-caches the shell *and* the repertory file, so Repertory mode works with the network off. | | **Readiness panel** | Service-worker state, cached file count and size, whether the repertory is available offline, record counts, and days since last backup. | | **Background reminder** | Where the browser supports it, a periodic sync wakes the service worker, reads the backup age from IndexedDB and shows a notification. Off by default | | **Backup reminder** | A dismissible banner appears when records exist and the last backup is older than your chosen interval (3 / 7 / 30 days, or off). Re-checked when you return to the tab. | | **Keyboard picking** | Arrow keys move between rows, Home/End jump, Space or Enter toggles, focus stays on the row you just changed, and a live region announces the count | | **Case sheet download** | One case as a self-contained HTML file — open it anywhere, print it, or save as PDF | | **Board → case** | Turn the active board into a saved case, keeping its symptoms | | **Study centre** | Daily remedy, nine practice modes in one grid, streak and card count — same visual language as the rest of the app, no emoji | | **Rare-rubric quiz** | Which remedy does this two- or three-remedy rubric separate? Four options, graded feedback, next question | | **Case comparison** | Two saved cases side by side: symptoms in both, added, dropped, and how the top twelve remedies moved between visits | | **Printable case sheet** | One page per case: patient header, complaint, notes, symptoms with chapter and frequency, top ten remedies with scores, and quotations for the top three, with the data edition and a disclaimer in the footer | | **Transfer codes** | Move one case, or several, between devices as an encrypted text code (PIN-protected) — copy it, save it as a file, or **show it as a QR** for a phone camera to read. No network, no account | | **Delta backup** | After a full backup, "Backup changes only" writes just the records that changed since — with deletions recorded too, and restored as a merge | | **Backup history** | The last ten backups, with date, record count and size, plus **how many records changed since the last backup**. | | **Encryption at rest** | Optional passphrase. Clinic cases, saved repertorisations and packs are stored as AES‑256‑GCM ciphertext; the key lives in memory only. A lock screen on start, auto-lock after 1/5/15 minutes idle, passphrase rotation with a reissued recovery key, and a "turn off" path that decrypts everything back to plain text. | | **Connection chip** | Top bar shows `offline-ready` / `offline` / `local file`, and updates as the connection changes. | Every saved repertorisation is stamped with the **data edition** it was scored against (`rp2008-297r-44710l`), so a case opened a year from now can say which dataset produced its ranking. ## Two builds, one codebase | | `remedy-finder.html` | `remedy-finder-full.html` | |---|---|---| | Size | 947 KB | 3.7 MB | | Curated symptoms (634) | yes | yes | | Full repertory search (39,737 rubrics) | no — the mode tells you so | yes | | Load time | instant | repertory index builds in ~0.3 s on first use | The repertory ships as a separate 1.9 MB file (`assets/repertory.js`) and is loaded **only when you open the Repertory picker**, so the default app stays small. The single-file "full" build simply inlines it. **What the 39,737 rubrics are:** every rubric in *Repertorium Publicum* that carries at least two of this app's 297 remedies, with the printed grade kept. Single-remedy rubrics are dropped — one remedy cannot discriminate — and 9,353 of the included rubrics carry exactly two, which makes them the sharpest material in the repertory. The app says so rather than pretending the repertory is complete. **How a rubric scores:** chapter weight (Mind 5, Generalities 4, modality 3, particular 2) × rarity `1 + 0.5·log₂(178/n)` × grade `1 + (g−1)·0.5`. Selected rubrics and curated symptoms add up into one ranking, so you can mix them in the same case. ## Architecture Deliberately boring: no framework, no bundler, no npm install. ``` index.html app shell (rail · top bar · picker · results · tab bar) assets/app.css design system — one stylesheet, light + dark, print assets/data.js window.HRF_DATA — 634 symptoms, 178 remedies, graded links assets/app.js data layer, index, scoring, storage, cases, SRS, exports, modals assets/ui.js view layer: picker, tray, results, view switching, tools sheet sw.js offline cache landing/index.html marketing page dist/remedy-finder.html single-file build (generated) build.py inlines the three assets into the single file ``` Rebuild the single file after editing: ```bash python3 build.py # → dist/remedy-finder.html ``` ## Keyboard | Key | Action | |---|---| | `/` | focus symptom search | | `?` | shortcuts | | `Esc` | close sheet | | `T` · `C` · `S` · `M` · `A` · `E` | theme · cases · study · matrix · audit · explorer | ## Verification The view and logic layers are exercised in headless Chromium: **68 method-level tests plus 100 broader checks** covering every module (storage, cases, SRS, exports, matrix, graph, audit, all modals, all header actions, the full select → repertorise → detail → export journey). # The Repertory Desk

[![0 dependencies](docs/assets/badge-tests.svg)](docs/play/index.html)
[![70 volumes](docs/assets/badge-deps.svg)](docs/play/index.html)
[![offline yes](docs/assets/badge-offline.svg)](docs/play/index.html)
[![CC0 1.0](docs/assets/badge-licence.svg)](LICENSE)

**A quiet reading room for sixteen classical homoeopathic repertories, six materia
medicas and forty public-domain treatises** — 352,063 rubrics, 1,429,263 remedy
links (751,907 of them graded) and 5,392 sections of prose, read straight from the open
JSON library on GitHub. No account,
no server, no tracking, no build step.

**Live:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/repertory-reader/>  · 
**The reader:** <https://drsamonline.github.io/repertory-reader/play/>  · 
**The library:** <https://github.com/drsamonline/homoeopathic-materia-medica-repertory-json>

![The Repertory Desk](docs/assets/app-desktop.png)

## The treatises

The library also carries prose works as a **treatise**: no rubrics, no remedies. A
numbered treatise (the Organon) shows a § against each paragraph; a chaptered one shows
its chapter title instead. Each is a separate volume and none is merged with another.

Forty treatises, from the two Organons to Clarke's *Dictionary* in three volumes:

- **B. L. Hill**, *An Epitome of the Homeopathic Healing Art* (1861) — 50 sections
- **C. H. Vilas**, *Therapeutics of the Eye and Ear: An Elementary Manual, with a Repertory of the Eye* (1883) — 17 sections
- **Constantine Hering**, *The Guiding Symptoms of Our Materia Medica* (1879) — 49 sections
- **E. H. Ruddock**, *The Lady's Manual of Homoeopathic Treatment* (1870) — 32 sections
- **E. H. Ruddock**, *The Homoeopathic Vade Mecum of Modern Medicine and Surgery* (1874) — 52 sections
- **Edward Bach**, *Free Thyself* (1932) — 12 sections
- **Edward Pollock Anshutz (ed.)**, *New, Old and Forgotten Remedies: Papers by Many Writers* (1900) — 125 sections
- **Frederick Humphreys**, *Humphreys' Manual of Specific Homeopathy* (1887) — 50 sections
- **Frederick Humphreys**, *Manual of Veterinary Homeopathy* (1922) — 41 sections
- **G. H. G. Jahr**, *The Venereal Diseases, Their Pathological Nature, Diagnosis and Treatment* (1868) — 230 sections
- **G. H. G. Jahr; A. Possart**, *Jahr's and Possart's New Manual of the Homoeopathic Materia Medica* (1853) — 409 sections
- **H. C. Allen**, *Keynotes and Characteristics with Comparisons of Some of the Leading Remedies of the Materia Medica* (1916) — 183 sections
- **Henry Newell Guernsey**, *The Application of the Principles and Practice of Homoeopathy to Obstetrics* (1866) — 77 sections
- **J. H. Pulte**, *The Homoeopathic Domestic Physician* (1855) — 223 sections
- **J. Henry Allen**, *The Chronic Miasms — Sycosis* (1908) — 23 sections
- **J. Henry Allen**, *The Chronic Miasms — Psora and Pseudo-Psora* (1908) — 25 sections
- **James Compton Burnett**, *The Curability of Cataract with Medicines* (1889) — 5 sections
- **James Tyler Kent**, *Lectures on Homoeopathic Philosophy* (1900) — 21 sections
- **James Tyler Kent**, *Lectures on Homoeopathic Materia Medica* (1904) — 251 sections
- **James Tyler Kent**, *Lesser Writings of James Tyler Kent* (1900) — 36 sections
- **James Tyler Kent**, *Clinical Cases* (1900) — 105 sections
- **John A. Tarbell**, *Homoeopathy Simplified, or Domestic Practice Made Easy* (1864) — 210 sections
- **John Henry Clarke**, *A Dictionary of Domestic Medicine* (1890) — 22 sections
- **John Henry Clarke**, *A Dictionary of Practical Materia Medica, Volume I (A–H)* (1900) — 435 sections
- **John Henry Clarke**, *A Dictionary of Practical Materia Medica, Volume II (I–P)* (1902) — 323 sections
- **John Henry Clarke**, *A Dictionary of Practical Materia Medica, Volume III (P–Z)* (1902) — 268 sections
- **John R. Kippax**, *A Hand-Book of Diseases of the Skin and Their Homoeopathic Treatment* (1890) — 138 sections
- **Joseph Laurie**, *The Homeopathic Guide for Family Use* (1870) — 89 sections
- **Joseph T. O'Connor (ed.)**, *The American Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia* (1883) — 580 sections
- **Margaret Lucy Tyler**, *Pointers to the Common Remedies (remedies by disease)* (1936) — 60 sections
- **Samuel Hahnemann**, *The Chronic Diseases: Their Specific Nature and Homoeopathic Treatment — the theoretical part* (1896) — 6 sections
- **Samuel Hahnemann R. E. Dudgeon**, *Organon of Medicine, fifth edition* (1849) — 294 sections
- **Samuel Hahnemann William Boericke**, *Organon of Medicine, sixth edition* (1922) — 291 sections
- **Samuel Hahnemann; translated from the latest German editions**, *Materia Medica Pura (A–I)* (1880) — 36 sections
- **Samuel Lilienthal**, *Homoeopathic Therapeutics* (1884) — 527 sections
- **T. C. Duncan**, *Diseases of Infants and Children, with Their Homoeopathic Treatment* (1879) — 165 sections
- **T. C. Duncan**, *Hand Book on the Diseases of the Heart and Their Homoeopathic Treatment* (1898) — 68 sections
- **Thomas Lindsley Bradford**, *The Life and Letters of Dr. Samuel Hahnemann* (1894) — 70 sections
- **Willis Alonzo Dewey**, *Essentials of Homoeopathic Materia Medica* (1894) — 6 sections
- **Willis Alonzo Dewey**, *Practical Homeopathic Therapeutics* (1900) — 102 sections

The two Organons are genuinely different books: 74 paragraphs are worded differently and
§292–§294 exist only in the fifth. Each paragraph carries the source it was read from and
the fraction of its 12-letter sequences found verbatim in OCR scans of that same edition,
so you can see for yourself that a paragraph is the book's text and not a reconstruction.

## What it is

A reader. It opens a volume on its own contents and shows each rubric the way the
book printed it — the symptom in the measure of the page, the remedies the book
sets beside it, and the printed grade marks where the source carries them. Every
remedy is a door: tap a chip to see the rubrics in that volume which list it.

It does not repertorise, score, rank, correct or complete anything. A repertory is
evidence; a reader that starts guessing stops being evidence.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Read** | A repertory opens chapter by chapter, in the printed order; a materia medica opens by remedy, with its portrait, clinical indications and symptoms grouped by chapter. Knerr's 43 chapters, Kent's 34, Gentry's A–Z; single-file volumes build their contents from the sections inside the file. |
| **Search** | Three scopes — the open chapter, the volume, then every volume already on your device. Remedy abbreviations and resolved names are searched too. |
| **Follow** | Remedy chips filter a volume to the rubrics that carry them; the rail can list a volume by its drugs instead of its chapters. |
| **Themes** | Paper, vellum, sage, slate, lampblack — remembered per device, with serif text at a measured line length. |
| **Offline** | Chapters are kept in IndexedDB and served by a service worker, so a second visit works with the connection off. HTML stays network-first, so a release is never hidden behind a stale cache. |
| **Fast** | No framework, no dependencies, no build. Rendering is windowed — a 13,000-rubric chapter paints sixty rows at a time. |

## This app is locked

`docs/play/` is hand-built and hand-maintained: no CI, no build workflow, no
bundler, and no packaging into an EXE, an APK or a Linux binary. It is not wired
into `app-builder` and no automation regenerates its markup or design. See
[LOCKED.md](LOCKED.md) — if a change cannot be made without a build step, the
change is wrong.

## Run it

```bash
git clone https://github.com/drsamonline/repertory-reader
cd repertory-reader/docs && python3 -m http.server 8000
# open http://localhost:8000/play/
```

By default the reader fetches the library from GitHub (jsDelivr, falling back to
raw.githubusercontent.com). To read a local mirror of the library instead — the
way this app was tested — put the library's files under your web root and add
`?lib=../lib/`:

```
play/?lib=../lib/
```

## The library

Every volume is public domain, transcribed from its own scan and published as
app-ready JSON with a QC report per book, plus a `catalog.json` manifest this
reader loads first. The library is versioned and rebuilt by scripts; this reader
is not.

Change it, then rebuild the release: ```bash npm install # installs terser (the only dev dependency) npm run build # src/retro-strike.html -> dist/retro-strike.min.html ``` --- ## 📦 Project structure ``` retro-strike/ ├── src/retro-strike.html # 📜 readable, commented source (edit this) ├── dist/retro-strike.min.html # 🎮 minified, playable release (~90 KB) ├── tools/build.mjs # 🔧 minifier (extracts + compresses src -> dist) ├── assets/ # 🎨 banner, logo, social preview, screenshots ├── docs/ # 📚 architecture, controls, performance, audit ├── .github/ # ⚙️ Pages workflow, issue & PR templates ├── package.json # 📦 build script (dev-only) ├── CHANGELOG.md · CONTRIBUTING.md · CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md · SECURITY.md └── LICENSE ``` **Source vs release:** `src/` is the human-readable single file you edit; `dist/` is the same game compressed for shipping. The GitHub Pages workflow publishes `dist/` so the repo is instantly playable online. --- ## 🛠️ Tech Built from scratch with **zero runtime dependencies** — only web-platform APIs: - **Renderer** — a hand-written software rasteriser on **Canvas 2D**: per-face camera-space projection, near-plane clipping and a painter's-algorithm depth sort. Sprites are cached to offscreen canvases and blitted in one `drawImage`. - **Audio** — procedural **chiptune** (bass + arpeggio) and all SFX synthesised live from `OscillatorNode` / noise buffers via the **Web Audio API**. - **World** — a seeded **xorshift PRNG** for reproducible arenas, flood-fill reachability so nothing spawns in a sealed room, and biome quadrants (default / ice / lava). - **Persistence** — settings, stats, achievements, leaderboard, campaign progress, run save and ghost replay in **`localStorage`** (every access guarded). - **Input** — Pointer Lock for mouse aim, multi-touch with a virtual joystick, and the Gamepad API. --- ## ⚡ Performance The game targets a smooth **~60 FPS** on modest hardware and caps its frame rate so high-refresh displays stay cool. | Optimisation | Effect | |---|---| | Precomputed wall/lava cell lists | Minimap no longer rescans the 48×48 grid twice per frame | | Quantised fog-colour cache | Avoids ~700 string builds per frame | | Cached sprite atlases | One `drawImage` per sprite instead of per-pixel fills | | Distance-culled particles/bullets | Fewer short-lived objects and closures per frame | | Hoisted palettes & sort comparators | Removes per-frame allocations | | `dt` clamp + FPS cap | Stable physics on any refresh rate | See [`docs/PERFORMANCE.md`](docs/PERFORMANCE.md) for the measured before/after. --- ## 🚢 Publishing 1. **Create the repo** and push: ```bash git init git add . git commit -m "Initial commit — RETRO STRIKE v1.1.0" git branch -M main git remote add origin https://github.com/drsamonline/retro-strike.git git push -u origin main ``` 2. **Make the badges yours** — find-and-replace every `drsamonline/retro-strike` in `README.md` with your GitHub username and repo name (the banner, star/issue badges and the **▶️ Play** link all use it). 3. **Turn on the live demo** — go to **Settings → Pages → Build and deployment → Source: Deploy from a branch**, then pick the `main` branch and the `/docs` folder. The site is served from the `docs/` folder on `main` via the legacy Pages build and is published at `https://drsamonline.github.io/retro-strike/`. 4. **Cut a release** — create a tag and attach `dist/retro-strike.min.html` as the release asset so players can download a single file: ```bash git tag -a v1.1.0 -m "RETRO STRIKE v1.1.0" git push origin v1.1.0 ``` 5. *(Optional)* **Social preview** — upload `assets/social-preview.png` under **Settings → General → Social preview**. --- ## 🗺️ Roadmap > 🧍 **Single-player only — permanently.** RETRO STRIKE has no servers, accounts, matchmaking or networking of any kind, and none are planned. Every item below runs entirely in your browser. **✅ Shipped** - [x] **v1.3.0** — new enemy archetypes (**Sniper**, **Healer**), a second boss (**Summoner**), and **custom arena seeds** - [x] **v1.4.0** — **12 campaign levels** (4 new chapters), **Bestiary** codex, **controller remapping**, **colour-vision palettes**, **3-step HUD scale**, and **variable arena size** (48 / 64 / 80) **💡 Ideas (all client-side)** - [ ] Daily mutator combinations / a weekly challenge - [ ] Weapon mastery perks - [ ] An endless "boss rush" mode - [ ] Replay export — share a run as a file > The old "optional WebGL renderer" idea is **dropped**: the software renderer already handles the largest arena size comfortably, so a second renderer would add a lot of complexity for no real gain. Large arenas are now a built-in setting instead. Have an idea? Saga

A small, dependency-free visual-novel engine for the browser.
Plain JavaScript · one stylesheet · no build step · works offline

Landing page  ·  Play the game it powers — Aethelgard: The Books  ·  Aethelgard — The Books

---

A small, dependency-free visual-novel engine for the browser.
Plain JavaScript · one stylesheet · no build step · works offline

--- **Saga** is a visual-novel engine that runs from a static file server with nothing installed. It was built to make *Aethelgard — The Books*, and it is released on its own so you can make something else with it. > **The engine is MIT.** It ships no story and no artwork — you bring your own. > The *Aethelgard* games' artwork and story are a separate work, © Dr. Sohil > Momin, all rights reserved — free to play, not open source, and not contained > in this repository. See [Licence](#licence). ## ▶️ See it in action This engine was built to make **Aethelgard — The Books**, a visual novel in three books — 36 chapters and seven endings, all authored in plain `.scene` text files that this engine reads. Play it here: **[drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/books/](https://drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/books/)** It is one of two games in the *Aethelgard* world; the other is an RPG on a different engine, [drsamonline/Aethelgard-Engine](https://github.com/drsamonline/Aethelgard-Engine). Both live together in **[drsamonline/aethelgard-games](https://github.com/drsamonline/aethelgard-games)**. --- ## Contents - [See it in action](#-see-it-in-action) - [Run the engine](#run-the-engine) - [How to play](#how-to-play) - [Features](#features) - [Project layout](#project-layout) - [Write a chapter](#write-a-chapter) - [Art](#art) - [Mods](#mods) - [Making it yours](#making-it-yours) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Contributing](#contributing) - [Licence](#licence) --- ## Run the engine The engine ships **code only** — no story, no art. To see it in action, play **[Aethelgard: The Books](https://drsamonline.github.io/aethelgard-games/play/books/)**, which is built on this engine. To build your own, see [Making it yours](#making-it-yours). The engine is served like any static site — it reads its scene files over http, so use a server (opening `index.html` by double-click will not work in most browsers): ```bash python3 -m http.server 8000 # open http://localhost:8000 ``` No install, no build, no dependencies. Any static server works (`npx serve`, nginx, GitHub Pages — anything). ## How to play You read the story and make choices. That's the whole game — but there are a few things worth knowing before your first run. ### Controls | key | action | |---|---| | `Space` / `Enter` | advance dialogue (clicking the stage works too) | | `Tab` + `Enter` | move to a choice and pick it — every option is a real button | | `D` | open the **Diary** (people, places, lore, decisions, deeds) | | `B` | open the **Backlog** — scroll back through everything said | | `S` | save to localStorage (you can also export/import a JSON file) | | `Esc` | close the current panel | Mouse and touch work throughout; the layout is tested from 360×640 up. ### Choices and gates Some options show a requirement like `[Bonds 2]`. If you don't meet it, the option is shown **greyed out with the reason** — never hidden. You should always be able to see what you missed. ### The four axes and the endings Every choice secretly moves one of four counters: **Mercy**, **Truth**, **Bonds** or **Conviction**. They stay hidden while you play and are revealed in the epilogue. The ending is not a score — it is the *shape*: which axis led, and how far the four spread. Seven endings resolve from that shape, from *Dawn* to *Hollow*: | ending | the shape that earns it | |---|---| | Dawn | every axis high — nothing was sacrificed | | The Long Road | mercy carried the run | | The Weight | truth led, and its cost | | Ash | a balanced, ordinary run | | The Crown's Shadow | conviction led, without mercy | | Silence | never committed to anything | | Hollow | refused everything | The resolver lives in `js/endings.js` and is pure data — rewrite it freely. ### Tips - Read the Diary as you go — it fills itself and tells you who matters. - There is no wrong way to play; the seven endings are shapes, not grades. - Reaching the end of a chapter list without an ending still returns you to the title screen safely. ## Features | | | |---|---| | **Dialogue** | per-line speaker, ten expressions, a portrait that changes with the mood of the line | | **Choices** | branching, with stat gates shown greyed-out and their reason visible — never a hidden lock | | **Branches** | `@label` / `@goto`, so a choice can rejoin the main line | | **Four axes** | hidden counters that every choice moves; the ending is their *shape* | | **Seven endings** | resolved from which axis led and how far they spread | | **The Diary** | people, places, lore, decisions and deeds, filled as you play | | **Intro cards** | a character card the first time someone appears | | **Achievements** | declared in the script, unlocked in play | | **Save / export** | localStorage, plus export and import as a JSON file | | **Backlog** | scroll back through everything said | | **Music** | synthesised with Web Audio — no audio files at all | | **Mods** | drop a folder in `mods/`, it is found; five safety rules enforced | | **Mobile** | tested from 360×640 up | | **Accessibility** | full keyboard play, visible focus outlines, dialog semantics, `prefers-reduced-motion` honoured | ## Project layout ``` index.html the page css/style.css the look js/core.js state, save, settings, the four axes js/script.js the scene-script parser js/chars.js the cast and the regions <- YOUR DATA js/graphics.js sprite lookup js/music.js synthesised sound js/play.js the runner: dialogue, choices, diary, cards js/ui.js title, Diary, settings, endings js/mods.js the mod loader and its safety rules js/endings.js the axis shape and the ending resolver js/boot.js wiring scenes/ the story, as plain text <- YOU ADD THIS assets/sprites/ the art <- YOU ADD THIS docs/SCENE-FORMAT.md how to write a chapter ``` Everything marked **YOUR DATA** is meant to be replaced. The engine does not know anything about any particular story. ## Write a chapter A chapter is a plain text file, one instruction per line. Full reference in `docs/SCENE-FORMAT.md`. ``` @title The Demo — Chapter One @bg road @mood uneasy narrate A road at dusk. wanderer neutral "You're the Keeper of the hall, then." keeper warm "I am." choice * "Tell the truth." => truth+1, bonds+1 * [Bonds 2] "Say you knew her mother." => bonds+2, mercy+1 end @label after @mood calm keeper warm "Then come in. It's cold." ``` Then add one line to `scenes/manifest.js` and the chapter appears. ## Art The engine finds a portrait by name: ``` char.. -> _.webp, then .webp bg. -> bg_.webp ``` Ship no art and the game runs text-only — a missing portrait simply hides. The sprites in `assets/sprites/` here are **generated placeholders**, PolyForm Noncommercial-licensed like the engine. Replace them. Rebuild the index after adding art: ```bash python3 tools/make-sprite-index.py assets/sprites ``` ## Mods Drop a folder into `mods/` with a `mod.js`, add a line to `mods/mods.json`, and the engine finds it. Mods can add chapters, cast, regions, achievements, and can also *replace* existing entries. Five safety rules are enforced so a mod can never break a running game: 1. Every load is wrapped in try/catch — a broken mod cannot take the game down. 2. Structural mods apply at boot only, never mid-session. 3. `requiresMods` is honoured. 4. Two mods claiming the same `provides` conflict; the first wins, the second is refused **visibly**. 5. `loadAfter` orders mods deterministically. See `mods/README.md` for the full manifest format and the example mods. ## Making it yours The engine ships **no story**. To make a game you replace three things: | file | what to put in it | |---|---| | `js/chars.js` | your cast, your regions, `G.TITLE`, `G.SLUG`, `G.ACHIEVEMENTS` | | `scenes/` | your chapters, and a `manifest.js` listing them | | `assets/sprites/` | your art | Nothing else needs to change. The engine starts at whatever scene the manifest lists first, so it never needs to know your chapter ids. ## Documentation | document | about | |---|---| | `docs/SCENE-FORMAT.md` | the full scene-script reference | | `mods/README.md` | writing a mod, and the five safety rules | | `assets/sprites/README.md` | the art naming convention | | `CONTRIBUTING.md` | how to send changes to the engine | | `CHANGELOG.md` | release history | ## Contributing Read `CONTRIBUTING.md` first — the engine is meant to stay small, with no build step and no dependencies. Bug fixes, parser features inside the existing format, accessibility work and new mod hook points are all welcome. ## Support Free, offline, accountless — and staying that way. If it earned its keep: | | | |---|---| | UPI (India) | `drsohilboi@ybl` — payee Dr. Sohil Momin, open amount, or scan [the QR](docs/assets/upi-qr.svg) | | GitHub Sponsors | [github.com/sponsors/drsamonline](https://github.com/sponsors/drsamonline) | | Ko-fi | [ko-fi.com/matneo](https://ko-fi.com/matneo) | | PayPal | [paypal.me/drsohilmomin](https://paypal.me/drsohilmomin?locale.x=en_GB&country.x=IN) | | My books | [Amazon author store](https://www.amazon.com/stores/author/B08ZT331LY/allbooks?ccs_id=aed72b9f-71d9-41dc-adee-e9368a317acc) | | More apps | [drsamonline.github.io](https://drsamonline.github.io/) | | Email | [sohilmomin2000@gmail.com](mailto:sohilmomin2000@gmail.com) | Nothing is gated behind it: no accounts, no tracking, no network requests. ## Licence **Two licences, clearly split:** | what | licence | |---|---| | The Saga engine — code, stylesheet, tools | **[PolyForm Noncommercial](LICENSE)** — use it, fork it, ship it | | The *Aethelgard — The Books* game's artwork, story and characters | © Dr. Sohil Momin, **all rights reserved** — free to play, not open source. Not contained in this repository | If you build a game on this engine, your content is yours; the engine stays MIT. ---

# Seance

<!-- shot:start -->

![Screenshot](docs/shot.png)

<!-- shot:end -->

[![live](https://img.shields.io/badge/live-online-22c55e)](https://drsamonline.github.io/seance/)
[![License: PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-PolyForm%20Noncommercial%201.0.0-blue)](LICENSE)
[![download](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/drsamonline/seance

**Sealed notes, opened once.** A message you can send that cannot be read twice: write it,
seal it with a passphrase, send the sealed text (or the `.txt` it downloads). The reader opens
it once on their own device — offline, no account — and the second attempt finds nothing.

Built with **crypto-kit** (AES-256-GCM) and **web-kit**.

## What it does

- **Seal:** a note + a passphrase → a sealed text (base64) you can paste anywhere.
- **Open:** paste the sealed text, or open the `.txt` you were sent, + the passphrase → the note.
- Authenticated encryption, so a wrong passphrase or altered text is rejected.
- Share the text and the passphrase **separately** — the text is useless alone.
- Everything happens on your device; nothing is sent anywhere.

## Run it

Open `docs/index.html`. That's the whole app — offline, from `file://` or Pages.
(It needs a **secure context** for Web Crypto: Pages is https, so the live site is
fine; some browsers restrict `file://`.)

## Structure

```
docs/index.html      the app
docs/web-kit.js      the shared runtime (drsamonline/web-kit)
```

## Honest limits

- A passphrase-sealed note is only as strong as the passphrase. Use a strong one.
- "Opened once" is remembered **on this device** — it is a courtesy, not
  enforcement; a determined reader can clear storage or open it elsewhere.
- Not a substitute for a vetted messaging app for anything truly sensitive.
